It is allied with Alaxa.

[2051 – later developments] Yamatetsu buys Biogene Technologies of San Diego on June 25 for its metahuman genetic research.

[2052 – later developments] Late in the year, Yamatetsu Seattle acquires CrashCart after a shadowrun on the outfit that owned it, and purges CrashCart's entire management structure.

[2053 – later developments] Yamatetsu's Integrated System Products facility at Fort Lewis is said to keep a couple of hell hounds patrolling the grounds at night.

[2054 – later developments] Street lore holds that Gentech -- which Aztechnology absorbed in 2048 -- was owned by Yamatetsu; the claim is unconfirmed.

[2055 – later developments] Yamatetsu owns the downtown tower in Denver's UCAS Sector where Fuchs-Auberlien Financial Services rents three floors. Its own people run building security, with passcard entry and a holding area for unvouched visitors, and internal problems have made the corporation unusually strict about security.

[2056 – later developments] Aztlan's records credit Yamatetsu with logistics, and allegedly California staging support, for Operation Reciprocity in 2048.

[2057 – later developments] In California, Yamatetsu has engineering, warehouse, shipping, education and metahuman-employment interests, with armed response, integrated magical security and parabiological assets, and draws criticism over discrimination. San Francisco employee Sho Kojima steals internal spreadsheets, published by the October 25th Alliance as 'The Little Red Schoolhouse', proving that Yamatetsu's touted metahuman-friendly 'schools' feed Central Valley testing labs; the corporation blames a rogue mid-level manager, promotes Sho's father as the internal 'hero' who exposed it, and funnels PR nuyen into Oakland.

[2059 – later developments] Chairman Tadamako Shibanokuji suffers a stroke in January and dies, leaving control of his stock to his estranged ork son Yuri. On 5 May the board approves moving the headquarters from Kyoto to Vladivostok: the free spirit Buttercup rallies enough shareholder proxies to pass the motion and then personally buys up the publicly traded stock, giving her roughly 37 percent of the corporation. The move becomes the founding catalyst of the Pacific Prosperity Group. Japan's Ministry of Trade answers with escalating regulatory harassment and economic punishment, and Japan's metahumans, who lose their most willing employer, take the public blame, sparking a spike in racial violence there. Amid regional conflict Yamatetsu pauses its Saotome AquaDomes project.

[2061 – later developments] Yamatetsu's Seattle representatives learn of Neuranalysis' SENSE neural scanner and see its value for CrashCart: exclusive use would pull customers from DocWagon, and later licensing would pay twice. Less than a month before the breakthrough they begin quiet negotiations to buy Neuranalysis outright, but Deus destroys the company first. Overwatch later forges Yamatetsu security identities, cyberware permits and plane tickets to fly runners armed into corporate-owned Hong Kong. Yamatetsu offers employee, family, regional and metahuman-oriented services.

[2062 – later developments] Buttercup, who sits on the board, strikes a bargain with Hestaby to divert some of the chi Wuxing has been accumulating under its Hong Kong Skytower to Yamatetsu's power site in Vladivostok -- Wuxing checked, Yamatetsu lifted. The new worldwide headquarters is on Popov Island, where the deposed former chairman Hideo Yoshida keeps a private estate and men personally loyal to him.

[2062 – later developments] Yamatetsu's Gagarin is the only probe to reach Halley's Comet on the Probe Race's first leg, but contact is lost just as its sensors begin collecting data, publicly humiliating the corporation. After perihelion a burst transmission shows it intact but crippled, on a course that will still drop its sensor module during the Earth flyby. CEO Saru Iwano orders total secrecy, but the traffic alerts rival corporations. Yamatetsu owns Alaxa, a small Everett biotechnology front, and feeds it zero-gravity data from the Shibanokuji orbital station. Thunderwalker's militia kills the first recovery team in Manitou territory; a second, led by Pierre O'Rourke under section commander Nikoli Rostov, may offer agreements Yamatetsu does not intend to honor. If Yamatetsu recovers the data, it learns that another craft reached the comet first and buries the evidence.

[2064 – later developments] Yamatetsu owns CrashCart and is always on the lookout for new medical technologies. When word of glowing, astrally active tissue in a DocWagon safety deposit box reaches it, it sends a six-member covert ops team from the Seattle division -- mostly Russian, five combat specialists and a mage, extremely loyal, trained closely enough to look Battletac-linked, and booby-trapped so neither they nor their gear can be traced -- into the Kethers Building. Seattle Chief of Operations Donald Watanabe is a DocWagon Platinum client. With AG Chemie and Paladin Medical Technologies, Yamatetsu wins the UCAS military pharmaceuticals contract, with Fort Lewis as testbed; the partnership is making money hand over fist. Yamatetsu is a paying customer of Griffin Biotechnology, and the same covert team strikes Griffin's facility on the same night as Rose Croix, with orders to demolish the underground half and close the tunnel, shutting down Griffin's nanotechnology work.

[2064 – later developments] Yamatetsu is hit first and hardest in the Crash: Ex Pacis seeds a Jormungand code egg in the MetaMatrix central routing hub, the Yamatetsu grid is among the first the worm takes, and the virtual management network collapses, cutting Vladivostok off from its subsidiaries. CEO Saru Iwano is blamed and removed -- he had nothing to do with it, but it gives Buttercup and Yuri Shibanokuji their opening -- and replaced by Anatoly Kirilenko, the maverick behind the Mars mission, with a radical five-year plan. Turkestan is on fire with Yamatetsu, Global Sandstorm and Saeder-Krupp fighting over its government; Yamatetsu preys on smaller Pacific Prosperity Group members, fails to take Cross Biomedical, and sets up joint ventures with the Genesis Consortium. Hideo Yoshida, now a half-ton rock-like SURGE changeling, has reversed his racism and funds odd archaeological digs in the Andes. Yamatetsu and Moscow bless President Rybinski's flight to Vladivostok with most of the Polish Central Bank's reserves.

organizations.name: Knight Errant Security Services
organizations.description: Knight Errant Security Services is the Ares Macrotechnology division that provides private and corporate security of every kind, physical and electronic: guard and response contracts, residential and home-security packages, municipal policing, crisis management, special forces and counter-insurgency. In Seattle it is second only to Lone Star among the firms protecting corporations, and it keeps a training academy at 715 NE Third where every cadet is cross-trained -- its deckers know weapons and site security, and its guards know computers. Beyond Seattle it is the leading private police provider in the capital and one of the three companies that police Manhattan. Officially Executive Vice President Roger Soaring Owl runs it; in practice Ares CEO Damien Knight takes a direct hand in its day-to-day operations.

organizations.notes:
Ares Arms' extensive military assets are believed to be available to Knight Errant on a contingency basis. Last year's well-publicized Renraku contract cut vandalism at the Arcology Project by half. Forged Ares/Knight Errant ID cards are in circulation; Fuchi's field agents used them hunting Karen Whisper in Seattle.

Knight Errant protects every Biogene Technologies facility; a six-trooper Biogene/KE team under Jason Walker is the optional cavalry at the DNA/DOA safe house. It supplies Global Technologies' guards, deckers and mages as needed -- three rent-a-cops were on the fourth floor the night of the heist, and two died to Griffin's razors -- sends a heavily armed pickup squad for Tee Hee if Urlan calls, and has raided Hollywood Simsense for BTL production.

[2051 – later developments] Strice Foods hires a four-man KE team (a cut above corporate guards, not elite: Predator IIs, HK MP-5TXs, concussion grenades, armor jackets; a Nightsky, an Americar lead car and a Wasp three minutes out) to guard Euphoria; MegaMedia switches all its security from Lone Star to KE and loses the team to Ant soldiers at Pacific Towers. Nearly a full company surrounds the Amber Gel plant during MegaMedia's raid, and a KE executive offers 1,000 nuyen per runner for a full report on the Hive. Lochlann Investments' guards retrain at KE's local facility. In Dragon Hunt KE's intelligence section faxes complete dossiers on the runners to the Cobalt Marie within minutes; its 'security teams' flash a card and walk away from Lone Star; it takes the Redmond Arms with about 75 troops, five APCs, a chopper and Citymasters under a short, bald plainclothes investigator; it runs an interrogation safehouse in Beverly Park, Everett (six guards, two interrogators, a forty-strong Urban Reaction team fifteen minutes out); and after Ares buys the contract from Lone Star it guards Seattle General with thirty of its best. A senior guard may recognize Coinspinner and stand aside. Its rank and file take a dim view of runners who waste twenty or thirty of their comrades.

[2053 – later developments] Caravan Productions books KE for The Shadows' Kingdome show, the only outfit big enough for the job. Shim Bright's KE bodyguards have a personal-defense contract only: they ask runners to drop weapons, defend Bright with less enthusiasm once he starts the fight, call for backup and will not engage Lone Star.

[2054 – later developments] Knight Errant is Lone Star's main competitor for law-enforcement contracts and is Ares's principal security division, reporting through Seattle and UCAS chains. It offers courier, escort, personal and private security in Germany. It finances a covert clinic in half of Xanadu Studios' Renton building, behind polished black doors with cameras wired to KE headquarters; four special agents track trespassers before abandoning the site. The Association of Advertising Producers honors a KE Seattle campaign apparently filmed during a subterranean security operation, and Knight Errant wins best commercial art at Cannes.

[2055 – later developments] Knight Errant holds the security and law-enforcement contract for Denver's CAS sector and guards Fuchs-Auberlien Financial Services and its employees' families there, reacting in force to anything at the Brandis Development (whose security it designed) and loitering in the Yamatetsu building. It cannot prevent Shawn Gaffney's kidnapping but takes control within fifteen minutes, sends a forensic magic team for blood within ninety and tracks him astrally; the ritual sample is astrally vulnerable, and a gutsy runner can track the Sending and destroy it. It works jointly with Eagle Security and complains in vain about Audrey W.'s reports. In Chicago it holds studio contracts and a temporary contract in Cabrini. Its August raid unleashes the Chicago insect hive on the city, and it then helps enforce the quarantine.

[2057 – later developments] Knight Errant provides corporate and government security in California. Its brutal suppression of Detroit riots against Chicago refugees draws criticism, later balanced by efficient, restrained riot control after Dunkelzahn's assassination.

[2058 – later developments] Ares's Strain III-Beta operation clears the Chicago hive in February. Knight Errant holds Boston's citywide enforcement contract, backed by the corporation Minuteman and neighborhood watches, runs Boston's gridguide with Novatech, and is the last-resort backup at the Dunkelzahn Magical Research Building. In Seattle its subsidiary offers discounted 'supplemental' security and a PR campaign against Lone Star's 'impersonal' image, hoping the Mob war gives it the metroplex contract at last, and may arrange runs to damage Lone Star's standing.

[2059 – later developments] During the paranormal-animal attack wave KE offers Seattle extermination teams, angling to embarrass Lone Star and take its contract. It patrols the Ares office park housing Parashield's facility on 45-minute cycles and can send a Citymaster of twelve officers and four combat mages if a break-in escalates.

[2062 – later developments] Knight Errant guards the AresSpace Silicon Valley office park under Major Layton. Its officers live on site and watch the leading scientists around the clock, with a security rigger always on duty (a troll running an Ares Sentinel on the gate wall and an Ares Guardian inside) and a night shaman who summons a city spirit at sunrise and sunset and a watcher at night. Kourou police may contract local work to KE.

[2064 – later developments] Knight Errant holds the contract for Griffin Biotechnology's Everett compound, taken at a discount because Ares is a prime investor, and fills every security post except the Security Director's. Four shift teams (Alpha, Bravo, Charlie, Delta) rotate through days, swings and mids, with the team on its three-day break as the recall pool; a normal shift is 28 guards and a high-alert shift 39 with K-9 teams. External guards carry all-Ares kit (light security armor with low-light, AZ-150 stun baton, Predator II with gel rounds, Ravener SMG, two flash-bangs); internal guards refit at the armory on any alarm. Guards radio in every ten minutes, have at least two years' service and combat experience, and are all but immune to fast talk, bribery and intimidation (+4 TN); the rapid response team wears full heavy security armor with Ares Alphas and air-timed mini-grenades. Doctrine is containment: investigate by sensor, put assets on the opposite side of any distraction, commit spirits and elementals, and hold until backup arrives. A black removal van hoses intruders with gamma-scopolamine from Ares Cascade rifles, and the drugged wake up in the Marine Drive Stuffer Shack lot minus their illegal gear. The control room confirms every gate opening by radio and telecom, which defeats magically dominated gate guards. A barghest and handler patrol periodically; the schedule costs a 2,000-nuyen bribe. Tired of repeated breaches, KE illegally captures a runner team, doses it with Laes and depressants, and trains its elite squads against it in a simsense copy of the facility in southern Tacoma. After the Griffin bombing KE stock dips a tenth of a point behind 'the Grey Wall of Silence'.

[2064 – later developments] Gregory Rasmussen, Seattle Division Chief of Operations for Ares/Knight Errant, is DocWagon Platinum client 99-815, and Rose Croix steals his clone to start moving security contracts its way -- of the four victims, his employer has both the investigators and the private army to find out who did it. KE exhibits beside Lone Star and the FBI at the Confederation of Security Providers show, and the three can be played against each other. It holds the security office of the downtown skyscraper housing the restaurant Selenium and logs every action of a decker given the restaurant's temporary password. Two KE guards at Laubenstein Plaza's reception do nothing about J.P. Morlock's ork thugs at Elevator Three. KE's Boston Division case 64-12-30.457F-05 -- a SINless John Doe found frozen in Charlestown who turns out to be Atlantic Logistics manager Leroy Carper, his SIN erased with the registry backups -- leads to at least eight similar cases, stonewalling by the UCAS and Global SIN registries, and a warning from Internal Affairs. On the morning of the Crash a KE dispatcher in the capital sends Unit 74 to the Smithsonian, where thieves took a Draco Foundation artifact less than ten minutes after the security system failed -- they knew it was coming.

organizations.name: Lone Star Security
organizations.description: Lone Star Security Services Inc. is a private, extraterritorial police and security corporation headquartered in Austin, with separate enforcement and corporate arms and national operations in Quebec, the UCAS and the CAS. Founder Clay Wilson patterned his operation on the Texas Rangers of the Old West, and standards have changed little since his brother James took over, though Lone Star now accepts women 'peace officers'; every employee is expected to be proficient with a sidearm. Lone Star holds the law enforcement contract for Seattle, where William Loudon, Marshal of the Seattle Division, serves as Chief of Police from the Lone Star Security Building at Second Avenue and Union Street. It responds promptly in the downtown AAA area and patrols corporate Seattle frequently, while patrols in the Barrens are few and far between.

organizations.notes:
Local operations include street patrols, armed backup, corporate escort work, offline evidence files, vice investigations, and outside help after a destructive Matrix incident. Lone Star only stopped the Night of Rage violence in 2039 after the United Corporation Council intervened.

Lone Star publicly accuses Aztechnology of staging military maneuvers with a company-sized unit, attack helicopters and urban assault vehicles at the Tacoma docks and petitions the Seattle Corporate Council (spokesperson Elyse Sunberg); Aztechnology blames Lone Star for the roughly one million nuyen in damage. Detective Lucas Niles tracks sewer-dweller deaths in Tacoma, which rise 300 percent if the Metavirus creatures got loose.

Lone Star is the likely buyer of Applied Security Concepts, the failing Seattle computer and physical security contractor that guards Mitsuhama's Cavilard Research Center.

A Lone Star patrol will pull over runners who look armed for war on a trip to the corner store. Police statements are a permanent record -- 'Just what is your SIN, citizen?' -- so runners clear out before the Badges arrive.

Lone Star patrols Underworld 93 on major nights and wants no incidents around its important patrons; police respond within minutes. Detainees spend a couple of hours in a holding cell and give statements for the record, while SINless detainees may also face a violent back-room interrogation. Bail is 500 nuyen each.

Patrols are rare in the Redmond Barrens until nine dissected prostitutes in four nights force them in -- beefed-up patrols, Wasp helicopters with searchlights, street samurai rousted and their razors swabbed with chemlab kits, and a lid on the media; five patrol cars in five minutes 'must be a new donut shop'. Lone Star pulls over anyone carrying more than a sidearm near Reno's and has raided HSE for BTLs.

It is opposed to The Teddy Boys, Iron Legion.

[2051 – later developments] The city contract is up for renewal. Lone Star confiscates over 20,000 BTL chips breaking one of the city's largest smuggling rings, is named co-defendant in Aztechnology's suit over the helicopter that crashed near the Pyramid the night Honey Brighton got out, and is dropped by MegaMedia in favor of Knight Errant. It investigates Euphoria's first kidnapping as an amateur fan-cult job, and does not patrol Pier 36.

[2051 – later developments] In June Wendy Manderscheid retires as board chairman and arranges for James Wilson to succeed her. Wilson gives up the CEO post, installs Theodore W. D. Winslow, and steers most of a new stock offering into Winslow's portfolio.

[2051 – later developments] Heavy patrols work Redmond Center Mall and the Redmond Business Nest, rousting loiterers and hauling in visible hardware; Bellevue-edge alarms draw a response in one to six minutes, Redmond Barrens silent alarms in about thirty. The 25th Precinct (Commander Wallace Haygood, Capt. Judith Bentz of Arson-Sabotage) closes the Grodin's Tavern fire -- freelance writer Zebediah Wanderly and decker Juli 'Icepick' Parkhurst dead in the basement beside the Shadowland server hub -- as a torch job gone wrong, no further action; the chip on Wanderly's body was 'blank'. Superdad's in Kingsgate is a favorite cop bar.

[2051 – later developments] Captain Grissim, transferred from Lone Star-LA and straight as they come, commands raids from a Citymaster with rigger Ronnie, a pair of wage mages for astral cover, Yellowjackets, Wasps and an Ares Dragon command post. Heat tactics include raids on every known haunt, media alerts naming runners Class A felons, homes staked out, vehicles impounded, squatters paid to snitch, 24-hour interrogation under Analyze Truth and astral surveillance on release. The board is leaned on by the Tir Tairngire ambassador. Lone Star will not fire a shot on private corporate property; its corporate spokesperson is Jacob Bright.

[2051 – later developments] Lone Star holds Seattle General's security contract when the Dragon crashes through the roof, until Ares buys the contract out from under it at an incredibly high price and Knight Errant moves in. A Knight Errant team leader's plastic card makes an irate Lone Star cop hand it back and apologize. Sgt. Jonathan Phillips speaks on the downtown squatter-gang massacre (Yakuza suspected).

[2051 – later developments] The Rhododendron Conservatory's guards hand impostors to Lone Star, and the local branch lets prisoners buy their way out for 1,000 nuyen. Lone Star handles crowd control at Club Zor for Concrete Dreams, and twenty-eight murders at Elby's Bar and Grill go uninvestigated for at least a day. PANICBUTTONs at Sylvan Information in Bellevue bring a carload of heavily armed officers in three minutes; a failed team wakes in a holding cell and is questioned for a couple of weeks. Lone Star answers alarms at APN headquarters and investigates both APN and anyone caught there. The armored van from the Grantleigh Park fracas turns up in a field in the northern Sprawl with traces of knock-out gas -- then the Feds clamp a UCAS security rating on the case because it is CIA-issue.

[2051 – later developments] On September 23 an anonymous tip leads Lone Star to several bodies in an abandoned International District warehouse. Desk Sergeant Toku Yoshihiro calls the deaths simple go-gang hooliganism and denies yakuza or Mafia involvement, while informed sources connect them to the disappearance of alleged yakuza officer Tokugawa Tetsuo.

[2051 – later developments] On October 26 an unidentified gunman enters Lone Star's Seattle Downtown precinct with an assault rifle and kills Officer Lucas Kidd and Ken Shaker, the missing Renraku technician Kidd was protecting. Commander Sam McMillin condemns the bombing of the Universal Brotherhood as terrorism. Lone Star relays the FBI's assessment of the runners, while attempts to contact either agency lead into a trap.

[2053 – later developments] In May, Seattle chief William Loudon treats the gang war as warfare, places every officer on active duty, cancels retirements and asks Governor Schultz to mobilize the Metroplex Guard. Spokesperson Carol Lake says the metroplex contract does not cover prolonged violence on that scale. Detective Koren Thark of the Street Affairs Division's Metahuman Gangs unit is reprimanded for dissent and uses discretionary funds to hire runners. Lone Star Data Services holds synopses on the Ancients, the incendiary attacks on Seattle gangs, Lucinda Tangier and St. John, although Tangier's file is deleted through an illegal intrusion. Lone Star's outside counsel on elven affairs, Shim Bright, is a Tir agent. Successful containment reduces overnight violence by seventy-one percent within a week.

[2053 – later developments] An anonymous tip plus manufactured evidence from Highstar has Lone Star issue warrants for the runners for Allenby's murder with the Rules of Apprehension waived -- dead or alive, and dead is easier. Proof of Teague's guilt gets the warrants recalled, with no apology and no restitution. Lone Star 'found' Jetblack's badly trashed body two years ago and never patrols Kobe Terrace Park hard enough to stop the night-time gang wars.

[2053 – later developments] Lone Star acquires military-surplus LAVs with riot-control equipment, to be stationed around Seattle for rapid emergency response rather than used as patrol craft. Governor Schultz's office supports the purchase, though one official warns that without more training, 'those LAVs will just be fraggin' big stun batons.' Lone Star has no leads on the missing Robert Gray Bear, son of Gaetronics president David Gray Bear, and discounts foul play.

[2054 – later developments] After Keane leaks that the runners killed Bubba, Lone Star seeks them on suspicion of murder; an officer contact can clear the team. Lone Star finds Baby Joe's body near the brawl zone the Friday after the game. On June 4, spokesperson Jules Nedich blames Preacher's 7,000-strong Redmond rally for three incidents and six arrests and warns 'if he continues to drive his people to violence, violence is what he'll get'.

[2054 – later developments] Precinct 249 in Pinehurst, Everett, under Lieutenant Dolchev handles the Dark Angel 'suicide'; a Lone Star executive ordered the cover-up at Edward Crull's request, and forensics privately knows the corpse was a murdered squatter. Dolchev sells what he knows for 5,000 nuyen to the 'Police Widows Fund' and arrests anyone who bribes clumsily. Renton patrols are better trained and corporation-friendly. One patrolman's report of an unleashed barghest sits unconfirmed in SPU-1.

[2054 – later developments] Lone Star's subsidiaries have included Bartholomew Security, Absolute Software, a Canadian subsidiary since reabsorbed, and its Quebec subsidiary. The Austin head office organizes patrol into foot, cycle and auto sections, and the Seattle Triad Task Force is not operational. Thomas Macmillan chairs the Division of Patrol.

[2055 – later developments] In Denver, Lone Star polices the UCAS Sector of the Front Range Free Zone through a wholly owned subsidiary, Lone Star Security Services Denver, with a separate border function; it is all over any grab in its sector 'in a matter of moments'. Why it tolerates Dreamland is disputed, and the explanations contradict each other.

[2055 – later developments] Detective Rick Gordon investigates Neil Scott's murder because a cousin of the city's chief executive was nearby in a similar vehicle; ballistics, thermographic footprints and the sniper's saliva will identify Multitech's shooter within days. Lone Star has a contract with the Hammond Necroplex and administers the city's ghoul bounty. Project Hope's enrollment computer queries the Lone Star warrant database on every applicant. Lieutenant Dan Akkison fights a two-and-a-half-hour running battle with a vanload of shadowrunners from Downtown into the Redmond Barrens -- eight bystanders dead, twenty-seven injured, two troopers killed. Lone Star declines to step up enforcement in Glow City despite about 110 disappearances this year. La Maison d'Indochine in Bellevue calls Lone Star when its security systems trigger, and troublemakers handed over are jailed for two months.

[2057 – later developments] DI, DOC and DPI officers trace Sergeant Franco Tanner to a Renraku black project beneath a Ravenna music store.

[2058 – later developments] Seattle chief William Loudon ups patrols and cracks down hard on the syndicates as the Mob War escalates, only to see the Mafia, the Yakuza and the Triads target Lone Star officers directly. He quietly considers hiring shadowrunners for jobs his officers cannot legally do, and uses the crisis as leverage in the metroplex contract renegotiation -- leverage undercut by Knight Errant Seattle's campaign to look like the more 'personal' alternative. Nationally, Lone Star is involved in law-and-order politics, faces competition in Boston, and figures in the debate over proposed magical controls.

[2059 – later developments] A three-night wave of paranormal-animal attacks overwhelms the Paranormal Animal Control Division: a piasma runs loose downtown, a hell hound and several cockatrices escape from a Saeder-Krupp facility, and six officers die in apparent deliberate ambushes. Sergeant Victor Crocker, night commander of PAC Substation 25, handles the worst of it. Loudon publicly promises more patrols after Knight Errant offers to lend extermination teams, while Lone Star secretly hires shadowrunners through a fixer called Mike to resolve the crisis quietly, paying in new SINs and cleaned records. Lone Star Quebec and Knight Errant hold rival security contracts in Quebec, a natural flashpoint in the Ares and Cross Applied Technologies rivalry.

[2061 – later developments] During the blackout every available officer is called up and the Star is still swamped by thousands of alarms, dozens of accidents and hundreds of violent incidents; most officers use restraint, but in some areas panicking officers use unnecessary force and riots break out, until Governor Lindstrom calls out the Metroplex Guard and relations between the two sour further over jurisdiction. Kiell Rauglos of the arcology Resistance carries a Ruger Thunderbolt he took off the body of the racist Lone Star cop who killed his brother.

[2062 – later developments] Alaxa, an Everett biotechnology firm secretly owned by Yamatetsu, conceals that ownership by hiring off-duty Lone Star officers who need extra income; they are tired, try to immobilize intruders with splatguns and tasers, and call Lone Star for backup as soon as they realize they face shadowrunners. Lone Star also polices Vertigo, the downtown changeling club where Annika Griebe holds meetings.

[2064 – later developments] Freeway Park in Downtown is policed on the cheap by probationary officers who are not fully authorized police, with a Lone Star mage patrolling astrally. Lone Star has contracted the Puget Recycling Cooperative to destroy recovered small arms; the Halloweeners believe the guns are melted at PRC's Tacoma warehouse and plan to raid it, but they go straight to the smelters. The close ties between Ares and Lone Star make Star contacts unsafe for Ares business: one in three are tapped. Lone Star investigated the Snake Lodge massacre -- no signs of entry, every member brutally murdered -- and has no leads.

[2064 – later developments] The Westin Seattle carries a silent PanicButton contract with Lone Star that grants pre-approval to take whatever action a threat requires; downtown rates AAA response, and Lone Star can reroute contract guards from nearby properties. Lone Star is one of the agencies holding a partial copy of the Griffin Everett facility's floor plans, and the endpoint of the PanicButton systems at Mackie Construction. The DocWagon plant in rural Snohomish sits outside regular patrol routes, with a ten-minute response time.

[2064 – later developments] Acting on anonymous tips and drone video, Lone Star raids DocWagon clinic #147 in Fort Lewis and uncovers over two dozen sets of DNA-typed organs; Devon Tyler is expected to be convicted of first-degree murder. Shadowland assumes every anonymous input came from Rose Croix. The corner of 3rd and West in Puyallup is dark and unpoliced at three in the morning, while Lone Star does respond in the more prosperous part of Puyallup.

[2064 – later developments] Lone Star is one of the agencies C5 pools with EuroPol, the Russian UGB and the FBI during the covert campaign against Winternight -- in practice snatching suspects, quite a few innocents among them, and disposing of interrogation survivors in apparent accidents. In Seattle the AI Deus turns the metroplex's surveillance network, Lone Star and GridGuide against a runner team. In Pueblo, spokeswoman Lana Feingold handles the Austin paranimal escape from an Aztechnology facility after the Crash failed its containment locks.

organizations.name: Seattle Yakuza
organizations.description: The Yakuza arrived in Seattle with the refugees who fled Japan's collapse in 1996, took over the gambling clubs and protection rackets of the International District, and spread across the city into drugs, extortion and prostitution. The High Oyabun of Chiba made the local clans Dungeness Crabs of the 87th Prefecture, and the oyabun moved from street muscle into land, stock buyouts and corporate takeovers. After the 2043 purge of the syndicate's Korean bosses, Hanzo Shotozumi arrived in 2044 as regional oyabun and brought back the old ways -- loyalty above all, body tattoos, and the finger of any yakuza who fails the oyabun. Its hold on property, extortion, BTL chips and prostitution is stronger than ever: it is the largest and strongest underworld syndicate in Seattle.

leadership.name: Hanzo Shotozumi
leadership.title: Regional Oyabun
leadership.notes: Since 2044.

leadership.name: Ethneos
leadership.title: Oyabun, Bellevue
leadership.notes: Purported.

leadership.title: Oyabun, Watada-rengo
leadership.name: Akira Watada
leadership.notes: [2058] Oversees the Seattle gumis from Japan.

organizations.notes:
Each district has its own clans. Ethneos is the purported oyabun of Bellevue's largest and most powerful clan. In Tacoma the yakuza dominate outright: twenty-two years ago Waino Aho, then a mid-level clan accountant, secretly bought up cheap Tacoma property with yakuza money, and after the Night of Rage his clan had a stranglehold on the district and he rose to oyabun. Orman Koseba's clan grips Renton's businesses; Kim Marsau heads Puyallup's clan, having earned the post by corrupting the Sioux Nation's White Rock government. The yakuza also hold Everett's commercial docks.

Yakuza wear colorful tattoos in concealable places, more of them the higher the rank. They follow the code of zuni and sustain vendettas for decades. Anyone who harms a member without yakuza sanction signs his own death warrant, and surviving an attack on an oyabun takes another oyabun's permission. Runners the yakuza identify lose 1 Karma.

Beyond Seattle the yakuza failed to expand into Quebec, are growing in Chicago, and are split into several factions in the capital. Ryumyo's Japanese power base works through the yakuza and, through them, several Japanese megacorporations, and the yakuza are fighting the Red Dragon Triad over black-market and smuggling traffic in the Sea of Japan.

The Rubber Suit, an exclusive giant-monster-movie club in Everett, is a known yakuza hangout -- Mr. Radek chooses it for a first meeting -- and a plausible site for a Mafia, Seoulpa, Triad or hired-ganger attack on the local kobun, with bystanders in the crossfire. Among the exotica in Rat Vanian's Redmond storeroom is a carved, silk-lined box holding a handmade pearl-handled pistol with silencer and five rounds (Ares Viper Slivergun stats); Etiquette (Street) 5 with two successes recognizes yakuza symbols in the carving, and somebody will come asking for it. Doctor What buys protection from a powerful yakuza gang. Sandii's razor teeth are rumored to be a dissatisfied oyabun's gift. Clean Steve is known to Yakuza Boss contacts.

[2051 – later developments] Lone Star Sgt. Jonathan Phillips says six mangled squatter-gang bodies found behind a downtown establishment after a 2:30 a.m. firefight of fifteen to twenty men 'indicated Yakuza involvement'.

[2053 – later developments] Hanzo Shotozumi's Dungeness Crab clan is Seattle's senior clan, with Kim Marsau's clan senior in Puyallup and Toshihiro Ino's Whispering Nights holding Loveland, among the many clans active in the sprawl.

[2054 – later developments] The Sword Water clan runs its part of the sprawl under senior oyabun Homatsu Jinjiro, with the younger oyabun Kat Akmura and Shiro Usaka beneath him; all three have their fingers in Mitsuhama. Baby Joe Johnson, manager of the Seattle Screamers, owes the yakuza money after borrowing to cover a bet on his own team, and the Mafia uses 'the yaks hired the runners' as its cover story -- so the runners hear of yakuza involvement from everyone but the yakuza. After the voided game the yakuza want their money back from a man the Mafia is already killing.

[2057 – later developments] Fixer Isao Yamazaki, Lawrence Carroll's middleman for Human Nation, hires gangs and a professional strike team (Eichi, Sato, Reiko) in a failed bid to recover Masaru's stolen dragon egg -- part of a plot to discredit Dunkelzahn's presidential campaign.

[2058 – later developments] The Japan-based Watada-rengo under oyabun Akira Watada oversees three Seattle gumi: the dominant Shotozumi-gumi under Hanzo Shotozumi, who wants an independent West Coast rengo; the older rival Nishidon-gumi under Isao Nishidon; and the smaller, more progressive Shigeda-gumi under Takeo Shigeda (not the crime cell of the same name run by Sumiko Hotoda and Toroshi). The 2043 purge was Watada's: in January of that year he killed nearly all of Seattle's Korean yakuza leadership in a week called the Schism after they refused to renew their loyalty, and the survivors went underground as the Seoulpa Rings, who have never forgiven it. After the Mafia capo's death the yakuza move aggressively into Mafia gambling and vice while fighting the Triads and Seoulpa Rings on other fronts. A disputed Shadowland rumor claims Ryumyo has secretly controlled the Watada-rengo since the 1920s, with great hidden influence over Mitsuhama and lesser influence over Renraku, Shiawase, Yamatetsu and Fuchi.

[2060 – later developments] The Seattle syndicate is called the Shotozumi-rengo; its sokaiya branch, led by Toju Shotozumi, handles corporate dealings, stock purchases and the choice of which corporations to pressure.

organizations.name: Seattle Mafia
organizations.description: The Mafia first infiltrated Seattle in the 1950s, gaining a stranglehold over the docks almost overnight and squeezing a percentage out of everything that came into the city. Its Seattle operation, always controlled from Chicago, fought the Yakuza until a 2030 truce after both sides' leaders were assassinated. When Hanzo Shotozumi took over the Seattle Yakuza in 2044, the Mafia lured James O'Malley out of retirement and made him Don of the Seattle metroplex in 2045. Under O'Malley the mob has shown renewed energy, building power in the business centers and the lower levels of government, recruiting muscle from the Barrens, and sharply stepping up attacks on Yakuza businesses and officers. Downtown's Harbor Island is its stronghold, and the Don lives in Magnolia.

leadership.name: James O'Malley
leadership.title: Don
leadership.notes: Don of the Seattle metroplex since 2045.

leadership.name: Vincent "Numbers" Ciarniello
leadership.title: Don
leadership.notes: [2064] Accountant by temperament; trades on advance knowledge of corporate upheaval.

leadership.name: Maurice "Butcher" Bigio
leadership.title: Capo
leadership.notes: [2058] Protects Al's Stuffer Shack in Puyallup and eats there after hours.

organizations.notes:
O'Malley's district bosses: Jefferson Higa is said to be capo in Bellevue. Matt Yuhl was flown in from New York to establish a foothold in Yakuza-dominated Tacoma. Gerard Vigilia, a trusted confidant of the Don, runs Everett's illegal gambling and prostitution around Casino Corner. Jonathan Giarritano controls Renton's illegal gambling. Capo Jake Macapagal has extended the mob's control through Auburn from a base in corrupt trucking companies and labor unions. In Redmond, Capo Theodore Atencio faces a renegade faction that declared independence in 2039 and is now led by Ra Halquist. David Galucci controls Puyallup and is one of the most powerful mob figures in the city, a likely successor to O'Malley.

[2054 – later developments] The mob quietly financed Baby Joe Johnson's purchase of Punch and Judy's contract for the Seattle Screamers, then, with the odds astronomical, bet heavily on the New York Slashers and told the two stars to throw the Super Brawl or play urban brawl in Puget Sound. Hearing that runners were sniffing around the pair, it leaned on Baby Joe, swallowed his lie that the yakuza had hired them, and sent the enforcer Carloni with four soldiers to the runners' doss with a 'you work for the yaks' story and a warning to stay out of urban brawl. The Don who briefed Carloni is never identified, and the runners' own Mafia contacts do not belong to his family. Runners who tell Carloni who hired them get Baby Joe executed in the Redmond Barrens the day after the game; after the botched game the mob finds out anyway and kills him within hours. Karma 2 for telling Carloni nothing.

[2058 – later developments] Capo James O'Malley is assassinated on January 1 by the Chimera operative Firebird, hired secretly by the Bigio and Ciarniello dons. His seat is contested between his daughter Rowena O'Malley (Finnigan family) and the two families that arranged his death; Don Leo McCaskill of Milwaukee holds the Commissione's mandate to decide who ends up on top and will back whichever Seattle family looks likeliest to restore order fastest. Capo Maurice 'Butcher' Bigio protects Al Preswick's Stuffer Shack in Puyallup and is fond of Al's soyburgers; his limousine and bodyguards appear on the security monitor, and they will be extremely disappointed to learn a team has hurt someone under their protection.

[2064 – later developments] Vincent 'Numbers' Ciarniello has been a don longer than anyone else in the city -- a smart man but an accountant at heart, who most enjoys the stock market when he has news ahead of a big move. He rides in a black Mitsubishi Nightsky with heavily cybered ork bodyguards, hears about shadowruns 'through the grapevine', and picks runners off the street to ask what is about to happen to a share price: politeness earns a 1,000-nuyen gratuity and a lift, refusal a gamma-scopolamine dart and an interview under a truth agent. The Family has an inside man at DocWagon's Kethers Building, senior programmer Thomas Duttman, who pays down gambling and BTL debts to Mafia bookies by supplying organs and sometimes whole clones from the vaults; runners with a Mafia contact can have him leaned on to open the building, at the cost of a marker. Rumor persistently links THE Sports Bar, at University Street and Terry Avenue downtown, to the Mafia, which is why fixers use it as a place where nobody starts anything; the fixer Rolando (Ray Marcello) dresses like a trid Mafioso without, as far as anyone can tell, belonging.

[2064 – later developments] After the Crash the mob pushes north: when MCT pulls out of Tsimshian the yakuza go with it, and the mob tries to move in against the Dogmen, a new syndicate branding itself the 'Amerindian Mob'. In Boston the O'Rilley family owns an East Coast Stock Exchange security programmer outright and hits a runner meet armed for federal agents, believing he has turned informant. A local don plans to launder millions while everyone watches the Novatech IPO.

organizations.name: Seoulpa Rings
organizations.description: The Seoulpa Rings are a loose network of small, semi-independent Korean gangs founded by the hundred or so survivors of the Yakuza's bloody 2043 expulsion of its Korean members. Each Ring works one street or neighborhood. Ring leaders recruit up to a dozen members a year -- often street toughs who believe they are joining a local gang -- and after a year promising recruits are encouraged to start Rings of their own. Rings cooperate through complicated codewords, symbols and computer data, and their secrecy means that uncovering one betrays no others. Small, swift and nasty, 'Seoulpa Squitos' run burglary and street gambling across the city and sometimes combine for elaborate scams, most often against Yakuza fronts. Beyond Seattle, the Rings contest San Francisco's Chinatown and run BTL distribution and prostitution in Atlanta's Southtown.

leadership.name: Karen Pok Moon
leadership.title: Leader, Divine Revenge
leadership.notes: Suspected.

leadership.name: Chun Lee
leadership.title: Leader, Lee Brigade
leadership.notes: Escaped the 2043 purge.

leadership.name: Xiem Nguyen
leadership.title: Leader, Yellow and Red Ring
leadership.notes: Rumored.

leadership.name: Park Jai Kyu
leadership.title: Founder and Strategist
leadership.notes: [2058] Since 2043. Survived the purge and organized the decentralized modern Ring model.

organizations.notes:
District by district: Bellevue's five known Rings dominate prostitution and chip-pushing and have traded some secrecy for a syndicate-like business structure; the largest are David Ockrassa's Phantom Lakers and Karen Pok Moon's Divine Revenge. Redmond's five Rings are a recruiting pool for the rest; Dan Aurigemma's Ill Squires are the most active. In Puyallup, Chun Lee -- one of the rare Koreans to escape the 2043 purge -- runs the Lee Brigade, which hits Yakuza warehouses and even a Yakuza decker academy. Tacoma's Rings stick to jewelry heists and bank robberies to spare the Korean community reprisals. Three Rings work Renton and two live on the crumbs of Everett's underworld. Many believe Xiem Nguyen leads the Yellow and Red Ring blamed for the assassination of Wayne Olson of the district zoning commission.

Ring deckers have a natural affinity for decker crime and appear to be getting high-powered outside training: Ring deckers were recently arrested with top-notch Soong Electronics decks, and one described being taught by men with heavy Korean accents who would not show their faces.

[2053 – later developments] A Redmond Ring runs a numbers business backed by the Leather Devils. A week after the Jump House bombing, a decker steals an unknown sum from the Ring's secret Matrix account and leaves behind a simple frame of an elf in Ancients colors surrounded by flame -- the second attack attributed to the group targeting the Ancients.

[2057 – later developments] In California the Rings have a Bay Area criminal presence and cooperate pragmatically against the yakuza.

[2058 – later developments] The Rings trace themselves to 'the Schism', the 2043 purge of Korean Yakuza leadership from the Watada-rengo's Seattle gumi; Park Jai Kyu survived it and organized the decentralized modern Ring model. Rings usually have fewer than thirty sworn members plus concealed recruits, cooperate only temporarily across street, magical and Matrix crime, and share only a thirst for revenge against the Yakuza. With O'Malley dead and the Yakuza fighting on several fronts, three major Seattle Rings move against Yakuza interests: the dockside Choson Ring, the Redmond Barrens Komun'go Ring and the Ork Underground's Tartarus Ring. Most work independently and sometimes at cross purposes, without a unified command.

[2059 – later developments] Vladivostok and Korean Rings are active in technical crime, information brokering, smuggling and maritime piracy; the Saegu Ring is independent.

organizations.name: Humanis Policlub
organizations.description: The Humanis Policlub opposes all legal rights for metahumans, twisting and bending existing laws to further its aims, and its members do not shrink from violence, usually with their faces concealed. Its international headquarters is in Philadelphia. Locally, members attack metahumans, sabotage public events and organize large hunts, and its membership runs from street toughs to corporate and technical professionals. The massive Humanis rally in Tacoma on February 7, 2039, the 'guardians of human purity', was the spark of the Night of Rage, though the Humanis Policlub Information Service publicly denies any role. Recent media investigations revealed that most members of Alamos 20,000, the largest anti-metahuman terrorist organization, are Humanis members; Humanis denounced the reports. Its recruiters have made alarming progress among Renton's bored and rebellious teenagers.

leadership.name: Karl Brackhaven
leadership.title: Central Seattle Chapter President
leadership.notes: [2051] 'A moderate'; ex-Aztechnology.

divisions.name: Humanis Policlub Information Service
divisions.description: A public propaganda and contact service operated by Humanis Policlub.

divisions.name: Humanis Denver Chapter
divisions.description: The local chapter promotes Humanis ideology and openly rivals Unity.
divisions.notes: [2055] Appears from 2055.

organizations.notes:
Alamos intended to use Humanis as the political front to legalize a Metavirus 'treatment' for metahuman pregnancies. Wendell Holmes was recruited through Humanis rallies.

It is allied with Hands of Five; it is opposed to New Weathermen.

[2051 – later developments] Humanis, rumored to be tied to Alamos 20,000, stages a City Hall demonstration against the city's plan to declare the second Monday of December an official Awakening Day; fighting breaks out when metahuman activist groups arrive to counter-protest.

[2051 – later developments] The policlub splits. President Karl Brackhaven's Central Seattle chapter ('cool heads do belong to the policlub') officially cuts loose the toxic shaman Jesse John and his plan to blow the NAN apart; the young members, borderline psychos and hotheads back him with everything they have. Brackhaven hires runners under an Aztechnology cover to stop him, because a Humanis-linked NAN war would kill the limited sympathy the club has built. The club is big enough to make life hell for runners who skip with a down payment, and FBI Agent Della Cooper hunts its members on sight.

[2051 – later developments] The High Chivalrous Order of Humanis Policlub meets in the back room of Cratchit's Family Entertainment in Auburn. Loosely affiliated with Humanis, its robed and hooded members conduct ritual trials of traitors and record recruitment videos. Rhododendron Conservatory teacher P. Grumblatt is a member, and Cratchit is an influential Humanis figure. 'The Humanis Threat' is a standing lecture topic at the Association Para-Nobilis' Thursday meetings; the elf-poser policlub sees Humanis as the enemy while murdering elves itself.

[2053 – later developments] The Ancients have harassed Humanis for years, and Lone Star identifies Humanis as one of the gang's known enemies.

[2054 – later developments] Humanis is organized in Berlin and connected to the Wolfsschanze (Wolf's Lair); defeated there in 2039, it lost influence for fourteen years before becoming active again. Lone Star sources allege repeated anti-elf bombings, and the police response is disputed. New York mayoral candidate Pat MacNamara's brother Rory was a Humanis member in his youth -- a 'youthful indiscretion' confirmable in a police database. Tir Tairngire's emissary sees 'the poisoned dregs of Humanis' behind MacNamara's populism; Humanis in turn says the elven Order of Stars plots world conquest. Mairtin O'Neill seeks strikes against Humanis policlubs in New York and Massachusetts.

[2055 – later developments] Denver has an active Humanis chapter in open rivalry with Unity; an alleged Alamos connection and an accommodation in Chinatown are reported but unconfirmed.

[2057 – later developments] Karl Brackhaven secretly runs his nephew Kenneth Brackhaven's Archconservative presidential campaign and will kill to keep the family's true history buried. The militant splinter cell Human Nation recruits from Humanis's more violent members and, opposed to Dunkelzahn's candidacy, seizes and threatens to destroy one of his VisionQuest facilities. Seattle chapter organizer Burt Aronson, disguised as an elf, orchestrates the Kinsey Zandras kidnapping to spark metahuman-on-metahuman riots to Kenneth Brackhaven's benefit and to blackmail Zandras Shipping's Salish-Shidhe routes into a weapons pipeline; his safehouse doubles as a records vault of Humanis operations, kept as leverage with his own superiors.

[2057 – later developments] Colonel Lawrence Fenmore, founder of the City of God cult army, is a longtime member, though his acceptance of magic as a weapon puts him at odds with most Humanis doctrine. Robert 'Doctor Bob' Khamdeng was seen at a couple of Humanis recruitment meetings around 2049, for reasons never clarified. In California, Humanis is active in the Central Valley and in reunion politics, is hostile to the Golden Acorn Society, and is alleged to have a link to Governor Anthony Whitman; the claim is disputed.

[2058 – later developments] Humanis has grown from post-goblinization violence into a prominent policlub, with a close relationship to Kenneth Brackhaven.

[2060 – later developments] Humanis supplies the muscle -- a sniper, a Raven-totem shaman, six thugs and three vehicle riggers -- for Brackhaven Investments' ambush of a runner team at the Salish-Shidhe border, hired through Kenneth Brackhaven's defected Yakashima fixer Anthony Munson.

[2061 – later developments] After the blackout, with dozens dead and hundreds of millions of nuyen in damage, Humanis representatives publicly blame Seattle's metahumans, calling the rioting orks and trolls beasts. Metahuman activists answer that the looting grew out of decades of oppression by the human majority. Race relations in the sprawl are set back a decade.

[2062 – later developments] Humanis and the hate group Human Nation both have more than a few supporters in northern California, where anti-elven sentiment runs high along the disputed Tir Tairngire border; metahuman or changeling travelers may draw attention from their human-only enclaves. A Humanis sit-in outside Vertigo, a downtown Seattle changeling club, is a standing hazard.

[2064 – later developments] An Or'zet-language flyer at the Snake Lodge calls for uniting the Ork Underground against its oppressors and the Humanis Policlub, and carries a password to a new secret part of the Underground where an unnamed militant policlub for orks and trolls is forming. Humanis occasionally does a drive-by at Crusher 495, the ork-owned bar on the edge of Touristville; it has not scared off the metas yet. Hearing that gifted youngsters from the Hillside Student Community are visiting the Fort Lewis zoo, Humanis members stage a demonstration at the gates, and some surround a metahuman student and tell the 'freak' to leave; unarmed, they will make any fight look like shadowrunners beating up defenceless normal people.

organizations.name: Halloweeners
organizations.description: The Halloweeners are a human street gang whose colors are orange and black, one of the gangs Downtown Seattle unwillingly hosts.
organizations.notes:
It is opposed to Elven Fire.

[2053 – later developments] An attack attributed to Elven Fire strikes the Halloweeners.

[2060 – later developments] The Halloweeners are the largest, and by far the most psychotic, gang in Downtown. They started as a thrill gang robbing the district's rich folk until they messed with a high-level Renraku executive; Renraku Security followed them home, and the gun battle left the hideout in flames and all but three of the original gangers dead. The survivor Slash-and-Burn, now leader, opened the gang to anyone willing to take on the corps, giving it the greatest racial diversity of any local gang. Colors are black clothing with orange bandannas at the arms, legs and neck; the symbol is a jack-o'-lantern against a fiery background, befitting Slash's pyromania. Gangers wear gaudy Halloween masks on the job, and Slash wears masks all the time to hide the burn scars on his face and neck. They control most of the Seattle docks south of the Renraku arcology, are rumored to know secret ways into the arcology, and Slash wants any dirt on Renraku.

[2064 – later developments] Crawler and Toss stage a lunchtime demonstration in Freeway Park to build their reputation; Lone Star knows the gang and shows little concern for citizens who defend themselves against it. The gang sometimes parties in Greenwood Memorial Park, a rundown Renton cemetery. It planned to hit the Puget Recycling Cooperative warehouse in Tacoma for Lone Star's confiscated small arms, but the tip was wrong; the member sent to case it, 'Burpie', saw the Eliminators carry in a bound girl, was shot at, and is hiding in his older brother Eddie's Renton coffee shop. Eddie is a former Halloweener, and ex-members are treated as family there; handled well, the brothers can raise the gang as a diversion or an extraction.

organizations.name: Crimson Crush
organizations.description: The Crimson Crush is an ork street gang in red and gold, one of the three most infamous metahuman gangs of the Redmond Barrens, where it hounds the people of Bargain Basement.
organizations.notes:
Blood Rumblers ride openly through Crimson Crush territory, and nine of them ambush a group of Crush enforcers in the street -- preliminaries to Khan's war for all of Redmond. The Crush are the biggest local gang in the horde's path.

[2051 – later developments] A lone Crush member on a Rapier nearly runs Eclipse down outside the Pink Pitbull, and a beat-up, heavily modified Crush Ford Americar is parked among the gang bikes outside Wildfire's Fantasy Arcade; the Crush honor the arcade's neutral ground like everyone else.

[2053 – later developments] Several Crush members are killed outside a Bargain Basement tenement in Redmond. The Crush and the Rusted Stilettos are the 'more famous brethren' whose mayhem the low-profile Nightstalkers never match.

[2060 – later developments] The Crush hold turf in Bargain Basement east of Touristville around 228th Avenue, wear red leathers, and act somewhat like a neighborhood watch protecting the local orks. They clash regularly with human gangs aligned with the Humanis Policlub and Human Nation, and make money from protection, small-time smuggling and dealing. They trust none of the syndicates, but are getting a lot of new BTLs from the Triads -- 'Kong-chips' are selling like mad in Bargain Basement and Touristville, to the dismay of the Mafia and the Yakuza.

[2064 – later developments] Two days after the Crash, the Redmond Metro credits the Crush with saving several locals' lives when out-of-area gangers come looking for easy pickings in the blacked-out district. 'Those drekwipes ain't gonna frag with our place, scan?' says Crush member 'Bloodbath'; reporter Orrin Washington chooses not to ask where the gang got its brand-new matching synthleather jackets.

organizations.name: Ancients
organizations.description: The Ancients are an elven go-gang in dark green and blue, an international gang with Seattle as its main branch, and politically active. They are unique among Seattle's major go-gangs in claiming no real territory, preferring to attack a rival gang suddenly and then disappear almost miraculously. Seattle has banned them as a militant elf-rights policlub. In Manhattan they oppose the Blood Monkeys and the Axemen.

leadership.name: Sting
leadership.title: Leader
leadership.notes: [2053] He succeeded Wasp.

leadership.name: Alejandro Kylisearn
leadership.title: Second-in-Command
leadership.notes: [2053] Goes by Green Lucifer. Exiled Tir lord; killed Wasp.

organizations.notes:
Since its founding, the gang has secretly provided the High Prince of Tir Tairngire with information and influence in Seattle in return for weapons shipped across the border.

It is allied with Eastsiders, Silent P's; it is opposed to Elven Fire, Meat Junkies, Emerald Dogs, The Tigers (Eighty-Eights).

[2052 – later developments] Vivianne Geldhausmann's husband Jacob, a photojournalist moonlighting as a Lone Star informant, is murdered in late 2052 during a gang war involving the Ancients, shortly after his footage helps clear the Ancients of starting the conflict. His killer is never identified.

[2053 – later developments] The Ancients are an exclusively elven gang with go-gang tendencies, active in metahuman communities and the elven district north-northeast of Denny Park, with roughly one hundred to one hundred fifty Seattle members. They smuggle weapons, take mercenary work and push pro-elven and pro-metahuman action, reportedly recruit political outcasts from Tir Tairngire, reject cyberware, and at their best approach the capabilities of a tactical military unit. They assist the Silent P's and count the Emerald Dogs, the Humanis Policlub and the Meat Junkies among their enemies.

[2053 – later developments] Under Wasp and then Sting, the gang has expanded into corporate muscle and mercenary work, alienating Tir intelligence. Misled opponents of the High Prince decide to destroy the gang and replace it with a loyal copy organized by Shim Bright. During a corporate-funded consolidation against the Meat Junkies on Dexter, Green Lucifer kills Wasp with a sniper rifle, although the street blames a Meat Junkie sniper. Wasp's lieutenant and critic Sting now leads, with Green Lucifer second and Falchion and Viper in the inner circle. The mercenary policy causes dissent and rumors of internal civil war, while Bright buys the loyalty of peripheral members including Vandal and Tirade. Street contacts can arrange a meeting at Highland and Terry, after which visitors are escorted to a Tacoma dry dock for a leadership parley. As Tir shipments dwindle, the gang buys weapons locally even though weapons keep crossing the border to another recipient. Once Bright's operation is exposed, the Ancients lose some prestige but gain the runners as friends, while everyone involved lands on a Tir list of meddlers.

[2054 – later developments] The Ancients have a Portland chapter and a city-wide presence there at night; the Tir chapter's leaders are said to use their social rank to protect the gang, a claim that is unconfirmed.

[2058 – later developments] The Ancients' colors change to black and green. Their branches include Boston (about 50, operating around the Rox), New York (100-plus), new New Jersey and Baltimore factions, Milwaukee (about 25), Chicago (status unknown after the Wall), Los Angeles and Denver (about 75 each), Atlanta and England (about 50 each), Miami (about 25), Tir Tairngire (100-200, mostly inactive or training), France and Germany (about 50 each) and Spain (about 25); a Tir na nOg branch is only rumored. They are long-time street rivals of the Eighty-Eights' Tigers gang.

[2059 – later developments] The Ancients run a major Seattle-to-New Orleans smuggling pipeline.

[2064 – later developments] In the days after the Crash, with Redmond stripped of food by panicked crowds, the Ancients and the Crimson Crush provided security and quelled some of the worst rioting and looting. An Ancients member jacked a car Downtown and passed a pocket secretary from it to a decker friend -- which is how Dr. Adderson's interview with Alexandra Paris and the first detailed account of the Idols reached Shadowland. Contacts within the Ancients are especially useful sources on the Sidhe Devils, and the gang is a reference point for telling genuine elf-gang activity in Seattle.

organizations.name: Spikes
organizations.description: The Spikes are an all-troll gang led by the elf-hating Lord Torgo, blamed for the spectacular demise of the Silent P's, an elf gang with ties to the Ancients.
organizations.notes:
The Ancients may take revenge on the Spikes for the Silent P's.

[2060 – later developments] The Spikes are Tacoma's largest go-gang, troll bikers who control most of Intercity 5 south of downtown and have strengthened their hold under Torgo, a skilled tactical leader with a mean streak a kilometer wide. A recruit's initiation is killing an elf, and the gang's symbol is a crude elf's head with Xs for eyes and a spike driven through it. Torgo dreams of taking down the Ancients and leading the plex's largest and toughest go-gang, but the Ancients outnumber the Spikes about three to one and have better weapons and skills.

organizations.name: 405 Hellhounds
organizations.description: The 405 Hellhounds are a human go-gang in red and orange that lays claim to Intercity 405. With the Leather Devils they are the largest go-gangs in Bellevue, and at least twice a month the two gangs lock horns at the highway intersection near Factoria, fouling traffic throughout the district and littering the highway with broken bodies and burning vehicles.
organizations.notes:
Most Seattle go-gangs have ties to the Mafia or the Yakuza and carry out their orders with little long-term loyalty: they may work for the Yakuza one week and the Mafia the next.

[2053 – later developments] An attack attributed to Elven Fire strikes the Hellhounds in the wave that hits the major gangs. It is opposed to Elven Fire.

[2057 – later developments] Yakuza fixer Isao Yamazaki hires the Hellhounds to trail the stolen dragon egg's Seattle delivery without engaging; they hide their colors and drop back rather than risk damaging the cargo.

organizations.name: Rusted Stilettos
organizations.description: The Rusted Stilettos are a troll street gang in rust and black, one of the three most infamous metahuman gangs of the Redmond Barrens; they haunt Glow City.
organizations.notes:
A car full of Rusted Stiletto trolls is seen fleeing a mixed pack of Red Rovers and Blood Rumblers in the run-up to Khan's war on Redmond.

[2053 – later developments] The Stilettos and the Crimson Crush are the 'more famous brethren' whose mayhem the low-profile Nightstalkers never match.

[2058 – later developments] The Stilettos are the Komun'go Seoulpa Ring's greatest non-Yakuza enemy in Redmond, repeatedly trying to muscle in on its protection rackets; Komun'go leader Chulsoon Gray-Wolf suspects the Yakuza is quietly arming and informing them.

[2060 – later developments] The Stilettos claim the territory near Glow City in southern Redmond along Route 202, recruiting from Glow City's squatter communities, and are mostly trolls and orks in black and rust red. Many look sickly and pale; the trolls carry excessive dermal bone deposits that make their skin pale and lumpy but tougher, and dye what little hair they have pale green. Their money comes from protection rackets and from smuggling and dealing BTLs and other mindbenders to the squatters. The syndicates leave Glow City and the Stilettos to themselves, which suits the gang. They clash with the Spiders.

[2061 – later developments] The Stilettos hold an abandoned three-story parking garage off Roscoe Street in Woodinville as their hideout, with the Raven shaman Brisbie hired for astral security -- which is how he saw Wally Huggins stash the SENSE prototype and murder Regis Doss, and took the case for himself. During the blackout the Red Hot Nukes ambush the Stilettos with explosives while they loot an electronics store, then booby-trap the hideout. Five are left, two orks and three trolls, badly hurt; they open fire on anyone who appears without concealment, assuming they are Nukes.

organizations.name: The Cutters
organizations.description: The Cutters are a human street gang whose colors are green and gold, one of the gangs Downtown Seattle unwillingly hosts. They run the gang like a corporation, across several cities, and their business covers smuggling, extortion, drugs and chips, kidnapping and the occasional corporate security job.

leadership.name: Blake
leadership.title: Leader
leadership.notes: [2058] Commands the rebuilding Seattle branch.

leadership.name: Vladimir
leadership.title: Lieutenant
leadership.notes: [2058] Deal-maker.

organizations.notes:
[2055 – later developments] The Cutters keep safe houses in Denver, have their own criminal reputation there, and pursue a deliberate arms-dealing strategy.

[2058 – later developments] Branch strengths: New York about 50; Los Angeles, Denver and Las Vegas about 25 each; Atlanta, Miami and New Orleans about 15 each; Detroit and Toronto about 10 each; the capital and the Caribbean League about 5 each; Chicago lost behind the Wall. The Seattle branch nearly collapsed and is rebuilding under Blake, with lieutenants Springblossom and the deal-maker Vladimir and war boss Bubba; the Choson Ring absorbed most of the dockside smuggling it lost.

[2060 – later developments] A Seattle go-gang has payback to deliver to the Cutters. One of its riders, Tony 'Tiger' Okawa, was locked in the Renraku Arcology for a year and is 'outta vacation time'; he never makes the meet at the Joint -- at 2:58 p.m. he opens a fiber-optic junction box with his knife, snaps in a datacord and jacks in, and two minutes later he is part of whatever is reassembling itself in the Matrix out of the arcology's released refugees.

organizations.name: Shigeda-gumi
organizations.description: The Shigeda-gumi is a powerful Seattle yakuza syndicate, and any Seattle runner knows the Shigeda are not to be messed with. It runs dreamchips into the rock trade, holds loan-shark paper through its moneylender Toroshi, and keeps an 'off-Matrix' policy for its real business. Its soldiers are cybered professionals who work in pairs, charge gunmen with katana drawn and die rather than fail; its goons are tattooed irezumi legbreakers with stun batons who run when outmatched.
organizations.notes:
The Shigeda secretly own New Horizons Development as a real-estate front. Toroshi holds talent agent Max Foley's 500,000-nuyen debt, and the syndicate uses it to blackmail him; it supplies the strike team, led by the mage Sumiko Hotoda, that tries to kidnap Maria Mercurial. Sumiko brings (opposing characters minus one) soldiers to the hideout fight and cannot call reinforcements; they fight Maria only with sheathed swords or bare hands. Goons carry Fichetti Security 500s and stun batons and wear lined coats; one is missing the little finger of his left hand.

The Shigeda bribed a phone-company worker to plant a false directory number for Hernandez (555-7395) so 'Kathy Sakura' could intercept his calls; his real number is 555-9845. Sorayama's clinic in Chiba can call two Major League deckers from a Japanese yakuza syndicate. Afterward the Shigeda still hold New Horizons and its poisoned land, and they and Aztechnology plan to replace Perfekto's management together.

It is allied with New Horizons Development.

organizations.name: Perfekto Polymers
organizations.description: Perfekto Polymers is a plastics manufacturer wholly owned by Aztechnology. Its Seattle plant closed overnight in 2045, and the neighborhood around it went to slum; Perfekto still owns the Taetzel Building and the abandoned plant site.
organizations.headquarters: Seattle (plant and Taetzel Building, Barrens); parent Aztechnology

leadership.name: Miguel Allende
leadership.title: Seattle Regional General Manager
leadership.notes: Missing.

organizations.notes:
In 2045 the bright lad running the Seattle plant cut costs by dumping industrial waste into a large underground tank instead of recycling it or shipping it to UCAS dump sites far from NAN territory -- and Seattle law comes down harder on dumpers than on murderers. The cover-up shut the plant, and the only record of the tank's location went into Maria Aguilar's sealed memory. Street contacts remember Kyle Morgan doing business with Aztechnology and Perfekto around the time Maria married, and Punch and Judy tell the same story.

New Horizons' ultimatum: give up the tank's location and pay for the clean-up, or the media get the story and New Horizons sues. Perfekto's own runners found that New Horizons is a Shigeda front. The fallout could wreck Aztechnology's delicate trade negotiations with the Seattle City Council. If it breaks, Perfekto faces a City Council investigation backed by damning documents and a formal Salish-Shidhe protest; CEO Andrew Masterson dies of a reported heart attack on Queen Anne Hill, Seattle general manager Miguel Allende leaves for a 'special managerial briefing' with no return date, and management is slated for wholesale replacement.

It is opposed to New Horizons Development.

organizations.name: Salish-Shidhe Council
organizations.description: The Salish-Shidhe Council is the Native American nation that surrounds Seattle: a decentralized federation, headquartered in Bellingham, that balances self-governing tribes with shared military and diplomatic institutions. Its economy rests on resources, and it controls international access closely. It trades tariff-free with the California Free State, and its relations with the UCAS are tense. The Treaty of Denver makes it sudden death on industrial pollution in or near NAN territory, and it will protest loudly when a Seattle polluter is caught. Council Island, in Seattle, is Salish-Shidhe territory: crossing to it means crossing a national border, and practically everyone there works for the Council government, its embassy, the wildlife preserve or Gaeatronics. Seattle residents need a Blue Ticket from the Council Lodge on the island to travel on Council land, and the Council runs daily sightseeing bus tours from Seattle to Mounts Rainier and Saint Helens (50 nuyen, a one-day visa, bags searched at the border). Its Border Patrol and its Rangers -- 'a lean, mean fighting machine' -- guard the crossings. Paranormal animals enjoy strong legal protection in its lands.
organizations.headquarters: Salish-Shidhe Council lands surrounding the Seattle metroplex

leadership.name: Jon Moses
leadership.title: Chair, Council Island Session
leadership.notes: [2051] Chairs the October 2051 Council Island session.

divisions.name: Salish
divisions.description:
A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

The Salish are the Council's largest member tribe and a major regional economic power.

divisions.name: Sinsearach
divisions.description:
A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

The Sinsearach are an elven Council tribe centered around Mount Rainier.

divisions.name: Makah
divisions.description:
A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

The Makah are an Olympic Peninsula tribe with major naval and forestry interests.
divisions.notes: Military chokepoint strategy is not publicly known.

divisions.name: Cascade Crow
divisions.description:
A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

The Cascade Crow are an agricultural Council tribe east of Seattle.

divisions.name: Cascade Ork
divisions.description:
A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

The Cascade Ork are a mountain tribe with mining, herding, and tourism interests.
divisions.notes: Smuggling and environmental claims are not publicly known.

divisions.name: Nootka
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

divisions.name: Musqueam
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

divisions.name: Squamish
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

divisions.name: Tsawassen
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

divisions.name: Selune
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

divisions.name: Wenatchee Elf
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

divisions.name: Mount Curry
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Salish-Shidhe Council.

divisions.name: Friendship Lodge Administration
divisions.description: The Council administration based at Friendship Lodge in Bellingham.

divisions.name: Ranger Forces
divisions.description: The Council's principal territorial ranger organization.

divisions.name: Border Patrol
divisions.description: The Council service controlling land-border crossings and inspections.

divisions.name: Coast Patrol
divisions.description: The Council service patrolling coastal approaches.

divisions.name: Council Island Police
divisions.description: The police service responsible for Council Island.

organizations.notes:
The land that became Tir Tairngire once belonged to the Council; in 2035 Council forces tried to end the secession and were repeatedly driven back.

Council Island is guarded by the Salish-Shidhe Council Armed Forces rather than police: reinforced gates, pillboxes, cameras, guards, mages, patrol boats and a military-police Courtesy Patrol. Gate guards are Professional 3 (HK227, Ares Predator, Ultimax MMG, Wildcat 4); the gate shaman is an elf follower of Dog with a powerful city spirit on call. The annual Qatuwas Festival at Burbank Park, one of a coastal series, is one of the few times non-natives can visit legitimately.

Border Patrol officers carry Predator II smartguns and armor jackets, and most care only about being able to say they did their job. The Rangers wear heavy security armor, carry Beretta 70 smartguns and spurs, roll in Citymasters with coaxial LMGs, and field combat mages with Powerball 5; they answer favors for the UCAS FBI, and their fastest response is astral -- a pair of combat mages in 1D3 turns if convinced by radio that a corporation is waging war on tribal land. Patrols stop vehicles at random on Routes 12 and 101 (four Former Tribal Warriors per patrol car, Browning Max-Powers, an Enfield AS7, two Remington 750s), fine Seattle residents without a Blue Ticket 200 nuyen and escort them home, and confiscate narcotics and non-hunting weapons. Kill a warrior and nearly the whole population becomes an enemy; warn them of a corporate raid and they say 'This is not the way in our land.'

The least-patrolled stretch of the Seattle line lies beyond the outer Redmond Barrens, but the forest a day inside it is sacred to the local tribes and patrolled more often. Captured intruders are taken to patrol headquarters, magically questioned, fined heavily, given a month's hard labor and sent home. Tarislar sits almost on the border, and Underworld 93's 'Pure Earth' foods come from Council land. Some Nations shoot down unidentified aircraft as smugglers.

John Whitefeather, 'Son of Coyote', grew up among the Salish, was forced into the tribal military by his father, deserted to Seattle to escape a court-martial and now runs with Blackwing. The Scots druids are said to have friends on the Council. The All-Salish Nations Bank has cut its hours and suspended international wire transfers pending a government audit.

Shim Bright files a flight plan into Council land without naming a destination and uses forged papers to claim Salish-Shidhe diplomatic immunity; helifield officials accept the lie at gunpoint.

The Salish border guards facing any run into Tir Tairngire are elite troops, armed at least as well as Aztlan's Jaguar Guards, with Yellowjacket reinforcements minutes away. The wolf shaman Tarn has a contact among them who can open a crossing.

[2051 – later developments] Harold Gray Bear, the Council's spokesman (sometimes called its chief), has a brother, David Gray Bear, who is president of Gaeatronics, and a fourteen-year-old nephew, Robert, missing in Seattle with a 20,000-nuyen reward posted. The Council numbers the human Fayette Myers among its people under a name of its own giving, and its Seattle Lodge names 'Martha Newblood' as the honored woman who speaks for the elves of Shoalwater, a former reservation on North Cove that is now a pinkskin elven holding; Nicholas Voigt bought a twelve-moon Blue Ticket. Ranger choppers shoot down Jac's thunderbird near Shoalwater. Twenty HNAL soldiers board the Tsimshian ferry Queen of the North at Port Hardy, at the north end of Vancouver Island, and take the ship an hour out. In October the Council holds a special open session on Council Island to show goodwill, chaired by Jon Moses, with the Metroplex Guard and Rangers reinforcing the Council Island Police. The agenda: tribes accusing the Cascade Orks of abetting illegal panzer runs, the Sinsearach furious over a Cascade Ork uranium mine near Cle Elum, the Nootka demanding cuts to industry around Prince George, and a UCAS representative complaining about dirty cargo through the Port of Seattle. Jesse John's tonal generator nearly turns the session into an urban brawl game; on success the news reports a 'false alarm', an accord on several key issues and three representatives sent to the Sovereign Tribal Council.
