After Eclipse's party cuts down a patrol on its way in, Salish-Shidhe authorities report four bodies found at dawn in a clearing rumored to draw Awakened creatures -- Twilight's place of power, near a ghoul-infested burial site. After Mount Saint Helens' third eruption, Council troopers and a unit of guardsmen try to seal the mountain.

[2053 – later developments] Gang violence spreads from Seattle into neighboring Salish-Shidhe territory.

[2055 – later developments] Susan Hands-as-Wings has smuggling and fixer ties inside the Council and risks political friction around the Cascade Orks; Alfredo Garcia and Sukie Redflower are cultural and magical contacts within it.

[2057 – later developments] Humanis organizer Burt Aronson targets Zandras Shipping's exclusive Salish-Shidhe routes as a weapons pipeline for Humanis sympathizers in Council territory; breaking the blackmail foils it.

[2059 – later developments] On 11 July, Flight 1118, a Tokyo-Seattle semiballistic carrying Corporate Court justice David Hague, crashes in the Redmond Barrens near the Salish-Shidhe border, killing about 200.

[2064 – later developments] The Salish border patrol's pharmaceutical supply contract goes to DocWagon's ten-percent underbid, the third contract Paladin Medical Technologies loses in a month. Border violence with Tsimshian has been common since the Salish broke the ceasefire in 2062; after the Crash a company of Tsimshian Regulars kills all twenty-seven people in a Salish border station and holds it until the Rangers arrive, a short battle becomes a military standoff, and Chief George Lodgepole's 'The only response can be war' alarms the Council. Tsimshian blames the Salish for the EMP bombing of Kitimat, despite Winternight's claim, and closes all trade routes. Once Tsimshian is occupied, Great Chief Littletree describes an eco-friendly, non-Japanese buyer for MCT's abandoned infrastructure that sounds exactly like Gaeatronics, and Salish influence over the new government becomes the central political issue in the north.

organizations.name: Seattle Metroplex Guard
organizations.description: The Seattle Metroplex Guard is the metroplex's emergency peacekeeping force, the former National Guard renamed under the political accommodation with the Salish-Shidhe Council. Guardsmen answer directly to the governor. Undermanned and ill-supplied next to corporate armies and professional security police, they are nonetheless citizens proud to serve -- and quietly envious of the heavy hardware the private armies play with. Guard choppers sweep the bay at night looking for debris, human debris included. 'It's our job to keep the peace. But if you want to make trouble, we can accommodate you there as well.'
organizations.notes:
On the Night of Rage (February 7, 2039) the Guard enforced Governor Allenson's 'deplacement' order: riot vehicles with water cannon and machine guns, thirty riot police per block, convoys to the Tacoma docks and the liner Asian Princess, drones over the warehouses. Some Guardsmen exchanged the Hands of Five salute, and older orks remember.

Guardsmen cordoned off the scene of a 2049 Sons of Sauron bombing, retaliation for a Humanis strike into the Ork Underground, and kept paramedic Seth Palatine from reaching the wounded -- among them, unknown to him, his own mother, who later died of her injuries.

Eight Guardsmen with AK-98s reinforce the Council Island Police for a special session of the Salish-Shidhe Council. Governor Schultz's office backs Lone Star's purchase of GMC Banshee VI armored vehicles, provided the firm backs the hardware with more officer training.

A downtown AAA hotel such as the Westin is the Guard's to reinforce: runners who walk in dressed for the Desert Wars draw Lone Star special response teams and, if enough hardware shows, the Guard.

[2051 – later developments] In January the city cancels the third Amber Gel show, planned for a park near the Aztechnology Pyramid, after the coliseum show ends in rioting. Before dawn on September 23, Guard helicopters answer a distress call from the freighter Adelaide Mistress, powerless off Maury Island, and rescue more than three hundred people; the owners refuse to explain why the ship was so overcrowded.

[2053 – later developments] In May the Guard, based at Fort Lewis while the UCAS carrier Koontz flies heavy air operations between the Pacific and the fort, deploys with advanced support equipment; martial law follows and the gangs turn on it. By the sixth day 118 people are dead, mages have destroyed Captain Mickey Colton's armored vehicle and the International District has lost power, and Washington considers putting the Koontz battlegroup under Guard command.

[2058 – later developments] Colonel Ben O'Neil commands the Guard. He would favor martial law against the syndicates, but on the governor's orders stays out of the fight with organized crime and protects essential government services from the fallout of the Mob war. The Choson Ring pays Guard personnel to look away from its dockside smuggling.

[2061 – later developments] Twenty-four hours into the 48-hour blackout, with riots in several neighborhoods, Governor Lindstrom calls out the Guard with elements of the Army's Joint Task Force Seattle. Military vehicles in the streets feed rumors of martial law and soldiers shooting civilians, and a curfew the next night only reinforces them. The Guard stays active well after power returns, keeping order and repairing damage, and its never-friendly relations with Lone Star sour further over jurisdiction and chains of command.

organizations.name: Alamos 20,000
organizations.description: Alamos 20,000 is the most infamous anti-metahuman terrorist organization in North America. Its leaders are violently opposed to any genetic mutation of the human race or any other species. On February 7, 2039 -- the Night of Rage -- it corralled and burned thousands of metahumans in the Tacoma dock warehouses. Its members operate hooded, in urban fatigues and combat gear with Alamos 20,000 armbands. Media investigations have found that most of them are also members of the Humanis Policlub; Humanis headquarters in Philadelphia denounces the reports, and the newsnets still describe the policlub as rumored to be tied to Alamos 20,000.
organizations.headquarters: Underground, nationwide; Seattle presence through the Tacoma chapter (Hands of Five)

divisions.name: Hands of Five
divisions.description:
A terrorist arm implicated in the Night of Rage.

The Hands of Five are the Alamos 20,000 arm implicated in Chicago's Sears Tower attack.
divisions.notes:
The organization was later suppressed; preserve it as Alamos history rather than an independent 2050 row.

The Hands of Five was later suppressed and remains part of Alamos 20,000's history. It was also called the Hand of Five.

divisions.name: Central Executive
divisions.description: The Central Executive is the disputed command body described within Alamos 20,000.
divisions.notes: [2057] The Central Executive formed before the Night of Rage. Accounts conflict over the number, identities, distinctness, and authority of its members; the five labels may be codenames or factional archetypes rather than legal identities.

leadership.name: the Nazi
leadership.title: Central Executive Member
leadership.notes: Associated in the 2057 file with metagenetic research and supremacist activity; identity and membership are uncertain.

leadership.name: the Troll
leadership.title: Central Executive Member
leadership.notes: Associated in the 2057 file with Humanis and political activity; identity and membership are uncertain.

leadership.name: the Zealot
leadership.title: Central Executive Member
leadership.notes: Associated in the 2057 file with Ministry activity; identity and membership are uncertain.

leadership.name: the Senator
leadership.title: Central Executive Member
leadership.notes: Associated in the 2057 file with Unity Coalition activity; identity and membership are uncertain.

leadership.name: the Loon
leadership.title: Central Executive Member
leadership.notes: Associated in the 2057 file with Howling Lodge activity; identity and membership are uncertain.

organizations.notes:
Alamos wants the Metavirus as a tool to purify the human race: inject fertilized metahuman eggs to turn them human, wipe out every metahuman species within a generation, then have Humanis lobby to legalize a variant as a treatment for genetic damage during pregnancy. After DNA/DOA it knows the runners' identities but is driven further underground in Seattle for a while; its thirst for vengeance winds down over a month or two. The Hands of Five salute is arms crossed over the chest.

Humanis members connected with Alamos draw the Ork Rights Committee's attention; a local chapter publicly threatens David and sends a supporter against him.

Its funding and founders are the subject of rumor and accusation, not proof. It is an enemy of the Wilhem Park Enclave.

[2055 – later developments] In February, Alamos is blamed for the masked gunmen who shoot up the Ork Rights Committee's storefront distribution point in the Redmond Barrens -- six dead, one a four-year-old boy; the believed target is the rising ork activist Preacher (John Picarille). Later that year it is blamed for destroying Chicago's Sears Tower, creating the Shattergraves. Some accounts name its strike arm the Hand of Five.

[2057 – later developments] A damaged intelligence file sketches a Central Executive, cutouts, candidate front organizations and a factional hierarchy, much of it still guesswork.

[2064 – later developments] On 3 November 2064, Major General Angela Colloton names UCAS Senator Jonathan S. Braddock -- public face of the New Revolution coup, whose anti-metahuman policies were disguised as health-care reform -- as a senior member of Alamos 20,000, and announces that he was killed that day trying to escape loyal troops. Whether the New Revolution recruited an Alamos man or Alamos placed him inside the New Revolution goes unanswered.

organizations.name: Greenwar
organizations.description: Greenwar, sometimes written Green War, is an eco-terrorist policlub whose extremism is measured against TerraFirst!'s. Its Seattle cell once cracked Perfekto Polymers' mainframe and came away with a secret report on how much the plant was saving by dumping waste into a hidden underground tank, and then vanished.
organizations.headquarters: Cells worldwide; the Seattle cell was wiped out in 2045

divisions.name: Green Cells
divisions.description: The German cells organize environmental direct action.
divisions.notes:
[2054] Appears from 2054.

[2059 – later developments] Green Cells form a loose international eco-activist network using autonomous local cells and attacks on polluting operations.

organizations.notes:
Greenwar meant to hand the report to the newsnets -- meganuyen fines, clean-up costs and NAN pressure to pull Perfekto's Seattle license -- but the people in charge had the urge to gloat and left a nasty note in the CEO's mailbox first. That gave Aztechnology time: Reynaldo Texamachach had the plant closed, the manager shipped to Mexico City, the night-shift technicians killed in accidents and the whole local Greenwar cell wiped out by a strike force of Aztechnology shadowrunners. Surviving Greenwar cells elsewhere are natural allies for runners who go public with the waste-tank data.

[2054 – later developments] Greenwar is active in Germany's fallow camps and near the AG Chemie complex at Leverkusen.

[2064 – later developments] Winternight cultivates guarded alliances with extremists of every description as cover, fronts and scapegoats: deep-green eco-terrorists (Green War and the Green Cells, a loose successor network), neo-fascists (Nationale Aktion, White Resistance), neo-Luddites (the Crying Masks in the NAN), apocalyptic cults and chaos-bringers (Kali cults in India). It occasionally helps them in return -- the toxic spill on the shores of Pomorya is one example -- but none knows its full plans, and it has little respect for any of them. Runners hired to watch suspected Winternight members inevitably end up tangled with groups like these instead.

organizations.name: Global Technologies
organizations.description: Global Technologies is a rather grandiose name for a small Bellevue skillsoft company of 127 employees, mostly deckers. Thomas Martelli Sr. and Urlan Manes founded it fifteen years ago and ran it out of an apartment before it became a corporation. Years of lackluster products ended when a wave of University of Seattle graduates joined, and its Colt L36-Mark VII is now the premier handgun skillsoft in Seattle. Its divisions are Back Door Technologies, a think tank run by Urlan's right hand Roxanne Wunter, and Martelli Entertainment, an entertainment simsense house under Thomas Martelli Jr. that was once a separate company, nearly bankrupted by Hollywood Simsense and reacquired three years ago. Global keeps no military assets and hires its guards, security deckers and mages from Knight Errant as needed. Its building has a blue neon sign, Armorlite acrylic doors and a fourth-floor think tank.

leadership.name: Urlan Manes
leadership.title: President/CEO
leadership.notes: Inherited most of Martelli Sr.'s stock two years ago.

leadership.name: Roxanne Wunter
leadership.title: Head of Back Door Technologies
leadership.notes: Urlan's right hand; number two at Global.

leadership.name: Thomas Martelli Jr.
leadership.title: President of Martelli Entertainment
leadership.notes: 'Junior'. Conspiring with HSE to take the company.

organizations.notes:
Global is financially over-extended: no dividend in four quarters and a high-powered loan to finish its new product, and it is history if it does not score major cash by the end of the quarter. The Back Door think tank's Global Dreamchips -- BTL with skillsoft personality overlays such as Jack the Ripper, Cleopatra and Genghis Khan -- are illegal even as prototypes; Ares passed on the pitch, so Urlan took it to the UCAS military. Tee Hee wiped all the research data, and the only backup is on Junior's desktop (I/OP-6). Junior is conspiring with Hollywood Simsense to take the company; his speech demanding Urlan's head for gross financial mismanagement at Friday's 9:30 a.m. board meeting is on his pocket secretary. Roxanne's card number, 567-3272, is an unlisted line routed directly to her. Urlan inherited most of Martelli Sr.'s stock two years ago.

Success: a record dividend of 113.34 nuyen per share. Failure: Hollywood Simsense names Booker Pengrave vice president to oversee the acquisition. Either way the persona-BTL story may break publicly, credited to 'the mysterious Dr. Raven' working for Lone Star, with the CAS military named as highest bidder; the stock drops dramatically, and rumor says Hollywood Simsense will use the moment to complete its takeover.

[2051 – later developments] 'GLOBAL TECH VP DEAD': former vice president Edgar Kepple, head of Global's TerraForming Division and responsible for much of its work in NAN lands, is found suffocated in his downtown apartment five days after resigning; David Wuo takes over the division.

organizations.name: Red Hot Nukes
organizations.description: The Red Hot Nukes are a dwarf street gang of the Redmond Barrens, organized by Grinder, an African-American dwarf adept, after a short shadowrunning career. Grinder says he is preparing the gang to prevent a terrible future event; he meditates with his palm over a lighter flame, reads the future in exploded firecrackers and never forgets a grudge. The gang specializes in explosives. Its members are hard-nosed but approachable, and they value high-grade electronics for their devices.
organizations.headquarters: Redmond Barrens (a favorite bar with no front window any more)

leadership.name: Grinder
leadership.title: Founder and Leader
leadership.notes: Grinder is an African-American dwarf adept who meditates by holding his palm over a lighter flame and practices divination by reading exploded firecrackers.

organizations.notes:
A Blood Rumbler on a bike sprayed flechettes from a light machine gun through the window of the Nukes' favorite hangout, and they want revenge on the Rumblers -- or on whoever the runners point them at. Use the Street Gang Member archetype with dwarf modifiers.

The Nukes have the Rusted Stilettos besieged in a Woodinville parking garage.

[2057 – later developments] About two dozen Nukes can be hired as a decoy assault on a safehouse, drawing fire while a strike team comes in the back -- as the yakuza did at the runners' Redmond firehouse to steal back the dragon egg.

organizations.name: MegaMedia Entertainment
organizations.description: MegaMedia Entertainment is one of the Big Six international simsense and trideo producers and distributors, headquartered in Seattle under President and CEO William Welsh, with MegaMedia Productions (simsense and trideo production, under Andrea Stueban) and MegaMedia International (distribution, under Nick Nathan). It owes its success to an uncanny knack for finding and grooming unknowns: Cindy Cyclone, Ted Morgan, David and Helen Variable, Honey Brighton, Euphoria. It bought SportsBlast in 2022, after that broadcaster aired the first official freestyle match, and released Honey Brighton's breakthrough simsense, Free Fall, in 2046. The recent defection of Brighton and her famed producer Witt Lipton to Chicago's Brilliant Genesis has analysts speculating about internal problems, and another blow like it could be fatal. MegaMedia has just dropped Lone Star for Knight Errant on all facility and personal security.
organizations.headquarters: Seattle, UCAS (the MegaMedia building near the Aztechnology Pyramid)

leadership.name: Robert Carrone
leadership.title: Vice President
leadership.notes: Manages Euphoria's career. Formerly her manager.

divisions.name: SportsBlast
divisions.description: A sports broadcaster that aired the first official freestyle match in 2015.
divisions.notes: MegaMedia acquired SportsBlast in 2022; freestyle later entered common use.

organizations.notes:
The Brighton defection will cost billions, and every half-nuyen corporation in the business now sees MegaMedia as fair game. Aztechnology is suing MegaMedia over the helicopter that crashed near the Pyramid the night Brighton got out, with Lone Star named co-defendant (the Ares Dragon in the DNA/DOA news). SportsBlast tried and failed to keep exclusive control of freestyle once the sport entered common use.

Robert Carrone, formerly Euphoria's manager and now a vice president, manages her career. MegaMedia has Whitecastle interrogated and firebombed, hires the runners under threat, and runs the Hive assault as an 'official corporate action' under the Corporate Interaction Act of 2038 (overseen by August Dorn, Independent Contract Overseer; bonded Russel Overland transport; a Knight Errant company on standby). It hides simsense recorders in the loaned armor and releases 'Against the Hive Masters' six weeks later. Euphoria retires. Loaned gear must be returned.

On January 15, 2051, MegaMedia rushes out Euphoria's Final Fling, her first production without Hans Vandenburg, against Brilliant Genesis's Rock Solid.

The street's take on the Elementals is that none of the corporations want them ('too radical, and not that popular') and that the music corporations will not like a self-released chip.

organizations.name: Universal Brotherhood
organizations.description: The Universal Brotherhood is a charitable, quasi-religious organization that is expanding rapidly across North America. It offers food, shelter and a sense of belonging to the poor and the SINless through chapterhouses with soup kitchens, clinics, counseling services and support groups, and it promises its members awareness, brotherhood and a better tomorrow. Its Seattle chapterhouses each have a bookstore lobby, a soup kitchen, counseling rooms, offices open around the clock and uniformed guards with UB shoulder patches, and new recruits are drawn in through weekly Discovery Meetings. It is a non-profit corporation with about 300 chapterhouses in North America and 100 more worldwide, including Quebec City and Irving. Neighborhood support is growing, though some city leaders call it a front for anti-establishment sentiment. 'Our only purpose is to raise an individual's personal awareness.'

leadership.name: The Fly Queen (Redmond)
leadership.title: Redmond Hive Queen
leadership.notes: See The Fly Hive (Redmond Chapterhouse).

leadership.name: 'Pre' (the Ant Queen)
leadership.title: Everett Hive Queen
leadership.notes: See The Ant Hive (Northside Chapterhouse).

divisions.name: London Octagon
divisions.description: The Brotherhood's London meeting branch.

divisions.name: Folkestone Educational Facility
divisions.description: A Brotherhood educational branch at Folkestone.

organizations.notes:
The Brotherhood is the facade of the shunned insect totems. Its spirits use human and metahuman members as hosts, and every chapterhouse is a hive: recruits meet in groups of six with six counselors, work up the ranks, and when 'ready for the Inner Circle' are drugged, stripped of jewelry and walked into a warm, blood-lit room of cocoons. Policy on snoops: brush them off the first time, geek them the second. Each chapterhouse has a powerful astral barrier and identical Matrix systems. Its declared UCAS cash flow is under a million nuyen, and its records are coded too deeply to prove anything.

Seattle has four chapterhouses: the Octagon (ten stories, Eighth and Westlake), Redmond (Kingsgate, Belmont and Waveland; a Fly hive), Puyallup, and the 'northside' house in Everett (an Ant hive). Through a bewildering network of subsidiaries and shell companies the Brotherhood owns Project Hope (ten relief camps in the Barrens), New Dawn Environics (whose computer names the parent as 'Universal Brotherhood International') and Lifeline Education, a glorified cult school. Ant spirits have saturated the organization: at the Hive Queen's behest it diverts most of what Renraku pays Project Hope for medical experiments into a hive of 500-plus spirits under Faith Relief Camp, and it plants flesh-form workers such as Garder Armstrong and camp director Jonathan Tung wherever the public looks.

Human muscle: the Brotherhood's gangs are brainwashed ex-gangers aged fifteen to eighteen in bright red, yellow and orange denim and leather, cheerful punks until their smiles drop as if programmed; they never retreat, each believing he is immortal, and the cover story is a protection racket run by Mally the Melon. Its unpossessed enforcers are well-trained men of violence who have found fulfilment in the Brotherhood; they fight to the finish, say nothing and break fingers for tips. Green-shirted Company Men reach a decker's real-world location within ten minutes of a trace. A Brotherhood member serving as a Fort Lewis supply officer ships machine-pistol APDS ammunition and Flash-Paks, and the unusual ammunition carried by street children is an early clue. Members' assets are 'donated' and liquidated.

Journalists Zebediah Wanderly and Frederick Davitt died for their Shadowland file 'The Universal Brotherhood' (June 2050; Wanderly in the Grodin's Tavern blast in spring 2051); a 20 Mp copy sits in every chapterhouse's Datastore-3. The Brotherhood will not make a huge effort to find a team that lies low, but anyone the runners tell dies mysteriously and the data is wiped. Rektracir, as Madame Ulishia, reports interested parties.

Spokesperson Niles Patrick announces 'awareness centers' in downtown Seattle and Tacoma by summer, modeled on those in low-income neighborhoods, pitched at executives leading unfulfilled lives. In January 2051 the Brotherhood announces three more missions in the Barrens.

It is allied with Project Hope, The Ant Hive (Glow City), The Fly Hive (Redmond Chapterhouse) and Security Savings.

The Brotherhood also keeps a London Octagon branch and an educational facility in Folkestone.

[2051 – later developments] The Brotherhood tries to establish itself in Salem; Tir authorities refuse, close the operation, and do the same in Portland the following year, jailing some organizers. Early on October 26, a bomb kills five people at a Tacoma chapterhouse; a black Westwind 2000 is seen outside shortly before, and Lone Star Commander Sam McMillin calls it terrorism against a fine, upstanding group. Attacks on chapterhouses continue across North America, and a Brotherhood soup kitchen in the St. Louis Moolah Temple burns after an unexplained explosion.

[2055 – later developments] The UCAS government learns of the insect connection but dares not say so. It issues warrants for executives of the Seattle chapter for tax evasion and corruption, calling Project Hope a criminal tax-write-off sham, and the FBI and other agencies raid the hives beneath many chapterhouses, which the media reports as random terrorism against the Brotherhood. Within a couple of months the Brotherhood is destroyed as a major force in the UCAS and goes underground elsewhere; a Warrens chapterhouse still advertises a clinic, soup kitchen and support groups. After Knight Errant's nuclear device partly destroys the Chicago Hive, the surviving good merges go underground as the Secret Hive.

[2064 – later developments] The collapse is still claiming casualties. Kevin Cooper, a Caring Gardens patient and once a true believer, snapped when the truth broke and now believes himself possessed by an insect spirit. He is neither possessed nor Awakened, but he fears light and cleanliness, wears faceted goggles and wire antennae, chitters, and crawls along drop ceilings. He retains Universal Brotherhood 4 as a knowledge skill.

organizations.name: Tir Tairngire
organizations.description: Tir Tairngire is the elven nation carved out of the old Portland-Salem-Eugene axis, which rebuilt its population and civic life and declared independence on May 1, 2035. It is ruled by the High Prince, Lugh Surehand, with the Council of Princes and the Star Chamber, and it administers its borders, law, public services and a modern national telecom network centrally. Society runs on a rigid caste structure -- gentry ('Squire'), chivalry ('Sir'), nobles, counts and dukes, then royalty at Royal Hill -- and discrimination against non-elves is masked as a matter of status rather than stated outright. Portland is the only border-zone city open to non-citizens, run under modified martial law by a military tribunal and the well-armed Tir Peace Force; visitors submit to blood tests and cyberware deactivation at customs. Foreign-owned companies cannot operate directly inside the Tir, and Aztechnology and Saeder-Krupp are banned outright -- the latter because its dragon CEO Lofwyr sits on the Council of Princes. The Tir has pushed its frontier south since 2036, and its occupation of northern California is the central border conflict of the California Free State. Paranormal animals enjoy strong legal protection there. The Tir keeps an embassy in Seattle.

organizations.notes:
Some accounts date the declaration of independence to 2037. The Tir has a secret police whose elite are called Paladins. Founding public Council members include the Princes Sean Laverty and Jenna Ni'Fairra; Prince Aithne Oakforest works to link elven interests around the world.

Bottled Demon: news of Templeman's find spread through the Tir and reached an unnamed noble, who hired the assassin Blackwing to get the idol by any means -- quietly. Blackwing carries a diplomatic pass as an Associate Ambassador, and the embassy leans on Lone Star's board to get him back. Some of the back-to-nature elves -- the three murdered scholars -- wanted the idol too, and street rumor says the Tir has sent Paladins after the runners. Blackwing returns with an inert idol or none and must explain himself. The noble claims the samurai tried to double-cross him with a forgery; Blackwing is found guilty of treason and sentenced to death, and the Tir military combat mage Rhiannon deserts to break him out and flee with him to the California Free State. Both are back in Seattle from mid-2051, working for Emerging Futures. The young dragon Eliohann roamed the mountains of the Sinsearach and the Tir before runners trapped him.

The High Prince, who has a history with Ehran, stays out of the chal'han but sends spies and then four of his personal guard, the Bratach Gheal (White Banner) -- Allaech, Aimsir, Sruth and Taelech -- with diplomatic passes and a Princely Order for Ehran and 'this Harlequin' to appear before him; any hint of elven dissent is leverage for national and corporate powers. Sruth is a lesser plant of the Paladins. Ariel's coded wristphone reaches one of Ehran's Tir numbers at commcode 3503, 395-6985; it self-destructs if any other number is dialed, and the record is erased after twenty-four hours. Lancelot Windtree vanishes back into the Tir; Taelech no longer believes in the Land of Promise.

Quicksilver, a unique elf born in Wales in 2021, traveled the Tir before 2048. The elven Scots druids of Skye and Loch Ness probably have friends in Tir Tairngire -- a druidic grudge from Scotland could arrive in Seattle by way of Portland. Andrew Shalene lived in the Tir and left over its politics. Arden of Shoalwater wears the sash of a former office in the Tir hierarchy. The decker Dodger, a spike baby born before the Awakening, was trained in the service of Prince Sean Laverty and broke from his inner circle of proteges for personal reasons; he now co-leads Overwatch, which makes his old teacher's circle a standing hook.

Lord Erindil, a well-known Tir Tairngire spokesman, is a man-shaped target on the automatic-weapons range at Cratchit's Family Entertainment in Auburn -- shoot only the points off his ears for a prize. Fax-a-Tabloid rumor has Tir sorcerers reviving bride abduction ('Seelie honeymoons'). The Council of Princes' elite adept squad hunted a stolen orichalcum talisman from Portland to Seattle under agent Speren Silverblade, killing the Illuminates of the New Dawn's Portland contact Birch Kirby for information.

A Puyallup elf-poser gang, the Sidhe Devils, is devoted to the Tir, which wants nothing to do with it. Its real elf leader Heather has spent years trying to get the Tir to acknowledge her, and decides a stolen Aztechnology prototype will buy her credibility; her mentor, the wolf shaman Tarn, does have contacts inside, and they send a Telestrian GMC Banshee to a point a mile outside the Salish border to collect the car, the shamans and the gangers, who are held in protective custody until their story checks out. Delivering the Amanecer 5000 to the Tir is worth two karma, against one for handing it back.

It is opposed to Elven Fire.

[2051 – later developments] The Universal Brotherhood tries to open in Salem; the Tir refuses, closes it and, after a second attempt in Portland in 2052, jails some organizers. Portland's trade shifts in 2052.

[2053 – later developments] The High Prince's court is divided. A powerful opposing cabal runs agents in Seattle, including Shim Bright, the city's consultant on elven affairs for ten years, and orders the destruction and replacement of the Ancients, the Prince's covert intelligence conduit in Seattle. The Prince secretly places the failed coup leader Lord Alejandro Kylisearn with the Ancients to defend them while publicly claiming to have imprisoned him. Tir foreign intelligence smuggles weapons to the Ancients, though shipments are dwindling and some now go elsewhere. Captured foreign agents, among them Michael Dumont, are re-educated at a camp called the House. Bright escapes aboard a Tir-registered Federated Boeing Commuter on forged Salish-Shidhe papers, the embassy refuses comment, and runners who expose the operation go on a Tir list of meddlers. Hestaby turns back an attempted Tir invasion of northern California. The North American Basketball Association again denies Portland a team in the proposed 2055 expansion, which Portland calls anti-elf prejudice.

[2054 – later developments] Prince Oakforest runs the elven mage Nathair MacSweeney, a distant cousin of his wife Mealla, as a sleeper in New York politics, having paid for his hermetic studies at University College Dublin. Through the Portland emissary Corrame the Tir hands MacSweeney a file on Pat MacNamara's Mafia debt in return for an operation inside Tir na nOg and for mediating secret preliminary talks between Oakforest and the Danaan-mor druid Dominic O'Brien. Oakforest's personal Matrix system holds the MacSweeney file, a covert INLA contact number, MacNamara's Mafia ties, the Humanis membership of his brother and a thick file on the O'Brien talks. The Order of Stars has members in the Tir. The High Prince already has his hands full with militant demands from Tir na nOg.

[2055 – later developments] Serena Day, an elf of the Haoles Don't Surf marked for death in Honolulu, plans to buy a suborbital to Seattle and 'find shelter in Tir Tairngire'.

[2056 – later developments] Pobre credits revolutionary elements in the Tir with financial and logistical support; it is not official policy.

[2057 – later developments] Hestaby's appointment to the Council of Princes alienates many in the Northern Crescent of California, who had counted on her as their deterrent against elven aggression and now call her a traitor; it also splits the Shasta Lodge. Tir patrols may shoot down aircraft crossing their territory, few smugglers cut through the Tir into California, and anti-elven feeling runs high near the border. Hestaby will not discuss her Tir business.

[2060 – later developments] Prince Oakforest uses Telestrian Industries as deniable cover to frame Lofwyr for a Universal Omnitech theft, hiring runners through his agent Count Evan Parris -- formerly the assassin Blackwing -- and Telestrian's handler Banshee, then sending a borrowed unit of the Tir's black-ops Ghosts to clean up the loose ends, Banshee included.

[2064 – later developments] The Tir changes radically after the New Revolution's failed coup. Days later a longstanding contact offers runners good money to hide and protect a mysterious figure coming out of Sinsearach lands: Lugh Surehand, now the former High Prince, on the run from Ghost commandos sent by the new regime and needing to finish urgent business in Seattle before going into hiding.

organizations.name: Seattle News-Intelligencer
organizations.description: The Seattle News-Intelligencer is Seattle's principal daily news service, in print and on the Update-Net, with local, world, sports, weather, business, lifestyle and entertainment sections and an At-A-Glance News Digest. Louise Berns is the publisher. City editor George Harmon, the paper's first elf reporter, is known for even-handed coverage of metahuman and human affairs. A reporter here is a natural contact for anyone who needs to know what Seattle is talking about.
organizations.notes:
Harmon retires to a retreat in Salish-Shidhe land on February 1, 2051, and investigative reporter Bruce Krasnow II ('Higher, Faster, Weaker', a North American Press award in 2048) replaces him. Regular bylines include T. Gallagher, M. Colton, N. Findley, A. Lucas, W. G. Smith, M. Perneta, L. Erickson, D. Fister, P. Daza and T. A. Dowd.

January 15, 2051: the Lochlann massacre (or fire); Universal Brotherhood awareness centers coming to downtown Seattle and Tacoma; Justice Evan 'Hanging Evan' Gooch -- who prosecuted the Screamin' Meemies, the first ork gang eradicated by the Gang Task Force, and gave organized-crime leader Hano Tomas 24 consecutive life sentences -- named to Governor Schultz's Crime Commission Select Panel on Containment; a go-gang hit-and-run that killed seven-year-old Tamsin Douglas-Kinsal near Kobe Terrace Park (Lt. Avery Milkuski; 5,000 nuyen family reward); a MindTrips 'Tourist Log' chip recall; the Des Moines sewer protests (Clayton Lucas, Commissioner Kenneth Keenan); a squatters' fire in Alki that killed Birdie McGee, Shamus and an unidentified man, with Gemma and Freddie the Lip missing; and the releases of Brighton's 'Rock Solid' and Euphoria's 'Final Fling'.

June 8, 2051: the heads-of-state summit; UCAS Marine Corps recruiting orks and trolls (Major Feanor Oldtree: 'You don't need to be 2.5 meters tall and covered with warts to be a good marine'); the Arcology fire elementals; Fuchi Cyber stock; the Me 'n' My Shadow jewelry melee; Commissioner Michael Mount McKinley keeping the 'Dwarf at the Plate' rule; Governor Schultz's 1 a.m.

September 23, 2051: electrical storms black out much of Quebec; 37 arrests at the Stonehenge equinox (the UK denies 'major supernatural happenings'); paranormal boars loose downtown; five KAN-Triangle officials commit suicide together ahead of huge losses; 'Big Rumble in Little Japan?'; the Tsimshian ferry delayed or wrecked and 'Dead Zone Rumors Dismissed'; 'Champion Dethroned!' -- Vegas pitfighter 'Jackman' Davis knocked out by 'Stringer' under motion-tracking autoguns (Renraku Entertainment holds the simsense license); 'Freighter in Distress'.

October 9, 2051: Montreal denies a new VITAS strain (unnamed sources: 16 UCAS visitors dead); Ueber Corporation goes public and hires parabiologist Prof. Alexander La Grande; Mitsuhama's storm-damaged helistat; the Fortified Twist dance craze; the Kingdome readied for a Panzer Pull; the Watermark Greetings extraction at the Neon Spraygun; six squatter-gang dead downtown, yakuza suspected; 'Global Tech VP Dead'; and either 'Ares Announces Takeover' of Emerging Futures or 'Hospital Patient Assassinated' at Seattle General.

October 26, 2051: cemetery bodies; 'NAN Breakup Imminent?' (Jeanine Hormsley of the Annacis Institute, Alexis Potter of UW International Relations) or 'False Alarm at Grand Council Lodge'; a downtown police slaying; the Brotherhood blast; Eurocar stock soaring on rumors of a cheaper Westwind; corporate mages forming a professional body.

November 14, 2051: CAS rioting around Atlanta's Fulton County Stadium squatter habitat; Governor Schultz's task force on Shiawase Envirotech bid-rigging; a Humanis riot at City Hall on Awakening Day; Renraku courting the Seattle Public Ferry System; the Kingdome closed until about May after the troll Red Death gang trashed it; the Global Technologies stock crash; Maria Mercurial back on tour; 'Ninja Dragon Wars'; the all-troll Road Hogs against the Ratchet Squad at Duster's Drag Strip; and either 'Elemental Magic' or 'Death of the Elementals'.

[2053 – later developments] May 20: a Spirit Air pilgrim charter with 254 aboard crashes in the Andes; the British Royal Family visits Seattle and Fort Lewis; Mariners owner Jerome Einsdorff denies a move to Oakland; the Seattle University expedition returns with four survivors; Ellen Donnelly dies in a car bombing outside Matchstick's; a 1.63-meter geoduck; and, depending on the gang war, either violence falling sharply while Carol Lake calls the attacks a hoax, or a sixth day of martial law with 118 dead and Governor Schultz preparing to ask President Alan Adams for federal help. August 25: Hurricane Ethelbert wrecks the DC-New York corridor; a blue slime hundreds of kilometers across washes up on New Zealand; the All-Salish Nations Bank cuts hours amid failure rumors; insurers review cyberinsurance; the St. Louis Moolah Temple fire; either 'Executive Suicide' (Jonathon Teague of Highstar) or 'Gang War on Vashon Island'; Fuchi's Symbolic Processor fireworks; the blast at the University of Seattle; an ork-and-troll attack on Crusader Security's Chicago offices. Other reports that year cover Johnny Spinrad's acquisition of Monaco, Johnny Pomp-Adore leaving a Manhattan hotel through a questionable portal, Lone Star LAVs, the disappearance of Robert Gray Bear, and turmoil on the board of a powerful United Kingdom corporation.

[2054 – later developments] June 10: the Veil sinks the Gilded Hope; Preacher draws 7,000 orks and trolls to a Redmond rally while Lone Star's Jules Nedich and the troll Half-Horn trade threats; the Super Brawl assassination attempt or massacre; Atlantis relics off Crete; TOUBA pickets KSTS; 'hyperactive' Puget Sound geoducks. September 8: Knight Errant wins best commercial art at Cannes; parazoologist Luke Emerson killed by torpedo sharks; Friends of Trolls' second drive; and either 'Fallen Angel' or 'Back From the Dead' for Dark Angel's second album, Earth Dawn.

organizations.name: UCAS Federal Bureau of Investigation
organizations.description: The Federal Bureau of Investigation is the federal police of the UCAS. Its counter-terrorism capability reaches across borders into threats involving Seattle and the Native American Nations, and Special Agent Clive Drummond's counter-terrorism team is legendary: with Agent Della Cooper and a Federal Fast Response Team, the elite of the FBI's combat arm, with dermal plating, wired reflexes, Beretta 70 smartguns, heavy security armor and an unmarked armored van. The Bureau's Washington laboratories set the federal standard for forensics. Its Anti-Gang Squad recently tried to lean on the Ancients and has been attending memorial services since.

divisions.name: Federal Fast Response Team
divisions.description: A specialist federal counter-terrorism response team.

organizations.notes:
Peacekeeper: the Bureau knows Jesse John's plan and his Humanis link, believes the policlub's leaders back him, has tailed Brackhaven, and concludes the runners are Jesse's backup. It calls in markers with the Salish-Shidhe Border Patrol to plant a passive location transponder (inertial reckoning, answers an FBI interrogation pulse; worth 4,500 nuyen to the right buyer) in a getaway van. Orders: capture with minimum damage while Drummond lives, execution under Cooper if he dies. Phoning the Feds later is an invitation to a trap. Afterward Drummond and Cooper become contacts, acquaintances or nemeses depending on how many body bags carry FBI crests.

A special FBI task force is investigating corruption and collusion in an entertainment industry 98 percent owned by a few megacorporations. It hired contractor Darryl 'Ripper' Wallace, ex-Special Forces and an ex-New York musician, to check false payola rumors around Lew Allenby of Caravan Productions. Caravan came up clean and the Bureau has no homicide jurisdiction -- FIIGMO, 'frag it, I got my orders' -- but Wallace wants Teague and Highstar down and will pull strings to clear runners who deliver. His superior is in Washington; the Bureau keeps 'clones' to replace a dead contractor and a Fast Response Team for anyone who holds one hostage.

The Bureau is investigating UCAS Senator Moe Dennelly, who denies taking part in black-magic rituals involving the deaths of four Kansas teenagers.

It is opposed to Project Hope and The Ant Hive (Glow City).

[2055 – later developments] The Bureau had an inkling of Renraku's use of Project Hope and saw tremendous leverage in it, so it sent Special Agent Clint Ranger into the camps as a vagrant; he disappeared within two months. Special Agent Simon Juarez then filmed a runner team on two set-up runs and blackmailed them into going in (30,000 nuyen each, snipers at the meet, postmortem mail). Once the government learns of the insect connection it will not admit it: the FBI issues warrants for Project Hope's whole management (never served) and Seattle Brotherhood executives, a crack UCAS team destroys the Glow City hive with fuel-air explosives within a day, and FBI strike teams hunt the hives beneath Brotherhood chapterhouses across the country under cover of the 'heat wave'. Renraku is left alone -- the dirt is being saved -- and Juarez keeps copies of the vids and a combat team for the 'protective custody' of anyone who talks. The same year the Bureau keeps only an advisory eye on the Gaffney kidnapping in Denver, which the victims' corporation and Knight Errant are running.

[2057 – later developments] Special Agents Scott Cohen and Meagan O'Rourke hunt the runners for General Yeats's assassination. Cohen turns out to be an unwitting Secret Hive wasp-spirit host; depending on how the case ends, the Bureau and the wider government may quietly start rooting out Hive infiltrators, perhaps with O'Rourke leading the cleanup.

[2064 – later developments] The Bureau has a booth at the Confederation of Security Providers show in the Seattle Trade and Convention Center. Special Agent Barnaby Mason, an ambitious junior agent, watches the fixers' meeting in Freeway Park without telling anyone else in the Bureau, hoping to recruit a shadow source; he trades file access and word of what the Feds and Lone Star are working on, and can quietly lose a minor indiscretion, for information of comparable value.

organizations.name: Native American Nations (Sovereign Tribal Council)
organizations.description: The Native American Nations are a federation of sovereign nations -- Salish-Shidhe, the Sioux, the Pueblo Corporate Council, the Ute, the Algonkian-Manitou, the Athabaskan Council, the Trans-Polar Aleut and Tsimshian among them -- joined through the Sovereign Tribal Council, the standing forum where the member nations meet. First Speaker Wilson Gold Eagle opens each session with a ritual invocation. The federation was built by treaty, relocation and hard bargaining, and its detractors have predicted its collapse for years; so far, it works.
organizations.notes:
Whether Tsimshian still belongs is disputed: some count it among the member nations, others say it has seceded.

Peacekeeper: Jesse John plans to stir trouble in several nations so that each blames another -- the Sioux against Pueblo, the Ute against the Sioux, the Cascade Orks against everyone -- and to break the Salish-Shidhe Council on top of it. Aurora once smuggled a recorder into a Council session to prove it could be done. Whatever the runners fail to stop (the Pueblo Net run, Westlake's murder, the Council brawl) sours relations for a while, but pressure from the other nations heals the wounds and the federation may emerge stronger; keep that hidden from the runners for a while.

The Haida National Front spent five years spreading word of Tsimshian's repression of the Haida and Kwakiutl, hoping the Council would act; it did not, and many Council members do not realize the peaceful HNF and the terrorist HNAL are different organizations.

Runners who warn NAN authorities about an evil free spirit reviving in Salish-Shidhe forest are ridiculed and ignored; by the time the red tape clears and a patrol goes out, Twilight is healed and wipes it out, and the runners and their NAN contacts answer to angry, suspicious Council members.

[2064 – later developments] The New Revolution's cover story for its 3 November coup is that the Native American Nations, with Aztlan, collapsed the UCAS Matrix as the opening salvo of a nuclear strike -- a lie General Colloton has to contradict publicly on trid to stop a continental war. With Tsimshian's government gone and its military still fighting on the Salish border, the Sovereign Tribal Council assembles a multinational army led by Sioux Wildcat assault teams, and the Tsimshian army soon surrenders; the Council backs the Haida National Defense Force as a temporary tribal police force.

[2065 – later developments] In January the Council invites the Haida National Front, the Longhouse Brotherhood and all three Tsimshian political parties to name an interim tribal council.

organizations.name: Pueblo Corporate Council
organizations.description: The Pueblo Corporate Council is the NAN member run like a corporation: its citizens are shareholders, its elected government is administered from Santa Fe through a board and executive departments, and it is computerized to the hilt -- every hotel room has an ISDN jack. Its corner of the Matrix, 'the Net' with the capital N audible, is half a decade ahead of anything else: black IC as the norm, 'party ice' that calls in IC from other nodes, and SPASIC adaptive architecture that rewires datalines under a decker's feet. The PCC Matrix Defense Force fields young, keen corporate deckers on Fuchi Cyber-5s, and Pueblo Security Force soldiers arrive ten minutes after a trace. Pueblo trades technology profitably with the Sioux and keeps a cool, non-hostile relationship with Aztlan. It and the Trans-Polar Aleut are the only NAN members that ban urban brawl.

organizations.notes:
A sore point with the Sioux: Pueblo feels the Sioux government does nothing about, or is part of, the BTL trade. Jesse John's Vegas trap is meant to leave Sioux-tagged military code ('Wildcat MILCOMP SSF-1284') in the Parks Board watchdog subsystem, so Pueblo loosens its NAN ties and edges toward secession; if Ram's copy is also dumped, the PCC finds it untagged and smells a frame. The Pueblo sector of Vegas has PCC security within reach.

A Fuchi 'delta clinic' -- an unregistered cutting-edge cyberware research facility -- operates secretly inside Pueblo territory near Santa Fe under the Villiers faction's control. Pueblo Security Force once arrested a runner team investigating a virtual bank tied to Arthur Vogel's Ares stock purchase on suspicion of espionage and treason.

[2055 – later developments] Pueblo administers its own sector of the Front Range Free Zone in Denver, with its own immigration and justice, policed by Pueblo Security Enterprises. The sector holds the exclusive Shining Bright School (near 10th Avenue and Depew Street), whose public line is on the NA/PUE grid (429-3329); PSE gives the Gaffney kidnapping low priority once Knight Errant claims a megacorporate dependent.

[2057 – later developments] Pueblo takes shifting positions in the California water and former-reservation disputes.

[2059 – later developments] The PCS Tangakwunu sails under Pueblo registry (the crew jokes about a landlocked country flying a ship), chartered by Phoenix Biotechnologies to carry Dr. Albert Dicristofaro's escort team -- and, unknown to the PCC, Dicristofaro himself as forced cargo -- to Sekondi.

[2061 – later developments] Pueblo organizes its Matrix by function and protects it with dedicated security patrols.

organizations.name: Ute Nation
organizations.description: The Ute Nation is governed from Provo through an elected council, a judiciary, a security service and a border force. Its great cities could not be more different. Las Vegas makes Seattle look like a church picnic: security forces that look like an army, with armor, APCs and gunships; honest citizens packing more hardware than most runners; and Ghost Wheel Street, where the wealthy business traveler drives a panzer and deals in military-grade weapons. The Vegas Metro Police are well trained, non-lethal first and professional with prisoners. Provo has no Anglos on the street and a SecForce with a flat, calculating stare. Salt Lake is an autonomous enclave.

Peacekeeper: Jesse John's second bombshell is the assassination of Provo anti-BTL crusader Maureen Westlake, framed on a 'Sioux Special Forces' troll. If it succeeds, chilly Ute-Sioux diplomacy turns into a cold war.

Coyote, bassist of the Elementals, served for years in the Ute military operating weapons aboard rotorcraft before boredom sent him to Seattle to play music.

[2055 – later developments] The Ute administer their own sector of Denver, including Boulder and western Denver, with their own immigration, policing and justice.

[2057 – later developments] California water, reservation and border disputes and Mojave rhetoric strain relations with Ute interests.

organizations.name: Sioux Nation
organizations.description: The Sioux Nation is governed from Cheyenne through councils and autonomous bureaus, with a strong high-technology economy and national police and military institutions. It is home to the Wildcats, the Sioux Special Forces, with their mountain-lion shoulder flash -- and to an underworld that recruits 'local representatives' in other nations to distribute its BTLs. The Cheyenne system holds paydata every Vegas decker dreams about. Cheyenne is also the home office of Fuchs-Auberlien Financial Services.

organizations.notes:
Pueblo suspects the Sioux government tolerates or runs the BTL trade. In Peacekeeper, Jesse John frames the Sioux twice: Sioux-tagged intrusion code in the Pueblo Net and a dead troll with stapled-on Sioux patches on a Provo rooftop. The Sioux underworld's Provo distributors are the Barrelhouse Boys.

[2054 – later developments] The Sioux Council's urban brawl franchise is the Lakota Arrows.

[2055 – later developments] The Sioux Council Sector of Denver takes in downtown, with its own governance, immigration, law and security contractor, Eagle Security Services. It holds the Brandis Development corporate enclave (near East 71st and Lafayette) and Jack Drew's safe house; Anna and Shawn Gaffney live there as resident aliens on UCAS passports, and Corporation X's forged travel passes cover the sector.

[2064 – later developments] In January, Sioux OMI intercepts a carrier drone outside Butte carrying one of Winternight's modified warheads: Futhark runes in orichalcum, radiation output fluctuating well above and below norm, and so many thaumaturgical safeguards that OMI cannot tell what the modifications do. The Sioux still hold it after the Crash; Michael Steiner tells the Corporate Court they would probably hand it over if the Court brought its weight to bear. One of only two agents ever to infiltrate the cult was a Sioux OMI man in Tsimshian, placed to help extract the Hel base's cell leaders. After the Crash, Sioux Wildcat assault teams lead the Sovereign Tribal Council army that occupies Tsimshian, and the Sioux at once endorse the Haida National Defense Force as a temporary police force. The Sioux are among the nations badly bruised by the New Revolution's coup attempt.

organizations.name: Cascade Ork
organizations.description: The Cascade Orks are a Salish-Shidhe Council tribe of orks and trolls whose chief, the troll Paul Shaggy Mountain, speaks with the power of a heavy club. Other tribes accuse them of aiding and abetting illegal panzer runs, and the Sinsearach are furious about a Cascade Ork uranium mine near Cle Elum. Some of their warriors come to Seattle as mercenaries for bigger nuyen.

organizations.notes:
Rat Mash Dancer, a Coyote shaman of the tribe, leads seven tribal warriors working in Seattle as mercenaries; her tribal standing is part of why they obey her. Hired through Juzu Clinic for Aztechnology's d'Venescu affair, they massacre Elby's Bar and Grill downtown; the twenty orks on the Shoalwater helicopters use the Ork Mercenary archetype. It is allied with Rat Mash Dancer's Mercenaries.

[2055 – later developments] Susan Hands-as-Wings has high-level friends in the tribe amid recurring political friction; the tribe works as a contact affiliation.

[2061 – later developments] The troll Kaztok forms a rogue splinter gang, the Tooth Warriors, in the Tooth, using a nature spirit held captive in its own mind (the Old One) to rob smugglers who have traditionally traded peacefully with the tribe. The wider Cascade Ork leadership never sanctioned it, and it is resolved one way or another within about a month.

organizations.name: Tsimshian Nation
organizations.description: The customs sign on Route 16 bills the nation as a land of hope and promise. The reality is slate-gray cloud, cold torrential rain, suicide hairpins above the river valleys, and a government run by members of the Tsimshian and Tlingit tribes under Great Chief Deborah Jim, who has held office since 2038. The economy is built on forestry, mining, smelting and trade and bound by caste: the Haida and Kwakiutl are denied higher education and limited to the lowest-paid manual labor. The Peace Force answers terrorism with guns blazing, the police break up demonstrations with live rounds, and the courts jail people for 'criminal rumor-mongering'. The capital is Kitimat on Douglas Channel; Kemano is a smelter town; Prince of Wales Island, once part of the Alaska panhandle, is virtually deserted. Route 16 is in better shape than Seattle's highways, but there is no inbound bus service, airlines are expensive and wary of armed travelers, boats are slow, and entry requires official papers.

organizations.notes:
The government's repression of the Haida and Kwakiutl and its covert ties to Japanese corporations are not publicly admitted. The bureaucracy may detain augmented visitors who report a bioweapon threat, and the government avoids admitting such dangers: its news service admits the Kemano substation fire was sabotage but denies the HNAL did it, and a Tsimshian Environmental Service spokeswoman denies the Dead Zone. Tsimshian's standing within the Native American Nations is contested.

The yakuza traffic Haida women out of Tsimshian to Seattle as corporate wives; Sarah Crull, born Cold-Stream-Water, is one.

[2054 – later developments] Tsimshian fields the Tsimshian Warriors in the North American Urban Brawl League.

[2064 – later developments] The nation is destroyed and rebuilt in three months. MCT announces a total pullout a week before the Crash -- timed, forecasters speculate, to be buried under IPO coverage -- taking the country's main employer, the yakuza who came with it and the MCT troops supporting Tsimshian units. Kitimat is hit by one of Winternight's EMP bombs; despite Winternight's own claim, the government blames the Salish, steps up border attacks and cuts all trade after a company of Tsimshian Regulars massacres a Salish border station. The Haida use the distraction to march on the capital with thousands of soldiers hidden among protesters, storm the capitol and behead Great Chief Deborah Jim on the balcony on live trid. A Sioux Wildcat-led Sovereign Tribal Council army occupies the country and the national army surrenders.

[2065 – later developments] In January the STC convenes the Haida National Defense Force, the Longhouse Brotherhood and all three parties. The interim election goes to the Tlingit moderate Edward Littletree over the Haida icon John George, with George and the Potence Party's Nathan Jance also on the nine-member council. The Kwakiutl and Haida are now the power brokers and the Tsimshian tribe a shadow of itself. Wolverine and Minuteman make fortunes protecting neighborhoods from the police, and the Dogmen have branded themselves the Amerindian Mob.

organizations.name: TerraFirst!
organizations.description: TerraFirst! began in the late twentieth century as low-level tree-spikers. Its current incarnation makes Greenpeace and even Greenwar look like geriatric knitting circles: hard cases who pay lip service to ecology and bomb for the shrapnel. The main group is based in the California Free State, which has a long history of TerraFirst! eco-terrorism and has tried hard to stamp it out -- some on the street believe the CalFree government killed them all a year or so back, and they are wrong. Marta, a Toxic Dog shaman, moved north five years ago and created a chapter operating in Tsimshian, the Athabaskan Council and Algonkian-Manitou; under her, the northern group is far more violent than its California counterparts.
organizations.headquarters: California Free State (main group); northern arm in the Tsimshian, Athabaskan and Algonkian-Manitou nations under Marta

leadership.name: Marta
leadership.title: Leader of the Northern Arm
leadership.notes: Toxic Dog shaman (Avenger); Grade 4 Initiate.

organizations.notes:
Marta is an initiate who travels with powerful toxic earth or water spirits. Her people include the freelance hit man Cutup, the manic Maumau and her emotional disciples Smoke and Fire. Her assassination team attacks the runners' hotel at night, grounding fire spells through an astral sentry. If she survives, she and her colleagues keep waging war on the Tsimshian region and may pursue the runners.

Before 2050 TerraFirst! was linked, without proof, to sabotage during the evacuation of the station Freedom, later Zurich-Orbital, and to an earlier raid on a Shiawase nuclear facility. Reported operations include raids, kidnapping, blackmail, data theft, sabotage and hired outsiders, with support networks and backing in the Sierra Nevada.

Years ago a TerraFirst! cell sabotaged a Hawkshorne Chemical plant on Arthur Vogel's secret orders. The only survivor, the badly burned elf Alan Riv, became a deranged Toxic Dog shaman bent on killing Vogel; if runners stop Riv's attack on a rally, TerraFirst! and nearly every other eco-terrorist group try to recruit them.

[2057 – later developments] Joshua Keller -- later Brother Joshua Morningstar, prophet of the Denver Children of the Dragon -- was involved with TerraFirst! and civil-rights causes after the University of Virginia, before joining Dunkelzahn's 2057 campaign and being dismissed for using violence against the dragon's opponents.

[2057 – later developments] TerraFirst! publicly advocates environmental restoration while keeping its aggressive California reputation.

[2058 – later developments] TerraFirst! is described as a major group that has been quiet for about a year. Reports that Arthur Vogel and Gary Grey command or blackmail it are unconfirmed.

organizations.name: Athabaskan Council
organizations.description: The Athabaskan Council is the resource-rich northern nation just over the Tsimshian border, governed through Upper, Lower and Grand Councils, a governor and judiciary councils. Its relations are close with Salish-Shidhe and the Trans-Polar Aleut, cool with Tsimshian and strained with Algonkian-Manitou. The Stikine River country is rolling foothills and snow-covered tundra, and the weather has changed drastically since the Awakening for reasons nobody knows. The town of Telegraph Creek sits on the Stikine. Snowmobile thrill gangs like the Polar Bears work the region. The name is also spelled Athabascan.
organizations.headquarters: The northern NAN member east and north of Tsimshian; the Stikine River region near Telegraph Creek

leadership.name: Mary Windwalker
leadership.title: Governor
leadership.notes: [2052] Governor.

leadership.name: Billy Windwalker
leadership.title: Upper Council Spokesman
leadership.notes: Unofficial spokesman with real political influence.

divisions.name: Upper Council
divisions.description: The upper body in the Athabaskan Council's national government.

divisions.name: Lower Council
divisions.description: The lower body in the Athabaskan Council's national government.

divisions.name: Grand Council
divisions.description: The combined national council responsible for major government decisions.

divisions.name: Judiciary Councils
divisions.description: The councils administering the national judicial system.

organizations.notes:
The three-kilometer 'Dead Zone' lies just south of Telegraph Creek, and the HNAL and TerraFirst! camp is ten kilometers north; Marta's chapter of TerraFirst! operates here. Several days after Klawock, 'officially substantiated reports' of an unidentified plague killing all mammalian life in a three-kilometer radius fill the newsnets; Tsimshian's Bernice John calls it migration.

Billy Windwalker, unofficial spokesman of the Upper Council, has real political influence.

organizations.name: DocWagon
organizations.description: DocWagon is the contract emergency-medical service whose cards everyone knows: pay for Gold or Platinum and an armed response team and a trauma bay come for you wherever you fall. It was founded in Atlanta in 2037, bought its first hospital and set up its Acute Care Clinic model in 2041, franchised across the UCAS in 2042 and came to Seattle in 2043. It has recently begun operating in the CAS, but it does not operate in Quebec. Each franchise answers to no home office and bids on contracts itself; the standard business is emergency medical care, private clinics and tissue replacement -- stored clones -- for contract holders, with Crisis Response and High Threat Response teams for dangerous calls.

leadership.name: Garrett Walsh
leadership.title: Chief Executive Officer
leadership.notes: Conservative; refuses defense contracts; approved Snohomish and Griffin.

leadership.name: Michael Davenport
leadership.title: Chief Operations Officer
leadership.notes: Faked his own death at the 2060s shareholders' meeting; becomes Walter Broward of Rose Croix.

leadership.name: Margo Fleming
leadership.title: Vice President of Marketing
leadership.notes: Rushes to Davenport when he falls.

leadership.name: Rupert Agawamnapur
leadership.title: Kethers Director of Operations
leadership.notes: Night elf; rumoured front-runner for the vacant COO post.

leadership.name: Dr. Kevin O'Hara
leadership.title: Head of Cryogenics and Genetics
leadership.notes: With DocWagon since the beginning; reputation above reproach.

leadership.name: Ignatius O'Malley Riordan
leadership.title: Head of Matrix Security
leadership.notes: Reports to the DocWagon CIO; sometimes pulls a shift as building rigger.

leadership.name: Devon Tyler
leadership.title: Senior Executive
leadership.notes: Directs the Fort Lewis organ storage facility (clinic #147). Ordered the Raikun massacre; charged with murder in the first degree.

leadership.name: Dominic Woodhall
leadership.title: Chief Financial Officer
leadership.notes: [2064] Fronts the division's first record quarterly loss.

divisions.name: DocWagon Acute Care Clinics
divisions.description: DocWagon's clinic network grew from the Atlanta hospital it acquired in 2041.
divisions.notes: Reports indicate clinics with varying functions; it names no individual clinic or address.
divisions.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchists' Guide to Real Life

divisions.name: Denver/FRFZ Franchise
divisions.description: The local franchise coordinates metro and outlying response stations across sovereign boundaries.

organizations.notes:
DocWagon contracts may not apply in the United Kingdom; visitors buy the British equivalents from Careline or BUCM (Gold 600 pounds a week, Platinum 1,500), and nothing covers the Scottish Wild Lands. Hooks around the sprawl: contract verification, a contract maliciously cancelled in the middle of a yakuza hit, and DocWagon bills used in debt collection.

Dragon Hunt: Blackwing carries Gold, Render and every Cobalt Marie hostess Platinum, and Dr. Justine Grier's Platinum coverage bought her a new left arm after the dragon's 'accident'.

It is opposed to the Raikun.

[2053 – later developments] DocWagon sells tiered subscriptions, transfers patients between clinics and runs Standard, Crisis and High Threat operations.

[2054 – later developments] Punch and Judy both carry Platinum contracts and Bubba a Silver one, which does not save him in a Puyallup squatter camp.

[2055 – later developments] Denver's franchise serves the Free Zone from metro and outlying response stations. Shawn Gaffney carries a Gold contract with an emergency trigger in a sealed-band wrist phone (Tomita has Gold, Audrey W. Platinum, Jack Drew Basic, and the Shining Bright School the equivalent of Platinum). DocWagon has agreed to notify Knight Errant whenever anyone under KE protection requests service, so the boy's bracelet is a homing beacon: KE troopers arrive in three times DocWagon's response time, and Shawn is likely to trigger it around 58 or 92 hours into captivity. Mary Falls carries a Super-Platinum contract and her security chief Bounder a Platinum one; DocWagon's reach in Hawai'i is uncertain. In Seattle, DocWagon moves DNA sample boards and blood in a refrigerated case from its facility at Cherry Street and 13th Avenue to Response HQ 1 at Pacific and First in Auburn in a lone Chrysler-Nissan Jackrabbit around 10 a.m. -- Juarez's second set-up run; the loss of hundreds of man-hours of samples is his other blackmail lever.

[2057 – later developments] In late August DocWagon launches the Temporary Response Personnel program, devised by Michael Davenport -- runner-caliber security temps embedded two weeks at a time with undermanned High Threat Response teams -- on trial through August 2058. Expert Team Three (Seth Palatine, Vivianne Geldhausmann, Gordon Kurtz, Shawn Ferrer), out of the 83rd Street Clinic, harbors a mole selling client DNA and records to a mercenary handler known as 'Mr. Brown'; runners posing as TRPs expose the leak.

[2059 – later developments] A real DocWagon Crisis Response Team answering the July crash of Flight 1118 in the Redmond Barrens finds a fake 'DocWagon' team -- Renraku operatives -- already working the wreckage, and the two shoot it out. A Platinum-tier executive uses a false 'bone rupture alert' to summon a High Threat Response team in the middle of a corporate defection.

[2061 – later developments] During the 48-hour blackout DocWagon is overwhelmed along with CrashCart, Lone Star and Franklin Associates; ambulances cannot get through the gridlock and rely on helicopters. CrashCart, backed by Yamatetsu, aims to beat DocWagon on response quality with exclusive use of the SENSE portable neural scanner. Street wisdom: 'I hope your DocWagon bill is paid up.'

[2064 – later developments] DocWagon Seattle, under CEO Garrett Walsh, holds a near-monopoly on metroplex health care -- no one has seriously competed since Crash Cart died in the early 2050s, and its shares have risen steadily since the Redmond crash of '59 -- and it has grown static and overconfident. COO Michael Davenport runs deniable black operations against other Seattle corporations with the security director. Key sites: an automated pharmaceutical plant in Snohomish, built in two months from prefab duraplast on land bought from Shiawase, whose surplus, priced with data lifted from Paladin's JSR database, undercuts rivals' bids by ten percent and costs Paladin three contracts in a month before the plant is blown up (guards with implanted Jazz auto-injectors, lethal force authorized, reinforcements 30 minutes out; a wounded runner who calls DocWagon is treated, then blacklisted or prosecuted); and the Kethers Building at 1366 Crescent Boulevard, Tacoma, holding the tissue samples and clones of every client in the metroplex, the main databases and offline data storage for other firms, whose security sets the standard for DocWagon worldwide, and whose bored, overconfident staff run side businesses selling clones to ghouls, fake rejuvenation baths to socialites and organs to the Mafia. Kethers staff: Director of Operations Rupert Agawamnapur, cryogenics head Dr. Kevin O'Hara, Matrix security head Ignatius 'Iggy' Riordan, maintenance head Timothy Van der Loff, senior programmer Thomas Duttman, security head Malcolm Smith and magical security head Yeardley Runs the Night. DocWagon led the investment in Griffin Biotechnology with close to 100 million nuyen.

[2064 – later developments] The Rose Croix war: Davenport fakes his own death at the shareholders' meeting (HTR team #27 out of Renton is murdered for its ambulance) and walks off with the customer lists and codes. The Kethers run costs four Platinum clients' clones and the trust of the magical community, which moves en masse to Rose Croix. With its organ stocks destroyed, executive Devon Tyler runs Operation LifeRaft from clinic #147 at Fort Lewis and hires the Doom Squad to murder SINless people for their organs; Lone Star raids the clinic, Tyler is charged, DocWagon is fined and sued, and Rose Croix nearly doubles its client base. The Seattle division posts its first record quarterly loss (CFO Dominic Woodhall) after the Griffin research is destroyed, and loses 60 percent of its value in a year. Walsh, CFO Craig Gillespie and four trusted directors, under pressure from Atlanta, end the war by hiring Rose Croix's own fixer, Saint James, and staging a filmed hit on a Duwamish warehouse (runners paid 15,000 nuyen each and their DocWagon dossiers wiped); in one ending DocWagon buys Rose Croix outright, in the other it releases the truth. Rose Croix's corner-cutting in its race against DocWagon is also why Caring Gardens ended up under a corrupted mage.

organizations.name: The Shadows
organizations.description: 'The Shadows -- they're It. Wiz. The megastars to end all megastars.' Their newest disk or chip sells out in two days, and T-shirts and posters net more a year than most bands gross in a career. Marli Bremerton sings, writes and handles outside affairs; Joey Nightmare plays lead synth-guitar; Sid Id and Ernest 'Emile' Hawkins play synths. They wear street leathers, look bored at parties, smash their glasses after a private toast, and are guarded from time to time by a scuzzy biker gang nobody can explain. Caravan manages them; Highstar is trying to poach them, and Allenby will fight hard to keep them.
organizations.headquarters: Seattle; between shows they hole up at a musician friend's condo in Richmond Highlands

leadership.name: Marli Bremerton
leadership.title: Lead Singer
leadership.notes: Main songwriter and spokeswoman.

organizations.notes: The band has known about Jetblack's vampirism almost from the start and respected his disappearance; their toast to absent friends is the key that unlocks his help. The best flacks in the business keep street monsters away from them, and claiming to know Jetblack earns only ridicule. Runners who help them earn 100,000 nuyen 'for services rendered', Kingdome tickets, a private jam session with Jetblack and a bootleg simsense of it, and good contacts who may send work. If they fail, the band becomes Highstar's unwilling property.

organizations.name: The Tigers
organizations.description: The Tigers are a Seattle gang that fights the old-fashioned way -- staffs, shuriken and bare hands, with Browning Max-Powers only as a last resort -- and is tied to the Yakuza's Dungeness Crab clan. Their warlord, Robert Ejima, an adept of the 'Tigers of the Neon Jungle', sits at the oyabun's left hand. They are long-time rivals of the Ancients, and the Ancients came off worse in their last clash.
organizations.headquarters: Loveland / Puyallup (stationed near the Witches' Circle)

leadership.name: Robert Ejima
leadership.title: Warlord
leadership.notes: Adept, Initiate grade 5.

organizations.notes:
The Tigers are on loan to the Whispering Nights as soldiers, and Ejima has volunteered to bring Sting's head in a basket. Elven Fire hit them three weeks ago. Their orders are to find Lucinda Tangier and bring her to the Whispering Nights, on pain of a hundred lashes before their master; it is not a death mission, so they fall back if outmatched and kill their own wounded rather than leave them. The Tigers can provide an introduction to the Yakuza.

It is opposed to Elven Fire.

organizations.name: The Ragers
organizations.description: The Ragers are an ork gang of the Tacoma waterfront, descended from survivors of the Night of Rage. They are violently anti-human and sometime allies of the Meat Junkies.
organizations.notes:
The gang is suspected of supporting an underground movement.

The Ragers spotted the Ancients escorting the runners to the dry dock and sold the location to the Meat Junkies; they bear a grudge against whoever tipped the Junkies off in turn.

organizations.name: NewsNet
organizations.description: NewsNet, also called NN and formerly Turner Network Television, is the only major news network independent of corporate ownership and government control. It supports a large investigative news division, keeps substantial legal defenses, and runs bureaus in Seattle and Boston; its Seattle wire, with bylines such as T. A. Dowd and Walter G. Smith, runs in the Seattle News-Intelligencer Update-Net.

divisions.name: World Boxing Association
divisions.description: An Atlanta-based boxing body and the leading North American boxing organization.
divisions.notes: The WBA is a front for NewsNet's sports division; this ownership is hidden private information.

divisions.name: NewsNet Seattle Bureau
divisions.description: NewsNet's Seattle bureau operates from Renton.

organizations.notes:
Just before the Jump House bombing, NewsNet staff found a message in the company computer calling for the city to be purified by the searing heat of an Elven Fire and dismissed it as a prank until the hits began. Its system has been penetrated once already, and Elven Fire's decker was never identified.

Zebediah Wanderly, killed in the Grodin's Tavern blast in spring 2051, had been a NewsNet journalist until three years earlier; his last work, with Frederick Davitt, was the Shadowland file 'The Universal Brotherhood'.

[2054 – later developments] NewsNet (Seattle) carries the Super Brawl stories and NewsNet (Boston) the Atlantis find. The World Boxing Association is a concealed front for NewsNet's sports division.

[2060 – later developments] The Seattle bureau remains an independent news operation hunting corporate and arcology leads.

organizations.name: Concrete Dreams
organizations.description: Concrete Dreams formed at Club Penumbra in 2030 and first reached the public through RockNet's New Notes on March 21, 2032. Warren Cartwright, Andrea Frost, Moira Thornton and Francois Nyanze combined musicianship with influential custom technology and became megafamous; their surreal city-street logo is everywhere. The band refused lucrative simsense recording rights, considering simsense a substitute for reality. Its last concert was at Penumbra in 2044, but it still puts out a release every year, reunited at Penumbra for Cartwright's 2049 acoustic jam, and is known for unannounced appearances at the watering hole regulars call Club Zor, drawing several hundred people with no publicity and bringing Lone Star out for crowd control.
organizations.headquarters: Seattle (touring; surprise gigs at Club Zor)
organizations.notes:
The simsense rights the band turned down in 2044 are rumored to have been worth five to ten million nuyen.

On June 8, 2051, the lead singer denies rumors that the band is breaking up, and a sound technician says the members resolved their personal disputes long ago. Rumors persist that one or more may leave over the licensing deal for the band's latest T-shirt line.

organizations.name: Mothers of Metahumans
organizations.description: Mothers of Metahumans is a metahuman-rights policlub -- 'We're all loving brothers under the skin, chummer, ain't that so?' -- founded by Betsy Grant-Masterson after her son was lynched. Its pamphleteers are a familiar sight at Sea-Tac.

leadership.name: Betsy Grant-Masterson
leadership.title: Founder and President
leadership.notes: Built the national support and lobbying network.

organizations.notes: [2058 – later developments] Mothers of Metahumans is a genuine national policlub with a network of several hundred thousand members, providing support and rights advocacy and lobbying successfully. It works directly with Anne Penchyk's Timmons fund; reports of covert financing and use of shadowrunners are unconfirmed.

organizations.name: Transys Neuronet
organizations.description: Transys Neuronet was formed between 2013 and 2017, when four British high-tech companies merged to protect the British research base from American and Japanese domination. The Transys Group's home office is in Edinburgh's 'Silicon Glen', with the Meadows research campus; the ailing Sir Iain Greig is president and CEO, and Johnathan Cooper runs the principal division, Transys Neuronet GB. It makes experimental communication systems, lasers, advanced and medical cyberware, Matrix software and neural skillsofts, and its share of the European medical-cyberware market has more than doubled in five years, from 11 to 24 percent. A network of small U.K. labs does military, medical and personal-enhancement research for clients, and it holds the Lord Protector's permits for a versatile range of intrusion countermeasures.
