Once the scrolls are stolen, its own initiated wujen join the ritual hunt; it is also on the list of parties who might crash the New Orleans handover.

[2061 – later developments] Wuxing holds a stake and board representation in the Malaysian Independent Bank and draws the hostility of the Sons of Thunder.

[2062 – later developments] The free spirit Buttercup, working for Yamatetsu, covertly diverts the Skytower's chi to Yamatetsu's Vladivostok site; the runners' feng shui 'redecorating' couples the tower to Vladivostok, the astral shallow disappears, and Wuxing suffers a run of minor setbacks. The rivalry stays secret, and the two remain formal allies.

[2064 – later developments] Wuxing's Seattle branch stages an attack demonstration for the Confederation of Security Providers show, flying three Azure Cloud VTOL drones down the I-5 canyon, low over Freeway Park and into the Convention Center to shoot up dummy targets; a minor bureaucrat routed the registered flight plan over the park for the thrill, so the guns come in lined up on the runners. The drones ignore everyone unless fired on; destroy one and Wuxing sends a heavily armed retrieval team and buries the incident, and the humiliated manager becomes a minor enemy.

[2064 – later developments] Wuxing holds one of the five rotating C5 seats and, with Saeder-Krupp and Ares, argues for patience against Winternight before the IPO; Li Feng loses the argument that Zurich-Orbital should not be removed from the scene. The Crash costs Wuxing a long breakdown of its shipping, but otherwise runs its way: devastated PPG members become easy prey, and its biggest trophy is the Malaysian Independent Bank, the IPO's book-running manager and a smoking ruin after the Crash. That puts Wuxing at odds with Saeder-Krupp and HKB, since only a handful of banks can offer global services -- expect globe-trotting operations between them. Tsimshian's interim government asks Wuxing to clean up its most toxic regions in exchange for permission to run monitored experiments there.

organizations.name: Pacific Prosperity Group
organizations.description: The Pacific Prosperity Group is a coalition of Pacific Rim corporations on the model of NATO or OPEC: any corporation based in a Pacific Rim country, from Siberia to Australia and the Athabaskan Council to Chile, that agrees to its charter may petition to join, each member has a seat on the board, and the board elects the chairman -- currently Izu Cheng of Wuxing, a gregarious and cunning negotiator. Its founding members, on 8 July 2059, were Yamatetsu, Wuxing, Tan Tien, Eastern Tiger, Kwonsham Industries, the Malaysian Independent Bank, Shibata Construction and Engineering, Lam Look Pagkaon and PacRim Communications Unlimited; more joined that September, and Gaeatronics and Universal Omnitech are members too. Membership brings favorable rates from the Malaysian Independent Bank, favored trade status, joint research programs and a united front, at the cost of competition rules and production limits. Centered on Hong Kong, and backed by two AAA megacorporations with Corporate Court seats, it now rivals any single Japanese AAA for influence in the region, though not the whole Japanese bloc.

leadership.name: Izu Cheng
leadership.title: Chairman
leadership.notes: Gregarious, cunning negotiator from Wuxing; balances big members like Yamatetsu against numerous smaller ones.

organizations.notes:
The free spirit Buttercup courted the founding members through early 2059, and Yamatetsu's move to Vladivostok became the coalition's rallying point. Federated Boeing and Lockheed have both petitioned to join; neither has been accepted, over conflicting interests and Fed-Boeing's cavalier attitude to Pacific Rim resources.

[2060 – later developments] The PPG seeks favorable trade treatment in Seattle while its members pursue competing agendas.

[2061 – later developments] Hong Kong, Singapore, Vladivostok and Vancouver are being developed as PPG-favored centers of commerce, and smaller members such as Mangadyne, Polynesian Fuels and Red Wheel Engineering have profited greatly.

[2062 – later developments] Wuxing and Yamatetsu are allies within the PPG, but Buttercup has no fondness for Wuxing and diverts its accumulated mystic power to Yamatetsu to keep Wuxing from dominating the group -- preferring Wu Lung-Wai never learn of it. Afterward Wuxing suffers minor setbacks and Yamatetsu helps maintain its ally's position -- the balance Hestaby was buying.

[2064 – later developments] The PPG comes out of the Crash as a carcass and a battlefield: many members are devastated, the Malaysian Independent Bank most spectacularly, and Wuxing, Yamatetsu, Federated Boeing and others prey on the smaller members and even a few Japanacorps. Eastern Tiger uses its PPG connections to win Matrix service contracts across Asia and North America and forms a cooperative to rebuild the grids of Seoul, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur and Seattle as wireless networks. The balance shifts sharply toward whoever can still fund reconstruction.

organizations.name: Eastern Tiger Corporation
organizations.description: The Eastern Tiger Corporation is a Korean second-tier corporation based in Pusan, a significant player in the regional corporate struggle of 2041 and 2042. Since 2050 it has expanded fast into Australia, Brunei, the Salish-Shidhe Council, Seattle and Hawai'i and diversified into biotechnology, entertainment, consumer goods and agriculture, with maritime interests and an underwater project near Cheju. It offers the Pacific Prosperity Group little more than lip service and would probably quietly withdraw if competition with the Japanese megacorporations got too fierce -- though CEO Se-jong Lee's personal grudges against Renraku and Mitsuhama might push it the other way. Lee is shrewd but cautious, quick to seize an opportunity and sometimes too quick to cut and run.

leadership.name: Se-jong Lee
leadership.title: President/CEO
leadership.notes: Shrewd but cautious -- quick to seize an opportunity, sometimes too quick to cut and run.

leadership.name: Yong-jo Moon
leadership.title: Head of Seattle Division
leadership.notes: Se-jong Lee's nephew, shares his uncle's caution; denied extra security despite the go-gang Red Rovers repeatedly hitting ETC's trucks.

organizations.notes:
His nephew Yong-jo Moon heads the Seattle division and shares his caution, refusing extra security even though the go-gang Red Rovers keep hitting ETC's trucks. ETC has a manufacturing plant in Everett; a Mitsuhama-seeded rumor of a military-grade weapons shipment could draw every gang in Puyallup after its trucks. Accounts of a 2054 takeover involving Eastern Tiger, Ares and Graz-Burya conflict.

[2064 – later developments] ETC weathers the Crash in good shape on its industrial assets and moves straight into augmented reality, using its PPG connections to win Matrix service contracts across Asia and North America. It snatches the defunct Pacific Rim Communications Group's shares from under Renraku's nose, and its Wireless Pacifica Group now owns what is left of PRC and fully expects Seattle to renew the contract -- but the Lindstrom administration gives the metroplex-wide AR network to Novatech and Transys-Erika. ETC is also trying to take over Hynix Semiconductor, a division of Yang-Su Enterprises under CEO Melissa Kwan, and meeting unexpected resistance because Yang-Su and Hynix supply Saeder-Krupp with crucial grid components. Expect plenty of sabotage between ETC and Renraku.

organizations.name: Federated Boeing
organizations.description: Federated Boeing is Seattle's largest corporate employer and a major producer of aerospace systems, aircraft, remote vehicles and maritime craft, with its military and experimental aircraft built at the Auburn plant. It keeps offices in San Francisco and a long-standing presence and air service in Chicago, and runs major plants in Vladivostok, Malaysia, Indonesia and elsewhere in the Pacific -- often on natural-resource or facility deals that have made it deeply unpopular with several host nations. It has petitioned to join the Pacific Prosperity Group; the PPG has not accepted it, but gladly takes whatever help it offers unofficially. President and CEO Jessica Sirianni grew up poor in Auburn watching Fed-Boeing planes overhead and worked her way up from draftswoman through aircraft weaponry and Auburn operations to the top job in late 2057; she is ruthless, hands-on, not afraid to break rules and keeps unusually shady connections. The company sponsors the Tacoma Wings urban brawl team.

leadership.name: Jessica Sirianni
leadership.title: President/CEO
leadership.notes: Self-made from a poor Auburn childhood watching Fed-Boeing planes overhead; worked her way up from draftswoman through weapons and Auburn operations to the top job (late 2057). Ruthless, hands-on, keeps unusually shady connections.

divisions.name: Federated Boeing Aerospace Research
divisions.description: The corporation's Seattle aerospace research operation.

divisions.name: Federated Boeing Assembly Plant
divisions.description: The corporation's Seattle aircraft assembly operation.

divisions.name: Federated Boeing Marine Division
divisions.description: The corporation's marine and shipyard operation.

divisions.name: Federated-Boeing Air Carriers
divisions.description: Federated-Boeing Air Carriers operates Seattle air taxis.
divisions.notes: Flights use filed plans and monitored routes.

organizations.notes:
Stories cling to its Chicago headquarters -- aircraft, a cemetery, fires along the Wall, a haunting.

[2062 – later developments] Federated Boeing is one third of the Aztechnology, Shibata and Federated Boeing consortium behind the Kepler probe, the last serious rival to Ares's Velox II. It flies out of Ares's Cape Canaveral facility with its own representative at the second and third checkpoints, and its security uniform is the cover Annika Griebe buys for the Apollo run -- Fed-Boeing jumpsuits, clearance visas and ID badges that hold up to scrutiny. Its shuttle briefing warns that magic or astral contact outside Earth's atmosphere has been linked to severe trauma and death. It is allied with the Kepler Project.

[2064 – later developments] Federated Boeing moves fast on the wreckage of the PPG, preying on the smaller members on Wuxing's heels. Its aerospace engineer Alexandra Paris, in Stockholm on a joint venture with SAAB, was online when the Matrix failed, lost her family to a GridGuide failure the same morning, and came back able to perceive the Matrix without hardware.

organizations.name: Tan Tien, Inc.
organizations.description: Tan Tien, Inc. of Beijing is a rarity among Chinese corporations: a company that has made an impact outside China without being swallowed by a AAA. It is barely third-tier by cash flow but a research leader in protein-chip storage, cranial cyberdeck design and non-intrusive neural interfaces, licensing its patents rather than manufacturing. Fuchi, Renraku and Mitsuhama have all tried to take it over -- Renraku more than once -- and every attempt has mysteriously fallen through, fueling rumors from 'homegrown otaku sabotage' to a hidden stake held by the great dragon Lung. President and CEO Sau-hok Chu, enigmatic and reclusive, is highly respected across the Chinese republics, and other Chinese corporations followed his lead into the Pacific Prosperity Group. Its research into interfaces between semi-intelligent creatures -- dolphins, satyrs -- and the Matrix has it competing with Phoenix Biotechnologies and JHIH, and the project would also win a Draco Foundation award. Tan Tien employs no magicians as a matter of policy.

leadership.name: Sau-hok Chu
leadership.title: President/CEO
leadership.notes: Enigmatic, reclusive, highly respected across the Chinese Republic; other Chinese corporations followed his lead in aligning with Wuxing and the PPG.

organizations.notes:
Tan Tien is developing Parallel Thought, a multi-user cyberdecking interface still in prototype; it is expected to be licensed to PPG members only, which would probably provoke another Mitsuhama or Renraku takeover attempt.

Its Gold Coast division runs a compound on the Volta River near Mampong in the Asante Nation, guarded by mercenaries and by camera- and sonic-implanted paranormal animals -- ekyelebenle spitting mambas, gomatia chameleons, asonwu pack-monkeys -- controlled by a security rigger, and linked to the Tan Tien Research Computer host; its West African facilities at Bouake, Ferkessedougou and Sekondi answer to regional coordinator Meng-Chen Tsao. When its spies learned that Phoenix Biotechnologies was shipping Dr. Dicristofaro to Africa, Tan Tien hired the Aidoo Clan's Ewe pirates to snatch him during the crossing. It bears a grudge against the runners whatever the outcome, but has little reach in North America.

organizations.name: Yakashima Technologies
organizations.description: Yakashima Technologies built a compact, efficient corporate empire on insight and dirty tricks. It grew impressively in the early 2050s and received a Dunkelzahn bequest, but its growth drew takeover attempts from Yamatetsu and Ares that stunted it for years. With Yamatetsu gone from Japan it has resumed grabbing undefended ex-Yamatetsu subsidiaries. President and CEO Hiroshi Yakashima takes visible pleasure in laying off metahuman workers from acquired firms, and the company's PR now frames Yakashima as fighting for 'human purity', which plays well with Japan's human public.

leadership.name: Hiroshi Yakashima
leadership.title: President/CEO
leadership.notes: Takes visible pleasure in laying off metahuman workers from acquired firms; the company's PR now frames Yakashima as fighting for 'human purity', and it is playing well with Japan's human public.

organizations.notes:
Yakashima runs the trained double Marianna Che into Proteus AG's new Salish-Shidhe facility to learn its rotating staff schedules, through the fixer Anthony Munson and an outside runner team. Munson is turned mid-job by an operative called 'Kat' and defects to Brackhaven Investments with Marianna's file, and Yakashima's real Johnson manager, Jonathan Copass, hires the same runners again to extract her before Munson can sell her out.

Yakashima's African operation, managed by Iwamatsu Mariko, is in agribusiness and is said to back Fanti pirates. Yakashima executive Hiro Senzeni led the 2059 joint attack on Beppu.

organizations.name: Shotozumi-rengo
organizations.description: The Shotozumi-rengo is Hanzo Shotozumi's independent yakuza league, founded when the Tacoma oyabun finally broke away from the Watada-rengo after months of trying and failing to keep the plan secret from Dimitri Makaroff of the Vary v Zakone. Its sokaiya branch, run by the oyabun's cousin Toju Shotozumi -- a man with strong business skills -- handles the yakuza's dealings with local corporations, choosing stocks and applying pressure for profit.

leadership.name: Hanzo Shotozumi
leadership.title: Oyabun
leadership.notes: Split from the Watada-rengo despite Makaroff's blackmail attempts; the break ends Makaroff's leverage but hands him new enemies to ally against.

leadership.name: Toju Shotozumi
leadership.title: Head of the Sokaiya
leadership.notes: Strong business skills; buys into and applies leverage to metroplex corporations.

organizations.notes:
Once the split is public, Makaroff loses his blackmail hold on Shotozumi but gains an opening to ally with Shotozumi's new rivals in the old Watada-rengo. Some still call Seattle's yakuza the Watada-rengo.

[2064 – later developments] Toju hears about the DocWagon assassination through the grapevine: an event that moves DocWagon's share price is his business. He rides in a black Mitsubishi Nightsky with heavily cybered ork bodyguards and collects runners off the street for an interview; courtesy earns a lift and a 1,000-nuyen gratuity, refusal a gamma-scopolamine dart or a sniper and questioning under a truth agent. Of the four parties with access to the insider information, the sokaiya is best placed to act, buying into DocWagon before the news breaks and Rose Croix after.

organizations.name: The Pentagon
organizations.description: A tight, professional smuggling crew who call their own shots and answer to no Johnson: Pounder (founder, contact man and spokesman), Breetva (negotiator), Heeley (rigger), and the ork twins Red-Scale-Snake (shaman) and Night-Strike-Woman (physical adept). They have worked for the talismonger Daisy Quallon before, running quality telesma and other magical goods up from New Orleans. Smugglers live and die by reputation -- no nuyen means no biz -- so the Pentagon will fight, deal, or do both in the same conversation to protect a delivery and their name on the street.
organizations.headquarters: New Orleans (mobile; runs the New Orleans-Seattle route via Denver or Minneapolis)
organizations.notes: Ambushed at the Tooth by the Tooth Warriors under cover of a spirit attack from the Old One; their cargo and ready weapons taken, their T-bird downed by the spirit's Accident power on the escape and crash-landed at Hemlock Pass. Cut a deal with the player characters (or the runners' muscle) to hit the Tooth Warriors' camp and recover both Daisy's telesma and the Pentagon's own stolen goods. Keep their word: become a smuggling contact for the team if the exchange goes honestly, spread word of the runners' help on the street either way.

organizations.name: Telestrian Industries
organizations.description: Telestrian Industries, also known as TIC, is a Tir Tairngire corporation headquartered in the Telestrian Habitat arcology in Portland under President and CEO James Telestrian III. Its biotechnology and computing divisions work on crops, bacteriophages, neural networks and expert systems, and do licensing, government and military contract work. The company has deep family ties to Prince Aithne Oakforest, who owns a significant stake, and like every corporation in the Tir it is by law five percent government-owned.

divisions.name: Telestrian Biotechnology
divisions.description: The Telestrian division responsible for biotechnology, crop, and bacteriophage work.
divisions.notes:
Family politics are not publicly known.

[2060 – later developments] Telestrian Biotechnology contributes to the corporation's Seattle research portfolio.

divisions.name: NeuroTech Computing
divisions.description: The Telestrian computing division develops neural-network and expert-system technology.
divisions.notes:
AI, smart-IC, espionage, and Matrix claims are reported but unconfirmed.

Claims about elven cognition is reported but unconfirmed.

[2060 – later developments] NeuroTech Computing pursues advanced neural modeling.

divisions.name: Telestrian Industries Seattle
divisions.description: Telestrian Industries Seattle manages the corporation's metroplex operations.
divisions.notes: Sean Telestrian leads the division; family factional conflict is not publicly known.

organizations.notes:
Beneath its own genetic-research programs, Oakforest uses Telestrian as deniable cover for black operations against his rival on the Council of Princes, the dragon Lofwyr of Saeder-Krupp; the mandatory government stake suits the arrangement perfectly. In Double Take, Telestrian orders the Universal Omnitech datasteal through its handler Moire Ferguson ('Banshee'), plants forged evidence naming the runners 'known Saeder-Krupp operatives', then moves to silence Banshee and the runners with a borrowed unit of Tir Ghosts. The Telestrian Habitat is Banshee's base. If exposed, Telestrian retracts its media story rather than let blackmail stand, but hunts down anyone who pushes too hard.

Telestrian is also the hand the Tir extends to a Puyallup elf-poser gang holding a stolen Aztechnology prototype. When the wolf shaman Tarn calls his contacts inside the Tir on Heather's behalf, they send a Telestrian GMC Banshee to collect the party a mile outside the Salish border and take Tarn, Heather, the Amanecer 5000 and the surviving Sidhe Devils into protective custody until their story is verified. Heather thanks the runners at the landing zone; she does not know when she will be able to leave. Delivering the car this way is worth two karma, against one for handing it back to Aztechnology.

Rumors swirl around the family's ownership, mandatory government equity, succession tension, AI and smart-IC research and biowarfare work; none is confirmed.

organizations.name: Universal Omnitech
organizations.description: Universal Omnitech is an aggressive biotechnology firm that specializes in biological products and keeps expanding across the field. Dunkelzahn's will gave it 120 million nuyen, and it has since bought up smaller gene-mapping firms across the Pacific Prosperity Group, chasing the ten-million-nuyen prize the will offers for explaining the genetic basis of magical ability. It runs the Anderson Hospital and Research Facility in Houston, a research facility in Portland -- three stand-alone buildings behind a sculpted hedge, only one of them in use -- and a corporate retreat on private land along Marine Drive in north Everett. It is not an Aztechnology subsidiary, but Aztechnology treats it as exclusive territory or a close partner.

divisions.name: Universal Omnitech Seattle
divisions.description: Universal Omnitech Seattle manages local biotechnology operations.
divisions.notes: Donovan Giotti leads the division.

organizations.notes:
The Portland lab has made the breakthrough Telestrian wants. Weekend security is a bored gatehouse guard, two floor patrols, an on-call (unmanned) security rigger and a powerful bound water elemental; a six-member response team (one hermetic security mage, five samurai) and a second wave of five samurai and a physical adept from a neighboring building answer any alarm within a few Combat Turns. Its Matrix host is sculpted as an undersea castle: fish for data, sharks for IC, deckers as mermaids. After the theft UniOmni believes the leaked evidence naming Saeder-Krupp, pursues S-K through the Corporate Court with real teeth, and sends its own street team after the runners. It will trade captured runners' freedom for Banshee's identity, then turn them over to the Tir military tribunal anyway.

Thomas Roxborough entered experimental germline treatment at the Anderson facility in 2049 and has stayed physically confined there, active only through the Matrix. Dr. Evan Kincaid, an expert on the human-metahuman vampiric virus and its effects on children, worked for UniOmni until 2055 before moving to Shiawase.

[2061 – later developments] Deus's Johnson uses Kincaid's picture and a thin bio as a red herring pointing at Shiawase; nothing suggests UniOmni or Kincaid did anything.

[2064 – later developments] Paladin's Mr. Johnson poses as 'Smithers of Universal Omnitech' because the cover is plausible, and UniOmni is left holding the blame for the destruction of DocWagon's Snohomish plant, which it had nothing to do with. A rumor that it plans to enter Seattle's emergency medical market is deliberate misinformation.

[2064 – later developments] The Everett retreat (item 4 on the aerial reconnaissance photo) adjoins Griffin Biotechnology's grounds between the Draco Foundation complex and Ares property; runners nosing around Griffin from next door are on somebody's land whichever way they turn.

[2064 – later developments] Dr. Alex Heffernan's fraudulent CV, which got him the directorship of Caring Gardens, cites UniOmni executives as references without the company's knowledge.

organizations.name: The Ghosts
organizations.description: The Ghosts are Tir Tairngire's secret special-forces unit for counter-insurgency, hostage rescue and deniable black operations, loyal to two things only: the Tir and each other. Well trained, highly intelligent and frighteningly efficient, they are the country's answer to a shadowrunner problem, and they favor shadowrunner teams as training targets.
organizations.headquarters: Tir Tairngire (on loan to Prince Aithne Oakforest for Double Take)
organizations.notes:
A six-person unit (Sergeant/unit leader, Fire Support and Demolitions Specialist, two Tactical Support Specialists, a Small Arms Specialist, a Magical Support Specialist), all elves, Grade 3-4 adepts and initiates, in Medium Security Armor with ruthenium-coated coats. Ordered to keep Banshee under surveillance and kill her once the runners are dealt with; a second squad hunts the runners directly, tracking them by the blood samples taken at customs via ritual sorcery if street methods fail. Ambushes Banshee at the Ivanhoe once she tries to meet the runners, forcing her to fight alongside the team she was sent to betray. Has home-field advantage over every other faction hunting the runners in Portland.

Count Evan Parris hand-picked the unit assigned to Double Take, using Prince Oakforest's personal authority.

organizations.name: Proteus AG
organizations.description: Proteus AG is a German AA corporation that grew to its stature 'right in Saeder-Krupp's backyard' by building arkoblocks -- offshore arcologies, partly underwater -- for Japanese corporations. It has completed nine worldwide: five in the North Sea, two off Japan, one in the South Pacific near Fiji, one off South America, and its newest off Salish-Shidhe. It works in heavy industry, aquaculture, marine biotechnology, deep-sea mining and underwater habitation, and it has held extraterritorial status for about a decade. It entered Dunkelzahn's aquasphere-prize competition and lost on a technicality: its spheres sit above sea level rather than fully submerged. Its own staff rotate teams and postings on a whim, and no employee learns a new assignment except by physically entering a Schedule Room fed a single-use burn chip over a satellite uplink isolated from the Matrix. Eco-groups consider Proteus target number one for toxic dumping and mass sealife kills, and are in open, unresolved warfare with it.
organizations.headquarters: Germany; North American facility on the Salish-Shidhe coast, ~70 km north of Vancouver
organizations.notes:
The North American facility is a black polished-glass building behind a monowire fence, with glare-trap lighting, jammers, cameras, sentry turrets and a rotating perimeter patrol. A tram tunnel connects it to an offshore aquasphere about a kilometer away with its own security staff, deckers, patrol boats, gunship and water and air elementals. The onshore host is Red-7 (ACIFS 14/13/14/12/14), the offshore host Red-9 (13/13/16/18/15), sculpted as an aquarium with shark IC. Yakashima's mole Marianna Che is inserted here to learn her cover identity's real assignment; when the facility goes to red alert it evacuates all non-security staff to a Seattle apartment complex, and Proteus quietly closes the affair by planting the real (already dead) Marianna's burned body in a Seattle alley.

Proteus executes captured intruders or coerces them into its shadow-operations division with cortex bombs. Its backers and hidden research are the subject of rumor.

[2062 – later developments] Proteus is a significant contender in the Halley Probe Race, relying on a few scientific geniuses rather than the large staffs of rival space corporations. Its probe Gotterbote ('God-messenger') travels from the Iles du Salut complex in French Guiana -- probably the South American arkoblock, only a small part of it underwater -- to the Treffpunkt Raumhaufen orbital platform to be joined to a deep-space rocket, and the company is expanding into aerospace through its launch complex there. It may also seek Yamatetsu's lost Gagarin sensor module.

organizations.name: Brackhaven Investments
organizations.description: Brackhaven Investments is the investment firm of Kenneth Brackhaven, who nearly won the UCAS presidency on an archconservative, anti-metahuman platform before Dunkelzahn spoiled it. Brackhaven has since grown rich funding companies that quietly, or not so quietly, share his politics, and has become one of Seattle's wealthiest and best-known men by softening his public stance without changing his private one.
organizations.notes:
Open bigotry makes it hard to staff a corporation, so Brackhaven tricks and poaches disgruntled executives from rival corporations into 'creating their own extractions', hiring shadowrunners to check up on dissatisfied executives and nudge them toward defecting. His muscle comes from the ranks of the Humanis Policlub.

Brackhaven recruits Anthony Munson away from Yakashima after 'Kat' softens him up at Angry Jake's; Munson steals Marianna Che's file on the way out to curry favor. Once Munson learns the runners have extracted Marianna, a Humanis ambush squad (a sniper, a Raven shaman, six thugs and three vehicle riggers) hits them at the Salish-Shidhe border, and Munson leads a second attempt at her Seattle apartment building himself.

organizations.name: Dunkelzahn Institute of Magical Research
organizations.description: The Dunkelzahn Institute of Magical Research was established by Dunkelzahn's will and has become the world's foremost cutting-edge magical research body, with access to many of the world's most powerful magical items and sorcerers and the clout to make corporations, universities and even the Atlantean Foundation cooperate under one roof. It works closely with the Draco Foundation and can call on its shadow-operations team, Assets Inc.
organizations.headquarters: Western Cambridge, Boston, off the Fresh Pond Parkway
organizations.notes:
The dragon Hualpa lent the DIMR the Elemental Scrolls of Ak'le'ar, which Dunkelzahn had bequeathed to him, and the Institute arranged a two-week joint study at MIT&T's thaumaturgy department with Mitsuhama's Thaumaturgical Research Unit 13 as co-funder and second security provider. Unit 13 then stole the scrolls from the MIT&T lab, ending the partnership. MCT did not keep them; after passing through several hands they end up with Hestaby, who returns them to Amazonia to score a point in the Rite of Succession.

DIMR security shaman Daniel Gammemnos is on site at the MIT&T building, and the Institute begins its own ritual-sorcery search within ten minutes of discovering the theft, using a retained scrap of scroll material. It wants the loss kept quiet and is, in one contact's words, 'scrambling to kiss Hualpa's feathered hoop to avoid a big incident'. It is not the most dangerous of the seven pursuing factions, weaker than the Draco Foundation's operative, and treats returned scrolls warmly, paying the runners and asking, without threat, who hired them. It may send its own team to intervene in the New Orleans handover.

organizations.name: Finnigan Family
organizations.description: The Finnigan family was founded early in the twenty-first century by the old-world Irishman Ian Finnigan and rose to lead the Seattle Mafia through aggressive, tradition-bending business -- and paid for it when the Yakuza decimated its leadership, killing Ian and his sons James and Michael. The Commissione twice imposed outside Milwaukee dons over the family (Brian, then James O'Malley) rather than trust an unblooded Finnigan, and Ian's widow, Mary Finnigan, has never forgiven either. With James O'Malley's murder on 1 January 2058 the family is headless again, caught between his daughter Rowena's claim -- resisted by those who will not accept a female capo -- and Mary's decades-long plan to install her grandnephew James Michael instead.

leadership.name: Rowena O'Malley
leadership.title: Heir Apparent
leadership.notes: Claims the Family and the capo's seat; backed by Al Cavalieri.

leadership.name: Al Cavalieri
leadership.title: Consigliere
leadership.notes: James O'Malley's oldest Milwaukee friend; Rowena's closest advisor.

leadership.name: Mary Finnigan
leadership.title: Matriarch
leadership.notes: 78 Years old, plots to install grandnephew James Michael instead of Rowena.

leadership.name: James Michael Finnigan
leadership.title: Caporegime
leadership.notes: Patrick's son, 29, obsessed with marrying Rowena to claim the Family.

leadership.name: James O'Malley
leadership.title: Don
leadership.notes: Assassinated on 1 January 2058.

organizations.notes: O'Malley stood above the Finnigan family as capo of Seattle. The family is allied with the magical street gang the Merlyns through a deal Al Cavalieri made two years ago after Triad mages defeated the Finnigans. An unconfirmed rumor holds that O'Malley meant to offer the Merlyns a place in the family and that hard-liners killed him to stop it. Runners investigating the murder find Bigio and Ciarniello behind it. James Michael later kidnaps Al Cavalieri to force a marriage to Rowena, while his father Patrick Finnigan secretly hires runners to stop him.

organizations.name: Chimera
organizations.description: Chimera is a small freelance assassination organization, an offshoot of Kamera, working out of Seattle since 2054. Most of its members came from a branch of Russian intelligence that disintegrated after the Euro-Wars troubles in Moscow, and in about four years they have built a fearsome reputation as kick artists known for patient surveillance and precise, deniable work.
organizations.notes: Chimera considers the O'Malley hit a closed business transaction -- another Seattle target is another deal -- but it will kill to protect its own security, including silencing its own operative Firebird if she becomes a liability. Maurice Bigio sends Firebird after anyone nearing the truth, which puts the runners in direct conflict with Chimera. The street has only rumors about its size, cyberware, killings, a coded public-BBS contact method, possible magical support and Lone Star's tolerance of it. Anubis joined after 2057 and received specialist training.

organizations.name: Shotozumi-gumi
organizations.description: The Shotozumi-gumi was formed from the wreckage of the Schism and built by oyabun Hanzo Shotozumi over fifteen years into an efficient, feared organization that enforces Yakuza tradition strictly and conservatively; few women or metahumans hold any real position, the notable exception being wakagashira-hosa Miko Ishikawa. It is the senior of Seattle's three gumi within the loose Watada-rengo, keeping its own oyabun. With James O'Malley dead and the Mafia in disarray, Shotozumi is moving to secure the loyalty of the other two gumi and seize the gambling and 'entertainment' turf long contested with the Mafia, especially Casino Corner in Everett -- and finds himself fighting the Mafia, the Triads and the Seoulpa Rings all at once.

leadership.name: Hanzo Shotozumi
leadership.title: Oyabun
leadership.notes: Inscrutable, coldly efficient; wants his own West Coast rengo independent of the Watada-rengo.

leadership.name: Shiro Tanaka
leadership.title: Wakagashira
leadership.notes: Utterly loyal; handles Shotozumi's most delicate business personally.

leadership.name: Miko Ishikawa
leadership.title: Wakagashira-hosa
leadership.notes: Rare female power-holder; secretly a spy reporting Shotozumi's activities to Akira Watada.

leadership.name: Toju Shotozumi
leadership.title: Head of the Sokaiya
leadership.notes: Hanzo's cousin; runs corporate blackmail/stock operations against Seattle businesses.

divisions.name: Isogashii
divisions.description: A Shotozumi-gumi sokaiya operation led by Toju Shotozumi.

organizations.notes: Shotozumi wants his own West Coast rengo, independent of Watada. Shiro Tanaka, his utterly loyal wakagashira, handles his most delicate business; his cousin Toju runs the sokaiya's corporate blackmail and stock operations; Miko Ishikawa secretly reports his activities to Akira Watada. His daughter Keiko ran away years ago and works the shadows as the decker 'Kiku', quietly undermining her father's operations. The gumi uses the Amerindian gang First Nations as deniable front-line muscle, and is allied with it. It is drawn into a Triad-framed trapdoor intrusion through BrightSky Finances, Miko's double game and Kiku's revenge heist. It is financed in part through Isogashii. A disputed Shadowland thread by 'Dragonslayer' claims the great dragon Ryumyo is the real power behind the Watada-rengo and so behind this gumi.

organizations.name: Shigeda-gumi (Takeo Shigeda)
organizations.description: The Shigeda-gumi is the least powerful of Seattle's three top gumi, formed after the Schism from the remnants of clans decimated by the purge of their Korean leadership; its members, like its oyabun, are mostly long-time Seattle residents. Takeo Shigeda, born in San Francisco and in Seattle for twenty-three years, prizes safety and prosperity over expansion and is likely to side with whichever Yakuza faction seems strongest and likeliest to stay that way. It is the most progressive of the three, with more women and magicians in real positions than the Shotozumi or Nishidon gumi, though the traditional bar on metahumans still holds. It is not the Shigeda cell that tangled with Maria Mercurial.

leadership.name: Takeo Shigeda
leadership.title: Oyabun
leadership.notes: Prioritizes safety and prosperity over expansion; likely to side with whichever Yakuza faction seems strongest.

leadership.name: Jiro Egami
leadership.title: Wakagashira
leadership.notes: Investigates security breaches personally; cautious and thorough.

organizations.notes: Shigeda's underlings tend to handle problems themselves rather than bring them to him -- usually to the clan's benefit, but sometimes he only hears of trouble once it has become a crisis. Wakagashira Jiro Egami, cautious and thorough, investigates security breaches personally: when runners use a trapdoor planted by the Eighty-Eights through BrightSky Finances in Fort Lewis to reach a Shigeda host (Red-10, with IC running from Trace and Probe up to Black), Egami and a squad equal to the team arrive just as they are making their changes.

organizations.name: Yellow Lotus
organizations.description: The Yellow Lotus is a Triad society active in Seattle's protection, gambling, vice and smuggling markets. Lodgemaster Zheng Li Kwan -- a physical adept, high-grade Triad initiate and collector of ancient Chinese art -- left Hong Kong, a city the Triads had already subdued, for Seattle's rawer opportunities, took over the Yellow Lotus six years ago and has more than doubled it by recruiting metahumans from the Barrens and the Ork Underground whom the Yakuza and Mafia shut out. He has offered the Eighty-Eights and the Octagon a standing alliance against their common Yakuza enemy.

leadership.name: Zheng Li Kwan
leadership.title: Lodgemaster
leadership.notes: Physical adept, high-grade Triad initiate; collects ancient Chinese artwork; wants to unify Seattle's Triads under himself.

leadership.name: Su Cheng
leadership.title: Incense Master
leadership.notes: Actually an ancient Chinese vampire bound to obedience because Zheng controls the vase holding his Hidden Life; resents his servitude.

organizations.notes: Zheng's private long-term plan is to absorb both into a single Triad under his own control. His Incense Master, Su Cheng, is an ancient Chinese vampire bound to obey because Zheng holds the vase containing his Hidden Life; Su Cheng secretly hires runners to recover the soul-jar from Zheng's warded Tacoma warehouse while a decoy sits in Zheng's Bellevue home. Yellow Lotus mages of the Heaven and Earth Circle plan to replace Seoulpa Ring leaders, including Kyu of the Choson Ring, with shapeshifted impostors. During the Mob war the Lotus cooperates with the Eighty-Eights against Shotozumi's gambling interests. Dragonslayer's disputed Shadowland thread claims the great dragon Lung controls the Red Dragon Triad and, through it, much of the Triad world the Yellow Lotus answers to.

organizations.name: Komun'go Ring
organizations.description: The Komun'go Ring is led by Chulsoon Gray-Wolf, about 29, a Korean-Amerind whose Yakuza father died in the Schism and who grew up hidden under his Amerind mother's surname. It recruits from the Redmond streets, Amerinds included, and fosters the idea that 'the streets take care of their own'. Chulsoon's chief lieutenant and spiritual advisor, the full-blood Haida Wolf shaman Black-Cloud-in-Morning, conducts its initiations and reads the will of the spirits for every major decision. Its symbol is a black wolf's head with the Korean word for 'honor' in white.
organizations.headquarters: Redmond Barrens, near the NAN border

leadership.name: Chulsoon Gray-Wolf
leadership.title: Leader
leadership.notes: Korean-Amerind, ~29; father a Yakuza killed in the Schism; hid under his Amerind mother's surname growing up.

leadership.name: Black-Cloud-in-Morning
leadership.title: Lieutenant
leadership.notes: Full-blood Haida; conducts initiations, reads omens for Chulsoon.

organizations.notes: The Ring has twenty initiated members plus ties to small Redmond gangs and runs protection rackets across the Redmond Barrens near the NAN border, enforced partly by the threat of hearth and city spirits disrupting a non-payer's business. Initiation includes a shamanic mind probe, which gives the Ring lasting leverage over its members. Its greatest non-Yakuza enemy is the Rusted Stilettos, whom Chulsoon suspects the Yakuza is quietly arming against him.

organizations.name: Winternight
organizations.description: Winternight is a cult rooted in Nordic mythology that seeks to bring about Ragnarok, the end of the world, so that its members can take their place in the pantheon of Nordic gods who will rule the Earth again. It was born in the fall of 2031, when Frida Kohlman met the gode Wednesday at a Viking blot. Its creed is the Eddas with a lie at its heart: that Loki, chained for Baldr's death, was never freed as prophesied, so Ragnarok was cheated and the world left to stagnate and rot. To Winternight the great powers of the Sixth World are the corrupt Old Gods, and the Matrix is the worldly form of Loki's shackles -- full of lies and illusion because his evil has seeped into it. Its members call themselves the Einherjar, the Elect who will ride from Valhalla when Heimdal's horn sounds; they do not fear death and revel in violence. The cult works in clandestine cells of three to twenty, linked by drone or spirit courier, each pursuing the goal independently so no cell knows enough to compromise the rest. Many members are toxic shamans, most often poisoners or followers of Raven or Wolf, alongside Twisted Way and berserker adepts, riggers and trained combatants. It avoids the Matrix entirely and works through ritual sorcery, custom-built untraceable drones, anonymous tips, hired local muscle who never learn whom they serve, and deep-cover agents placed inside corporate science.
organizations.headquarters: None -- clandestine cells; the French Guiana cell works out of Kourou

leadership.name: Wednesday
leadership.title: Norn
leadership.notes: Prophet and gode. Toxic high initiate; masterminds Operation: Firnbul. Magical suicide after capture.

leadership.name: Friday
leadership.title: Norn
leadership.notes: Frida Kohlman. God chips, drones, WMD acquisition. Breaks under mind probe -- too late.

leadership.name: Thursday
leadership.title: Norn
leadership.notes: Berserker adept, ex-MET2000. Detonates Heimdal at Valhalla.

organizations.notes:
Only the three Norns -- Wednesday, Friday (Frida Kohlman) and Thursday, a berserker adept and ex-MET2000 soldier -- know the whole plan. Home base is Valhalla, a Cold War submarine installation carved into an island in the Bay of Bothnia inside the Haparanda Anomaly Zone; the North American base is Hel, in Tsimshian.

Two long-term schemes fund everything: turning inconspicuous but useful officials through violent blackmail and God-chip addiction, and, for over twenty years, recruiting susceptible young people from turbulent backgrounds, indoctrinating them and reinserting them through corporate scholarship programs such as the New Frontiers Foundation, so they take technical degrees, join the sponsoring corporations and bring the cult the technology it lacks. Its BTL-programmed deep-cover agents are placed by years of arranged training and referrals from other highly placed puppets. The God chip produces euphoria and divine ecstasy, strips away moral restraint, fuels violence and is highly addictive, causing schizophrenic fugues and paranoia; it is believed to be recorded from the Norns' own thoughts and dreams, and the combat version, programmed from Thursday's imprint, is issued to Einherjar on missions. Both burn out after limited use.

EuroPol case 234/54-WN estimated 500 to 600 core members, up to 25 tactical nuclear weapons and viral and nanotech weapons from Belarus, Kronstadt and General Jehangir's Pakistan, and a 75 to 80 percent chance of a major strike within two years. Only three cells were ever exposed; every member committed suicide, later found to be reinforced by implanted fail-safe chips. Its operations are disguised as corporate black ops and screened behind other extremists -- Nationale Aktion, Runenthing, GreenWar, White Resistance, the Crying Masks, Kali cults, the Siida and the Aesir Society -- none of whom know the real plan. The cult has been known to keep hidden caches and run catastrophic research programs; the case of Harding and the New Frontiers pipeline is reported but unconfirmed.

The Guiana cell: Anderson (toxic Raven shaman, cell leader), Howe (rigger, the only non-shaman who knows the employer), Hausmann (deep-cover Proteus scientist) and the razorboys Ein, Zwei and Drei, paid in nuyen, cyberware and BTL chips, who think their boss's mutterings about destroying life on Earth are a joke. Hausmann loads a Winternight drone into the Gotterbote payload before launch, guides the probe to a soft landing on Halley and detonates a small but powerful nuclear bomb meant to knock the comet into the Earth. The Messenger is a target of opportunity, not part of the master plan. The cult does not normally pursue revenge -- too much risk of exposure -- but will hire outside guns to silence anyone who knows too much or foiled it; if Anderson's cell is wiped out, no one else knows enough about Gotterbote to carry on the vendetta.

[2064 – later developments] The dozen radical Asatru of 2031 have become several hundred members worldwide. The plan runs in three stages: Operation Firnbul seizes ten major mana nexi and invokes great-form storm spirits with sacrificial blood magic to bury the sprawls under an unnaturally early winter; Operation Jormungand seeds Ex Pacis's Dissonance virus as code eggs in Matrix nexi, timed to release twenty minutes before the Novatech IPO; and Operation Mjolnir, which Pax knows nothing about, detonates fifteen magically modified EMP nukes hidden in advertising blimps over the world's Matrix junctions and five multi-megaton warheads buried on tectonic fault lines. Wednesday, a toxic high initiate, masterminds Firnbul and commits magical suicide after capture; Friday breaks under a mind probe too late; Thursday detonates Heimdal at Valhalla. The cult is beheaded at Valhalla and in the sweeps that follow, but it does not forget survivors, and may hook individual runners on God chips to turn them into expendable pawns.

organizations.name: Algonkian-Manitou Council
organizations.description: The Algonkian-Manitou Council is the Native American nation of the northern woods, governed from Saskatoon by civil, war and ceremonial leaders, with a mixed agricultural and industrial economy and controlled immigration. Its commercial heart is Thunder Bay, a major smuggling port. The Republic of Quebec counts it as its one notably friendly neighbor, while friction with the Athabaskan Council has never been resolved. Aztechnology holds significant clout inside the Council -- some think it is the power behind the throne. The government is losing control of its north: the mostly elven, anti-technology Manitou have declared independence and seized everything above the Churchill River. Council troops guard that line to stop Manitou sabotage and keep aid from reaching them, while the Manitou mine or destroy the bridges and expect an invasion backed by Aztechnology money. Northern towns such as La Ronge have been reshaped overnight, filling with resentful newcomers and quiet sympathizers alike.
organizations.headquarters: Thunder Bay is its economic center; military deployed along the Churchill River

leadership.name: Robert `Bobby` Bear
leadership.title: Civil Chief
leadership.notes: Hereditary peace chief and nominal head of the police.

leadership.name: Carl Hillborn
leadership.title: War Leader
leadership.notes: Elected war leader.

leadership.name: Laura Hawksford
leadership.title: Ceremonial Leader
leadership.notes: Elected ceremonial leader.

divisions.name: Algonkian
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Algonkian-Manitou Council.

divisions.name: Ojibwa
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Algonkian-Manitou Council.

divisions.name: Iroquois
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Algonkian-Manitou Council.

divisions.name: Navaho
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Algonkian-Manitou Council.

divisions.name: Apache
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Algonkian-Manitou Council.

divisions.name: Algonkian-Manitou Armed Forces
divisions.description: The Council's national military service.

divisions.name: Algonkian-Manitou National Police
divisions.description: The Council's national police service.

organizations.notes: The Council is large and has long stretches of unmonitored border. Crossings may bring tense moments but little real trouble -- fording wide shallow stretches of the river or walking across the ice. The AMC army, Manitou patrols or Aztechnology forces make optional hostile border encounters, and neither side pursues over the line. Elves of tribal ancestry may get a cold shoulder in Thunder Bay from anyone the secession hurt. A team fleeing Niwimaja with the module can expect trouble from the AMC military, Aztechnology troops, or corporate rivals who mistake them for Yamatetsu.

organizations.name: French Guiana
organizations.description: Often called simply Guiana now that the neighboring Guyana has been swallowed by Amazonia. It is one of the few pieces of northern South America Amazonia has not conquered, surrounded by it on three sides with the Atlantic on the fourth -- not for lack of interest or any strength of Guianan arms, but because Guiana is a protectorate of France and Amazonia will not take on Europe over a hundred thousand square kilometers. Physical resources are minimal: subsistence agriculture, forestry and gold mining. The country's one real asset is that it sits almost directly on the equator, ideal for launching into geostationary orbit. The population splits hard between a small wealthy, highly educated corporate class at the aerospace facilities and poor, uneducated masses on the farms, in the lumberyards and down the mines -- with rampant crime, alcoholism, drug and chip use below, and a lot of resentment aimed upward that the well-defended corporate compounds simply absorb.
organizations.headquarters: Cayenne (capital); Kourou is the corporate town
organizations.notes: The nation is not security-conscious; the only significant national industry revolves around Saeder-Krupp's and Proteus' space programs, which are responsible for their own security, and Cayenne customs treat anyone the UCAS let on a plane as harmless. Aerospace holdings: Proteus' offshore arkoblock at the Iles du Salut, the former European Space Agency base at Kourou now owned by Saeder-Krupp, and a massive Novatech launch complex going up outside Cayenne. French is official but most people speak a French-Amerindian creole and English is widely spoken. Yellow fever and rabies are fairly common, vaccinations recommended; avoid local milk and dairy and stick to bottled water outside the cities. The one public hospital of any size is in Cayenne -- overcrowded, understaffed and suspicious of tourists with gunshot wounds; a shaman in the slums will heal for money.

organizations.name: Shibata
organizations.description: Shibata Construction and Engineering is a Philippine-based corporation working in construction and metahuman housing, and a member of the Pacific Prosperity Group. It is one third of the Aztechnology, Shibata and Federated Boeing consortium behind Kepler, the dark horse of the Probe Race to Halley's Comet, and it is deeply invested in winning.
organizations.headquarters: Japan; Kepler consortium operations with Aztechnology and Federated Boeing
organizations.notes:
Shibata was the corporation Sherman Royce's outside contacts pointed him at when he went shopping his sabotage virus, and it paid him a significant sum on delivery to derail Velox I. When Royce auctions the last Liberty activation code on Asgard, Shibata bids, and win or lose it sends people to New Orleans; if it gets the code, Velox II is doomed and the consortium scores a publicity coup by reaching the comet first. Recommended default: Shibata wins the auction and Ares crashes the meet.

The Shibata Major Assets Recovery Team (SMART) is led by Commander Colin Walton, a grizzled black-ops veteran and a troll who leads inside a Japanese corporation on sheer skill. A SMART team may be seen on the New Orleans streets asking about Mercy before the exchange.

It is allied with the Kepler Project.

organizations.name: Council of Dragons
organizations.description: Dragon society is older than any metahuman history, and almost all of its culture exists to keep predators who are territorial by nature from destroying one another. There had not been a council of the great dragons in longer than the young races reckon their history; the Matrix let them follow each other's affairs at a respectful distance, which Hestaby thought would ease tensions and which instead made it feel as though they were all in each other's domains at once. Business is done through rites -- the Rite of Honored Greeting, the Rite of Opening, the Rite of Parting -- and postures: the Posture of Defiance, the Pose of Challenge, the lowered head of assent. Dragons address each other by use-names: Lofwyr is Gold-Master, Ghostwalker is Doll-Maker, Celedyr is Stone-Diver, Hestaby is Orange Queen, Mujaji is Rain Queen, and the dead Dunkelzahn is Far-Scholar. Hestaby, Lofwyr, Ghostwalker, Hualpa, Mujaji, Arleesh, Lung, Ryumyo, Masaru, Rhonabwy, Celedyr, Alamais and Aden attend; Sirrurg, Schwartzkopf and Kaltenstein stay away.
organizations.headquarters: An isolated mountain plateau, attended in spirit form

leadership.name: Lofwyr
leadership.title: Loremaster
leadership.notes: Opens the council by right of the Jewel; concedes a full Rite rather than admit to arranging Dunkelzahn's death.

leadership.name: Ghostwalker
leadership.title: Convenor
leadership.notes: Calls it, then refuses to recognise it until a Loremaster is chosen by the old ways.

leadership.name: Hestaby
leadership.title: Council Member
leadership.notes: Argues for another path, is answered with silence, and takes the Pose of Challenge anyway.

leadership.name: Hualpa
leadership.title: Council Member
leadership.notes: Backs the Rite -- the fate of his own bequest is already in doubt, so he has little to lose.

organizations.notes:
The rules that make the campaign playable: dragons act through chosen agents and may not directly attack another dragon's agents unless those agents attack first (defense is always allowed); agents may freely attack each other; and agents are protected from retribution after the Rite, which is why Lofwyr's threats at the Citadel are largely empty. Great dragons are more like elemental forces than beings a runner team can hope to overcome.

Ghostwalker calls the council, then refuses to recognize it until a Loremaster is chosen by the old ways. Lofwyr opens it by right of the Jewel of Memory and concedes a full Rite rather than admit to arranging Dunkelzahn's death. Hestaby argues for another path, is answered with silence, and takes the Pose of Challenge anyway; Hualpa backs the Rite, having little to lose. A dozen dragons ring the plateau, each glowing with multicolored light, and bow one by one until only Ghostwalker, Alamais, Hestaby and Lofwyr stand. Handing the essence to a neutral dragon (Rhonabwy, Celedyr, Hualpa) is accepted as a surprising compromise; to an extreme one (Alamais, Masaru, Ryumyo) it voids the Rite or awards it to Lofwyr as runner-up; destroying it leaves no Loremaster and Hestaby defends the runners; splitting it works surprisingly well and creates a true council; keeping it forfeits the Rite's protection.

organizations.name: Draco Foundation
organizations.description: The Draco Foundation administers Dunkelzahn's will. Against all draconic tradition the dragon used metahuman legal machinery to dispose of his hoard, and the Foundation was in place to carry out the bequests the moment the will was read; the text of the will is public. It put the Jewel of Memory into Lofwyr's hands, making him Loremaster in fact if not by right, and sent the rest of the hoard to the winds: the Elemental Scrolls of Ak'le'ar to Hualpa, the Silver Songbird to Rhonabwy, the Shroud of Shadows to Aden, the Second Coin of Luck to Lung, the Ring Ouroboros to Ryumyo, the Jade Dragon of Wind and Fire to Wu Lung-Wei of Wuxing, and to Hestaby the encryption key to a private datastore aboard Zurich-Orbital. It also runs the will's great prizes -- among them the underwater-city prize, which it refused Proteus for arkoblocks that sit above the waves -- and has been working with the Dunkelzahn Institute of Magical Research to recover the stolen scrolls. It keeps a complex on wooded Marine Drive in north Everett, among large estates, corporate think tanks and research facilities.

divisions.name: Draco Foundation Northwest
divisions.description: Draco Foundation Northwest manages the foundation's Seattle operations.
divisions.notes: Sassinian leads the division; identity rumors is not publicly known.

organizations.notes:
The Foundation's handling of the bequests is the reason the Rite exists. Accounts differ on Aden's bequest: Aden says he rejected it, which is why the Shroud still lies beneath a Tehran mosque rather than in his hoard on Mount Ararat. The Foundation's special operative is tougher than anything the DIMR fields, and the Foundation is one of the ways out of New Orleans the fixer Toshi Akimura offers.

[2064 – later developments] The Everett complex sits three properties from Griffin Biotechnology's compound and is item 3 on the aerial photograph in the runners' security package; any approach across the terrain passes between Draco Foundation and Ares property, with the Brackhaus and Dohner estates and Puget Sound beyond. Many vehicles on the road run with security escorts.

organizations.name: Red Dragon Triad
organizations.description: The Red Dragon is one of the major Triads of Hong Kong, and the name is not decoration: the street says it ultimately answers to the great dragon Lung on the mainland, though nobody can say what a great dragon wants with a criminal syndicate. It has had difficulties lately that may or may not be connected to Wuxing's swelling influence in the Free Enterprise Zone, it has been fighting the yakuza over black-market smuggling in the Sea of Japan, and it has been coming down harder than usual on anyone who crosses it. Its reach runs from Denver's Chinatown, where it works with Golden Triangle interests under the local leader Choi-Mu, to Boston, where it backs the Mutual Prosperity League. Its oaths are not decorative either: a soldier magically coerced into talking bursts into flame and burns to ash.
organizations.notes:
A Shadowland leaker calling himself Dragonslayer claims the Red Dragon is the Hung Lung Mun ('Red Dragon Association' is a literal translation), the most powerful Triad in Hong Kong and along the Pacific Rim, secretly controlled by Lung since at least 2019; other posters dispute it.

The geomancer Sen Lo owes the Triad a large gambling debt from games rigged in the house's favor; it ransacked his apartment, left a watcher on it, and wants him alive if possible and dead as an example if not. Its soldiers are well trained and literal about orders -- sliverguns first, then hand-to-hand, submachine guns only when they must, because noise draws attention -- and at least as many as the runners. They let the team walk if Sen Lo is handed over without trouble and kill everyone if not.

organizations.name: Knights of Rage
organizations.description: The Knights of Rage were founded at Caerleon in 2043 in the service of the great dragon Celedyr, and later set up a presence in Brixton. They guard Caerleon and support its magical research, and they hold Celedyr's lair more than fifty meters underground behind reinforced ferrocrete. They are not corporate suits: they dress as Celedyr's servant Amon does, in ceremonial garb that would look at home on a film set -- wide gold collars, belted kilts, sandals, cloth headdresses -- and watch visitors with cold stares and their hands near the submachine guns at their belts. They are not the Cyberknights of Glendower or the New Sons of Glendower.
organizations.headquarters: Celedyr's underground complex beneath the Transys Neuronet facility at Caerleon, Wales
organizations.notes: They stand at each door of the composite-walled corridors between the elevator and the amphitheater and use lethal force. Amon states the terms; the Knights are the punctuation. Runners who decline Celedyr's job after being wined and dined are detained until someone else completes the Songbird operation.

organizations.name: The Banded
organizations.description: Deus tattoos between one and seven black bands around a servant's left arm; the more bands, the higher the rank. Cybereye color gives the caste: Whites are otaku, Blues are security troops, Greens are the AI's hands and administrators. Most Whites serve willingly. The implants -- simrig, simlink and commlink, dedicated chipjack with customized BTLs, invoked memory stimulator and an auto-injector of lethal nanites -- keep Deus in constant contact, using them as its eyes and ears and steering them almost like drones across three separate remote-control networks, one per caste.
organizations.headquarters: Renraku Arcology (SCIRE), Downtown Seattle; outposts at Tin Man Scrap Works and in bought-out companies across the sprawl

leadership.name: Pax
leadership.title: Leader of the Whites
leadership.notes: Highest-ranking White; intermediary between Deus and every other Banded.

leadership.name: Tadashi Marushige
leadership.title: Leader of the Blues
leadership.notes: The arcology's former Security Director.

leadership.name: Hiroshi Ushida
leadership.title: Leader of the Greens
leadership.notes: The arcology's former Director; smuggled out to run Deus' outside operations.

organizations.notes: The Banded include Blue Samurai who become more heavily augmented and armored as they rise through the hierarchy. Senior Blue Mages are corrupted initiates who revel in the arcology's misery and can call on an elemental. Green Technicians and Green Experiment Facilitators wear coveralls and hardhats and conduct Deus' experiments. White Otaku possess increasingly powerful living personas, but after their god abandons them, the Whites fare worst of all.

organizations.name: Overwatch
organizations.description: Overwatch is the electronic cavalry: otaku from all over the world, aged roughly eight to twenty, almost all of them orphans of otaku tribes destroyed by Deus's schemes, the madness of Ex Pacis or corporate exploitation, and transformed by the Deep Resonance so that they work the Matrix with no cyberdeck at all. Most are technoshamans, a few cyberadepts. Under one banner they try to protect other otaku and the wider world from Matrix threats most people do not understand -- and revenge plays no small part in it. They have no money and no muscle, and their rundown safehouses and hired security show it; what they have is some of the best deckers alive, a spy inside the Banded, and children who grew up in battle and lost something incalculable doing it. Ronin, once the otaku called Babel, founded and leads them.
organizations.headquarters: Seattle: a derelict Redmond software office, then the Choco-Tarts factory in Auburn, then a red brick house in Bellevue; more safehouses across western North America

leadership.name: Ronin
leadership.title: Founder and War Leader
leadership.notes: Born Michael Bishop; formerly the otaku 'Babel'. Born Michael Bishop; fights Deus as a personal vendetta.

organizations.notes:
Its members range from inexperienced young otaku to seasoned ones carrying Ares Viper Sliverguns. What they can pay: about 10,000 nuyen scraped together, stolen Matrix services up to full channel subscriptions, cyberdeck hardware, utilities and hard-to-find gear acquired by hacking. What they prefer to pay with is leverage: favors owed by the runners' own contacts, or hacker pranks from unexplained phone bills and slashed credit ratings up to forged warrants, death certificates and military enlistment. They keep watching the arcology refugees afterward; they know something is not right.

[2062 – later developments] Overwatch learns of the Network in January while watching arcology survivors and is the first outside force to act against it, identifying Nodes and trying to free or eliminate them.

[2064 – later developments] Overwatch numbered about 150 across the globe; the arcology and the fight against the Network halved it, and Winternight's campaign on Ex Pacis's behalf cuts it to a few dozen by the Novatech IPO -- and the survivors grow more desperate, focused and dangerous. It recognizes Winternight's hand before the Corporate Court does, and with its people stretched between a mobilized Ex Pacis and a reestablished Deus it turns to runners for protection, surgical strikes and intelligence. It is desperate to get its hands on the White called Scarecrow, so Puck can use it as a patsy. None of its survivors can scry past November. It hires runners for a globe-hopping bounty hunt on Ex Pacis enclaves -- while Winternight, through Mr. Lyesmith and his like, hires runners to wipe out what looks like a Matrix gang and is really a cell of Overwatch children barely in their teens. Leave traces on that job and Overwatch becomes a recurring, vengeful enemy.

organizations.name: Gaeatronics
organizations.description: Gaeatronics is owned by the Salish-Shidhe and is barely a multinational -- not even double-A -- yet it is one of the most influential corporations in Seattle, because it supplies most of the city's power and water and has enormous pull with the Salish government: its president, David Gray Bear, is the brother of Harold Gray Bear of the Salish-Shidhe Council. It generates power from a major fusion plant near Olympia, with geothermal, solar and wind plants besides, and the Seattle grid runs from Olympia through a chain of small, unmanned, lightly guarded substations. Fusion financing and treaty-regulated utility leverage make it a political power as much as a business. It keeps an office in the United Kingdom.
organizations.headquarters: Salish-Shidhe Council territory; a fusion plant at Olympia, offices and executives on Council Island, substations across the Seattle metroplex

divisions.name: Gaeatronics U.K.
divisions.description: The corporation's United Kingdom operation and publicity office.
divisions.notes: A Cambridge laboratory claim is attributed 2051/2052 commentary rather than baseline fact.

divisions.name: Gaeatronics Eireann-Tir
divisions.description: The Tir subsidiary operates from Dublin and holds an exclusive North American SES export license.

divisions.name: Gaeatronics Seattle
divisions.description: Gaeatronics Seattle manages the corporation's metroplex utility business.
divisions.notes: Deborah Joshua heads the division.

organizations.notes:
The substation hosts dial the main system once an hour through a vanishing SAN to dump performance data and take new instructions. Deborah Joshua also works in Seattle operations. The company is sometimes written Gaetronics or Gaiatronics.

[2051 – later developments] David Gray Bear's fourteen-year-old son Robert vanishes; Lone Star first calls it gang-related, then suspects a kidnapping, with no leads and no ransom demand, and Gray Bear offers a 20,000-nuyen reward.

[2052 – later developments] Commentary claims Gaeatronics runs a laboratory in Cambridge, among other operations; it is unconfirmed.

[2053 – later developments] Unconfirmed reports describe biometric and shapeshifter security at a Port Gamble research facility and bound-spirit astral security at a Gaeatronics nuclear plant.

[2054 – later developments] Shiawase Atomics distributes Gaeatronics' fusion output to the Seattle grid.

[2061 – later developments] Deus's opening move: two separately harmless programs -- a data-copying utility in an east Tacoma substation's power-monitoring subsystem and an email virus on an executive's personal computer at the Council Island Inn -- merge when the executive mails his status report, and the substation deletes its own consumption limits and overload alerts. The executive's host password, recovered from the bungalow computer, sells for up to 10,000 nuyen or gives temporary access to a Gaeatronics host; it dies after one use or within a week. Gaeatronics and Shiawase Atomics blame each other publicly for the blackout.

[2064 – later developments] A Gaeatronics distribution transformer in the Duwamish industrial area is deliberately sabotaged to set up a run: wrecking the ground-level steel box cuts six buildings off the grid, and only a Gaeatronics technician has the equipment to replace the part -- the runners' one clue that the 4 a.m. power failure was no accident.

organizations.name: CrashCart
organizations.description: CrashCart is Yamatetsu's emergency medical service in Seattle, competing head to head with DocWagon for the high-threat response market and running a growing network of clinics under President and CEO Melissa Ranshandani. Yamatetsu Seattle bought it in late 2052 after its long fight with DocWagon. Its parent is constantly on the lookout for new medical technology. The name is also written Crash Cart.
organizations.notes:
Shadowland attributes a 'Black Monday' management purge, missing senior personnel, Osprey's adoption and later equipment sell-offs to the takeover. Yamatetsu's restructuring, executive placements and clinic expansion, and rumors of missing patients, follow CrashCart everywhere.

[2061 – later developments] CrashCart is the corner of Yamatetsu that stands to gain from SENSE: exclusive use of a portable neural scanner would let it pull customers from DocWagon on response quality alone, after which Yamatetsu could license SENSE back to DocWagon and the hospitals. The clues in the case are meant to point at Yamatetsu or even DocWagon, so that nobody looks at Deus. During the 48-hour blackout CrashCart is swamped along with DocWagon, Lone Star and Franklin Associates.

[2064 – later developments] Seattle's shadows speak of CrashCart's 'mysterious debacle in the early fifties' as the end of DocWagon's last real competition in the sprawl; when Rose Croix appears, a Shadowland poster asks, 'Another Crash Cart??' Yamatetsu sends its own covert team into the Kethers Building after the glowing tissue in box 89-661 the same night as the runners.

organizations.name: Sons of Sauron
organizations.description: The Sons of Sauron are troll terrorists with a taste for the direct approach. After a Humanis Policlub strike into the Ork Underground in 2049, a Sons of Sauron retaliatory bombing killed 38 people. Their style is a threat, a concession and a grudge that outlives both: the Palace of China in Tacoma kept a 'No Troll' door policy for a decade until the Sons phoned in a bomb threat over it, and owner Dustin Kien lifted the ban -- though trolls still draw suspicious glances inside.
organizations.notes: An irate Sons of Sauron troll queueing outside the Palace may pick a fight with runners who use Dixie's name to bypass the line. The Sons of Sauron operate under a midnight deadline and seek to avoid inflicting severe wounds. The same encounter is offered again for the second Palace of China meet months later.

organizations.name: The Netwalkers
organizations.description: The Netwalkers are an otaku tribe living in the Rox in Boston, technically capable and known for locating data, salvaging computer equipment and Matrix work. Ex Pacis, Deus's Whites and the corporations all give a Boston otaku tribe reason to be paranoid and well hidden. They have a long history with the decker Ronin.
organizations.notes:
Renraku once sent the covert-operations agent Michael Bishop, loaded with advanced cyberware, to learn the Netwalkers' secrets. Bishop underwent their initiation and came out a genuine otaku, but Deus interfered in the transformation, stole his memories of his former life and named him Babel; the tribe never learned what it handed over. The same interference is how Deus first learned to make otaku of its own. Everything Ronin is, and everything he later does to Deus, starts here.

[2064 – later developments] When Mirage learns that Deus has converted Matrix Systems' CEO and is preparing to seize the East Coast Stock Exchange, it warns the local tribes, and the Netwalkers reach out to Ronin. On IPO day they are among the few dozen otaku who pool their abilities inside the Exchange host to raise a Resonance Well at the roots of Deus's World Tree and attack with the Deep Resonance behind them -- knowing they cannot win, and that their job is to distract him long enough for Ronin's Nodes to reach his code and for Dodger to wake Megaera. Jormungand is programmed to avoid Resonance Wells; the serpent's tail turns theirs into a Dissonance Pool instead of attacking it directly.

organizations.name: Franklin Associates
organizations.description: Franklin Associates is the corporation that holds Seattle's fire-control contract, one of the metroplex's emergency-response providers alongside DocWagon, CrashCart and Lone Star.
organizations.notes: [2061 – later developments] When the grid fails and thousands of alarms go off across the metroplex, Franklin Associates is overwhelmed; fires in looted shops and stalled traffic burn far longer than they should, and ambulances that cannot get through the gridlock fall back on helicopters.

organizations.name: Ex Pacis
organizations.description: Ex Pacis swears allegiance to no one but itself. Where Resonant otaku strive to become one with the global network, Ex Pacis believes in the Dissonance -- making the Matrix become one with them. To Pax's tribe the other otaku are not the heirs of the Matrix but its slaves, weaklings shaped by the network when they hold every tool needed to shape it. Founded by Pax after she escaped Deus's abandonment at the Renraku Arcology, the tribe claimed a cure for Fading in the Dissonance and set out to convert or eliminate any otaku with the potential to threaten her. Driven out of North America by Overwatch, Ex Pacis fled to the Far East, where the intense data traffic and state-of-the-art grids hid them and the disorganized local otaku made willing recruits; enclaves now exist in North America, Europe and Asia, with Dissonance Pools seeded in hidden corners of the world. Pax's grip has flagged as her Fading worsens and she leans on her lieutenants Amor and Honos to keep young upstarts in line; the tribe's most promising scryer is the young Solitude. When outside talent is needed, Ex Pacis uses its older members as fronts and conceals operations as ordinary industrial sabotage and corporate intrigue.
organizations.headquarters: A hidden UV host inside the Morgue datahaven, itself secreted in Singapore's Market Research Group system; other records place Pax in Kuala Lumpur

leadership.name: Pax
leadership.title: Tribe Leader
leadership.notes: Designed Jormungand; brokered the Winternight alliance in person at Valhalla.

leadership.name: Amor
leadership.title: Lieutenant
leadership.notes: Keeps the ranks in line with Honos; pulled Pax out of the Dissonance Pool after her vision.

leadership.name: Honos
leadership.title: Lieutenant
leadership.notes: As Amor. Both vanish with Pax after the Crash.

leadership.name: Orion
leadership.title: Regional Cell Leader
leadership.notes: Ran the Magestone contract and planted the Alcatraz code egg.

organizations.notes: No Ex Pacis otaku -- and no Overwatch otaku either -- can scry beyond November '64 with the Info Sortilage Echo, which is what turned the naysayers in the ranks back to Pax's cause. Ex Pacis calls Deus's Nodes 'the Banded'. A Dissonant otaku must be physically present to upload a Jormungand code egg from his own mind into a host's firmware, which is the whole reason runners get hired to ferry them into RTG and PLTG hubs. During the Crash, Dissonant otaku surf in the worm's wake, hitting their Resonant brethren's strongholds while Jormungand itself avoids Resonance Wells (nobody knows how Dissonant code and a Well would interact). Aftermath: Winternight's betrayal costs Ex Pacis nothing directly -- Pax and her trusted lieutenants simply vanish in the chaos, leaving the tribe scattered and the new Matrix not remade to their liking after all. Ex Pacis harassment of runners who cross them is petty and endless: emptied accounts, mixed-up credit records, SINs marked deceased.

organizations.name: The Network
organizations.description: On 11 May 2061 Inazo Aneki's killswitch shattered Deus's code -- and instead of falling into Renraku's Mousetrap deck, the fragments went into roughly a thousand metahumans the AI had spent two years testing, culling and wiring in the Arcology's zombie rooms. A live Matrix connection lets Deus possess a Node, using its senses, memories, and body as his shell. When a Node connects, a decentralized network opens its locked memory with the right passcodes and feeds it a fresh set of compiling instructions; the brain works on Deus's code for a set period, then the Node is returned to the physical world until the next session. No single Node holds much of the AI and not all are ever online at once, which makes the compilation almost impossible to track and harder still to shut down.
organizations.headquarters: Decentralized -- roughly a thousand metahuman minds scattered across the globe
organizations.notes: Megaera's code was fragmented into the same Nodes when she distracted Deus for the killswitch, so the Network has been a shadow war ever since -- Deus's instruction sets ignored or subverted whenever her Nodes outnumbered his, each side trying to take the other's without wrecking the whole. A third faction formed under the decker Ronin. Deus won it by planting Whites-made Nodes in positions of power worldwide and by simply destroying Megaera's -- runner wetwork dressed as corporate hits, or loyal Nodes ordered to attack disloyal ones in the Matrix until they were traumatized or dead. Outside pressure came from Overwatch, Shiawase's MIFD, and units formed by Renraku and Transys-Neuronet; Transys-Neuronet captured a Node in December 2062 and got little out of its code fragment but a great deal of interest in the implanted technology. On 31 October 2064 compilation completed and 1,342 people around the globe fell into deep comas while connected to the Matrix -- a medical mystery that got some media attention before the IPO dwarfed it. If a Node is killed or captured, its stored code image can simply be transferred to a newly created one.

organizations.name: Shadowland
