organizations.description: Shadowland is the shadow community's archive and message board: a low-traffic shadow Matrix of local nodes hanging off the Denver Nexus -- L.A., New York, Cheyenne, Havana, Berlin, Sicily, Honshu, Seoul, Sydney, Guam, Hawai'i, Paris, Frankfurt, Mersey, Kuwait and Seattle, among others -- each with its own sysop, politics and grudges, mirrored through the Nexus and trading data with other havens. Its editors handle sources in layers and warn that signed commentary may be useful, biased, contradictory or deliberately false. Captain Chaos has spearheaded Shadowland Seattle for more than fifteen years and is the closest thing the network has to a leader. Its routes and hubs have changed many times.
organizations.headquarters: The Denver Nexus, with nodes worldwide; Shadowland Seattle run from a small Everett apartment
organizations.notes:
Captain Chaos reports about six major penetrations of the network over the years, all but one or two linked somehow to Aztlan or Aztechnology.

Because the nodes are not the high-traffic zones Jormungand seeks, the worm reaches them late -- long enough for Captain Chaos to call every sysop willing to listen into a war council while the grids die, and for the Nexus to forward Zurich-Orbital's data dump before it vanishes. Then the choice: fight the virus at its roots, or abandon their own nodes and spend the last minutes hacking every channel they can reach to get the warning out. Shadowland chooses the warning: in 'Rush Hour' the surviving war circle hacks the globe from failing grids, subverting housekeeping computers, vending machines, commercial boards and credstick units to display it, which is how runners hear about the nests and blimps at all. The era of local Shadowland nodes ends here. Several nodes burn with their sysops and drones, Captain Chaos most prominently; Sydney is destroyed live on the link; Seoul and Kuwait are gone before the council convenes; Hawai'i refuses the call; Sionedd takes Mersey offline mid-meeting. Sysops at the war council include Sequoyah (Cheyenne, ultra anti-corporate), Tell (Frankfurt), Drackenfelts (Paris) and Sionedd (Mersey); Captain Chaos's crew -- DionySys, Juggler, Smiley, Diabolique, Thumper, Raid, Syzygy -- loses Diabolique, DionySys, Juggler and Thumper. Afterward the Helix and Retro's improvised nodes are the first things to come back.

organizations.name: Matrix Systems of Boston
organizations.description: Matrix Systems of Boston descends directly from Echo Mirage: the hosts that housed the AI Psychotrope were stolen by former Echo Mirage deckers and made part of the corporation, which later fell into Richard Villiers's hands at Fuchi and passed to Novatech, for which it is now a major Matrix-design operation. It pioneered the Portal cyberdeck. It is the contractor for the East Coast Stock Exchange's massive host upgrade -- the gothic-cathedral architecture unveiled on IPO launch day. Max Burnwell is its CEO.

leadership.name: Max Burnwell
leadership.title: Chief Executive Officer
leadership.notes: Converted to a Network Node 4 August 2064; survives a near-assassination in early September.

organizations.notes:
The AI Mirage has lived quietly in Matrix Systems' hidden hosts ever since, which makes the corporation the AI's home in the most literal sense. On 4 August 2064 Burnwell missed a scheduled ECSE/SEC briefing on the upgrade and reappeared a day later citing a personal emergency; Minuteman Security, who guard him, were skeptical but never discovered that he had been converted into one of Deus's Nodes. Mirage noticed, and the infiltration of its home brought the eldest AI out of self-exile: in early September a near-successful assassination attempt on Burnwell and, a week later, sabotage of the Exchange's hardware were both Mirage's warnings to Deus.

'Echoes of Mirage': Mirage hires runners through an intermediary to investigate Matrix Systems' senior staff and bug their cyberdecks so it can scan them for Node conversion when they come online. With the IPO near, Villiers has all his subsidiaries under close scrutiny, and Miles Lanier's security catches wind of someone snooping, assumes a rival megacorp, and hunts the team.

organizations.name: Trans-Latvian Enterprises
organizations.description: Trans-Latvian Enterprises is an investment banking house whose sole purpose is to invest in other companies, and the largest single owner of Novatech after Richard Villiers himself, with 24 percent. Villiers founded it during the Fuchi debacle to shield his personal assets from bankruptcy law, cut every formal tie and handed it to someone else to make the shield work, transferring in enormous blocks of private stock and even taking out a Novatech loan against them that he never meant to repay. Whoever he gave it to liked being at the helm of a multi-billion-nuyen corporation, refused to take orders and called in the loan; Novatech defaulted, TLE took the collateral, and the shell became a real investment bank. Its attorney of record, Oskari Laine of Tallinn, answers media inquiries and nothing else, confirming only that Villiers neither runs nor owns any part of it -- which Villiers has publicly acknowledged under obvious duress. Among its assets is one of Fuchi's most important possessions, the Delta-class shadow clinic in Pueblo, now aligned to no AAA and open to anyone with enough cash.
organizations.headquarters: Tallinn, Estonia -- at a registered address that is a parking lot
organizations.notes: The Chromed Accountant can say with 99.99 percent certainty that the identity of TLE's controller is nowhere on the Matrix. Shadowland's theories: it was Charles Lyons, Villiers's best friend from high school, who moved to Tallinn months before the fiasco and turned up in an Estonian sewer with his fingerprints sanded off and every identifying feature mutilated -- and the current holder is unknown; or Villiers stole Lyons's identity and the body was a Tallinn bum; or a Fairlight asset-tracking expert system gifted to TLE woke up and was found, after Lyons's death, to have been appointed vice president. TLE's open-door policy drives Villiers up the wall. Hook: Samantha Villiers offers TLE her 7 percent of Novatech for a loan big enough to bid for Renraku; if TLE takes it, the mystery shareholder holds 34 percent of Novatech right after the IPO.

organizations.name: The New Revolution
organizations.description: The New Revolution is the nickname of a secret group that has conspired for years to reunify the United States of America. Key figures in North America's power circles belong to it or have been blackmailed into working for it, and political murder, terrorism and corruption have all been its tools. The Crash took the conspirators by surprise, but the chaos handed them their opening: on 3 November 2064, using secret military channels, they launched a coordinated strike against every North American government. Tanks rolled, helicopters bombed government buildings, leaders were detained, protestors were executed and the trid and radio played military music and censored news; the stars and stripes flew over historic landmarks again -- for a while. The cover story, to be delivered at nine o'clock by Senator Braddock and senior commanders over the Public Broadcast Network, was that the Native American Nations and Aztlan had collapsed the UCAS Matrix with nuclear strikes.
organizations.headquarters: Distributed through North America's power circles; safehouses around Washington FDC

leadership.name: Pete Reynolds
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: Calls the coup dead the moment Colloton speaks, and runs.

organizations.notes: The New Revolution bit off more than it could chew. Loyal troops fought back, surviving authorities bought corporate support at a price, and civilians and militants faced rebel units with whatever they had, sometimes words alone. The worst blow came from inside, where some leaders had plans of their own. President Kyle Haeffner was kidnapped from the White House, refused to cooperate and was murdered in a 'failed' rescue by the very team that freed him, on a garbled radio order. Secretary of Defense Stratta was murdered; Vice President Nadja Daviar survived an assassination attempt in Seattle; General Angela Colloton denounced the coup on trid and declared martial law on Daviar's orders; President Pro Tempore Gene Simone filled in until the principals were found. Elections were postponed on 4 November. Director Pete Reynolds calls the coup dead the moment Colloton speaks, and runs. The UCAS and the Sioux are badly bruised, Tir Tairngire and the Ute change radically, and California and the CAS pretend it was business as usual.

organizations.name: Seers' Guild
organizations.description: The Guild is the organized body of the Sixth World's professional seers, with novices, a Disciplinary Committee that can make lethal examples of oath breakers, and an inner elite -- the company Via Stellae, which accepts only the cream of the crop.
organizations.headquarters: Europe; the elite company Via Stellae draws on Athens and the Guild's Equinox Rituals
organizations.notes:
The Guild's Equinox Ritual in 2064 produced a very secret prophecy about the Matrix: something enormous is coming that will destroy or change it, though not when and, more usefully, not how. The Guild is divided over what to do. Some want to warn the world, or at least the powers-that-be. Some push their own readings of the omens and arrange shadow operations to keep competing interpretations from being published. Some keep quiet and invest in the sectors least affected by a Matrix crash, or best placed to profit from the rebuilding. Others sell their exclusive knowledge to powerful clients -- which is how Yohann De Kervelec came to stand before Lofwyr and confirm that the days of the Matrix are numbered, and how the dragon came to smile.

As the day approaches, prophecies from every faction multiply, all describing a major upheaval, often contradictory and sometimes completely off base. Omens of the coming Crash include unusual animal behavior, weird weather, conspiracy-buff paranoia (Dankwalther and Villiers, Winternight, the Network, Deus, and red herrings) and direct visions. The fraud Jack Dylan publishes a made-up prophecy that someone will crash the Matrix on IPO day to hide huge illegal transfers, and lands too close to a Mafia don's real laundering plan. New York stockbroker Gardhia Obasegan owes his success to the elderly expatriate shaman Monji Sanko, who conjures the ancestor spirit of Obasegan's grandmother and has just received a very troubling prediction. The seer Hiro Tanawa has had an accurate vision and hires protection from whoever wants him silenced. The media-savvy rivals 'Orlando Bonnetoile' and 'Magnificent Gary' will do anything to discredit each other's visions.

organizations.name: Metahuman People's Army
organizations.description: The Metahuman People's Army is the armed metahuman resistance in Saito's Protectorate, working in Oakland and San Francisco under constant pressure from air patrols, flash raids and Protectorate Marines. Besides fighting, it runs social services and local policing in its neighborhoods and negotiates ransom exchanges. It shelters the people the regime wants, and it is suspicious of strangers with good reason, but its price is simple: expand any operation into a rescue of its own people and it will provide logistics and manpower without hesitation. Alcatraz, refurbished to house Saito's intelligence division and hold dissidents for interrogation, is the target it has waited for someone to make possible.
organizations.headquarters: Oakland and the San Francisco Bay Area, California Free State
organizations.notes: The MPA saves its firepower for emergencies and escapes; stealth is essential against the experienced Marine garrison, whose reinforcements arrive ten minutes after an alarm. The irony none of them learn: the Alcatraz jailbreak is cover for Orion planting a Jormungand code egg in the Rock's data hub, which is wired into several corporate backers' communications and security -- a perfect vector into Japanacorp grids across the West Coast and the Pacific Rim. The Oakland-born ork decker Cal Lowry was drawn to the MPA, and Magestone's surviving representative meets outsiders under its guard. It is said to work with communes and other resistance groups.

organizations.name: New Islamic Jihad
organizations.description: The New Islamic Jihad was Ibn Eisa's instrument of terror inside the Islamic Unity Movement, and its mark was on the car bombs and assassinations of officials that tore through Riyadh in the weeks after the Crash, while Arabian security was in shambles. After Ibn Eisa was unmasked at the al-Nasiriyah palace and driven into hiding, the NIJ cut its ties with the Movement and became a radical terrorist outfit feared throughout the Islamic world, its members dispersed across the globe vowing to bring down the Caliph and the IUM. Many of them are Ibn Eisa's Jinn bodyguards, and they appear to have inherited his powers.
organizations.notes: Important people in the IUM want deniable assets for a worldwide hunt for Ibn Eisa's surviving cronies. If the Shadowland poster Sadiq is right that shedim took Ibn Eisa over, his Jinn are far more dangerous than terrorists. Ayatollah Juvayni in Najaf is a potential target -- and may be a powerful shedim who will not fall without a fight.

organizations.name: Paladin Medical Technologies
organizations.description: Paladin Medical Technologies is a Seattle medical-technology corporation with a pharmaceutical supply division, a marketing arm, a clinic staffed by a dozen or so technicians, and a Special Security Directorate whose job is to solve problems without Paladin's name appearing anywhere near them. It is nowhere near triple-A: it competes with the likes of DocWagon for hospital and government supply contracts, and DocWagon is at once its biggest customer and a competitor. On paper it posts profitable quarter after profitable quarter thanks to shrewd business moves; on the street, much of that success is credited to CEO Dr. Fredericks being unafraid to hire shadowrunners for prototypes, research data and special shipments. Fredericks sets the tone personally -- he once smashed a datapad on the boardroom table hard enough to lacerate his chief operations officer's face and arms, and everyone understood the injury was the point. Paladin regards Griffin Biotechnology as its only serious competition in the sprawl.
organizations.notes:
Leadership: Dr. Fredericks (CEO, 'the old man'), Dr. Bob Struthers (chief operations officer, who traced the JSR database intrusion), Katey Nagahara (contract intelligence, who identified DocWagon and the Snohomish plant) and Brian Wallace (Special Security Director, who hires as 'Mr. Smithers' through Saint James and claims to be from Universal Omnitech). Alexandra 'Alex' Detwiler is a professional ork Johnson on Fredericks's staff; Lyle Green is one of a long list of intermediaries. Paladin owns a beta-grade clinic Alex can open to runners who impress her.

Demolition Run: three contracts lost in a month (Seattle General and the Salish border patrol among them, about 1.5 million nuyen each) leave Paladin a year from the wall. Its deniable contractors destroy DocWagon's Snohomish plant, costing DocWagon six months of production and forcing it to buy from outside vendors, Paladin included. No culprit is ever publicly named, but the rumor that Fredericks hired runners to hit a DocWagon facility to win the Seattle General contract circulates on the street.

Griffin: Fredericks noticed DocWagon Seattle and Ares investing in Griffin Biotechnology, hired runners to scope the new Everett compound for later use (FORCEd Recon, paying 1,000 nuyen guaranteed per runner plus 500 to 5,000 per information category), and bought the Griffin researcher Don Kukalakee with drinks and loans; Paladin now pays his gambling debts at Stuck's Carnival in Auburn. Kukalakee delivered Dr. Renee Josario's badge and keycode, and Alex put out the datasteal (1,000 nuyen down, 10 to 20 percent of the paydata, 48 hours, no bloodshed, damage or trace, because 'Ms. Johnson's sponsors have assets inside Griffin'). Paladin wants the resulting Ambidexterity Router field-tested fast enough that it offers the prototype to the team that stole the plans. Fredericks believes people are the weakest part of any organization.

Later in the arc Paladin, with Yamatetsu and AG Chemie, wins the UCAS military pharmaceuticals contract Michael Davenport had spent two weeks preparing DocWagon's bid for, with Fort Lewis as testbed; that contract alone is keeping Paladin afloat, which makes it an obvious acquisition target. Rose Croix may open negotiations with Paladin for the router once field testing is done.

In the Insider Trading scene Fredericks picks up a runner with corporate contacts in a black Mitsubishi Nightsky, between heavily cybered ork bodyguards, and asks what is about to happen to DocWagon. Polite answers earn a lift and possibly a 1,000 nuyen gratuity; refusal earns a gamma-scopolamine dart and an interview under a truth agent.

The company also appears as Paladin Systems, Paladin Medical Services and Paladin Biomedical.

organizations.name: Griffin Biotechnology
organizations.description: Until very recently Griffin Biotechnology was one of the small biomedical firms scraping along in the Seattle sprawl, leasing offices in Aztechnology's Huitzilopochtli Plaza across from the Pyramid. Then its lead researcher's work on using signals from healthy brain tissue to compensate for damaged tissue became real progress on epilepsy and, more valuably, a whole family of bioware and cybernetic spin-off technologies. CEO Dr. Sumihiro Asikawa courted the majors for capital; DocWagon Seattle led a field that came to include Ares Macrotechnology, Seattle University and UCAS Department of Defense grants. In a few months Griffin has become one of the largest biomedical research firms in the metroplex, bought out an entire neighbourhood in north Everett and built a state-of-the-art research, manufacturing and clinical compound on it, guarded by Knight Errant. It recruits heavily at the sprawl's universities, especially Seattle University, for biotechnology, cybertechnology, traditional medicine and nanotechnology posts.
organizations.headquarters: Huitzilopochtli Plaza, downtown Seattle; new research facility off 172nd Street, north Everett
organizations.notes:
Leadership: Dr. Sumihiro Asikawa (CEO), the lead neurology researcher (Dr. Indira Chontel in most accounts, Dr. Chandra Dasari in others -- the same person and the same work), who has a private lab and office on the second floor, and Rebecca Owls-Breath, the Security Director and the one security post Knight Errant does not fill. Griffin paid the metroplex agencies to keep only partial floor plans on file.

Personnel policy: Griffin has decided its people matter more than its secrets. Every employee is told to cooperate with captors, hand over passcodes and passkeys, then report the compromise so systems can be changed. Damage that heals naturally is tolerated; anything needing cyber replacement or expensive healing brings the corporation's active wrath, and killing a captive is punished (Etiquette (Corporate) 4 to know this). Staff are pushed onto public transport and car pools, but senior people drive between downtown and Everett, and most carry a PanicButton trackable by radio direction finding: take a VIP without isolating every device and four Knight Errant response teams with close air support arrive shortly after.

The Everett compound has been hit repeatedly: an unidentified probe before it opened, Paladin's reconnaissance, Paladin's datasteal through the gambling-addicted researcher Don Kukalakee (passed over twice for promotion, who sold his team leader Dr. Renee Josario's badge and keycode to end her career), and Dr. Joselito Santiago of Aztechnology Seattle, who glimpsed his former wife during an invited tour. Griffin research biologist Amanda Sanchez is really Amanda Santiago, formerly of Aztechnology, hiding under a changed identity with a son Griffin knows nothing about; Joselito's year of surveillance ends in an abduction at a zoo and a blood ritual in a warehouse.

DocWagon CEO Garrett Walsh approved Griffin as his only diversification, and delayed it longest, which Michael Davenport resents. Davenport announces the partnership at the shareholders' meeting, with the lead researcher in the front rows under two tense bodyguards posing as her dates.

The prototype that bought DocWagon's support is a rapid custom-organ system: generic 'marker-free' cultured organs retagged with a patient's genetic markers in hours instead of months. It works for several organs but succeeds only about fifteen percent of the time. Rose Croix wants it or wants it gone, and Yamatetsu strikes the building the same night. Afterwards Griffin drops seven points and sits in a tenuous position while it assesses the damage to its microbiology and nanotechnology labs; Walsh begins to feel the Everett complex has drawn too much attention for its likely return.

The company also appears as Griffin Biotech and Griffin Biotechnologies.

organizations.name: Ares Arms
organizations.description: Ares Arms is the military-systems subdivision of Ares Macrotechnology. It fields a competitive Desert Wars force, a large staff of trained test-and-evaluation personnel who can put any new weapon or support system through its paces, and a team of end-user consultants who train buyers of Ares military products to use them efficiently. With the possible exception of Aztechnology, Ares has the most extensive military capability of any megacorporation, and Ares Arms reliably has the best new military-grade toys on the market. Its combat troops and security forces are almost always cybered to the gills, in full military armor with tactical communications gear, and standby teams can reach another Ares Arms facility by helicopter or tilt-rotor within ten minutes. Its arcane security is just as serious: combat-trained adepts and mages, paranormal animals and spirits.
organizations.headquarters: Ares Macrotechnology; Seattle divisional operations at Fort Lewis

divisions.name: Ares Arms Seattle Division
divisions.description: Seattle's Ares Arms division works out of and supports Fort Lewis and the military base there. Its offices are spread throughout Seattle, including space in the main Ares Macrotechnology enclave for administration; Fort Lewis holds operations and the divisional headquarters; a facility in Everett manufactures armor plating for all drones and vehicles; and the division routinely uses the Puyallup and Redmond Barrens for weapons testing and demonstrations -- a habit that provides convenient cover for a black research site in Redmond that has nothing to do with weapons testing at all.
divisions.notes: This is the enemy card the module hands out, and the mechanics matter. Modifiers earned in this run: minimal damage or killing +0/+0/+0; significant damage or killing +0/+1/+0; selling information about the facility +0/+1/+0, cumulative with either of the first two. A runner photographed committing heavy property damage, looting or killing every guard they meet AND later identified as selling the data takes +0/+2/+0. Note it on the Mission Log -- having an Enemy means a file is being kept and that the division will appear in later adventures and act according to its current level. Fencing the facility data yourself rather than through Manny brings five Ares fast response teams to ambush the deal.
divisions.source_adventure: SRM 00-05 A Dark and Stormy Night

divisions.name: Ares Arms Special Magic Corps
divisions.description: The Ares Arms unit consists of ten five-person containment teams, a captain, a rigger, a decker, and medical doctors in environmentally sealed security armor, transported from Fort Lewis in Ares TR-55 VTOLs. Its commander, Captain Kenneth Brooks, announces over the facility loudspeakers that his containment team is taking over security. Every five-man element pairs two heavily cybered security specialists with two grade 4 initiate warrior adepts and a grade 4 hermetic combat mage, with bound elementals in support.
divisions.notes:
The unit deploys in five-person teams supported by water and air elementals. Additional teams reinforce any engagement.

Subordinate unit of Ares Arms Seattle Division.
divisions.source_adventure: SRM 00-05 A Dark and Stormy Night

divisions.name: Tagmatic
divisions.description: An Ares Arms invention division associated with the Smart Goggles project.
divisions.notes: Wyn Carver is a young inventor frustrated by the slow Ares approval pipeline. No broader product line, headquarters, security, or leadership is established.

organizations.notes: Ares Arms is running an operation far outside its public weapons business. Several months ago it built a four-sublevel research facility in the Redmond Barrens to bioengineer a toxin more effective against insect spirits, and stocked it with live true-form and flesh-form ant spirits as test subjects -- hence the unusual amount of magical security around the specimen rooms. Security is built for containment rather than intrusion: chemical rounds instead of lead, insecticide-foam dispensers in the labs, Ares ELD-AR assault rifles with insecticide rounds in the alcove outside the main testing lab, chemsuits in the decontamination room, protocol CHARLIE, and a containment team at Fort Lewis that arrives by TR-55 VTOL. The security-cleared guards may not enter the labs unless an alarm sounds, and trade theories about mutants from the Glow, space aliens from the crashed suborbital and things that go bump in the night.
organizations.source_adventure: SRM 00-05 A Dark and Stormy Night

organizations.name: Rose Croix
organizations.description: Rose Croix Biomedical Solutions is the newest contender in Seattle's emergency medical services market, certified as an emergency medical response company at a launch the governor attended. Its CEO and chairman, Dr. Walter Broward, a Boston University graduate and a recent addition to Seattle's skyline, has hired some of the best young minds in business and medicine and makes no secret of wanting to crush 'imbeciles like Garrett Walsh'. It runs three clinics -- near the centre of downtown, near Fort Lewis and near downtown Everett -- and a state-of-the-art cryogenic storage facility, all newly equipped. Service tiers run Standard, Silver, Gold, Platinum and Ebony. Instead of DocWagon's bulky wristband, clients carry a rice-grain subdermal implant, activated on demand and tied into their medical records, with continuous vital-sign monitoring at the higher tiers. It fields a High Threat Response division with armored ambulances, keeps security mages who sweep its facilities astrally, runs a magical healing program, and has bought a state sanitarium in Puyallup and reopened it as Caring Gardens. Its growth has been so fast that investors are already circling its promised public offering.
organizations.headquarters: Seattle metroplex, before the headquarters is publicly announced.

leadership.name: Walter Broward
leadership.title: Chief Executive Officer
leadership.notes: Michael Davenport with reconstructive surgery and a new identity.

leadership.name: Dr. Alex Heffernan
leadership.title: Director of Caring Gardens
leadership.notes: A fraud with no accreditation; a corrupted hermetic mage who took the facility for himself.

organizations.notes:
Walter Broward is Michael Davenport, DocWagon Seattle's former chief operations officer. Davenport spent months seeding encrypted caches of DocWagon client lists, security codes and operational data through the company, then hired two teams of runners to stage his own assassination so he could walk away with them. He came back from the Caribbean with a new face, funded by what he embezzled, his own money and private venture capital. His strategy: DocWagon has gone soft without competition since Crash Cart died in the early fifties. His fixer and enforcer is Mr. Bones, the ex-runner Dredd, who always has a back-up plan; his executive assistant is Lucy Turnbull. Before the company was public, its elite extraction team -- a rigger, a shaman with a greater city spirit, mages with anchored invisibility -- murdered a DocWagon High Threat Response team for its ambulance.

The campaign against DocWagon: the Tacoma vault hit for Earl Peabody's clone and the clones of Platinum clients (magically active clients flee DocWagon because a stolen tissue sample is a ritual link); the Doom Squad footage, bought through a friend of a friend and followed up by new Johnson Vincent Capello, which reaches Lone Star through 'anonymous sources' and nearly doubles Rose Croix's client base; and three runs on Griffin Biotechnology through the fixer Lyle Green, the last paying 3,000 + (3,000 x TR) per runner to bring in the organ prototype or 1,800 + (1,800 x TR) to destroy it, noise and bodies no object. A trideo action hero is signed as the Ebony-tier spokesman, and Rose Croix may open negotiations with Paladin for the ambidexterity router.

Caring Gardens was a corner cut: its director Dr. Alex Heffernan, hired on references from Transys Neuronet and Universal Omnitech executives without a background check, is a fraud and a corrupted mage. He holds video of a Rose Croix run on DocWagon's tissue banks and audio of a Rose Croix Johnson arranging it through a street fixer (worth about 20,000 nuyen, fenceable for 10,000). Rose Croix needs deniability if patients die, resolution inside 24 hours and minimal press. Broward negotiates in person at 0230 in the back room of a jazz club, and can loan combat mages such as Trey 'Boltar' Harris to a runner team.

Before the IPO Broward puts all shadowruns on hold -- the silence his favorite fixer notices and sells. Ending 1: DocWagon buys the company, Broward cites family reasons, and all pending Corporate Court grievances are dropped. Ending 2: DocWagon releases the truth, Davenport is warranted and vanishes, and what is left of Rose Croix might survive if it can pin everything on him -- it found a perfect niche, and it will be cheap to buy into.

organizations.name: Corporate Court
organizations.description: The Corporate Court is the extraterritorial judiciary of the megacorporate world. It grew out of the Inter-Corporate Council formed in 2012, became the International Corporate Court, and moved to the Zurich-Orbital space station in 2023. It governs pan-corporate law and settles disputes among extraterritorial corporations. Its thirteen justices sit in rotation, and it has no police or security force of its own: its authority rests on the megacorporations agreeing to honor it. It authorized Operation Reciprocity and the Veracruz Settlement and then took authority over the Pan-Corporate Zone and its canal mission. Corporations facing one another before the Court usually prefer a settlement, and evidence strong enough to win there is worth a great deal outside it.

divisions.name: Corporate Court Matrix Authority
divisions.description: The Corporate Court Matrix Authority regulates Matrix jurisdiction and electronic commerce and negotiates with governments and grid providers.
divisions.notes: Grid Overwatch Division is deferred beneath this authority because nested division parentage is not representable.

organizations.notes:
DocWagon and Rose Croix have each filed grievances with the Court against the other for tortious interference with business relations. DocWagon tried and failed to stop Rose Croix by legal means; what Saint James offers instead is photographic proof that shadowrunners were hired to hit DocWagon, which DocWagon can use to force a contract buyout or win a Court lawsuit. In Ending 1 the low-balled buyout Broward signs to avoid a fight before the Court drops every pending case; in Ending 2 the cases remain, and Michael Davenport is suspected of involvement in several of them alongside the UCAS Department of Justice warrant for conspiracy, fraud and identity theft.

Court conditions make blackmail preferable to litigation and photographic evidence more useful than testimony; shareholders tolerate questionable profits unless their own reputations are threatened.

The Court's first Omega Order declared open season on QZE Corporation during the corporate crisis of the early 2040s.
organizations.source_adventure: SRM 01-09 For Whom the Bell Tolls

organizations.name: United Corporation Council
organizations.description: The United Corporation Council, founded in 2030, brings Seattle's major corporate interests together and has become a defining force in metroplex politics and economic policy. Its members include Samantha Villiers of Fuchi Industrial Electronics, Shigeru Aoyama of Shiawase, Siony Ecklund of the Independent Information Network, Brian W. Gates III of Microdeck Industries, Stanton Haukshorn of Haukshorn Chemicals, Sherman Huang of Renraku, Alberta Johnson of Dassurn Securities and Investments, Deborah Joshua of Gaeatronics, Karen King of Ares Macrotechnology, Thormond Lordstrung of the Lordstrung Retail Consortium International, William Loudon of Lone Star, Cassandra Paul of Pacific Rim Communications Unlimited, Salvador Ramirez of Aztechnology, Vera Sassinian of Ingersoll and Berkley Soy Products Unlimited, and Johnathan Takano of Mitsuhama. It is also called the United Corporate Council.

divisions.name: UCC Central Planning Committee
divisions.description:
The council's original sixteen-member Inner Circle directs central planning.

The committee supports the Council's advisory and planning role.
divisions.notes: William Vogel chairs the committee in 2050.

leadership.name: William Vogel
leadership.title: Chair
leadership.notes: Chairs the original Inner Circle.

organizations.notes:
The council keeps political-financing and hotline networks and a permanent observer in Bellevue, and its leverage over the metroplex government amounts to de facto governmental power.

[2060 – later developments] The council coordinates corporate advice, services and political pressure while its members remain at odds with one another.

organizations.name: Microdeck Industries
organizations.description: Microdeck Industries is a Bellevue software corporation owned by the Gates family, which built it from home and small-business products into military and aerospace work. It is known for affordable software and advanced research, including trials of infants in the Matrix, and it keeps a well-protected internal Matrix. Brian W. Gates III holds its seat on the United Corporation Council, and it is one of Seattle's major homegrown corporations.

divisions.name: Microdeck research department
divisions.description: Microdeck's research department tests advanced programming and Matrix-construction work.
divisions.notes: [2055] Jeff R. Gates leads the department and Deborah Gates is a chief programmer. Infant Matrix trials and family access are not publicly known.

organizations.notes: [2055 – later developments] Alex Gates's value to the corporation, and his unusual access, are growing.

organizations.name: California Free State
organizations.description: The California Free State declared its independence in 2037, after decades of upheaval -- the Anti-Indian Riots of 2009, the VITAS plague, the first elf and dwarf births in 2011 and the goblinization that followed -- hoping at last to master its own destiny. Whether it will is doubtful. Much of the Free State is under foreign occupation: Tir Tairngire holds the north, Aztlan holds San Diego and the south, and San Francisco is under a Japanese administration. The Sacramento government, under Governor Anthony Whitman -- who publicly refuses to rejoin the UCAS -- has little real authority outside its secure regions, and powerful corporations fill the gap. Its legal code resembles the UCAS's, but enforcement varies: Los Angeles, with high crime, little jail space and a libertine culture, sentences lightly; San Francisco's Japanese administration imposes maximum sentences and hands convicts to the central authorities; rural areas enforce strictly.

leadership.name: Anthony Whitman
leadership.title: Governor
leadership.notes: Current office is later history; public refusal to rejoin the UCAS.

leadership.name: Lester Brown
leadership.title: Director of Education and Morals
leadership.notes: Humanis and funding allegations remain disputed.

divisions.name: CFS Congress
divisions.description: The national legislature of the California Free State.
divisions.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

divisions.name: CFS Navy and Armed Forces
divisions.description:
The California Free State's military forces.

The Free State's armed forces conducted the 2046 Los Angeles campaign and remain a national military institution.
divisions.notes:
The tracking of the Novograd-San Diego incident is attributed current-frame evidence; no force totals, systems, or mechanics are retained.

The 2046 El Infierno action and reported February 2057 weakness are later history, not a claim about 2050 strength.

[2056 – later developments] California Free State air defenses maintain heightened vigilance along the San Diego border.
divisions.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

divisions.name: California Rangers
divisions.description: The California Rangers collect road tolls, maintain highways, and provide road patrol and enforcement across much of the Free State.
divisions.notes: [2057] Alternate name: California Road Rangers.

divisions.name: California Transportation Authority
divisions.description: California Transportation Authority is a surviving national transport branch associated with the Caldecott corridor.
divisions.notes: [2057] Shortened name: CalTrans. Historical committee work and corridor security remain notes; no telecom or Matrix endpoint is created.

divisions.name: State Water Board
divisions.description: The State Water Board is a pre-Secession bureaucracy responsible for the Free State's major water systems.
divisions.notes: [2057] Corporate and political capture in 2057, infrastructure security, sabotage, and allocation disputes are not publicly known.

leadership.name: Bradley Lynfield
leadership.title: Board Member
leadership.notes: [2057] Economic Coordinator

leadership.name: Dolph Hensen
leadership.title: Board Member
leadership.notes: [2057] Ares Arms-California leader

organizations.notes:
Governor Whitman's cabinet includes social policy director Forrest Moginie, economic coordinator Bradley Lynfield, director of education and morals Lester Brown (dogged by Humanis and funding allegations) and director of national defense Lee Shadix. Census data is unreliable, justice is often anti-metahuman, water is politics, and the Sacramento Matrix is unreliable; researchers enjoy unusual latitude. Accounts disagree on whether the legislature is a Congress or an Assembly. Tracking data from a Novograd-San Diego incident is circulating as evidence.

[2056 – later developments] The San Diego border with Aztlan sees heightened vigilance and air-defense activity.

[2057 – later developments] The Free State is fractured: hostile borders, weak central reach, regional governments, dependence on the corporations, and major transport systems in the north and south. Reunion with the UCAS is a live political question.
organizations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

organizations.name: Confederation of American States
organizations.description: The Confederation of American States is a union of ten southern states that seceded peacefully from the new UCAS in 2034, angered by its demands for revenue; Atlanta is its capital, and the states keep strong authority of their own. With the U.S. armies gone, Aztlan moved into southern Texas in 2035 and took San Antonio and Austin before it was stopped; Dallas-Fort Worth became the Texas capital, and when the other states would not send troops Texas left the CAS, found no help from the UCAS and rejoined in 2036. Bordering Aztlan, the NAN, the UCAS and the Caribbean League, the CAS has become the northern hemisphere's shipping hub -- 'all roads lead to CAS' -- and its high tariffs make it the black marketeer's promised land. It is also called the Confederated American States.

divisions.name: CAS Sector Management
divisions.description: The appointed sector government administers Denver territory, immigration, and law.
divisions.notes: [2055] Appears from 2055.

divisions.name: Department of Immigration and Naturalization
divisions.description: The department controls CAS immigration and sector work-visa processing.
divisions.notes: [2055] Appears from 2055.

divisions.name: CAS Office of Industrial Security
divisions.description: The named office handles industrial-security matters.
divisions.notes: [2055] Appears from 2055.

divisions.name: CAS Armed Forces
divisions.description: The national force supplies personnel history and equipment provenance to Denver security.
divisions.notes: [2055] Appears from 2055.

divisions.name: Texas Air National Guard
divisions.description: The Abilene-based Texas Air National Guard responds to incursions into the Aztlan border buffer.
divisions.notes: [2056] Appears from 2056.

organizations.notes: [2055 – later developments] The CAS has its own sector of Denver, with its own administration, security, immigration and law.
organizations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

organizations.name: Republic of Quebec
organizations.description: The Republic of Quebec is a French-speaking North American republic governed through a National Assembly and a president, with strict language laws and a growing number of corporate enterprise zones. It seceded from Canada under President Celinne DeGaulle; after the Great Ghost Dance of August 2017 made the Treaty of Denver inevitable, she invited the Maritime provinces to join, and only Labrador accepted. Quebec abstained from the Treaty of Denver in April 2018, confident in its ties with the region's Native Americans. Its politics are democratic but exclusionary. The government's own tourist line promises a peaceful land of friendly people; runners call it uptight, contradictory and more than a little crazy.

divisions.name: Quebec National Assembly
divisions.description: The elected national legislature of the Republic of Quebec.
divisions.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

divisions.name: Quebec Tourism Department
divisions.description: The national tourism office maintaining visitor information in Quebec City.
divisions.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

divisions.name: Quebec Defense Force
divisions.description: The republic's military force, headquartered at La Citadelle.
divisions.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

organizations.notes: Its 2050 politics are democratic but exclusionary. Tier is conservative catalog policy.
organizations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

organizations.name: United Canadian and American States
organizations.description: The United Canadian and American States is the union of what remained of the United States and Canada after the Treaty of Denver and the secessions that followed, governed from the Federal District of Columbia. The Federal District's administrations are arms of the national government.

divisions.name: FDC Commission
divisions.description: The commission governing the Federal District of Columbia.

divisions.description: The regional administration for Arlington within the FDC.

divisions.description: The regional administration for Fairfax within the FDC.

divisions.description: The appointed commissioner's office administers Denver-sector borders, visas, and law.

leadership.title: Sector Commissioner
leadership.notes: [2055] Commissioner since 2046.

divisions.name: UCAS Armed Forces
divisions.description:
The national force supplies personnel referrals to Lone Star Denver.

UCAS forces establish and enforce the Chicago quarantine by land, water, air, and astral approaches.

The UCAS Armed Forces joined Knight Errant in Operation Extermination and maintained personnel around Chicago after the corporate withdrawal.
divisions.notes: [2055] Army, Navy, Coast Guard, support, supply, Wall, and counterforce activity remains later history. No separate service, National Guard, temporary counterforce, or Marine division is created.

divisions.name: UCAS Department of Business
divisions.description: A high-level corruption lead points into this federal department.
divisions.notes: [2055] Department security allegedly suppresses investigation of the lead. The claim is not publicly known and no independent top-level organization is created.

divisions.name: UCAS Consular Operations
divisions.description: ConsOps is a classified direct-action and intelligence service that plans deniable insertion into Aztlan.
divisions.notes: [2056] Also known as ConsOps. Mission analysis, cover constraints, and file paths remain documentation rather than mechanics or Matrix objects.

divisions.name: Data Processing Branch
divisions.description: The branch analyzes alteration and insertion of Aztlan citizenship records for ConsOps missions.
divisions.notes: [2056] Operationally, this unit reports through UCAS Consular Operations.

divisions.name: Operations Department
divisions.description: The department decides whether legal-entry restrictions are acceptable for inserted ConsOps assets.
divisions.notes: [2056] Operationally, this unit reports through UCAS Consular Operations.

divisions.name: UCAS Army Special Assets Division
divisions.description: A UCAS Army unit that tracks, handles, and stores weapons of mass destruction.
divisions.notes: [2057] The unit is subordinate to the Army and handles nuclear, chemical, and biological threats. Lucius Harding's reports of interference and coercion remain disputed.

leadership.name: Lucius Harding
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] Until about May 2057. Brigadier general; deceased in the 2057 account.

divisions.name: UCAS Department of Justice
divisions.description: The UCAS Department of Justice administers federal records and Matrix-facing public services.
divisions.notes: [2061] Its private systems, investigative access, and chokepointed network are not publicly known. INS and the UCAS Marshals are deferred children, not flattened peers.

organizations.notes:
[2055 – later developments] In August the UCAS quarantines Chicago and builds the Containment Zone around it, covering the insect-spirit outbreak with a VITAS story; relay sabotage, shootings, supply drops, military enforcement and talk of a nuclear response follow.

[2057 – later developments] Reunion with the California Free State is on the political agenda, decades after the UCAS refused California aid in 2036.

[2058 – later developments] The State of the Union, the Scott Commission's investigation, new magical-security policy, continental diplomacy and the reopening of Chicago dominate national life.
organizations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

organizations.name: United Kingdom
organizations.description: The United Kingdom is a monarchy governed by Parliament -- a House of Commons and a House of Nobles in which elven and human aristocrats wield real power -- with a Green Party government whose governing force is the New Druidic Movement, and an increasingly powerful Lord Protector. Its Constitution Act of 2025 defined the powers of local and national government, the Lord Protector's Office and the Crown, but Britain has no Bill of Rights or Freedom of Information Act. It is a very secretive society in which centralized record-keeping on the population employs almost 200,000 people, through three great datanets packed with fearsome IC: the Central Criminal Register (the police computer, at Hendon in the London sprawl), the Public Health and Welfare Datanet (DNA typing, health and welfare, in Oxford) and the Chancellery Net. Security across the Channel has been so tight since the Euro-Wars that smuggling is dangerous, and it is almost impossible for a foreigner to get a permit for anything more dangerous than a hatpin. Beyond London lie the Wild Lands of Scotland and Cornwall, the Dragon Land and the Countess of Snowdon's Wales.
organizations.notes:
Runners call the Central Criminal Register a tough nut but not impossible -- a Red-5. Wild Britain holds unicorns around Castle Harlech and in the Cornish Wild Lands, wyverns in the Dragon Land, and toxic spirits in every toxic zone. Foreign runners usually have to buy their gear after they arrive, at a steep price.

[2052 – later developments] Britain's political circumstances change.

[2053 – later developments] SeaSource describes the U.K. under King George VIII, with a 540-seat Commons, a House of Nobles and a Green Party government.

organizations.name: Lord Protector's Office
organizations.description: The Lord Protector's Office, the former Ministry of the Interior, licenses magic, oversees magical education and registers practitioners; visitors who need licenses for magical operations or permits for restricted items such as cyberware must apply to it. Its myriad buildings sprawl along both sides of Chancellery Road in London's Temple District, the centre of official and judicial London, joined by overground walkways and underground passages and guarded, it seems, by the silver Stone Dragon of Temple Bar. Its power is growing, and some of the nobility -- the elven Duke of Oxford among them -- are openly hostile to it.

leadership.name: Lord Marchment
leadership.title: Lord Protector
leadership.notes: [2051] Lord Protector.

divisions.name: Licensing Bureau
divisions.description: The bureau licensing magical practitioners and magical trade.

divisions.name: Oversight Board
divisions.description: The board overseeing the Lord Protector's administrative system.

divisions.name: Information Directorate
divisions.description: The directorate handling institutional information and records.

divisions.name: Education Bureau
divisions.description: The bureau responsible for magical education oversight.

divisions.name: Administrative Bureau
divisions.description: The bureau administering the Lord Protector's national authority.

divisions.name: Templars / Field Officers
divisions.description: The field service enforcing the Lord Protector's authority.

divisions.name: Companies Directorate
divisions.description: The directorate overseeing licensed corporate magical activity.

organizations.notes:
The Lord Protector's authority overlaps with the Home Office, the War Office and the prime minister's in ways no one can quite pin down.

[2051 – later developments] Lord Marchment is Lord Protector, with Rupert Symonds and Sir Damian Green among his senior officials.

organizations.name: New Druidic Movement
organizations.description: The New Druidic Movement is the governing force behind Britain's ruling Green Party and has a firm grip on Parliament. It grew out of a jumble of sources -- Welsh nationalists of Plaid Cymru turned deep green, Freemasonry, Qabbalistic mysticism, arcane cults -- and the later split between Celtic-shamanic and English-hermetic druids dates from those days. Today it is a British movement, mostly English, with the Celtic druids standing outside it. It recruits by invitation only: people of rank, professional skill, influence or wealth are invited into the Druidic Lodges found in almost every town of any size, with three orders -- initiate, member and adept -- and rituals for each, much like the Freemasons, while power radiates outward from the central circles.

divisions.name: Inner Circles
divisions.description: The Movement's senior circles and principal ritual leadership.

divisions.name: Hidden Circles
divisions.description: Secretive circles operating within the wider Movement.

organizations.notes: Some of the nobility, the Duke of Oxford among them, are deeply suspicious of the Druidic Hidden Circles.

organizations.name: Special Air Services
organizations.description: The SAS -- the Special Air Services -- is Britain's particularly sinister secret police. Its original anti-terrorist brief was merged with the old MI5 anti-subversion role to form a security force whose accountability -- to the Home Office, the Lord Protector, the Chiefs of Staff or the prime minister -- is almost impossible to pin down. The SAS shun magical firepower and detection but carry technology of amazing ingenuity. Runners call them state terrorists, and anyone in his right mind keeps well away; the trouble is knowing whom they are after, and if it is you, you find out when the bullet goes through the back of your skull.
organizations.notes: SAS is published records abbreviation. Attributed tactics are not publicly known, not public baseline fact.

organizations.name: Amalgamated Technologies and Telecommunications
organizations.description: Amalgamated Technologies and Telecommunications (ATT) is a London-based information-technology corporation under Sir Arthur Gordon: telecommunications and allied systems, newsnet services, data archives, electronics and industrial robotics. Saeder-Krupp owns 57 percent of it; British, Japanese and North American investors own the rest. It deals in information as much as technology and has a happy knack for acquiring data archives -- demographic and time-series data that underpin predictions -- just before they become important for unexpected reasons. Its people are often aristocrats, and it works above all through contacts and information.
organizations.notes: How ATT manages its almost precognitive investing is far from clear.

organizations.name: British Industrial PLC
organizations.description: British Industrial PLC is a sprawl in itself, headquartered in the Angel Towers Arcology in London under Clive Woolford. British Electrical, under Sir Alan Fitzsimmons, makes and imports consumer appliances of every kind; British Food Products, under Walter Crowther, owns vast factory farms and chemical plants and chains of fast-food outlets, including Regal Burgers, the home-grown and terminally loathsome alternative to the Stuffer Shack. The elven Duke of Oxford, Justin Carmichael, holds a major stake.

divisions.name: British Electrical
divisions.description: British Industrial's electrical subsidiary.

divisions.name: British Food Products
divisions.description: British Industrial's food-products subsidiary.

organizations.notes: British Industrial and BI are shortened name, not separate rows.

organizations.name: Hildebrandt-Kleinfort-Bernal
organizations.description: Hildebrandt-Kleinfort-Bernal (HKB) is an aggressive, dynamic London financial and data-services group, founded in 2012, that has had a stranglehold on British financial services since Paul Bernal's daring takeover of Lloyds in 2020. Paul Bernal Jr. is president and CEO. HKB Financial Services, under Anthony Hildebrandt, handles insurance and commodity brokering and investment management; HKB Data Services, under Meredith McAlpine, handles data management and software security.

divisions.name: HKB Financial Services
divisions.description: The group's financial-services arm.

divisions.name: HKB Data Services
divisions.description: The group's data-services arm.

divisions.name: Risk Protection Factors Inc.
divisions.description: A risk-protection subsidiary within HKB Data Services.

organizations.notes: HKB is reputed to have some distinctly original ideas about stimulating demand in the market. The name is also given as Hildebrandt-Kleinwort-Bernal.

organizations.name: London Assembly
organizations.description: The London Assembly is five assemblymen -- one from Inner London and one from each of the four outer districts -- elected, in theory, one person one vote, with one seat up each year, currently led by Agatha Halper. In principle it is the prime body for liaising with central government through the Lord Protector's Office and the Home Office, and ministers regularly attend its meetings with civil servants. The metropolitan councils beneath it handle transport planning and building permission.

divisions.name: London Docklands Development Consortium
divisions.description: The consortium directing redevelopment on the Isle of Dogs and at Canary Wharf.

organizations.notes: Runners call the meetings media stunts: the Assembly has no real influence, the government pretends to listen and then finds fifty reasons why nothing can be done just now. When a metropolitan council refuses a corporation's planning request, the corporation appeals to the Ministries of Transport and the Environment, which usually overrule it.

organizations.name: The Tongs
organizations.description: The Tongs are the established Chinese criminal power in London's Soho and Chinatown, running protection, drugs and the traditional rackets. The yakuza have so far avoided competing with them or the Asian families, and the Mafia has never had a significant presence in Britain.
organizations.notes: Also known as the London Tongs. The row is not silently merged with an unrelated Triad organization.

organizations.name: Trans-Polar Aleut Nation
organizations.description: The Trans-Polar Aleut Nation is the far northern Native American nation, governed from Inuvik through community councils, a national chief and an executive committee. Inuit communities are the majority, while Aleut communities hold much of the political and commercial influence, and large stretches of the country see little effective government at all. Non-natives are not welcome outside the enclaves of the companies that employ them, and no 'pinkskin tribes' live there. Many people have taken up a back-to-the-land life by choice, and even those who have not have readopted the old adornments: boys' lower lips pierced at puberty, women's chins tattooed. Energy is Inuvik's great problem: a planned fusion plant on Cape Dalhousie was scrapped in 2039 after violent objections, a solar array works only half the year, and a proposed hydro dam died in 2043, so the city buys most of its power from the Athabaskan Council over superconducting lines. The nation bans urban brawl.

divisions.name: Aleut
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Trans-Polar Aleut Nation.

divisions.name: Inuit
divisions.description: A named constituent tribal community of the Trans-Polar Aleut Nation.

divisions.name: Trans-Polar Aleut Peace Force
divisions.description: The nation's paramilitary police service, based around Inuvik and trained alongside other national forces.

divisions.name: Executive Committee
divisions.description: The executive body serving the nation's community-council government.

organizations.notes:
Ininook and T'singlik belong to the nation's founding history rather than its current leadership. Marriage customs remain traditional: arranged marriages, a groom living in the bride's household for a year, and polygamous marriages. A native man may nearly get away with marrying a non-native woman if he has a native wife as well; a native woman who even considers a non-native man is ostracized.

Anglos who drink outside their company enclave learn the hard way: a Bathotech worker who tried The Ice Blink in Inuvik was ignored, then jumped by drunk young toughs.

organizations.name: Zurich-Orbital Gemeinschaft Bank
organizations.description: The Zurich-Orbital Gemeinschaft Bank is the central financial institution of the major extraterritorial corporations. It was founded in 2033, when Global Financial Services was moved to the Zurich-Orbital station and renamed. Its charter restricts any transfer of ownership and places it under the supervision of the Corporate Court, and it is independent of the habitat it sits in. Its directors are drawn from the megacorporations and live everywhere from London and New York to Kyoto, Denver and the station itself.

leadership.name: Derek Abernathie
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] Saeder-Krupp; resident in London.

leadership.name: Choy-Mu Laubenstein
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] Shiawase; resident aboard Zurich-Orbital.

leadership.name: William Marcus
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] Ares; resident in New York.

leadership.name: Sakehisa Noro
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] Yamatetsu; resident in Kyoto.

leadership.name: Kamako Otaku
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] Yamatetsu; resident aboard Zurich-Orbital.

leadership.name: Jeanne-Marie Roulleau
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] Saeder-Krupp; resident aboard Zurich-Orbital.

leadership.name: Xavier Talbot
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] Ares; resident in Seattle.

leadership.name: Samuel Wirth
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] Fuchi; resident in Berlin.

leadership.name: Atsutada Yogo
leadership.title: Director
leadership.notes: [2054] MCT; resident in Denver, Pueblo Sector.

organizations.notes:
[2055 – later developments] The bank monitors the multi-corporate portfolio used to benchmark the nuyen.

[2061 – later developments] The bank is the Corporate Court's data-only central bank and the exchange authority for corporate scrip.

organizations.name: Emerald Telecommunications Inc.
organizations.description: Emerald Telecommunications Inc. (ETI) is the national telecommunications operator that runs and maintains Tir Tairngire's regional grid and local grids. It guarantees an Orange-5 security standard throughout the Tir's corner of the network, and claims it uses no black IC and little gray.
organizations.notes: Orange-5 is the floor, not the ceiling: the switching nodes and billing routines are glaciers, all IC and much of it black. Hidden inside the RTG is a 'grid within a grid' reserved for government and military traffic, running on the same hardware with much tougher software -- Red-7 at least.

organizations.name: Church of Ireland
organizations.description: The Church of Ireland is the established church of Tir na nOg under the Establishment Acts of 2036 and 2049, and 67 percent of non-elven citizens follow it. Once a small splinter church, it grew as Catholic bishops who rejected the papacy's stance on metahuman children joined it and as the Catholic Church collapsed in scandal.
organizations.notes: Liam O'Connor let the Church of Ireland grow among non-elven citizens deliberately, to keep Catholicism from regaining its hold on people.

organizations.name: Catholic Church
organizations.description: The Roman Catholic Church has lost ground across Europe and the Americas since the Awakening. In Ireland its early condemnation of metahuman infants cost it the people's loyalty, and a wave of scandals brought it down; the Church of Ireland is now the Tir's established church, though rural folk still listen to the parish priest first and revere the monastic orders, above all the reconciling Sylvestrines. In Germany the diocese of Muenster broke from Rome in April 2014 to found the German Catholic Church, while Roman Catholicism remains the larger faith. In Aztlan the church, once a great landholder, was suppressed by the state in 2041 and survives underground.

divisions.name: Order of Saint Sylvester
divisions.description: The reconciliation order works in rural communities and includes magical adepts.
divisions.notes: Sylvestrines is an alternate name.

divisions.name: Aztlan underground Catholic Church
divisions.description: The underground branch has maintained clergy, congregations, and regional spiritual service since the 2041 suppression.
divisions.notes: This is a descriptive source identity, not a printed legal name. Covert cells, PAN support, subversion, weapons rumors, and the Portobelo cabal is not publicly known.

divisions.name: New Society of Jesus
divisions.description: The New Society of Jesus is a rumored church intelligence and paramilitary order serving threatened congregations.
divisions.notes: Also known as New Jesuits. Vatican headquarters, deckers, undercover agents, magic, arms purchases, and rebel liaison is reported but unconfirmed and sometimes contradictory.

organizations.notes:
Liam O'Connor saw Catholicism as the greatest threat to the elven state he meant to found, and between 2018 and 2025 engineered sexual scandals that ruined the bishops of Cork, Galway, Dublin and Derry and dozens of priests. Many Sylvestrines are minor magical adepts; were they to oppose the Danaan elves openly, they would find themselves mired in scandal too.

In Aztlan, the underground church is said to shelter covert cells, draw support from the PAN, and include the rumored New Society of Jesus, a church intelligence and paramilitary order; accounts of its weapons and methods are unconfirmed and sometimes contradictory.

organizations.name: Dublin City Corporation
organizations.description: The Dublin City Corporation is Dublin's civic government -- the city council under the Worshipful Graeme Patrick Finnegan, Mayor of Dublin, and committees for transport, culture and other services that report both to the council and to the relevant government department.
organizations.notes: Finnegan spent his formative years as a lackey of the Interior Ministry and is an acolyte of its minister, O'Molloy, which explains a good deal about the Corporation's policies. In practice the committees owe their allegiance to the government departments.

organizations.name: Eireann-Tir Publishers
organizations.description: Eireann-Tir Publishers (ETP), headquartered in Limerick under President and CEO Joseph P. MacNamara, handles all the business of education and culture in the Tir: licensing and marketing summer schools and festivals; licensing and producing books, VR-CDs, chips and skillsofts; and selling sculpture, music and literature. Instead of formal divisions it uses expert teams for each product, and its reach gives it broad influence on Tir business and cultural life.

divisions.name: McCarthy Group
divisions.description: The Killarney group produces artistic and cultural material.

organizations.notes: The MacNamaras balance the interests of two Danaan-mor families through ETP: the O'Briens dominate scholastic software, the McCarthys the poetic, literary and historical side. Foreign media companies can publish in the Tir only through ETP licensing, which lets the government keep out what it dislikes.

organizations.name: University of Galway
organizations.description: The University of Galway, in the Tir's province of learning, is home to biomedical research laboratories that work closely with the Integrative Biotechnics Division of Steward's Hospital in Tullamore on neuromuscular boosting; together they originated and patented the boosted-reflex system used by TRC officers. Its scholars include the prodigy Padraic Byrne, Professor of Comparative Literature.
organizations.notes: The labs sell less advanced versions of the TRC reflex system to a handful of other security organizations at unbelievable prices; though not legally a corporation, they act like one. Elven scholars at Galway 'discovered' a sixth verse of the Book of Invasions in 2038 that appears in no traditional version -- convenient for the Danaan mythos.

organizations.name: Danaan Families
organizations.description: The Danaan Families are the twenty-two families that produced extraordinary numbers of elven children during the Awakening, for reasons no one has explained, and that effectively rule Tir na nOg behind its public government. Most are Irish, though Norman bloodlines such as the Burkes, Fitzgeralds and Butlers are among them, and eight -- the Danaan-mor, including the O'Tooles, O'Briens, O'Neills, O'Connors, Byrnes, Roches and MacNamaras -- have dominated Ireland for centuries. They rule through the Council of Stewards and the Seelie Court and dominate the Senate, business and every aspect of Tir life.

divisions.name: Council of Stewards
divisions.description: The family council directs policy, influences the Senate, and selects a High Steward.

divisions.name: Coirt Danaan
divisions.description: The internal Brehon court hears judgments and appeals without public records.
divisions.notes: Cuirt Danaan is preserved as a alternate spelling variant.

leadership.name: Martin MacNamara
leadership.title: Brehon
leadership.notes: [2054] Life-appointed presiding official in the documented period.

organizations.notes:
The Cuirt Danaan, the families' internal court, adjudicates disputes within the Council of Stewards, keeps no records and is unknown to the public. The movement began with two TRC cells -- Liam O'Connor's in Derry and Seamus O'Kennedy's in Dublin -- which engineered the scandals of 2015-2034 against every other power bloc, leading to the bloodless coup of 2034. O'Connor established the Court of Stewards, married Brane Deigh, became High Steward in 2042 and vanished in May 2043 to walk his final Path; Brane then proclaimed herself Queen of the Seelie Court.

Some who have walked the Paths fear the families will one day make the Tir a wholly elven nation, driving out or degrading every other race.

organizations.name: AG Chemie
organizations.description: AG Chemie Europa, headquartered in Frankfurt-Hoechst under president and CEO Meinhard G. Beilstein, grew from a merger of the twentieth century's biggest German chemical corporations. It makes paints, plastics, pharmaceuticals, pesticides, biotechnical replacement parts and poison gas, much of it through specialized subsidiaries hidden behind such a maze of shareholdings and holding companies that the BIS keeps a special team just to watch it. Its publicly held subsidiary General Genetics Worldwide researches human genetics and pharmaceuticals, and the corporation holds stakes in the BuMoNa health service, Besser Leben, Darmstadt Bioptics, Magdeburg Compound Materials and several Swiss pharmaceutical firms. It owns most of Frankfurt in one form or another. Its factories cover dozens of square kilometers of Leverkusen, whose largely ork population works, lives, shops and is buried under the company's name, and it has had Ludwigshafen and Mannheim declared corporate enclaves.

divisions.name: General Genetics Worldwide
divisions.description: The wholly owned public subsidiary conducts genetics research and manages a documented legal conflict.

organizations.notes:
General Genetics conducts research that is technically prohibited in the German Alliance, and the confederate government in Hannover accepts its tax ecus anyway. Shadowtalk notes that the research subjects it hires for field testing in Haiti and the Dominican Republic are never seen again, and asks what the company tests on now that it claims to have stopped animal testing.

The noisy public rivalry with Britain's Zeta-ImpChem is an orchestrated facade: Zeta-ImpChem holds a majority of shares in one of AG Chemie's three core companies, the two long ago divided the chemical industry between them, and their industrial espionage has the spirit of a sporting contest.

Only people cleared by AG Chemie may work in Ludwigshafen and Mannheim; unwelcome individuals are deported or disappear, and damage-control teams hunt nosy reporters and loose-lipped employees almost every week while the company commits enormous ecological crimes in the name of prosperity. Its pollution draws Green War and FROMATES to Leverkusen, and runners say FROMATES found skeletons in the corporate cupboards -- literally -- and blackmailed the company into building new filters. Security is top-drawer at every level, with skilled combat mages and mercenaries.

[2059 – later developments] AG Chemie Europa operates North Atlantic and Norwegian Sea oil fields and rigs, competing there with Zeta-ImpChem and Saeder-Krupp.

organizations.name: Allied German States
organizations.description: The Allied German States is a loose confederation of German Lander bound by close cultural and economic ties, governed from the confederate capital of Hannover. Its borders and constitution were set by the congressional convention of 2045, which also admitted associate members: the Troll Kingdom of the Black Forest, the dwarf Grand Duchy of Westrhine-Luxemburg, the elven Duchy of Pomorya, the small states of the Upper Palatinate Forest, the Saar Special Legislative Zone and the Free City of Berlin. The Alliance covers some 329,000 square kilometers from the North Sea to the Alps and uses three currencies: the ecu and the nuyen for business and the deutsche mark in private life. Emergency numbers are 111 for police, 444 for fire and 447 for an ambulance; government information is (09) 1122.

divisions.name: ALI traffic guidance system
divisions.description: The national system coordinates automated road traffic guidance.

divisions.name: ALIOPs
divisions.description: Dedicated operators supervise ALI and road traffic continuously.

divisions.name: BND
divisions.description: The foreign intelligence service gathers and distributes intelligence.

divisions.name: Bundesamt fuer Innere Sicherheit / BIS
divisions.description: The domestic security office handles counterespionage and internal threats.

divisions.name: Bundesbahn
divisions.description: The federal rail organization operates conventional national passenger and freight service.

divisions.name: Bundesgrenzschutz / BGS
divisions.description: The federal border guard enforces border and constitutional security.

divisions.name: Bundeskriminalamt / BKA
divisions.description: The federal criminal office coordinates major investigations.

divisions.name: Bundesrat
divisions.description: The Land chamber exercises strong constitutional authority.

divisions.name: Bundestag
divisions.description: The elected federal parliament forms cabinets and passes confederate law.

divisions.name: Bundeswehr
divisions.description: The national armed forces provide collective defense and constitutional enforcement.

divisions.name: Confederate Patent Court
divisions.description: The court adjudicates technological and magical ownership using federal patent archives.

divisions.name: Confederate government
divisions.description: The cabinet administers foreign policy, defense, infrastructure, welfare, and federal law.

divisions.name: Constitutional Court / First Senate
divisions.description: The Karlsruhe court reviews constitutional disputes.

divisions.name: Foreign Ministry
divisions.description: The ministry conducts federal foreign affairs.

divisions.name: German Patent Office
divisions.description: The office catalogs technological and magical developments for ownership rulings.

divisions.name: Grenzschutzgruppen / GSG
divisions.description: Specialized border-protection groups answer high-risk federal incidents.

divisions.name: Karlsruhe garrison
divisions.description: The federal garrison controls military installations around Karlsruhe.

divisions.name: Umweltbundesamt
divisions.description: The federal environmental office administers national environmental work.

organizations.notes: A corruption scandal in 2050 and 2051 forced a government reform; the cleansed Hannover government normalized relations with Russia, signed a cultural and economic treaty with its former enemy and made the first attempts at detente with the Alliance for Allah.

organizations.name: Bavaria
organizations.description: The Bavarian Free State, governed from Freising by State President Anton Hofmayr of the Bavarian People's Party, is the hard-right heart of southern Germany. It led the secession movement of the 2030s, joined Baden-Wuerttemberg in the short-lived Union of Central European Countries, and has since lost three districts to Franconia and Swabia to Wuerttemberg over its repressive, anti-metahuman policies. Hofmayr's 'Bavaria First!' government runs a rubber-stamp parliament, preaches against corporate power and has only lately eased its restrictions: dwarfs, orks and trolls are grudgingly accepted, provided they speak broad Bavarian. The Munich sprawl, officially the Isar Metro Area, remains far more open and liberal than the rest of the state, with a liberal city government that defends the voting rights of all residents.

divisions.name: Bavarian state parliament
divisions.description: The Freising chamber represents the Bavarian state.

divisions.name: Bavarian state police
divisions.description: The force guards Freising government districts and enforces pass controls.

divisions.name: Bavarian state president's office
divisions.description: The Freising office and residence support the state presidency.

divisions.name: Presidential Guards
divisions.description: The unit protects the state president and Freising government area.

organizations.notes:
Hofmayr succeeded the assassinated Alfons Hunggarten; he won 68 percent of the last direct vote -- counting only people resident in Bavaria since ten years before the Euro-Wars -- and his eight-year term ends next summer. A decker claims to have seen bank records showing two million ecus a year paid into his account, and shadowtalk says his anti-corporate stance amounts to a protection racket that leaves room for deniable runners -- who die slowly if caught. Japanese corporations fare worst in Bavarian courts.

Munich's own count of five million residents against the state's 2.2 million official citizens shows how many refugees, mostly from the Balkans, live there without papers. Private 'Black Sheriffs' police the districts the state police neglect, keeping Munich's hospitals busy. Magical bombs killed 120 people at the Oktoberfest four years ago, and the Theresienwiese is now the most heavily guarded open ground in the world.

organizations.name: Brandenburg
organizations.description: Brandenburg, a civil democracy named for its capital, surrounds the Free City of Berlin and pays for the neighbor. It lost its former capital of Potsdam to Berlin, has almost no industry because the metroplex has drawn it all in, and has begun a modest recovery by turning the Havel and Spree country into a resort. The European Socialist Party governs. The 2045 convention that set the Lander borders gave Brandenburg the Spreewald, and relations with Saxony have been tense ever since.
organizations.notes: The Spreewald is Sorbic country, restored by its natives to its old green splendor; the ritual site outside Ljubenow (Luebbenau) draws witches and sightseers from Saxony, Brandenburg and Berlin at festival time, and legend makes the wetland the realm of the Snake King, whose silver crown brings luck and riches.

organizations.name: BuMoNa
organizations.description: BuMoNa (Bund fuer Mobilen Notfall-Arzteinsatz) is the only nationwide emergency medical service open to visitors in the German Alliance, loosely connected to DocWagon and Careline. Like DocWagon, it promises a unit within 15 minutes of a call -- even in dangerous or polluted areas, though not in war or revolution -- with one free resuscitation included. Coverage costs EC 30,000 a year and includes tissue cloning for replacement organs; a special contract for magical healing in a BuMoNa clinic costs EC 50,000. Visitors receive an emergency monitor through their embassy, and the service can be reached at 909.
organizations.notes: AG Chemie Europa owns a stake in BuMoNa. Runners report that BuMoNa does not care about a patient's SIN: its contract covers basic health care as well as emergency service, and it subsidizes cyberware.

organizations.name: Deutsche Medien und Kommunikations AG
