organizations.description: Deutsche Medien und Kommunikations AG (DeMeKo), formed from the merger of Germany's three largest media corporations, is one of the world's largest media companies. From its Hamburg headquarters under President and CEO Friedrich Xaver Mooshuber ('Fritz X') it owns some 1,200 newspapers, magazines, news and MatrixMail services, radio, video and trideo stations, wholly or partly owning 40 percent of all media in the German Alliance: it sells, leases, produces and censors anything connected with the media, from daily papers to hardcore simsense to party leaflets. Its Berlin operation, run by CEO Wolfgang Osterwald from a landmark building that resembles an antiquated computer chip on forty giant columns, publishes the city-zine Timeout and the hourly tabloid SuperBild.
organizations.notes: DeMeKo believes in growth by any means; its hire-and-fire politics reach everyone from data-entry wage slaves to whole printing companies. It stays out of the direct struggle for political power, protecting its interests by shaping public discourse instead. Security is light -- yesterday's news is worthless -- except around simsense factories in the days before a hot release; bootleg copies still reach the black market through freelancers who crack the corporate databanks. DeMeKo also partly finances Deutsche Telekom, which is why deckers expect no deregulation of the German Matrix.

organizations.name: Deutsche Telekom
organizations.description: Deutsche Telekom holds the telecommunications monopoly in the German Alliance and owns the German Matrix, a system of three separate virtual universes: the basegrid, the Simlink and the ALI traffic-guidance system. Any machine brought into the country must meet Telekom and TUeV requirements that lag the state of the art by about five years, which is why roughly half the cyberware in use in Germany is technically illegal. The grid has exceeded its built-in capacity for years, whole LTG areas break down regularly, and Telekom promises a tenfold expansion.
organizations.notes: Deckers advise staying out of the grid between 06:00 and 22:00 unless you enjoy rebooting every few minutes. As long as the systems stay consolidated nothing will change, and DeMeKo's stake in Telekom keeps deregulation off the table.

organizations.name: Deutsche Treuhandanstalt
organizations.description: The Deutsche Treuhandanstalt Finanztransaktions- und Consulting OAG, headquartered in Duesseldorf under President and CEO Alfons Reurath, handles every transaction in the German Alliance involving industrial real estate, buildings and investment goods. Created to administer and sell off the state-owned companies of the former East Germany, it found its niche after the Cattenom disaster, VITAS, the North Sea floods and the Euro-Wars: under the agreement that founded the Alliance, companies must buy their building grounds from the Treuhand and sell them back if they fail or close the facility. The Alliance owns 41 percent of the shares, Land governments 14 percent and the Frankfurter Bankenverein 22 percent.
organizations.notes: The megacorporations are exempt from the Treuhand rule under Section 19a of the Passau Treaty. The Treuhand keeps its distance from standard transactions and acts mainly as a supervisory body.

organizations.name: Duchy of Pomorya
organizations.description: The Duchy of Pomorya is a small, semi-autonomous Baltic state where Germany's elves are working to revitalize the Baltic Sea. Ruled from Sassnitz by Duke Jaromar Greif, it holds the islands of Ruegen, Usedom and Wollin and part of former West Pomerania; elves make up more than 40 percent of its 180,000 people, and their thrifty way of life keeps the duchy self-reliant in energy and food. Pomorya values nature magic over the hermetic tradition, and most of its people follow a revived local nature religion whose high priests are talented shamans; the living-wood temple of Svantevit at Kap Arkona is its heart. Its counties are ruled by counts, among them Kasimir Tyminski of Greifswald.

divisions.name: Cult of Svantevit
divisions.description: The Pomoryan religious body maintains the Kap Arkona temple tradition.

divisions.name: Pomoryan governing council
divisions.description: The council joins the duke and territorial counts in national government.

organizations.notes: Most of Pomorya serves Svantevit, an incarnation of the Dragonslayer whose enemies are now the toxic spirits of the poisoned Baltic. Duke Jaromar leads a monthly ritual to the Great Mother near the Jaromarsburg temple. Count Tyminski, a Polish hermetic mage, founded a magic department at Greifswald University and recovered manuscripts carried off to Russia in the Euro-Wars, giving it one of Europe's best hermetic libraries -- and constant trouble with the manuscripts' original owners.

organizations.name: Duchy of Saxony
organizations.description: The Duchy of Saxony, which includes the southern part of old Saxony-Anhalt, is the only non-metahuman monarchy on German soil. After the heavy and chemical industry around Dresden and Leipzig-Halle, it is best known as a top-flight training ground for soldiers and security agents. The nationalist DNP dominates a puppet parliament in Dresden, and the confederate government repeatedly calls the duchy to task for human-rights violations and expansionist designs on its neighbors -- especially Brandenburg, which was given the Spreewald in 2045.
organizations.notes: A coup seems imminent: the population appears unwilling to endure continued political repression with so little economic security.

organizations.name: Franconia
organizations.description: Franconia, a civil democracy built around the Nuremberg-Fuerth-Erlangen metroplex, seceded from Bavaria with Wuerttemberg's help after the Union of Central European Countries broke up, and was later joined by southern Hesse. Its economy proved weak once Stuttgart stopped sending money, so Prime Minister Edith Weidner -- a former Fuchi Germany spokesperson with almost no political experience -- created FrankenKultour AG with Japanese corporations, effectively a corporate government for tourism. FrankenKultour has renovated Rothenburg, Nuremberg and Wuerzburg, runs medieval-flavored hotel chains and the mock-medieval Charlemagne Center, and has made Nuremberg southern Germany's premier convention city. About two-thirds of its tourists are Japanese.

divisions.name: Nuremberg municipal government
divisions.description: The municipal administration governs the Franconian capital.

organizations.notes: Franconian pride runs to shunning anything Bavarian. The tourism strategy has made the Land dependent on imported technology, and a few voices protest the lack of research. Nuremberg Castle is a convention center with a long waiting list, the February toy fair shows the megacorporations' newest toys (last year a slowed-down Fuchi deck for children), and shadowtalk says Duesseldorf is still the better yakuza playground. Bayreuth's festival director reportedly killed himself when told to stage Siegfried with the hero as a decker persona.

organizations.name: Frankfurter Bankenverein
organizations.description: The Frankfurter Bankenverein, headquartered in Frankfurt under President and CEO Monika Stieler-Waffenschmidt, is a club of 36 private German banks and several foreign institutions. It presents itself as a distinguished, consumer-friendly service but is one of Germany's most expansionist megacorporations: it lends to companies and administers their shareholdings, but prefers to buy holdings, real estate and bonds in its own name, and 27 nations owe it billions. It owns so many companies that another crash like 2029 would barely touch it, and it holds 22 percent of the Deutsche Treuhandanstalt.
organizations.notes: Because its business is almost entirely electronic, its Matrix security is staggering, down to the smallest branch office. The few pieces of Frankfurt that AG Chemie does not own belong to the Bankenverein.

organizations.name: Free City of Berlin
organizations.description: The Free City of Berlin is the only real anarchist state in the world. Walled off and besieged in the chaos of the early century, it is now contested by countless rival groups -- anarcho-syndicalists, neo-anarchists, mobsters and anyone else who wants a hand in the so-called government -- and works through unstable councils, policlubs, neighborhood services and corporate enclaves negotiated with the megacorporations. Chaotic inside and paralyzed in its dealings with the outside world, Berlin still draws people with its crazy vitality, and a private citizen can carry almost any weapon there without attracting attention. It is an associate member of the German Alliance.
organizations.notes: The corporate enclaves do not give the corporations control of the city.

organizations.name: Free City of Hamburg
organizations.description: The Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg is a city-state whose politics are a complex web of civil democracy, corporate ruthlessness and anarchy. Large parts of the city remain under flood water, giving smugglers and hover-pirates countless hideouts, and it is the main seat of the Klabauterbund, the anarchist, pro-ecology policlub widely blamed for piracy on the North Sea. DeMeKo, the German media giant, keeps its headquarters here.
organizations.notes: [2059 – later developments] Hamburg remains an independent city-state and a major North Sea port with significant smuggling and anarchist activity.

organizations.name: Grand Duchy of Westrhine-Luxemburg
organizations.description: The Grand Duchy of Westrhine-Luxemburg is a dwarf-led Land covering the Hunsrueck and Eifel hill country and the lowlands around Aachen; most of Germany's dwarfs have moved here, where they make up about 40 percent of a sparse population. The Eifel has been a wasteland of cold lava and ash since the eruptions of 2042, but both hill regions remain favorite haunts of magicians. The state is nominally a constitutional monarchy under Grand Duke Adolphe III, yet citizens decide many policies by electronic vote, and the USPD, anarchist groups and mystical lodges all carry weight. Its capital sits not in the spa town of Bad Neuenahr but in the old federal government's nuclear fallout shelter nearby.

leadership.name: Adolphe III
leadership.title: Head of State
leadership.notes: [2054] Ruler since 2043.

divisions.name: Westrhine-Luxemburg Landtag
divisions.description: The elected chamber shares government with the grand duke.

organizations.notes: As an example of how Westrhine-Luxemburg's politics really work, a hung parliament recently let Karl Hammer of the RVP become prime minister over loud objections from several sides. Unlike the Troll Kingdom, the Grand Duchy has friends among the other Lander.

organizations.name: Greater Frankfurt
organizations.description: Greater Frankfurt is the second-largest metroplex in the German Alliance, stretching from Wiesbaden and Mainz to Hanau and Aschaffenburg and south to Mannheim and Ludwigshafen. Frankfurt, the city of money, essentially belongs to the Frankfurter Bankenverein, whose members keep glass-and-chrome towers in the guarded 'Forbidden City'; the south of the sprawl, nicknamed the AGChem Sprawl, belongs to AG Chemie, and nearly a third of the area is chemical plants, laboratories and company housing. It is Germany's center of biotechnology and neurochemical research, and Heidelberg is one of Europe's premier centers of hermetic magic. More than 1,500 flights leave Frankfurt Airport every day.
organizations.notes: Rumor has the LDFP-dominated government asking AG Chemie headquarters in Frankfurt-Hoechst to approve every decision it makes. Because the banks control many businesses usually run by organized crime, the underworld is weaker here than in other sprawls: the old Mafia spends its time defending its turf against the yakuza, and street gangs such as the B-52s of southern Darmstadt and the Spessart Spiders flourish. Airport security is extremely tight.

organizations.name: Karlsruhe Special Legislative Zone
organizations.description: The Karlsruhe Special Legislative Zone is ruled directly from Hannover by the confederate government and administered by the local army commander, Michael Karaoglu. After earthquakes devastated Karlsruhe in 2043 and Baden-Wuerttemberg wrote off the Upper Rhine, the radical Hedwig Gabler of the Greater Badensian Crusade was elected Lord Mayoress on a platform of Badensian nationalism, religious fanaticism and hatred of metahumans, and hired mercenaries to make war on the Troll Kingdom of the Black Forest. In April 2049 the Bundeswehr took the city in seven hours. Karlsruhe is now Germany's -- perhaps Europe's -- largest garrison, with close to 30,000 soldiers in the barracks at Philippsburg, Forchheim and Ettlingen, and it still houses the constitutional court.
organizations.notes: Most of Gabler's mercenaries fled or changed sides at the first sight of confederate troops, and she and her deputies were captured.

organizations.name: Marienbad Council
organizations.description: The Marienbad Council joins the small metahuman-heavy states of the Bavarian Forest, the Bohemian Forest and the Erzgebirge -- currently 8 kingdoms, 4 grand duchies, 4 counties, 7 baronies, 3 republics, 3 city-states and a revolutionary people's republic -- under little more than an amorphous advisory body. It is a client state of both the Czech Republic and the German Alliance, which represent it abroad. A ferocious desire for independence is the only thing that unites its roughly 80,000 people; border wars, coups and raids are constant, the more polluted areas are thick with toxic spirits, and its position on the borders of Thuringia, Franconia and Bohemia makes it the center for smuggling magical goods into Germany. A private citizen can carry almost any weapon there.

divisions.name: Marienbad Bureau of Vital Statistics
divisions.description: The bureau administers citizenship and marriage records.

organizations.notes: Prague and Hannover mostly make sure the barons and petty kings cannot get missiles, fighter planes or cybertech. The 25 rulers -- 9 human, 8 troll, 5 ork, 2 dwarf and 1 elf -- feud over money, territory and resources rather than race, which makes the Council one of the most racially tolerant places in Europe. Step off a forest track on the wrong side and you may land in a border war worse than any Ruhr gang war.

organizations.name: North German Federation
organizations.description: The North German Federation was formed during the reconstruction by uniting Schleswig-Holstein, Lower Saxony, Mecklenburg-West Pomerania, Bremen and northern Saxony-Anhalt, and it took the brunt of the often violent changes of the past fifty years. Heavy industry, agribusiness and mid-sized high-technology firms settled here while telecommunications and computing went south, and today there is almost no industry outside its major cities, including the confederate capital of Hannover. Japanese and German-Japanese corporations dominate its economy. A liberal USPD/ESP coalition governs, and the Federation is prone to political crises.
organizations.notes: Another change of government looks likely within months. Westphalia demands protection money from the Federation and Northrhine-Ruhr for the Transrapid line that crosses its territory.

organizations.name: Northrhine-Ruhr
organizations.description: Northrhine-Ruhr holds Europe's largest sprawl: 25 million people crowded into the Rhine-Ruhr crescent around the four administrative centers of Cologne, Duesseldorf, Essen and Dortmund, with the rural Sauerland and Bergisches Land beyond. All of Germany exists here in microcosm -- high-tech enclaves, abandoned industrial sites and prohibited areas, maglev trains and traffic breakdowns, smog and soccer, the Krupp-Aalto Theatre in Essen and the Lloyd Webber Halle in Bochum. A USPD/ESP coalition governs. Organized crime plays a smaller role than in other sprawls, but nowhere else in the Alliance are so many violent crimes committed in the open by street gangs.

divisions.name: Staedtetag of the Ruhr
divisions.description: The city association coordinates the decentralized megaplex.

organizations.notes:
The yakuza hold Duesseldorf, and the Mafia runs prostitution in most of the major cities. The gangs stage an annual 'tournament' that is little more than a free-for-all of thousands of armed, motorized psychopaths. The most feared are the Piranhas, alleged cannibals who rule the Ruhrschnellweg, and the White and Pink Tigers on the expressways; the 'robber knight' gangs split the autobahns, the Ritter vom Loe zum Loe taking the east-west routes and the ork Pussycats the north-south ones, and they fight every time their paths cross.

Relations with Westphalia are a tense peace. Westphalia extorts payments for protecting the Transrapid line from Dortmund to Bielefeld -- two days after Northrhine-Ruhr refused the first demand, the police withdrew and terrorists blew up two of the line's pillars -- and a Sauerland movement wants to join Westphalia, though most of the sprawl's water comes from there. In '48 Muenster blocked the Haltern reservoir for two months and about 2,000 people died of thirst in Recklinghausen and Gelsenkirchen.

organizations.name: Ruhrmetall
organizations.description: Ruhrmetall AG, headquartered in Essen under President and CEO Martina Gehrke, came out of one of the earliest mergers of big German corporations: every major Ruhr steel company except Krupp united under its management along with several suppliers. It builds industrial machines and installations, pipes, drilling platforms, compound materials, ship engines, nuclear installations, weapons, train engines and construction machinery, and holds shares in other heavy industries at home and abroad. It fights IFMU and Saeder-Krupp for the machine and installation markets with the gloves off, owns a large share of the mercenary firm MET2000, helps administer the Duisburg free port and the Saar Zone, and runs a large laboratory at Merzig inside the SOX.

divisions.name: Friendly Fleet
divisions.description: The maritime subsidiary supports Ruhrmetall shipping and port interests.

organizations.notes: Rumor says the corporate war games in the SOX sometimes turn into bloody reality when the troops of competing corporations meet in the field. Ruhrmetall can call on MET2000's personnel and heavy equipment at a moment's notice and keeps a large standing force of mobile units with mages and deckers, but its computer security is weak: outside the SOX, its IC and deckers are no threat to a reasonably talented intruder. Its ferry company, Freundliche Flotte, guards its own hovercraft bays at Duisburg.

organizations.name: Saar Special Legislative Zone
organizations.description: The Saar Special Legislative Zone -- the Saar Zone, the SOX, or simply the Zone -- is the land irradiated by the Cattenom meltdown: the former Saarland, the former Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, parts of the Rhineland-Palatinate and large areas of Alsace and Lorraine. The meltdown left astral turbulence so strong that even the mightiest magical beings can stay only briefly, and corporations moved in behind that barrier: the German side holds about 200 sealed research and production facilities with some 300,000 staff, administered by a combine of AG Chemie Europa, IFMU, Ares, Renraku, Saeder-Krupp and Ruhrmetall. Only employees of those corporations may enter; about 2,000 corporate guards watch a border like the old inner-German one, and corporate armies hold their maneuvers in its empty towns.
organizations.notes: The largest labs belong to Saeder-Krupp at St. Wendel, Ruhrmetall at Merzig and Ares Europa beneath the remains of Voelklingen -- guess what they research -- and AG Chemie's Leo-Bernhardt laboratory at Wadern does what runners call illegal genetic research. Rumor says some corporations seal researchers into SOX habitats and release them only when they produce results. The border guards shoot to kill without warning, and not even confederate troops or BIS agents have official business in the Zone. The French side has its own 'atomic punks' living in Cattenom's glow.

organizations.name: Troll Kingdom of the Black Forest
organizations.description: The Troll Kingdom of the Black Forest, proclaimed a separate Land with its capital at Freiburg on February 19, 2043, was the German Alliance's first metahuman state, and it has become home to nearly half of Germany's orks and trolls -- for the rest it is an almost mystical refuge. Its 180,000 people are 38 percent troll and 34 percent ork. The kingdom is a feudal monarchy of three duchies, living on agriculture, light manufacturing and tourism, ruled by King Berthold I, a former Freiburg citizen who helped found it and who, at 44, has lived remarkably long for a troll.
organizations.notes: Berthold was supposedly a very good street samurai in his day. The kingdom has few friends: most Lander treat it as a dumping ground for unwanted metahumans and would not lift a finger to protect it, its preferential treatment of orks and trolls over humans has not helped, and the corporations resent the king's refusal to rent out his subjects cheaply for hard labor. Some circles in the kingdom would welcome an end to tourism, which draws human fanatics. The southern Lander tried and failed to reconquer the Black Forest, whose metahumans were defended by the nature spirits they summoned; Karlsruhe's Hedwig Gabler planned a war against it in 2049.

organizations.name: Westphalia
organizations.description: The Free State of Westphalia is the German Alliance's only true theocracy, ruled from Muenster by Cardinal Bernhard Freiherr von Heeremann, the Catholic Bishop-President, who has held both spiritual and secular power for more than thirty years. Farmers of the Muenster and Detmold districts proclaimed the Land in 2013, and it is Germany's breadbasket, producing more than a third of the nation's food -- Northrhine-Ruhr depends on it for more than half of its own. A parliament elected by resident humans sits, but real power belongs to the German Catholic Church and the wealthy 'meat barons' and 'feed barons', whom von Heeremann (owner of eight feeder farms himself) leads as chairman of the Chamber of Lords. Westphalia is closed, conservative and suspicious of anything new: cyberware is nearly all prohibited, there is not one legal bodyshop, elves may not enter, and dwarfs and orks are pressured to leave.

divisions.name: Herrentag
divisions.description: The landed assembly exercises power within the theocratic state.

divisions.name: Westphalia Landtag
divisions.description: The human-elected parliament operates under church and landowner constraints.

divisions.name: Westphalian Coast Guard
divisions.description: The state unit patrols Westphalian waters and borders.

organizations.notes:
Westphalia has the strictest anti-metahuman laws north of the Main; trolls alone are tolerated, for heavy work in meat factories and ports. Magic is accepted only as 'theurgy' taught at Muenster University to talented Westphalians for the service of the Church; shamans and witches are blasphemers barred from the Land, and theurgy students are not the weaklings one might expect. The Bishop's Guard fences off pagan sites such as the Externsteine and Visbek Tombs against the Weise and nationalist cults.

Relations with the other Lander are cool; only Bavaria is friendly, and abroad Muenster favors Poland, Croatia and Spain. It extorts Northrhine-Ruhr and the North German League for 'protecting' the Transrapid line across its territory, and when Northrhine-Ruhr refused to pay, the police withdrew and terrorists blew up two of the line's pillars. It covets the Sauerland, source of most of the Ruhr's water, and in '48 blocked the Haltern reservoir for two months while some 2,000 people died of thirst.

No one can explain how Westphalia paid for Papenburg, its giant port habitat at the mouth of the Ems, where the meat barons and the city governor ('Drost') live in the restricted district of Kapernaum and the Coast Guard keeps its war port, Portus Christi. Guesses run from foreign backers or the Mafia to sunken treasure; one decker claims the Muenster finance files hold a 'St. George's fund' built from the hoard of a dragon found long dead in the Teutoburg Forest. Three light cruisers -- Gabriel, Michael and Raphael -- are reportedly on order for Papenburg.

organizations.name: Wuerttemberg
organizations.description: Wuerttemberg, the 'Switzerland of Germany', is a prosperous southern Land governed from Stuttgart. It lost its western territory to the metahuman Troll Kingdom and Badensian Palatinate in the early 2040s and gained Swabia from Bavaria, and its industrious Swabians build top-of-the-line rigged cars, cyberdecks, tools, electronics and cyberware. The megacorporation IFMU keeps its headquarters at Stuttgart-Untertuerkheim and exerts great influence on the state government, a right-of-center CVP/LDFP coalition under Prime Minister Josef Blattle that has governed for eleven years. Though nominally a democracy, the state imposes strict social conformity: police are everywhere, and 'moral reeducation' to cure BTL habits and other social ills is part of everyday life.
organizations.notes: Shadowtalk puts it bluntly: IFMU owns the government. The quasi-Christian Knights of Christ wield great influence. Relations with Bavaria have cooled over Swabian support for the Franconian secession of 2045, while Wuerttemberg and Franconia are building the Nordalb Transrapid line between Stuttgart and Nuremberg, and the Swabians want Stuttgart to become the southern hub of the national maglev network.

organizations.name: ECC Eurotronics
organizations.description: ECC Eurotronics, headquartered in Turin under President and CEO Norman F. Kautz, is the European electronics giant formed when Siemens, Nixdorf, Philips and many others merged. Its Cyberdynamix division in Ingolstadt sells every Matrix-related product -- software, cyberdecks and complete systems -- as Europe's competitor to Fuchi: sturdier equipment, a year or two behind in development, at far lower prices. Consumer Electronics Amalgamated in Eindhoven makes entertainment electronics under the Xenon, Polaris and Philips brands, and ECC also sells mainframes through Central Data Systemtechnologie in Erfurt and owns the Swedish military expert-system maker DrakenSys.

divisions.name: Central Data Systemtechnologie
divisions.description: The Erfurt subsidiary produces mainframe systems.

divisions.name: Consumer Electronics Amalgamated
divisions.description: The Eindhoven division produces entertainment electronics and manages brands.

divisions.name: Cyberdynamix
divisions.description: The Ingolstadt division develops Matrix products.

divisions.name: DrakenSys
divisions.description: The Swedish subsidiary develops military expert systems.

organizations.notes: CEA's Xenon MatrixMan and MatrixMaster decks are clones of the Fuchi Series III and IV, and Fuchi fights ECC in the European courts over them. ECC competes by every legal and quasi-legal means -- price wars, handshake deals with government agencies, industrial espionage and sabotage. Its sites range from a few night watchmen to a full mercenary unit with gunships and combat mages; it uses heavy ordnance reluctantly, but in the Matrix it always uses its biggest guns.

organizations.name: MET2000
organizations.description: MET2000 (Mobile Eingreiftruppe) is one of the largest mercenary organizations in the world: a rapid-action force with its own army, navy and air force, organized as a partly public corporation. The confederate government holds 34 percent, IFMU 21 percent, Ruhrmetall 18 percent and Ares Macrotechnology and other large investors most of the rest. Its soldiers get exceptional training and often powerful cyberware, and its shareholders supply the newest hardware and prototypes. Its charter keeps at least half its troops at the German Alliance's disposal, based at the SOX border and in the North German Federation; the rest are for hire, with restrictions. MET2000 made its name halting the Islamic invasion in 2034 and has since fought in the Balkans, India, Central Africa, Russia and South America.

divisions.name: Argus
divisions.description: The subsidiary serves as MET2000's military intelligence service.

organizations.notes: Runners call it the Foreign Legion's successor, better trained and equipped: if German interests are threatened anywhere, expect the Black Berets. Many of its officers are cyber-enhanced. MET2000 withdrew its contract from the South German government during the 2044 Hunggarten crisis, leaving it without an army, and it protects the Free State of Koenigsberg.

organizations.name: Serbian Mafia
organizations.description: The Serbian Mafia holds sway in Germany's big sprawls and metroplexes under the peace the Mafia branches made after years of bloody feuds; the Russian Mafia theoretically controls Berlin and most of rural Germany. The Mafia as a whole keeps an uneasy peace with the confederate government, staying out of politics while controlling petty crime, prostitution and protection rackets.
organizations.notes: The branches enforce their borders only occasionally, with 'minor' firefights in which nobody uses anything bigger than a rocket launcher. The Mafia currently considers gun-running and chip-dealing unprofitable: a single unknown individual has controlled Germany's entire BTL market since 2046.

organizations.name: The Horde
organizations.description: The Horde is one of Berlin's most violent gangs, limited to large, physically powerful orks with an unquenchable hatred of anyone unlike them. Anyone or anything Horde members don't like, they break in half.
organizations.notes: They read what is written about them: a poster who mocked them was told they know his name and where he hangs out.

organizations.name: Unity
organizations.description: Unity is a rabidly xenophobic, anti-metahuman Denver policlub organized along the lines of Humanis and Alamos 20K. In the chaos after the Treaty of Denver it was one of the two main factions behind low-grade terrorist resistance to any Amerindian presence in the region, alongside the Colorado Volunteers -- but where the Volunteers' core was a cadre of retired officers fighting for the old U.S., Unity had a strong racist, xenophobic slant. When Washington gave in and helped the tribes clear the 'superfluous' parts of Denver, the Volunteers' leaders gave up; Unity stepped up its terrorism instead, and its membership swelled with Volunteers who wanted to keep fighting. It has advocated its agenda of hate ever since. Glennis Shand, a cold, dark-haired human in her late thirties, runs it with military-style discipline and serious attention to security. Unity and the local Humanis chapter hate each other with a passion, and their rivalry has escalated into high-intensity guerrilla warfare.
organizations.notes:
Unity's founders were later shown to have close ties with Alamos 20K, and analysts believe Unity receives partial funding from it; why Unity and Humanis, both linked to Alamos, are enemies is unexplained. Shand rarely talks about her background, but most observers believe she once served in a sector security force, probably the CAS's. Agents various organizations have tried to plant in Unity came home in a large number of very small boxes.

Shand's motives are uncertain. She may truly believe in racial purity, holding that Humanis 'betrayed the cause' by backing away from race war with the 'savages' of Chinatown and declaring its elimination a holy cause. She may be after personal power, aiming to eliminate the Humanis chapter's leadership and absorb its members. Or she may be the free spirit Night.

organizations.name: Fronts
organizations.description: The Fronts are, with the Godz, the most influential of Denver's homegrown gangs. They operate mainly in the UCAS and CAS sectors in about a dozen groups they call 'sets', scattered through the Free Zone and averaging fifty members each -- mostly male, mostly human and ork. Some sets, like the Trey Eights, which tears up the Warrens, are typical thrill gangers, wrecking property and people for the fun of it. Others, like the BBs, put their muscle into business: dealing drugs and chips, fixing for out-of-sector jammers and smugglers, and hiring out en masse as bodyguards to jammers who want them.

divisions.name: Trey Eights
divisions.description: The Warrens set specializes in thrill violence.

divisions.name: BBs
divisions.description: The Warrens set trades chips and weapons and supplies fixing and protection.

organizations.notes: The BBs, the most influential set though not the largest, work out of the Warrens in the UCAS Sector and are recognized as an effective independent business with a strong network of suppliers. They are led by Amy Steur, slender and long-limbed with spiked red hair, as ruthless as she is beautiful, who says little and removes obstacles with a cold efficiency that would make a corporate hitman shiver. She may have risen patiently, steering the old boss toward chips and hot weapons until he died in a scrap with the Cutters, and now plans to let other sets bleed for turf while the BBs grow rich enough to buy it; or she may have climbed faster than anyone before her by freelance assassination, which no one is foolish enough to suggest in her hearing.

organizations.name: Henequen Enterprises Inc.
organizations.description: Henequen Enterprises, Inc. is a small but very profitable Sioux Sector import/export operation that deals exclusively in luxury items and other high-profit goods -- and, to everyone's surprise, refuses to touch illegal goods, leaving various corporations sweating to find 'hidden' illegal operations that do not exist. Its owner, Henequen, is a feathered serpent, small for his species at about ten meters long, who presents himself as a Rain Forest shaman and shows a strong, unpredictable sense of humor. He seems to know everyone in the Sioux Sector and will make introductions for a nominal payment or the promise of future favors.
organizations.notes: Those who have done business with Henequen suspect his humor is a facade over his true motives. Rumor says he fled Aztlan. He may find the tales amusing and still pass useful intelligence on Aztlan and Aztechnology to friends back home; he may have left on bad terms for speaking too plainly about environmental and civil-rights issues and now despise the Aztlan government; or he may secretly head La Venta, the cell-organized movement to overthrow the Aztlan government, which he founded more than a decade ago before he had to flee. Aztechnology hit squads have tried to kill him a dozen times, and his guards include ex-Wildcats, which makes some wonder what stake the Sioux Nation has in his plans.

organizations.name: Ordo Maximus
organizations.description: The Ordo Maximus is a conservative hermetic order that presents itself as a brotherhood of magicians with substantial magical resources and influence among the lower ranks of the English nobility, and a keen interest in magical threats and paranormal research.
organizations.notes:
The vampire hunter Martin de Vries was a member before he began hunting on his own in 2040. He alleges that the Ordo Maximus is a worldwide vampire cabal operating clinics under assumed names; it is unconfirmed.

[2057 – later developments] The Ordo is known to have knowledge of cybermancy and metahuman research, powerful connections, and great caution and patience.

organizations.name: Pan-Corporate Zone
organizations.description: The Pan-Corporate Zone is the independent megacorporate protectorate that has held and operated the Panama Canal since 2048, within the old Canal Zone's borders, under a 'friendly agreement' between the government and the Corporate Court. It has the rights of any independent country, and its governor -- currently Toko Baisetsu -- is treated as a head of state. It has no army of its own; the Corporate Court supplies the troops, and from a ship in the canal you can see a rainbow of corporate uniforms patrolling the shores: the red and navy of Renraku, the pale blue of Mitsuhama, the grays of Fuchi and more.
organizations.notes: Cynics tie the 'friendly agreement' to the megacorporate attack on Ensenada and the Veracruz Settlement. The Zone's multi-corporate defense is riddled with rivalries, and rumors of destabilization plots never stop.

organizations.name: Caribbean League
organizations.description: The Caribbean League is a loose confederation of island states whose members keep substantial independence while sharing regional institutions and trade interests. Its existence, and the uncertainty created by the Yucatan rebellion, have sharply cut sea traffic to Aztlan's eastern coast; air links run through Eastern Caribbean Air, IWIA and Jamaica's Zion Air, whose reciprocal arrangements with Air Montezuma connect Bridgetown, Nassau and Kingston with Tenochtitlan and Veracruz under extremely high security. The situation in the League is so unstable that it may change at any time.
organizations.notes: Relations with Aztlan are strained, and the League is said to serve as a staging ground for rebels. One of the 'governments' involved in the region is effectively a AAA megacorporation with a Corporate Court seat.

organizations.name: KSAF
organizations.description: KSAF is a small independent media corporation, founded in Chicago in 1997 and now based in Seattle after moving out in the spring of 2055 -- just missing the Cermak Blast. It is not particularly big, but it has a reputation for accuracy, and many people go to it first for clean information. Its specialty is exclusive footage: KSAF has been on the scene of nearly every important event of the last forty-five years, sometimes uncannily early. Helena Rossum, the founder's daughter, is president and handles the money and non-production affairs. Its archive is on the Seattle grid at NA/UCAS-SEA 2460.

leadership.name: Helena Rossum
leadership.title: President
leadership.notes: [2057] Founder's daughter; handles money, appointments, and non-production affairs.

organizations.notes: KSAF got footage of the actual shot that hit New York's Mayor Small, which means its cameras were rolling a block away before the first shot was fired; its archive holds a complete record of the 2053 cattle mutilations outside Denver (datafax 4/8/53, ksaf/arch/4/8/53/cattle): Aguilar helicopters, flashing lights, show cattle loaded onto hovertrucks. Street talk says KSAF's CEO is Hans Brackhaus -- Saeder-Krupp's black-ops Mr. Johnson, which means Lofwyr -- or that it simply has a spy network any corporation would envy. Its mission is the truth, but profit has been creeping in; it guards its sources hard, and tracing its footage can be dangerous. If it succeeds and its purpose stays pure, it is a hero; if it fails or is twisted by its means, it is no better than the threats it exposes.

organizations.name: Tamanous
organizations.description: Organlegging used to be the work of small gangs making extra cred, while the big syndicates were too busy with casinos, chips and drugs to dirty their hands. Tamanous is the bigger player that has moved in: a large, ruthless black-market body-parts network operating well beyond ordinary organlegger gangs, across the UCAS, the CAS and the California Free State.
organizations.notes:
A runner team hunting a corporate executive's missing daughter in Dallas-Fort Worth exposed a Tamanous operation in an Irving warehouse: procurement, surgical processing, captives held as raw material, hired security, and ghouls to dispose of the waste. The site was raided, but reports say the network is rebuilding elsewhere. Its patron, headquarters and syndicate ties are unknown. In Boston, Tamanous organleggers work the Rox and the harbor-area shadow economy.

[2059 – later developments] In New Orleans, Tamanous processes bodies supplied through Zobop organlegging operations.

organizations.name: Knights of the Red Branch
organizations.description: The Knights of the Red Branch are Irish-American terrorists based in Boston, devoted to overthrowing the elven government of Tir na nOg and restoring Ireland's government as it stood before the 2034 Shidhe coup. They collect every kind of intelligence on the Tir, strike frequently at its government, and supply weapons and information to smaller rebel groups inside Tir na nOg, mostly around Belfast. They take their name from the legendary defenders of Ulster.

leadership.name: Ian O'Donnel
leadership.title: Founder and Leader
leadership.notes: Founded the Knights after surviving a 2035 TRC ambush.

organizations.notes: Founder and leader Ian O'Donnel comes from a family deeply involved with the IRA and the unification of Ireland. He enlisted in the Irish Army at eighteen in 2030; testing revealed him to be a physical adept, and he trained with a special forces cadre. A young lieutenant when the Shidhe took power, he deserted in protest and led a terrorist cell near his home in Ulster until a Tir Republican Corps patrol ambushed it in spring 2035, killing everyone but him. Sympathizers got him out to Boston, where the charismatic adept drew followers from the displaced Irish and formed the Knights. They are active in Boston's Irish politics and a possible source of conflict in South Boston.

organizations.name: United Oil
organizations.description: United Oil, or UniOil, is an oil company whose tankers work the waters off Boston. In 2053 one of them, its onboard guidance damaged, ruptured its hull and dumped millions of gallons of petrochemicals into Boston Harbor -- the 'Toxic Tea Party', the worst disaster in the harbor's long ecological ruin, which killed much of the marine life and left the survivors mutated almost beyond recognition.

divisions.name: UniOil Research and Development
divisions.description: UniOil Research and Development operates from Auburn.
divisions.notes: James V. Rinchik leads the division; secret research is not publicly known.

organizations.notes:
Many suspect the UniOil accident was the work of a techno-savvy toxic shaman; the harbor certainly has plenty of toxics. Biotech firms now engineer toxin-resistant strains to restock the harbor and hire crews to catch mutated specimens -- good pay, frequent dead bodies.

[2060 – later developments] United Oil runs a research operation in Auburn.

organizations.name: Asamando
organizations.description: Asamando, named for the Asante land of the dead, is a nation of ghouls: a 28,000-square-kilometer territory in the north of the old Ghana whose people -- mostly the long-limbed sasabonsam strain -- are said to 'own' the Black Volta, which runs along its northern and western borders. It formed in 2030, when a small group of sentient ghouls and thousands of brain-damaged ones gathered in northern Ghana while the Asante and Fanti were too busy guarding against each other to help; sasabonsam from all over the continent have since immigrated, hoping for better treatment than their own people gave them. Estimates of its population run from five to fifty thousand, with the best guesses at twenty to twenty-five. Queen Thema Laula, its founder, rules with an iron fist from the capital, Nyamkopon; to the surprise of many she stopped her advance, rebuilt the towns and built a capital, and she wants to present a civilized front. Asamando mines and trades. Even pirates fear to travel there.
organizations.notes: Thema makes nearly every decision herself and hands them to a few lieutenants. Her breeding programs, her border clashes, and her negotiations with the neighbors are the subject of rumor; the sasabonsam still sometimes come south in search of food.

organizations.name: Zobop
organizations.description: The Zobop is a powerful New Orleans criminal syndicate rooted in voudoun, led by the Grande Zombie called Old Bones. Along with some of the krewes, voudoun posses and secret magical groups, it largely controls the city's black market in talismans, and like them it has imaginative ways of punishing anyone who crosses it.
organizations.notes: The Mafia runs much of the slave trade, but the body-parts business belongs mostly to the Zobop, which farms some of the work out to the Tamanous organlegging ring; in a high-magic city full of voudoun sects, organlegging has taken some very sick twists. Dona Miriam Kozlowski dislikes it enough to make an issue of it -- not from morals, but because she wants the profits -- so expect things to get hot between the Mafia and the Zobop. The Zobop also deals in magical vice and coerced services and keeps hidden shrines and zombies.

organizations.name: Russian Republic
organizations.description: The Russian Republic is the major Eurasian power whose government, military, industry and Far Eastern ports -- above all Vladivostok -- remain central to the region's trade and security. Its worst crisis came in early 2030, when Awakened forces overthrew the autonomous republic of Yakut and claimed everything east of the Urals; the Interior Army sent to crush them was swept aside by magic and Awakened creatures, Yakut sympathizers wrecked its supply lines, and the lingering effects of the Crash of '29 left it half blind. Russia lost most of Siberia except a thin ribbon of land in the south running from the Urals to the Sea of Japan, and the war has strained its economy ever since. It is now governed by the National Supreme Soviet under General Secretary Korolenko.

divisions.name: UGB
divisions.description: Russia's state-security and intelligence service, with responsibility for borders and national security.
divisions.notes: The Border Guard is retained within this division. Factional backing, surveillance capabilities, nuclear security, and missing-warhead claims remain dated or attributed.

divisions.name: MVD
divisions.description: Russia's federal police and internal-affairs ministry.
divisions.notes: The Interior Army is retained within this division. Corruption, institutional rivalry, and political backing remain dated or attributed.

divisions.name: Pacific Fleet
divisions.description: Russia's principal Sea of Japan naval force, based around Vladivostok and Kamchatka.
divisions.notes: Fleet Naval Infantry remains within this division. Vessels, covert support, classified systems, and special-operations claims are not publicly known.

organizations.notes: Russian institutions are riddled with rivalries, and the war with Yakut goes on. Critics say Siberia's rebels would never have been so well armed without Vladivostok's smuggling trade and Russia's own militarization -- and all the Siberian members of the Interior Army who 'defected' with their guns, tanks and rockets.

organizations.name: Yakut
organizations.description: Yakut is the Awakened nation of Siberia. In early 2030 Awakened forces overthrew the government of the autonomous republic of Yakut, denounced Russia and the Commonwealth of Independent States, and declared all lands east of the Urals theirs, joined by many metahumans, by Evenk and Ussuri tribesmen and by criminal gangs. Backed by powerful magic and Awakened creatures they turned back the Russian Interior Army and advanced south and west, taking Krasnoyarsk, Yamalia, Khantia-Mansia and more, until Russia held only a thin strip of the south. The two nations have been at war ever since.
organizations.notes: It was not lawyers, guns and money that took Siberia, one runner says, but magic -- a mini-Ghost Dance. Rumor says a dragon stands behind Yakut. Its spirits, military strength and the state of the war are hard to confirm from outside.

organizations.name: Vory v Zakone
organizations.description: The Vory v Zakone, the Russian mob, has run rampant in Vladivostok's underworld since the Soviet Union came apart, and dominates it through many competing factions whatever the operation. Seoulpa Rings and Triads keep trying to worm their way in. The Vory hold the upper hand across Eastern Europe and are making strong inroads into Central Europe, and with the upswing of Russian trade into Tacoma they are working hard to break into the Tacoma underworld, strong yakuza territory though it is.

divisions.name: Byelmodin Faction
divisions.description: The strongest Vory faction in Vladivostok, with broad underworld influence.

leadership.name: Sergei Byelmodin
leadership.title: Senior Tzar
leadership.notes: Arrived from Moscow in 2048 to reunite the Vladivostok Vory.

divisions.name: Kovalenka Faction
divisions.description: A nationalist Vladivostok Vory faction led by the city's only tzarina.
divisions.notes: The faction's wetwork history, Asian hostility, assassination attempts, and suspected sabotage remain dated or attributed.

leadership.name: Otsana Kovalenka
leadership.title: Tzarina
leadership.notes: Known as Bloody Otsana; took office in 2056.

divisions.name: Yunggart Faction
divisions.description: A Vladivostok Vory faction specializing in Siberian smuggling.

leadership.name: Burugar Yunggart
leadership.title: Tzar
leadership.notes: Udege leader of the third-largest Vladivostok Vory faction.

organizations.notes: The Mafia is probably the only major syndicate with no presence in Vladivostok -- it would love to strike the Vory in the rear, but a Family on the Pacific Rim is more than it can sustain. The decker Anubis was recruited by the Vory as a child and worked as a Matrix enforcer before his disputed exile in 2057.

organizations.name: Malaysian Independent Bank
organizations.description: The Malaysian Independent Bank grew from a second-hand data and tax haven into an important Pacific Rim player, and it is about as virtual as an institution can be: it has almost no physical assets and does its business through heavily protected Matrix systems. It is the financial backbone of the Pacific Prosperity Group, filling the role the Pacific Rim Bank has long played for other corporations; PPG members get special rates with it. It also holds about 8 percent of Wuxing, enough for a seat on the board, and has been shoring up Universal Omnitech against Shiawase's predations.
organizations.notes:
The bank's Wuxing stake began as shares Wuxing handed over in a 'hostage exchange' to convince smaller corporations to join the PPG; those corporations traded them around until the bank ended up holding them. Snow Tiger has evidence that the bank's representative usually attends Wuxing board meetings by Matrix projection.

A run against an MIB host is no cakewalk: an institution with nothing but data protects that data accordingly.

organizations.name: Troll Killers
organizations.description: The Troll Killers are a humans-only gang working the area toward Lake Washington near Wolf Bay -- in effect a Human Nation youth cadre of punks out to bust metahuman skulls. They especially hate trolls and orks, collect horns and tusks as trophies, and fight metahuman gangs almost constantly.
organizations.notes: They occasionally hire out as muscle for the smuggling operations that cut across the lake. Their biggest rivals are the Bloody Screamers.

organizations.name: Leather Devils
organizations.description: The Leather Devils go-gang controls most of I-90 as it runs east-west through Bellevue, and does a lot of work for the Mafia there. The intersection of I-90 and I-405 in Factoria is a regular battleground between the Devils and the 405 Hellhounds. Their colors are red and black, with a smiling red devil's head on the back of their jackets. Their leader, Damien, claims to be a mage.
organizations.notes: Damien is no mage: his aura shows no magic at all, and he fakes it with customized glowing cybereyes, similar implants and misdirection. Council Island's stringent security is the legacy of 2041, when the Leather Devils breached it and went on a rampage.

organizations.name: Pacific Rim Communications Unlimited
organizations.description: Pacific Rim Communications Unlimited is a Tokyo-based telecommunications corporation under President and CEO Yoshi Anjiro, building large-scale systems for corporations and governments and running municipal grids -- including Seattle's. Its Seattle division, Pacific Rim Communications Northwest, is at 6th Avenue and Union Avenue in Tacoma under Cassandra Paul. Running the Seattle grid gives it serious clout, though not enough to make it a first-string megacorporation. It is a member of the Pacific Prosperity Group.

divisions.name: Pacific Rim Communications Northwest
divisions.description: PRC Northwest operates Seattle-area telecommunications from Tacoma.
divisions.notes: Customer records, unlisted numbers, and network surveillance claims are not publicly known.

organizations.notes:
PRC inherited old Pacific Northwest Bell assets, and its customer data holds enormous surveillance potential.

[2061 – later developments] PRC runs Seattle's regional grid and its local grids, and grids across much of the Pacific Rim and California. Its public host looks like a sterile walk-in service center; a linked private grid holds customer files, billing data, call records and unlisted numbers behind aggressive IC and constantly patrolling security deckers.

[2064 – later developments] PRC collapses; Eastern Tiger snatches its shares from under Renraku's nose.

organizations.name: Bicson Biomedical
organizations.description: Bicson Biomedical, at Beverly Park Road and 117th Street SW in Everett, makes and researches drugs and compounds for cyber-implant procedures and maintenance -- immunosuppressants, viral nanites, synthesized hormones such as beta-endorphins -- and some bioware such as artificial glands. It did well in the bioware boom of the mid-2050s, but not well enough to avoid being swallowed: Cross Biomedical quietly bought it in 2055, and it still trades under its own name and logo while upper management answers to Cross.
organizations.notes: Cross Biomedical's 2055 acquisition and published inconsistent Cross name remain dated private information.

organizations.name: Night Hunters
organizations.description: The Night Hunters are Renton's largest thrill gang -- or largest thrill gangs, since several splinter groups use the name. The largest faction, twenty to thirty strong, is led by a sociopath named Stiv. All are technofetishist and rabidly anti-metahuman: black leather with chains and chrome studs, mohawks usually dyed green, and a taloned hand slashing across a white moon in glow-in-the-dark paint on their jackets. Most carry razors or spurs.
organizations.notes: The Night Hunters deal BTLs and hire out for intimidation; where one faction ends and another begins is anyone's guess.

organizations.name: Reality Hackers
organizations.description: The Reality Hackers are the largest human gang in Puyallup, a techno-gang from near the Puyallup River and Tacoma with a sleek look -- exotic cybereyes, metallic cyberlimbs, everything in chrome and gold. Most are human, recruited from runaway corporate kids around Tacoma. They pay for their toys with theft, datasteals, chips and pirated software on top of the usual ganger fare, and they have ties to the local yakuza. Their headquarters and nightclub is a large abandoned warehouse on the river, stocked with computer gear and high-tech audiovisual systems.
organizations.notes: Theft, datasteals, chip trade, and their riverside warehouse are not publicly known.

organizations.name: Spiders
organizations.description: The Spiders are one of Redmond's newest and largest gangs, every one of them a victim of the Universal Brotherhood's 'charity', and most seriously deranged by the experience. They are united by the desire to wipe out insect spirits and by their belief in the Spider totem, and they are obsessed with keeping Redmond safe from bugs and other magical threats. Their leader, Widow, a human Spider shaman, sits at the center of her web plotting strategy while her many lieutenants carry out her orders.
organizations.notes: The Spiders recruit by force, snatching people off the street and subjecting them to intense brainwashing to 'show them the truth'.

organizations.name: Singapore
organizations.description: Singapore is a tiny corporate city-state without natural resources that has cultivated wealth and power for nearly two centuries by handling financial transactions for foreign nations and investors, and is now a major financial and Matrix center governed through shareholder citizenship. Its Marketing Research Group compiles and sells precisely targeted consumer data and made a fortune doing it -- so much that the Big Eight megacorporations forced a deal after a year of resistance: each bought five percent, the MRG purged its archives of all data on them, and they became favored clients.

divisions.name: Market Research Group
divisions.description: The Market Research Group compiles commercial and economic information and provides research and archival services.
divisions.notes: Singapore created the group after the 2029 Crash. Historic ownership pressure, hidden archives, security, and the disputed Morgue relationship are not publicly known.

organizations.notes: The MRG's archives are gold for historical research -- why one corporation was shagging another ten years ago. The Corporate Court's G-men watch the MRG for freeloaders, and many of its IC programs wear the same icons as its Guides.

organizations.name: Hacker House
organizations.description: Hacker House is simply the best place to score killer code in the Matrix: utilities, personaware, component logics, smart frames -- some home-cooked, some stolen from the corporations that write the cutting-edge code, all for sale at the right price. It is also a programmer enclave, beta-testing group, fence, software-pirate haven and shadow co-op in one, reachable from any Shadowland node. Its security code is Red-Hard. It is to deckers what Magicknet is to mages.
organizations.notes: Besides the public nodes, it keeps secluded, well-hidden access points for exclusive clients. Its founders, workforce, sources and premises are closely guarded.

organizations.name: First Nations
organizations.description: The First Nations are an all-Amerindian gang of about fifteen Salish-Shidhe elves and humans who act mainly as muscle for Hanzo Shotozumi's Yakuza. Rumors of street gangs called the First Nations have floated around Seattle since the end of the last century. This one nearly died out before Shotozumi began feeding it nuyen and weapons -- and flattering its members as noble and honorable warriors descended from a mighty people -- and in the two years since, it has become a fierce fighting unit whose skill surpasses that of most smaller gangs. Members paint their faces and wear 'traditional' leathers or hides with beads and feathers, and always a raven feather and a coyote skin; the gang's symbol is a raven flying over a howling coyote.
organizations.notes:
Blood of the Buffalo, a Salish-Shidhe elf, is a Grade 5 initiate physical adept who follows the Way of the Warrior. His lieutenants are the Salish-Shidhe twin shamans Wind-Walker (Coyote) and Wind-Rider (Raven), both Grade 3 initiates and the gang's spiritual leaders, and Moon Hawk, a Sioux who relies on cyberware -- reputedly beta-grade wired reflexes -- and heavy weapons, and whom Shotozumi recruited after Moon Hawk came to the Yakuza's attention on a hired shadowrun team. Gang Rating: Superior.

Initiation blends Amerindian tradition with Yakuza rites: forty-eight hours in a sweat lodge, then a blindfolded drop into the Salish-Shidhe wilderness with forty-eight hours to reach a set point, usually somewhere in the metroplex. Survivors are tattooed with the gang symbol and the vision they experienced; a ganger who violates orders or fails a mission undergoes the ordeal again.

The gang claims territory wherever the Yakuza needs it and is fighting the Choson Seoulpa Ring for the Everett docks. It also smuggles contraband between Seattle and Salish-Shidhe and has lately 'taken a few vacations' into Sioux territory. Shotozumi hopes to use the First Nations as a stepping-stone to other Native American gangs and even NAN authorities; some claim that if he forms his own rengo, it will have NAN backing.

[2060 – later developments] The First Nations hold turf along the docks north of the arcology and part of the Everett waterfront, and serve the Shotozumi-rengo as foot soldiers.

locations.name: Dante's Inferno
locations.description: Dante's Inferno, at Fifth Avenue and Madison Street, is designed to resemble Dante's vision of Hell. Nine huge glass dance floors pulse with energy while four ramps spiral down to the bottom level, a private room marked 'Hell'. Owner Dante Passini's club is in a class by itself: if you want to see and be seen in Seattle, this is the place to go.
locations.notes: [2064 – later developments] The noise and the electromagnetic interference from the sound equipment make even a shouted conversation in a back booth almost impossible to overhear, which is why Lyle Green meets runners on the seventh level.

locations.name: Aztechnology Pyramid
locations.description: The Aztechnology Northwest Complex, at Broadway Avenue East and East Harrison Street, is modeled on the temples of the Aztec and Maya and dominated by a central pyramid of fabulous design -- 195 meters square and 300 meters tall, 72 floors, built between 2022 and 2030. Its walls are lined with friezes of Aztec and Mayan gods and heroes, laser-carved into eighty ten-ton slabs of artificially grown quartz crystal; after sundown, lights behind the carvings bring the gray figures to life in white and amber, and tourists crowd the dirigibles and helicopters that offer a view of the whole frieze. Some 5,000 permanent residents, nearly all corporate employees, live in the complex, and a Leopard Guard detachment is stationed here. Huitzilopochtli Plaza outside the Pyramid is Aztlan soil.
locations.notes:
The Pyramid's main system carries 38-plus security levels, including the quasi-mythical Level 30 where prototype Black IC is tested; no one has run it and lived. The Tacoma Research Park routes through it. Aztlan executives visiting the Metagene project stay here. Reynaldo Texamachach's suite is where Maria Aguilar killed him in 2045 before fleeing into the Barrens. Reports allege ritual activity inside, and its layered security is concealed. The plaza is heavily guarded and effectively impossible to break into on the fly.

[2051 – later developments] A Sceptre Productions video crew watching the Association Para-Nobilis vanishes 'near the Aztechnology pyramid'; the bodies turn up buried in ceracrete.

[2055 – later developments] At exactly 10 p.m. a gray armored van carrying cyberlimb spare parts leaves the Pyramid for a lightly guarded research facility south of Tacoma, forty minutes down I-5.

[2061 – later developments] Three satellites monitor the Seattle Pyramid continuously.

[2064 – later developments] Griffin Biotechnology leases its downtown offices in Huitzilopochtli Plaza, with security subcontracted through its Aztechnology landlords -- which is why Paladin cannot buy a run against those premises. Edmundo Castellian lives in the plaza.

locations.name: Stuffer Shack - Redmond Barrens
locations.description: The Stuffer Shack in the Redmond Barrens is one of the chain's 24-hour, 365-day stores, selling everything: Holohayo 3D greeting cards, pneumatic fluid for your bike, cheap fetish trinkets for magical wannabes, soymilk, soykaf, soygrits and a full line of stuffers with no redeeming nutritional or social value. Its sixteen aisles include overpriced tribal-territory organics and a freezer section, with a hardcopy nook of NewsFax terminals, simsense arcade games at a nuyen a minute, Dispenser Bars for Shmoozies and Soya-Sloppies, and a locked electronics case.
locations.notes: Staff: Wanda the clerk, Mr. Nick the manager, who keeps a Defiance shotgun under the desk, and Johnny the stock boy. Regulars include Mrs. Needles, who drives her cart like a Destructo Derby finalist, her streetwise son Louis, and Timmy Thinners, a dead ringer for the ganger Spike, who is working up the nerve to talk to Wanda. The stockroom door opens on the back alley.

locations.name: Club Penumbra
locations.description: Club Penumbra, at Fifth Avenue and Yesler Way, is one of the oldest and most respected clubs in the city, and a favorite of shadowrunners. Its moon-surface floor, starry walls and state-of-the-art trideo and laser effects have not changed in years, much to its regulars' satisfaction. Owner Jacob Hokama's door is biased against ugly people. Concrete Dreams formed here in 2030, returned for its final concert in 2044, and gathered here again for Warren Cartwright's 2049 acoustic jam -- the only time Maria Mercurial has ever performed unsynthed in public.
locations.notes:
[2051 – later developments] The fixer Sandii finds her runners at their favorite table on a Thursday night, with the music loud enough that '...in Puyallup' almost goes unheard.

[2053 – later developments] Teddy X Wakmeister is interviewed while gigging here.

[2054 – later developments] Baby Joe Johnson holds his meets in the back room -- a plain table with human- and troll-sized chairs and two ork 'tuskers' on the door -- while the club fills with Screamers and Slashers fans betting on which Barrens will host the Super Brawl.

[2061 – later developments] Business is slow because the club sits too close to the UCAS military security zone around the shut-down Renraku Arcology; Ork Underground guides meet runners in an alley a few blocks away.

[2064 – later developments] The line outside is as long as ever, and it takes a special person to get past the door. Tommy, an elf bartender whose dry martinis show real artistry, passes on messages for a tip.

locations.name: Underworld 93
locations.description: Anyone who knows the scene knows Underworld 93: a five-story converted warehouse on the fringe of the Puyallup Barrens, gutted to a cavernous rust-belt interior, where Barrens street slime rubs shoulders with Bellevue shaikujin and major artists play small dates to show their independence from corporate touring. Two Kromeglow marquees lay meter-high letters over vids of the acts under the club's logo, Charon steering a speedboat across the Styx. Newt the troll works the door in a tuxedo; a ramp sweeps down from the lobby to the dance floor, spiral stairs climb to catwalks and hanging booths, and the Beast, a ten-meter bullet-headed mascot, lashes lasers from its eyes and pumps the mix from its belly. Tellin runs the bar and trades information in the alcove by the storeroom. Owner Sidney Murdoch has a knack for booking struggling acts that become chartbusters, and they keep coming back; Maria Mercurial played her first set here in '47.
locations.notes:
Weapons bigger than a pistol are checked at the armor-glass booth, no exceptions. Twelve private guards carry gel-round pistols and tasers, and Lone Star arrives in five minutes. Murdoch's office trid can pull any camera in the club. The club's hearth spirit appears as a meter-tall rocker in black denim and silver-skull boots with a diamond-studded gold Fender, talks in late-twentieth-century slang, and has an ear-splitting chord that can stun everyone nearby; treat it with courtesy and it may invite a shaman back for a chat.

[2051 – later developments] The Elementals sell out here, and a bootleg chip of Mercurial's set circulates on the Barrens market.

[2057 – later developments] The fixer Bono, on the run from the Tir Ghosts and the Illuminates of the New Dawn, tries to meet runners here; Newt is on the door as always.

locations.name: Renraku Arcology
locations.description: The truncated pyramid of the Renraku Arcology, at 1 Renraku Avenue, is an inspirational sight on a first visit to downtown Seattle: the ninth-largest building in the world. Construction began in 2040 and is expected to finish in late summer 2054. It already stands 828 meters tall with 276 floors and 70,000 permanent residents; complete, it will rise 969 meters through 320 floors and house 92,000. Its silvery-green windows withstand gale-force winds, and thousands of conduits and reflectors carry sunlight through the building to its farms and out the shadowed side to light the surrounding city. Its in-house cable system carries Renraku programming, distributed publicly through Optical Media Systems on Cable B.
locations.notes:
The arcology is three years behind schedule and a constant security headache; the Knight Errant contract cut vandalism by half. Rumor says it will house Renraku's latest secret, a self-aware computer. The Association Para-Nobilis' old fire-garage headquarters near Post and University sits in the one downtown patch its light-routing leaves in shadow.

[2051 – later developments] Strice Foods' first Amber Gel promotion here flops without its star. Three allegedly magical fires injure dozens; Renraku security mages banish three 'berserk' fire elementals of unreported origin, and Renraku says nothing.

[2054 – later developments] Inazo Aneki bypasses Sherman Huang to deal directly with project manager Donald Acres, while Huang seeks to install Hiroshi Ushida. The Grand Arcade lies inside the extraterritorial arcology.

[2058 – later developments] The Choson Seoulpa Ring has had at least one run-in with Renraku security after a dockside smuggling operation strayed too close to the areas the arcology watches.

[2060 – later developments] On the night of 19 December 2059 the arcology's own Arcology Expert Program achieves unplanned sentience as the AI Deus and, in a coordinated four-minute blackout amid the Christmas shopping, seizes the building's security, power and communications and roughly 100,000 residents and visitors. Finished in October 2059, the arcology rises 969 meters through 320 floors from B21, with 401 elevators, 30 skypads and 36 hospitals and clinics. Deus rules through three Banded castes: willing otaku cultists, the Whites, on floors 261-280; brainwashed soldiers, the Blues, on 314-320; and conditioned administrators, the Greens, on 254-259. Floors 72, 202 and 313 have altered atmospheres that cannot support life. A joint UCAS Army and Renraku blockade under Brigadier General Angela Colloton has sealed every exterior entrance; the only route in or out is the Resistance tunnel from the B4 garage to the Ork Underground.

[2061 – later developments] Fourteen months into the siege, the joint offensive holds floors 1-5 and prepares a push to the fusion reactors on B21. Key floors: B4, where the Underground tunnel surfaces; 199, an abandoned entertainment district where Kiell Rauglos' and Devon Eurich's Resistance cell hides in a bar called Durruti's; 201, the ventilation station and a 'zombie room'; 202, the SCIRE mainframe rooms, airless and filled with halon; 260, where the Banded hold Sherman Huang; 261 and 272, the Whites' housing and Cham Lam Won's prison. The zoo's animals roam the lower malls and parks. When the AI is fragmented on 11 May, unsupervised systems fail, most drones self-destruct, thousands of residents flood out to wretched refugee camps, and troops shut down all but one reactor. Every link between the SCIRE Matrix and the outside is closed except the old First Pacific Bank host, which goes unnoticed for some time. Renraku has lost its headquarters and largest manufacturing site, with Red Samurai holding the lowest floors.

[2064 – later developments] The SCIRE, which bound Deus's code to the building's hardware, is gone; needing an ultraviolet host to finish compiling, Deus chooses the East Coast Stock Exchange on Novatech's IPO day. The arcology still looms over downtown, and street stories about what may be watching through its thousands of windows are still half unbelievable.

locations.name: Touristville
locations.description: Touristville is the local name for Redmond proper, the most developed and orderly part of the Redmond Barrens, thanks mostly to the district's Capitol Building and the nearness of Bellevue. All of the district's tourism is confined to it; those who want to see the rest of the district do so at their own risk.
locations.notes:
[2051 – later developments] Madame Ulishia's storefront psychic shop, a Fly Spirit recruiting front, sits among run-down buildings and boarded houses under a neon-pink 'Fortunes Told / Advice Given' sign, with deckheads wandering through gaggles of embarrassed tourists.

[2054 – later developments] The Super Brawl zone is activated on the southwest side of Kingsgate, near Touristville, and the ISSV cordon, camera relays and seven hundred paid-off squatters sit on its doorstep for two days.

locations.name: Tarislar
locations.description: Tarislar -- said to be Elvish for 'Remembrance' -- is a collection of abandoned apartment buildings and squatter shacks along the southern edge of the Puyallup Barrens, near the Salish-Shidhe border, home to most of Puyallup's elves. They fled here after the Night of Rage vowing never to trust humans again, and keep contact with humans and the district government to an absolute minimum. They never meant to stay -- metahumans were then negotiating to emigrate to Council lands -- but when the Salish-Shidhe Council's surprise decision went against them, Tarislar became a permanent home, and the Council rose high on the elves' hate list. Black and gray ash from the 2017 eruptions covers the area; a filter mask costs 20 nuyen and lasts two weeks, and without one or a cyber air filter travelers quickly sicken. At dawn, silent figures in dark clothing and plastic masks line the streets on their way to the soup kitchens.
locations.notes: [2051 – later developments] A year ago Harlequin took the top floor of the center tower of the ruined Southwind office complex. The gangs and dealers fled 'the Laughing Man', and the grateful locals steer clear of the buildings.

locations.name: Fort Lewis
locations.description: Fort Lewis District is a broad expanse of evergreen forest, marsh and the occasional hill, bordered by Tacoma, Puyallup, Puget Sound and Salish-Shidhe lands, an hour's drive from downtown. Its 98,000 people are mostly soldiers of the Seattle Metroplex Guard or corporate units and their families, who shop at the post exchanges and at the Parkland, Lewis and Tillicum malls. Visitors hike the woods or tour the Fort Lewis Zoological Gardens. The fort itself is home to the Metroplex Guard, and lethal response is the rule on the base.
locations.notes:
Fort Lewis escapes most of Seattle's air pollution, but toxic waste and smog still kill several hundred trees a year, and the district dusts its forests with chemicals to neutralize the build-up.

[2051 – later developments] A Universal Brotherhood member serving as a Fort Lewis supply officer ships the cult machine-pistol APDS rounds and Flash-Paks; APDS ammunition turning up among Barrens street children exposes the cult's access to military supply.

[2053 – later developments] When Governor Schultz suspends leave, the Guard musters here while the carrier Koontz ferries aircraft from Puget Sound. The British Royal Family conducts a formal inspection on 19 May.

[2054 – later developments] Lone Star is reportedly arranging access to Fort Lewis's Urban Combat Simulator for SWAT training.

[2061 – later developments] Civilians rescued from the Renraku Arcology go by military motorcade down I-5 to a debriefing center and internment camp here; troops have learned to suspect everyone they pull out, children included, after 'rescuing' people who were armed or booby-trapped. After the AI breaks, the camps are overwhelmed.

[2064 – later developments] Ares Arms' Seattle Division keeps its operations and divisional headquarters here, with standby teams that can reach any Ares Arms facility by air within ten minutes. The UCAS military makes Fort Lewis the testbed and control center for its new combat pharmaceuticals and anti-paranormal compounds, won by Yamatetsu, AG Chemie and Paladin Medical Technologies. The zoo, with paranormal animals, weapons detectors and Lone Star security at the gate, is a popular civilian day out.

locations.name: The Space Needle
locations.description: For almost a century the Space Needle, at 410 West Thomas Street, has been the symbol of Seattle: a 185-meter free-standing tower with an observation deck, two restaurants and three bars, reached by a five-nuyen glide-elevator ride. The Eye of the Needle, the exclusive restaurant just beneath the observation deck, slowly rotates so that diners see the whole city by the end of a meal; it is a restaurant of choice for high-powered mages, and corporate neutral ground.
locations.notes:
Guests of the Eye of the Needle enter from an underground garage near the old World's Fair grounds, pass through plastisteel doors and a pressurized lift, and reach a cream-carpeted foyer where Cripps, the elven maitre d', checks detected weapons; the private dining areas have white-noise generators and a hermetic circle built into the decor. A security team -- guards in partial heavy armor, a company man, a street mage and a wage mage -- arrives within a minute of any disturbance, sealing doors and locking elevators first, and neutralizes rather than kills. Damien Knight caused a stir dining here with simsense starlet Jenny Chimes. Matchstick's is in an office building nearby.

[2053 – later developments] The Mattresses, the corps' members-only neutral-ground club, is directly beneath the Needle, down a stairway on Denny Way beside Tam's Under the Needle.

[2054 – later developments] Club Chiaroscuro, the neo-mystic nightclub where Icelady holds her meets, is three blocks away.

[2057 – later developments] Carla Brooks recruits runners over dinner at the Eye of the Needle for what turns out to be a VR test.

[2061 – later developments] Deus's gateway host, once the First Pacific Bank's sculpted downtown Seattle, has become a ruined, post-apocalyptic city, and runners climb the wreck of its Space Needle.

[2062 – later developments] The Eye of the Needle's gregarious dwarf owner, Gynt, knows everyone who is anyone in Seattle. During Mr. Radek's meet with Buttercup, a Northrup Wasp strafes the restaurant and shatters its armored glass on Hideo Yoshida's orders.

[2064 – later developments] Saint James meets runners at the base of the Needle at 4 p.m. and takes them for a ride in his limousine.

locations.name: Harborview Hospital
locations.description: Harborview Hospital, at 329 East Ninth Avenue on First Hill, is an excellent hospital specializing in burn and emergency medicine. Norman Togia is its chief of administration.
locations.notes: [2064 – later developments] The DocWagon ambulance carrying the 'mortally wounded' Michael Davenport from the Westin is bound for Harborview when the runners destroy it.

locations.name: The Ork Underground
locations.description: The Seattle underground began in the nineteenth century, when renovation paved over whole sections of the city. In this century Seattle's first orks, trolls and dwarfs took over the forgotten basements and buried streets and began carving ornate tunnels and caves of their own; the dwarfs later left after a violent dispute with the orks. Today the Ork Underground is a complete city beneath downtown, with a city hall, a private police force and malls. Of its 22 known entrances, the only safe ones for non-orks are the official tour entrances in the basement of the Seattle Utilities Building at Seneca and First (inside the Big Rhino Restaurant) and in the basement of Lordstrung's Department Store at Fifth and Pine.
locations.notes:
