Rumor tells of many secret entrances -- ork thieves reputedly use some to reach the basements of buildings they plan to rob -- and of an ork government and a huge lore library at the center of the city. Some believe radical and criminal ork elements use racial prejudice as cover to build an impenetrable fortress beneath the streets. Rumor also places an ork underground city in Tacoma, where orks fleeing the Night of Rage escaped through the sewers.

[2060 – later developments] After every other entrance to the Renraku Arcology is sealed, the Underground's tunnel into the arcology's B4 parking garage becomes the Resistance's only route for moving rescued prisoners out and help in. Orks guard it around the clock, it is rigged with explosives, and access is jealously controlled: outsiders need strong ork contacts or a voucher, real compensation, and motives the mayor and elders judge more than mercenary, and the Underground holds visitors responsible if it is compromised.

[2061 – later developments] Guides Slant and Tholm lead runners through two hours of sewers and forgotten basements to a cavern where four trolls guard the final passage; on any trouble beyond it, they blow the tunnel. Deus has known about the route for some time and watches it quietly.

[2064 – later developments] Hunted through the city by Deus, runners follow the ork Node Kiva down the sewers with drones on their heels, until the Underground's homemade firepower -- and its own scores to settle with Deus -- takes the drones down; the Underground keeps Kiva safe and wants to know what becomes of her. The fixer Willy Daltree has worked the Underground for more than twenty years, deliberately low-key, related to a great many of its people, and many ork and troll runners got their first job through him. An Or'zet flyer calling the Underground to unite against its oppressors and Humanis carries a password to a new secret section where a militant ork and troll policlub is forming.

locations.name: Sorayama's Clinic (Chiba)
locations.description: Sorayama's clinic in Chiba -- 'the center of hot cyberware' -- belongs to a brilliant, eccentric street doc whose work leaves everything else in the dust. He does about fifty modifications a year at three to five times normal prices, treats his skill as an art, and signs only his 'Ultra' masterpieces, each a unique job, about 120 to date.
locations.notes: Rumor says much of his borderline work turns people into toys for corporate clients, like human bonsai trees. Ultra #84, done in 2044, was Maria Aguilar -- Maria Mercurial -- rebuilt for Reynaldo Texamachach with a sealed memory space, a datajack routed through her pleasure and pain centers, and ten days of forced custom-chip exposure. Her file sits in the clinic's samurai-castle Matrix host, and an Aztechnology representative recently had a copy delivered to Kyle Morgan. The R&D store holds eight cybermod design files; Sorayama hunts thieves through his Yakuza connections, and can call a Yakuza-affiliated 'Major League' decker crew to defend the host.

locations.name: The Barrens (Seattle)
locations.description: The Barrens are the sprawling slums ringing Seattle proper -- chiefly the Redmond Barrens in the east and the Puyallup Barrens in the south -- blighted, high-crime districts served by small neighborhood banks. Lone Star patrols are few and far between, gangs control the streets, and the newsnets steer clear until something gets too big to ignore. Redmond has the razor-guy dives, the rent-a-hideout industrial parks and the slum that grew up around the shuttered Perfekto Polymers plant; Puyallup has lain under ash, smog and despair since the Ghost Dancers blew the volcanoes, burying what was a suburb thirty-five years ago.
locations.notes:
Seattle's own heart of darkness includes The Armadillo and other razor-guy dives, the cheap brothel where Hernandez found Maria singing a cantamuerte, and the Taetzel Building. New Horizons Development made a quiet land grab here after the waste-dumping scandal. A murder spree and a gang war terrorize the Redmond Barrens' working girls and boys: Blood Rumblers ride through Crimson Crush turf, 'Khan Rules' goes up on the walls, and five Lone Star cars arrive in five minutes once the killings make the news. The Redmond/Bellevue border along Cascade Road is the decker fringe. 'It's not like when that werewolf was prowling the streets last year.'

[2051 – later developments] Nearly a hundred Barrens street people vanish in a few weeks, taken through manholes for Craft's hive; the street blames 'some cult'. In Puyallup, Jefferson runs through Asphalt Devil turf to Black's Junk Yard; in Redmond, the Sophocles neighborhood holds Topal's Guiding Hand and the Lochlann land nobody develops. The Cobalt Marie hides beneath a basement door near NE 75th and 151st Avenue NE, and the Redmond Arms Hotel rots among dog-sized rats on the Barrens' western edge. Redmond's landmarks include the Pink Pitbull, Wildfire's Fantasy Arcade in the thrill-gang heartland, Bloom's Troll Emporium, the Redmond Grand Hotel on its overgrown hill, and the Redmond Center Mall at the prosperous Bellevue edge; Lone Star takes about thirty minutes to answer a Barrens alarm. Hollywood, Kingsgate (Superdad's and the Universal Brotherhood chapterhouse) and Touristville are Redmond neighborhoods. The Young Elven Technologists keep their hall in an old Puyallup fire station, and Tarislar and the Southwind ruins lie on Puyallup's southern edge.

[2053 – later developments] In Redmond's Bargain Basement, half-squatted tenements with dead elevators house Half-Ace in flat 17J and Father Roe's youth shelter; during the gang war weapons are nearly free on the streets, with discounts for anyone hitting the Ancients.

[2054 – later developments] The ISSV picks Super Brawl zones in 'officially uninhabited' Barrens neighborhoods full of SINless squatters -- this year Kingsgate in Redmond.

[2055 – later developments] The Puyallup slum called Hope -- ruined buildings and duct-taped prefab modules, no addresses, no inspectors, no cops -- shelters people who want to disappear. Under the whole sprawl the sewers hold ghoul enclaves, the Lost Boys and the blind mage Alegheri, and the city's ghoul bounty sends gangs like the Iron Legion down the manholes. Project Hope runs relief camps in Glow City, and about 110 people disappear in and around the Redmond Barrens this year. The Ork Rights Committee's Redmond storefront is shot up, six dead, and Alamos 20,000 is blamed.

[2059 – later developments] A possessed Reginald Disball runs a pack of paranimal dogs near Hollywood, and Hollywood Hospital reports a spike in dog-bite cases. On 11 July, Flight 1118, a Tokyo-Seattle semiballistic, overshoots Sea-Tac and crashes into the Redmond Barrens, killing about 200 people and burning for more than a day.

locations.name: Matchstick's
locations.description: Matchstick's is a low-profile, members-only jazz club favored by runners, on the substreet level of an office building near the Space Needle. You enter as a member or a member's guest, and new members need a sponsor. A stairway leads down to a comfortably furnished bar done up like a jazz joint of a century ago, holding 70 to 100 people, and a door at the far end opens on a second stair and a white door: the private meeting room. The doorman, Saint John, a former street samurai with a photographic memory and an imposing presence, lets guests keep their weapons but makes clear that violence inside will not be tolerated.
locations.notes:
Eve Donovan briefs the Silver Angel team in the white-door room; the password is 'Steward'. The club serves as neutral ground for fixers' meetings.

[2053 – later developments] Ellen Donnelly, a woman with shadow-market and syndicate ties, dies when her Saab Dynamit explodes outside at 23:45; Lone Star calls it a professional hit and has no leads.

[2057 – later developments] Karl Brackhaven's go-between 'Mr. Smith' meets runners here to buy their silence.

[2060 – later developments] Banshee, working as Telestrian Industries' handler, hires runners here for the Portland job that opens the frame-up against Saeder-Krupp.

[2064 – later developments] Rose Croix CEO Walter Broward hires runners in the back room at 2:30 a.m., after closing; an ork bouncer lets them in on sight.

locations.name: The Kingdome
locations.description: The Kingdome is Seattle's domed stadium. Urban brawl games draw the crowds, pro bikers perform here, and when the Mariners win their fans storm the outer bunkers.
locations.notes:
[2051 – later developments] The field is repaired after extensive fire damage at the Battle of the Super Bruisers, ahead of the next weekend's Panzer Pull; later the dome closes for repairs after the troll Red Death gang of Puyallup gets inside and does considerable damage.

[2053 – later developments] The Shadows play their single Seattle show here: 65,000 tickets, hundreds of them counterfeit, sell out in an hour, ten people die and fourteen go missing at ticket offices across the plex, and scalped seats run from 250 nuyen to a thousand or two, with Knight Errant on security. Mariners owner Jerome Einsdorff seeks changes in Kingdome management and denies the team will move to Oakland. Shield Wall ends its tour here.

[2057 – later developments] Arthur Vogel's campaign rally, and Alan Riv's attempted mass poisoning, happen at a stadium called 'the Superdome', most likely the Kingdome.

locations.name: Council Island
locations.description: Council Island, formerly Mercer Island, in the middle of Lake Washington, is Salish-Shidhe Council territory and the site of the Council's embassy to Seattle. A beautiful, wooded spot reminiscent of the land centuries ago, it has about 3,000 permanent residents, swelled by half again by the daily tourists, and most of its buildings are, or look like, rough-hewn log. Visitors need the same visas and travel passes as for the nation proper, and come by the guarded ferry docks or the I-90 crossing. The island has its own police, and is home to the Grand Council Lodge and the Council Island Inn; the Salish-Shidhe Council Lodge here issues visas.
locations.notes:
The ambassador to Seattle and Chief of Council Island is Jon Moses, seconded by Lady Laura Drywell of the Wenatchee elf tribe; he mediates skilfully between Governor Schultz's people and the Council.

[2051 – later developments] The island hosts the Salish-Shidhe Council's special open session in October. Every visitor's credstick is checked and person scanned, and obvious cyberlimbs are disabled or the visitor turned away; Council Island Police, Metroplex Guard, Rangers, Yellowjackets and SAM teams make it 'the big leagues'. Council security hangs up on runners' warnings.

[2061 – later developments] Council Island is guarded by the Salish-Shidhe Council Armed Forces rather than police. Land access is through two heavily fortified I-90 off-ramps, West Council Drive and Island Crest Way, with the interstate walled on both sides against go-gangs, so the water route is far easier: six Seacop boats patrol the lake by eye, not radar, concentrating around Burbank Park, and a combat alert brings the rest plus an astrally projecting shaman. Everyone on the island works for the embassy, the wildlife preserve, the government or Gaeatronics. The annual Qatuwas Festival at Burbank Park, sundown to sunup, is one of the few times non-natives can visit legitimately.

locations.name: Elven District (Denny Park)
locations.description: The elven district north-northeast of Denny Park, framed by Dexter, Aurora, Harrison, Republican, Thomas and Denny Way with the monorail running along Dexter, is the Ancients' home territory and the front line of their turf war with the Meat Junkies. It is not to be confused with Tarislar, the elven district of Puyallup.
locations.notes: Sting grew up here and knows it better than anyone. The shooting at the KTXX truce parley happened here.

locations.name: Glow City (Redmond Barrens)
locations.description: Glow City, in the Redmond Barrens deep in the sprawl's blighted east, is burnt-out houses, cars stripped to their frames, street people shambling in rags, and walls under so many layers of gang paint that no insignia can be told from the next. Buses and cabs stopped running here years ago. Project Hope's relief camps sit inside it behind electrified fences, growing orchards in trucked-in soil over the Mount St. Helens ash, and a large complex of natural caves known to the UCAS Geological Service runs underneath.
locations.notes:
The bus from Seneca Street takes over half an hour, sealed, unventilated and nauseatingly hot. About 110 people have gone missing in and around the Redmond Barrens this year -- 'a normal 30 percent increase' -- and Lone Star reinforces Redmond generally but declines to step up in Glow City.

[2060 – later developments] The Rusted Stilettos claim the territory near Glow City along Route 202.

[2061 – later developments] Since the Glow City incident in Redmond, regulations bar new nuclear plants in populated parts of Seattle, leaving Shiawase Atomics no way to expand except through Salish-Shidhe land.

[2064 – later developments] Ares Arms' hidden insect-spirit research facility sits just off Redmond Fall City Road, dangerously close to Glow City, among ruins from the riots of the early 2000s now serving as makeshift homes; its guards trade rumors about mutants exposed to the Glow and aliens from the crashed suborbital.

locations.name: Mount Saint Helens
locations.description: Mount Saint Helens, about 150 kilometers south of Seattle in Salish-Shidhe Council lands, has erupted twice in living memory: in the 1970s, and again in 2017. The fissures and caverns left by the 2017 lava gases on the north slope are a tour stop with Parks Department lighting. The Salish-Shidhe Council runs daily bus tours -- 50 nuyen, three hours each way, four hours on site, small bags searched at the border -- for visitors with a one-day visa from the Council Lodge on Council Island.
locations.notes: [2051 – later developments] The mountain erupts a third time, blowing its top and going quiet, leaving fresh ash and rock on the slopes and a changed profile near the peak. Council troopers and guardsmen cannot cordon the whole area. The eruption was Ehran's magically controlled geothermal system venting when his spell rebounded. Beyond the tourist caverns, lava passages lead to a one-meter stone bridge over a river of molten rock, guarded by an Embracer, and a cleanly carved tunnel that was never natural; the illusions hiding the sanctum still hold. Afterward, Althain cannot be found again.

locations.name: Chicago Containment Zone (Bug City)
locations.description: The Chicago Containment Zone is the part of Chicago overrun by insect spirits in August 2055 and sealed behind the Wall: a barricade of demolished buildings, fencing, razor wire and guard towers ringing the city, with land, water, air and astral approaches all controlled, and UCAS Army units under shoot-on-sight orders for anyone crossing in either direction.
locations.notes:
Getting in means flying past sensors and powerful elementals under an astral combat mage, climbing the debris Wall past sentries with assault rifles and grenade launchers, or crossing the frozen lake in winter past Navy sensor buoys. Inside, the Zone has fractured into hostile enclaves -- the Volk, Ghoultown, and the Desolation Angels' turf around the fallen Sears Tower, the Shattergraves -- with scarcity, barter, disinformation, radiation, strange magical conditions, havens and warlords.

[2058 – later developments] The quarantine is formally lifted, but the former Zone remains isolated and dangerous, with refugees, gangs, warlords, Strain-III effects and reports of surviving insects.

locations.name: Site of the Great Ghost Dance
locations.district: A remote desert in the Southwestern United States (real-world site of the Great Ghost Dance ritual)
locations.description: The site of the Great Ghost Dance is an otherwise unremarkable stretch of hard desert in the American Southwest, reached from the highway by dirt track and then on foot. Nothing grows there.
locations.notes: The blood-magic cost of the Ghost Dance -- the deaths of many of its own dancers -- permanently raised the local background magic to a level the rest of the world will not reach for a thousand years, drawing the world-devouring Enemy across the metaplanes centuries ahead of schedule. Astral perception here can severely stun anyone who tries it, and the site greatly amplifies shamanic magic while weakening other traditions. Harlequin opens the astral quest here.

locations.name: Zurich-Orbital
locations.description: Zurich-Orbital, formerly the Freedom station, is the seat of the Corporate Court: a zero-gravity habitat of residence tubes, medical and exercise facilities, kitchens, entertainment areas, life support, docking and communications, with the Court's chambers and the Zurich-Orbital Gemeinschaft Bank at its center. Life aboard is a constant series of tradeoffs against the vacuum outside, and officials who can afford otherwise spend as little time there as duty demands.
locations.notes:
The station 'de-cloaks' from its usual communications posture only for Court business, and access is tightly controlled. Mir, sometimes called Wheelchair, was a separate predecessor that was destroyed.

[2059 – later developments] The Court convenes aboard in person for urgent business; an eighteen-hour communications blackout in June produces the ruling that sends Miles Lanier back to Fuchi custody. The Zurich-Orbital Gemeinschaft Bank holds the Renraku stock Lanier sold and Shikei Nakatomi bought back.

[2064 – later developments] The Corporate Court Crisis Coordination Committee runs the 1 November strikes on Valhalla and Hel from the station's Crisis Room. At 09:42 on 2 November Chairman Lynn Osborne orders all earth-based communications cut, suspending the station's sysop Atropos; a minute later Atropos and Clothos break isolation anyway, accidentally killing their colleague Lachesis, and broadcast the full C5 transcript to every station and the Denver Nexus. Leonard Aurelius is rumored to be preparing to retire here.

locations.name: Shibanokuji
locations.district: Yamatetsu orbital resort and research station
locations.description: Shibanokuji is Yamatetsu's orbital station: officially a party in orbit and a big tourist attraction, the hottest place to watch the comet, and a recuperation spot where some very big names have been patched up in low gravity. It also carries a genuine zero-g medical research lab, and apart from the sightseeing decks, access to the working parts of the station is very tight.
locations.notes: The zero-g lab shares data with Yamatetsu's quiet Everett subsidiary Alaxa over a dedicated satellite link on the same private LTG as the Gagarin mission and Yamatetsu's other classified space projects. The uplink fires once an hour while the station is overhead, in one-minute bursts. Other corps would love a competing platform, or an excuse to cause this one a problem.

locations.name: The Shasta Enclave
locations.description: The Shasta Enclave is the land the great dragon Hestaby has claimed and defended for years, dominated by Mount Shasta, one of the tallest mountains in North America, snow-capped almost always and watching over everything for miles. Interstate 5 runs through the middle and traffic is allowed, so a low-profile visitor can drive as far as Mount Shasta City, a town of a few thousand with a far larger transient population of gypsy tribes and families settling for weeks or months at a time. Around it the Northern Crescent is embattled, close to the Tir, with marauding gangs on the roads and anti-metahuman feeling running high -- but not inside the enclave, which is pointedly tolerant. The wilderness on the mountain is primal, mystical and a little frightening.
locations.notes: Radar and bound air elementals and wind spirits stop any aircraft not escorted by one of the enclave's spirits, forcing it down and engaging astral intruders; lost spirits are replaced within hours, and every intrusion is reported to the lodge and to Hestaby. Aircraft must land outside and cover the last forty-odd miles overland. Eyekillers, griffins, icedrakes, perytons, piasma, thunderbirds and horned bears roam the slopes.

locations.name: Denver Sector Walls and Checkpoints
locations.district: The UCAS / CAS sector boundary, Front Range Free Zone
locations.description: Denver's sectors are divided by walls and fences, and anyone crossing between them -- or arriving by air or rail -- needs a pass and has their identity verified. Procedure varies sharply from sector to sector.
locations.notes: [2062 – later developments] Since Ghostwalker took over, the nations that claim Denver have understood how vulnerable they are, and between terrorists and political dissidents border security has tightened until a shadowrunner can hardly make a dishonest living. The Free Zone is now more like five different cities walled off from each other and patrolled by paranoid, trigger-happy troops. The walls protecting the UCAS and CAS sectors are at least five meters of reinforced ferrocrete topped with concertina wire; at the checkpoints, vehicles queue while guards check identification, and anyone who fails is pulled from line, detained and searched, with backup within a minute. A captive like Morningstar is a liability here: unsedated he can cast, and even bound, gagged and blindfolded he can project astrally and manifest in the queue screaming for help. Runners captured at the wall are pulled out of custody by Ghostwalker and brought to his lair.

locations.name: Wuxing Skytower
locations.description: The Wuxing Skytower, the corporation's headquarters, is one of the tallest and best-protected buildings on the Hong Kong skyline. It stands on a power site, and its top floor is nothing like a corporate office: light falls through angled glass across a veined marble floor, calligraphy scrolls hang beside hexagonal mirrors in red lacquer, and at the center, inside a circle of raked gravel, a square pool of lotus and fish is crossed by a wooden footbridge bearing a jade carving of three leaping fish. It holds a five-storey marble ritual hall.
locations.notes: [2062 – later developments] Wu Lung-Wei intensified the site with Dunkelzahn's bequest, the Jade Dragon of Wind and Fire, and it has drawn more and more chi ever since, Wuxing's star rising with it; even mundanes feel the barely restrained energy on the top floor. The penthouse is reached by an executive elevator whose passcode only senior executives know, an alarmed stairwell, or from outside by the rooftop helipad; cameras catch anything bigger than a bird, three bound air elementals patrol outside, and the area is an astral shallow where astral forms are visible even to mundanes.

locations.name: East Coast Stock Exchange
locations.description: The neo-gothic East Coast Stock Exchange stands in the center of downtown Boston, a church to the Almighty Nuyen. Built after the catastrophic New York earthquake, it revitalized Boston and set off a boom in corporate business across the downtown sprawl. A traditional market floor still sits beneath massive displays and holographic tickers, but most trading happens on its virtual floor. Security is critical and entirely in-house -- deckers hired straight out of Boston's universities, security techniques fresh from MIT&T, and physical and magical staff answering only to the Board of Directors.
locations.notes:
The host is layered: the public trading floor must admit countless traders, while the higher levels are guarded by specialized IC and reached only by security deckers with limited random passkeys. It is smart and adaptive, senses even small tampering, and will shut itself down and close trading if it decides data is being manipulated.

[2064 – later developments] On Novatech's IPO day the Exchange unveils a new host built by Matrix Systems of Boston, an immense gothic church whose chancel holds a trading floor that dwarfs any physical one. At 09:16 on 2 November Deus exploits backdoors his Nodes planted, closes the host to the outside and trips it into ultraviolet, plunging thousands of logged-in users into a Matrix more real than reality; staff cannot issue commands and cut the host offline physically at 09:41. Deus, Megaera, Mirage, Ronin's Nodes, Dodger and the otaku all converge here.

locations.name: Freeway Park
locations.description: Freeway Park is one of the few green spots in the heart of Downtown, spread over several blocks on a deck above I-5, the busiest road in the metroplex, so the traffic arrives strangely muted. Towering buildings surround it, giving countless vantage points, and the Renraku Arcology looms over everything. Big plascrete planters of flower beds, shrubs and small trees keep sightlines short and cover plentiful, and interactive audio-visual units recite facts about the plants, Downtown landmarks and Convention Center events to anyone who comes near. At lunchtime it fills with wage slaves, tourists, SURGE cases, teens and the armored suits from the security trade show at the adjacent Seattle Trade and Convention Center. Lone Star polices it on the cheap with probationary officers.
locations.notes: Cameras and sensors everywhere feed the park host, but it is not watched constantly, only by pattern-recognition alerts; opening an audio-visual unit gives a dataline tap into the host. Residents include Scarper the Mouse shaman and a free field spirit that appears as a skateboarding girl and amuses itself with Accident.

locations.name: Stuck's Carnival
locations.description: Stuck's Carnival is a chipped-out casino serving working-class Auburn, with a bar, a restaurant, reading material on urban brawl and combat biking, and back rooms offering more sordid ways to spend a win.
locations.notes: [2064 – later developments] It is Griffin researcher Don Kukalakee's regular house, and not by accident: Paladin has been paying off his gambling debts, and even paying him to gamble, with the payments made here, well away from Everett. When he wins he blows it all at the bar, the restaurant or on Zoe. This is where the badge and keycode almost certainly changed hands, and where he is most easily found, watched and leaned on; Griffin's security, watching for his gambling in Everett, has never caught the leak.

locations.name: Downtown Seattle
locations.description: Downtown is Seattle's main business district, about half a million people across some 470 square kilometers, and not just a forest of skyscrapers rampant with crime: shops, parks, theaters, museums and hotels are sprinkled through it, and on weekends the sidewalks are packed with people in from the outlying districts to shop and have a good time -- even during a Stage Red smog alert, when they wear breathers. The rain is acid enough to pit buildings and ruin clothes, but it scrubs the air, and with the west winds keeps Seattle's air some of the cleanest on the continent; the city still averages about sixty Stage Red alerts a year.
locations.notes: The quaint shops are fine, assuming nobody lobs a firebomb into one while you're inside.

locations.name: Bellevue
locations.description: Bellevue has always been the favorite retreat of Seattle's rich and powerful. Its forested hills, where people once built homes away from the downtown crowds, have long since traded their trees for forests of apartment towers, but the district keeps its air of pristine beauty. Its wealth comes from computers and microtronics: Microdeck has its offices here, and Fuchi keeps important business and research facilities. Nearly nine in ten of its 209,000 residents have a corporate affiliation.

locations.name: Tacoma
locations.description: For decades Tacoma lived in the shadow of downtown Seattle -- blue collar to Seattle's white, polluting smelters and paper mills to Seattle's skyscrapers, the butt of jokes about 'Tacoma's Aroma'. Now its day has come: since 2039 the megacorps have been buying up land at an unprecedented rate, new skyscrapers are rising and freighters crowd its expanded port. The charming turn-of-the-century downtown has been meticulously preserved, along with many reminders of the Night of Rage. About 375,000 people live here.
locations.notes: In most of Seattle the Mafia and Yakuza fight on even terms, but in Tacoma the Yakuza dominate and the Mafia is reduced to the minor role usually left to the Seoulpa Rings. Twenty-two years ago Waino Aho, then a mid-level clan accountant, secretly bought up cheap Tacoma property with Yakuza money while everyone else was buying downtown and in Bellevue.

locations.name: Everett
locations.description: Everett -- 'Seattle North' to some -- is proving false its reputation as the backwoods district. Once dependent on the naval shipyard and the Federated-Boeing assembly lines, it is attracting large corporate investors and developers and building a more diverse economy; it no longer wants to be known only for ships, planes and stormy weather. About 229,000 people live here.
locations.notes: Neither the Mafia nor the Yakuza has ever thought much of Everett as a market. The Mafia, under Gerard Vigilia, a trusted confidant of Don James O'Malley, runs the illegal gambling and prostitution of Casino Corner, the district's only red-light zone; the Yakuza control the commercial docks and some small businesses. With Everett growing, both remember how the Yakuza bought up Tacoma just before it boomed, and a rise in Mafia-Yakuza clashes on the southern edge of Casino Corner points to a syndicate war.

locations.name: Renton
locations.description: Some say Renton is one big apartment complex where Seattle goes home to sleep, but it offers more. Its hills are the highest in the city, with breathtaking views of the plex and Mount Rainier, and it has fish-stocked lakes, places to shop and dine that are pleasantly empty by day, and several well-known nightclubs. Its 218,000 residents are among the plex's better-off.

locations.name: Auburn
locations.description: 'Simple pleasures for simple people' is how Auburn describes itself. Most of its 218,000 people work hard in the district's factories and play just as hard afterward: weekend baseball and urban brawl -- the Auburn Cardinals and the Auburn Rubblers are the best amateur teams -- the gyms, the races at the Seattle International Raceway, and a great many bars and nightclubs at night.
locations.notes: Crime is high, especially in the south, where squatters from the Puyallup Barrens work as pickpockets and house thieves.

locations.name: Snohomish
locations.description: Snohomish, with its fertile farmland, flowers and wide open spaces, is a startling contrast to downtown's concrete, and its people are known for their friendliness. The Seattle government has done everything it can to preserve the farmland, even vetoing housing that might ease the metroplex's shortage, because Snohomish crops save the city much of the cost of importing food. With few people, no heavy industry and high employment, it has one of the lowest crime rates in the plex.
locations.notes: Illegal chips, prostitution and gambling are confined to the more populated south, and the syndicates have virtually no other foothold. What Snohomish does have is racial tension: some local police make no secret of blaming metahumans and Indians, and will not go out of their way to protect them.

locations.name: Redmond
locations.description: Redmond -- the Redmond Barrens -- is one of Seattle's two great slums, home to half a million people. Once evergreen forest and farmland, it grew into a suburban sea of apartment complexes and then, around the turn of the century, a center of the computer and information industry, dotted with office complexes and skyscrapers. The Crash of '29 wiped that out almost overnight: eighty percent of the district's businesses collapsed. Only Touristville, around the district Capitol Building near Bellevue, is developed and orderly. Elsewhere lie the Rat's Nest dump, the Plastic Jungles -- twenty huge abandoned greenhouses, several kilometers across, now home to much of the district's metahuman squatter population -- and Glow City.
locations.notes: Rumors blamed metahumans for the disaster, and human supremacy groups -- Humanis, the KKK, The Order -- flourish here; many Redmond metahumans have banded together to fight back. The few companies with factories here have had to fortify them against looters, some hiring the biggest and meanest squatters as guards. Neither the Mafia nor the Yakuza makes much money in Redmond, but both run black markets and treat it as a breeding ground for warriors and thieves; the Yakuza are adept at spotting future fighters and magicians and training them.

locations.name: Puyallup
locations.description: Puyallup, a thousand square kilometers and half a million people, is Seattle's other Barrens. Mount Rainier's eruption on 17 August 2017 buried its farmland and apple orchards under tons of ash; a year later thousands of non-Indians fleeing the Native American takeover of the West settled on the ash, and after the Night of Rage tens of thousands of metahumans sought refuge here. Squatter camps stretch across it, but its black lava fields have a haunting beauty, and several corporations have lately taken an interest -- Mitsuhama has announced plans for a major plant. The tidy, middle-class Puyallup neighborhood around the district Capitol Building belies the poverty elsewhere; visitors are advised to come only on an escorted Metro Transit tour.
locations.notes: The Puyallup neighborhood's relative prosperity owes much to syndicate money in the hands of government officials.

locations.name: San Francisco
locations.description: San Francisco lives under Japanese protection. When the California Free State declared independence in 2037 the city was already wracked by disease, famine and upheaval, and when Japan recognized the new state, Japanese Imperial Marines arrived in strength, with a naval task force within striking distance, 'to protect Japanese lives and property' -- at the request of a governor who feared invasion by the Tir and Aztlan. The occupation has become an accepted fact of life. The Imperial Marines are the real authority: grim, silent and heavily armed, they man every checkpoint in and out of the city and check passes more thoroughly than the SFPD. Corporate police enforce their employers' holdings, Renraku's Red Samurai most notoriously. Weapons, adult simsense, BTLs, cigarettes and liquor are illegal or heavily taxed, and anyone without a job or valid travel pass is a vagrant subject to summary expulsion. Metahumans meet much prejudice, orks and trolls at the bottom. For all that, the Japanese have kept it one of the most beautiful cities in the world.
locations.notes:
Travelers are advised never to offer the Imperial Marines a bribe or back-talk. The governor has had to roll the Marines out of the Presidio to quell disturbances more than once in the last decade. Smugglers run the bay in hovercraft, fast boats and light aircraft.

[2057 – later developments] San Francisco is an occupied corporate enclave with a major airport, harbor, technology and transit, and active resistance.
locations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

locations.name: Los Angeles
locations.description: Los Angeles, despite severe depopulation by VITAS, is still the media capital, the leading producer of simsense and trideo; any aspiring actor, writer or director must do time in L.A. to succeed. Its society is as permissive and decadent as ever, with massive dreamchip abuse, debauchery and drinking the rule among the upper class. Beyond the urban core the go-gangs rule, fighting turf wars of ever-increasing severity, with the poor and homeless caught in the middle.
locations.notes: [2057 – later developments] Los Angeles, a Free City since 2046, is a patchwork of corporate enclaves, industrial districts, entertainment centers and neglected communities.
locations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

locations.name: Sacramento
locations.description: Sacramento is still the seat of the California Free State's government, where the President and an American-style Congress wrestle with the issues of the day while ignoring the fact that their authority barely extends beyond the San Joaquin Valley. Outlying counties and towns are left to their own defense, and the frontier-style remote communities are a law unto themselves; the Sacramento government rarely bothers them, having more problems than it can handle, including a cold war with Tir Tairngire in the north.
locations.notes: [2057 – later developments] Sacramento remains the capital and a transport, customs and political center, with an anti-metahuman climate; its government information systems, UTA operations and Matrix infrastructure are in transition.
locations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

locations.name: Atlanta
locations.description: Atlanta, capital of the Confederated American States, is a sprawl of more than six million people, nearly a quarter of them orks. Unlike most sprawls, it runs its own civic services -- police, sanitation and transportation -- under an elected mayor, Drew Anderson, and a city council, contracting out only fire control, to Franklin Associates. It is also home to the Georgia state government. Its neighborhoods range from Downtown and Buckhead to Decatur, Marietta, Norcross and Southtown.
locations.notes: [2054 – later developments] Lone Star keeps a Military Liaison office in Atlanta. Claims about mercenary forces, transferred assets and the national capital as camouflage are unconfirmed.
locations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

locations.name: Dallas/Ft. Worth
locations.description: Dallas/Fort Worth is the linked metroplex at the heart of Texas, near enough to the Aztlan border to feel it. In 2011 thousands of refugees from the bloody collapse of the Mexican government crossed into Texas, most of them ending up in San Antonio, Austin and DFW; the influx broke an already crumbling welfare and housing system, shanty towns sprang up under highway bridges, racial violence and crime soared, the police struck, and the governor called in the National Guard while residents lived under siege. Today the metroplex is shaped by corporate habitats, regional transport and that history.
locations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

locations.name: Quebec City
locations.description: Quebec City is the capital of the Republic of Quebec. Its sprawl is like any post-industrial city's, but its center is unique, because the Quebecois cherish their history -- the national motto is 'Je me souviens', 'I remember'. La Citadelle, a huge bastioned fort 85 meters above the St. Lawrence, is now the headquarters of Quebec's Defense Force; walls still surround parts of Upper Town; and the castle-like Chateau Frontenac, built as a hotel, is the official residence of the President and his advisors. Beyond the Old Town and the Latin Quarter lie modern government, manufacturing, corporate enterprise zones and a rough working waterfront in the Lower Town.
locations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

locations.name: Federal District of Columbia
locations.description: The Federal District of Columbia is the UCAS capital region, a multi-region sprawl of about 3.4 million people built around the business of government. Congress ousted the District's own government in 2003 amid charges of corruption, and by 2024 the economy of the whole Delaware-Maryland-Virginia intersection was dominated by government and the private industry around it. Its regional governments -- Arlington, Fairfax, Howard and the rest -- mix upper-class residential enclaves, office districts, federal offices such as the Pentagon, AAA-rated airports and the extremely high-security Lorton prison complex.
locations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

locations.name: Chicago
locations.description: Chicago -- the Windy City, or Wind City to the locals -- is a major UCAS trade and manufacturing city whose districts divide corporate power, heavy industry, simsense production, poverty and organized crime. O'Hare International is the busiest airport in the world and the hub of North American passenger and cargo traffic, so busy that the O'Hare Sub-Sprawl has grown up around it in the middle of the city; security there has been very tight since the assassination of a German chancellor. The weather changes every five minutes, which some mages in Little Earth blame on mischievous free elementals along Lake Michigan.
locations.notes:
So many runners are fed up with the situation in Chicago that they do part of the job as charity -- 'hooding', stealing from the rich to give to the poor -- and sometimes dig up dirt for the aldermen who are almost straight.

[2055 – later developments] Chicago's districts are the Elevated, the Core, the O'Hare Sub-Sprawl, Northside, Westside and Southside. Its underworld sees a renewed Yakuza-Mafia rivalry, the Noose community and shifting crime networks. From August to December an insect-spirit outbreak brings Matrix isolation, quarantine behind a wall, military action, a supply crisis and the consolidation of factions inside.

[2058 – later developments] Operation Extermination and the formal end of the quarantine leave Chicago physically, politically and magically unstable. Ares' claims of a clean sweep and reports of surviving insects contradict each other.
locations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

locations.name: New York City
locations.description: Manhattan is the legal City of New York. Rebuilt after the 2005 earthquake under a corporate consortium, it is controlled through an elaborate pass system. Its air is foul: pollution blows in from New Jersey, Pennsylvania and the offshore garbage facilities, and though cold air from Canada usually holds it off, in summer it settles right on the city, so visitors pack an aspirator with fresh filters.
locations.source_adventure: The Neo-Anarchist's Guide to North America

locations.name: Las Vegas
locations.description: Las Vegas, in the Ute Nation, remains the largest single site dedicated to gambling in the world. Gambling is allowed elsewhere in the Ute Nation under strict law, but in Vegas almost anything goes -- even rigged games, as long as the fix is no more than 1 percent, and the casino must prove it or lose its license. The city is run by a city governor and City Council appointed from Provo, and policed by the Las Vegas Metropolitan Police, who are more heavily armed than police elsewhere in Ute and gear up like shock troops when things get heavy. Five Judiciary Councils mean one is always open.
locations.notes: The governor's letter of office may come from Provo, but the street says Vegas is really run by a Mafia lackey, and the Mafia has a death grip on every gambling concern in the city.

locations.name: Salt Lake City
locations.description: Salt Lake City -- the 'Salt Lake Empire', depending on who you talk to -- is an autonomous Mormon enclave within the Ute Nation. It has no border guards, and anyone may enter, live and look for work, but few non-Mormons are employed there, because the faithful prefer to hire their own. It has its own Brigham Young University campus with a good academic reputation, which non-Mormons call 'Saint U', and one of the Ute Nation's three major international airports.

locations.name: Provo
locations.description: Provo is the capital of the Ute Nation and a major center of its government and economy, with one of the nation's three major international airports, able to take suborbital and semiballistic traffic.

locations.name: Cheyenne
locations.description: Cheyenne is the capital and principal seat of government of the Sioux Nation.

locations.name: Santa Fe
locations.description: Santa Fe is the capital of the Pueblo Corporate Council, with one of the most modern and efficient international airports in North America, perhaps the world: suborbital and semiballistic flights on dependable schedules, and Vega flights to the Skyport orbital stations for those with government authorization. The nation's 'Airlink' network of small auto-piloted aircraft has pads in and around almost every population center.

locations.name: Denver
locations.description: Denver is a divided international city. Under the Treaty of Denver its six regions are each policed by the security forces of one of the Council nations, and the city is governed jointly through the Council of Denver. The Treaty forbids any country to levy tariffs or taxes on Denver, so that no one nation can gouge the city -- and the unforeseen result is a free port unlike any other. Each sector's security will detain traders carrying contraband that threatens its own nation, but the neighboring sector may not care, so by entering the right sector a smuggler can deal in almost anything under the noses of officials who would love to stop him. Denver has become the hub of a well-developed smuggling network.
locations.notes:
Sector lines are taken seriously: a Wildcat detachment chasing a smuggler's panzer out of the Sioux sector into Pueblo's was cut down by Pueblo security, which then let the smuggler go once it established he carried nothing Pueblo considered contraband.

[2055 – later developments] Denver is the heart of the Front Range Free Zone, home to most of its 3.6 million people. Public services vary sharply from sector to sector, and the city's own spirit, the Spirit of Denver, is fragmented.

locations.name: Bellingham
locations.description: Bellingham is the nominal capital of the Salish-Shidhe Council, whose monthly Council meetings, usually on the day of the new moon, are held in the Friendship Lodge downtown -- though extraordinary sessions meet almost anywhere, and many important meetings lately have been held on Council Island. Once a sleepy port with a silted-up harbor, Bellingham boomed when its harbor was dredged during the Chaos, then faded again once the nation was formed. Most capitals are bustling, high-energy places; Bellingham is not. Its airport handles medium-range and V/STOL traffic.

locations.name: Vancouver
locations.description: Vancouver is a major Salish-Shidhe port and urban center. Its international airport is one of only a few in the Council able to take the largest suborbital and semiballistic carriers, barely: the main runway runs out onto a causeway into the sea, and heavily loaded planes sometimes roll to a stop with their noses over the Pacific. The Nootka tribe around the port includes many 'pinkskins', non-Amerinds who have fully adopted the native way of life.
locations.notes: The small, vociferous Tsawassen band of pinkskins tried to block the airport's development in 2047 as 'intrusive technology'.

locations.name: London
locations.description: London -- the Smoke, the locals call it, because it has been old and gray for so long -- is a vast, sprawling metropolis of more than 9.7 million people covering hundreds of square miles: Inner London at its center, ringed by large, mostly featureless commuter districts. It is the financial center of Europe, and offers everything from the Stock Market in the City and the Changing of the Guard at Buckingham Palace to the British Museum and the night clubs of the West End. About three-quarters of Londoners are human, with sizable ork and elf populations; nearly half have a corporate affiliation, and a third live below the poverty line. The river divides it: north of the Thames are the financial, shopping and entertainment centers and the best of everything, and south of it is the Squeeze.
locations.notes: What the establishment has never grasped, behind all its heritage and tradition, is that an entire underclass lives in the shadows of London's safe little world. The police do not venture into many parts of the central sprawls, and law there is in the hands of those strong enough to use it.

locations.name: West End Underplex
locations.description: The West End Underplex, built in record time beneath the heart of London, is a four-floor underground shopping complex stretching almost a mile down Regent Street North to Piccadilly. Shops stack four levels high along both sides of a central well under an arched roof hung with lights, figures and plants and pierced by daylight domes, while cafes, restaurants, plazas, playgrounds and exhibitions fill the floor of the well. Visitors learn to treat its halls and malls like streets. Entry is free, and security staff in brown and orange uniforms are on hand to help; most of the people who work there arrive by Tube.
locations.notes: The unarmed security guards were once a joke to the street -- hop the barriers and run for the central wells -- but since striking shop workers occupied the Underplex one Christmas, a new, armed Underplex police division patrols it too.

locations.name: Lambeth Containment Zone
locations.description: The Lambeth Containment Zone -- the Squeeze, or LCZ -- is south London, sealed off. At the turn of the century the neighborhoods south of the Thames were low-class commuter housing and ailing light industry, then vast estates onto which cash-starved councils dumped families. After a number of terrorist outrages, the government used the medical emergency that followed the failure of the Adams-Hoffmann 'Project 42-20' to create the Containment Zone and bring back the rule of law. It has only partly worked, and a state of emergency still holds. Visitors are advised to stay out, or to go only with the appropriate security escort, and an LCZ stamp in a passport invalidates most travel and medical insurance.
locations.notes: The official line undersells it: south London rioted in 1979, '82, '92, '98, 2004, '05, '17 and '21, besides hundreds of lesser disturbances, as councils went bankrupt and businesses fled, and the Metropolitan Police had already needed a special task force for the area long before the Zone.

locations.name: Angel Towers Arcology
locations.description: Angel Towers, on Battersea Park Road, is the arcology headquarters of British Industrial PLC. It is split into a low-rise section to the northwest and the larger 78-storey executive arcology across the road. The 30-storey main block has two levels of underground parking and then three floors of shopping malls selling British Industrial's consumer and electrical goods, while the ground-floor plaza showcases British regional achievements and manufactures to the many millions of curious visitors who come every year.
locations.notes: Reports describe hidden areas and heavy security within the arcology.

locations.name: Castle Harlech
locations.description: Castle Harlech, overlooking Tremadoc Bay in Wales, is the seat of Rhiannon Glendower, the enigmatic Countess of Snowdon, and of her Cyberknights of Glendower. From its spires it is not the Chief Constable but the Countess who holds the reins of power in the Welsh Wild Lands.
locations.notes: Rhiannon's Knights of Harlech were created partly to keep the Templars at bay and to keep Gwynedd safe for metahumans. The Countess uses her personal wiles to win nobles over to Welsh, metahuman and environmental causes, but is neither tactful nor patient; one admirer calls her a true free spirit.

locations.name: Birmingham
locations.description: Birmingham, the industrial district of 3.4 million people, is home to most of Britain's remaining heavy industry -- chemicals, plastics and heavy machine tools -- and British Industrial PLC and Zeta-ImpChem both run large plants here. It is a hideous city: vast swaths are virtually solid concrete, much of it badly corroded, and buildings fall down regularly, often with people inside. Huge inner-city road networks lead into its heart, and the central Bull Ring, a 186-storey concrete monster of shopping malls, cheap offices and coffin hotels, dominates the skyline. Nearly a third of its people live below the poverty line.

locations.name: Merseysprawl
locations.description: Merseysprawl is the vast metropolis of 6.5 million people formed as Liverpool and Manchester fused into one -- to the anger of Mancunians, since the name comes from Liverpool's River Mersey. Liverpool is a port city that now sees very little trade; some light industry remains, but nearly 30 percent of its people are unemployed and its prospects are grim. The government has pumped in aid and 'reclaimed' parts of the inner city, so the unemployed can look at banks of flowers on grassy knolls as they struggle to survive amid torpor and decay.

locations.name: Newcastle / Tynesprawl
locations.description: Newcastle and Tynesprawl, about 1.4 million people in Newcastle alone, is home to the Geordies -- famously hard-drinking, badly dressed, sexist and quick with their fists, but affable, honest and humorous, and cheerful in spite of exceptional pollution. The sprawl sits near the fringes of the Northern Toxic Zone, and 'bleeds' -- eruptions of toxic effluent into the water supply, or subsidence from chemical corrosion -- are commonplace, along with chemical smogs and outbreaks of serious viral disease. A third of its people live below the poverty line.

locations.name: Nottingham
locations.description: Nottingham, the self-styled 'Queen of the Midlands', has avoided being ruined by skyscrapers and heavy industry. Its major industry is armaments, led by Integrated Weapon Systems, whose national headquarters is in the Eastwood suburb, and its elite subdivision Bond & Carrington, which makes customized weapons for top corporate customers; a swarm of small firms work in communications, entertainment and traditions like lace-making. It also has the Sherwood Theme Park, a bewildering mix of Robin Hood nostalgia and paranimal zoo. A large share of its human population is of Asian, Chinese and Afro-Caribbean descent.
locations.notes: The Tongs are active in Nottingham, notably in drugs.

locations.name: Cambridge
locations.description: Cambridge is a major center of research and development. Its wealthy university has a reputation second to none in Europe for life sciences, cyberscience and electronics, and turns public-school products into politicians and civil servants; around it are many research institutes where professors and dons consult on the side. Fuchi Industrial Electronics has its European headquarters here, in a 44-storey habitat three miles north of the city center -- an amazing feat of architecture in a city whose planners allow nothing taller than sixteen storeys.

locations.name: Cardiff / Caerdydd
locations.description: Cardiff, or Caerdydd, is the center of Welsh local government, where the regional Parliament meets, and home to many Welsh national institutions: the National Sports Centre, the Welsh Royal Infirmary -- where researchers eagerly experiment with shamanic and 'alternative' therapies -- Cardiff Arms Park, home of Welsh rugby, and the National Museum of Wales. Cardiff Castle, a fine medieval walled castle, has become a druidic meeting place since a stone circle erupted in its cellars in 2011.

locations.name: Edinburgh
locations.description: Edinburgh is the regional capital of Scotland, whose Parliament meets in the castle on Arthur's Seat. It has a tradition of culture, literature, theatre and the performing arts -- and parochial snobbery, all deserved. Its university's Royal Infirmary is reputed the best all-round medical center in Europe, its neuro-ergonomic labs do advanced skillsoft-implantation research, and its Parapsychology Department teaches occult studies of the highest quality. Edinburgh is also the site of New Tolbooth Prison, the second most important high-security prison in the United Kingdom.

locations.name: Saskatoon
locations.description: Saskatoon is the capital of the Algonkian-Manitou Council, with a large international airport linking it to most of the continent's big cities and commuter flights around the Council. Winters are brutal, with wind chills near -60 degrees.
locations.notes: Airport security is a joke -- yet the Council's per capita rate of violent crime is among the lowest on the continent. The flights are always late.

locations.name: Inuvik
locations.description: Inuvik is the capital of the Trans-Polar Aleut Nation, a loose affiliation of tribal communities living mainly by hunting and fishing; only the Inuvik region has a national economy worthy of the name. The city has half a million residents, several large companies and significant investment in modern technology, and thousands of hectares of tundra around it are covered by a hydroponics and greenhouse project. Sub-sea firms such as Bathotech and Pisces mine and drill the sea floor. Energy is its great problem: a solar array works only half the year, and the city buys most of its power from the Athabascan Council over superconducting lines from a Mackenzie River hydro station.
locations.notes: Bathotech bought enough Soviet technology to start a pilot geothermal plant beneath the ice cap, but it produces negligible power and is unlikely ever to be finished. Plans for a power station and for a dam on a Mackenzie tributary were both killed by public objections.

locations.name: Kitimat
locations.description: Kitimat is the capital of the Tsimshian Nation and home to its one major airport, whose runways are too short for suborbitals; short-haul flights link it to Vancouver, Anchorage, Juneau, Edmonton and Calgary, and Tsimshian Airways connects it to Prince Rupert, Terrace and the nation's other towns. The weather is cold, stormy and depressing: since seven planes went down in storms in 2041, Tsimshian Airways is grounded by law from December to mid-February, and at other times on an hour's notice from the Kitimat weather office.

locations.name: Portland
locations.description: Portland is Tir Tairngire's northern trade city and its principal point of contact with the outside world, and it is walled off from the rest of the country like the Berlin Wall of a century ago. Movement between Portland and the rest of the Tir passes through heavily armed checkpoint stations, the largest -- 'Checkpoint Charlie' -- where Highway 5 meets Durham in West Portland. Ships putting in here must take on a Tir pilot, who is also a mage hunting stowaways, and foreign cargo vessels are held in bond while Tir longshoremen work them and the crews stay aboard. Once the mercantile center of the elven nation, Portland has been demoted to a cargo way station since most international freight moved through Seattle in 2052.
locations.notes: Portland was a boom town in the 2040s; now it has gone bust, fortunes have drained away in bankruptcy, and something stronger than dissatisfaction runs through the city. Why the Council of Princes made a decision that would wreck one of the Tir's major cities, nobody knows.

locations.name: Eugene
locations.description: Eugene is the southern city of the Tir's rebuilt Portland-Salem-Eugene urban axis, governed by an appointed mayor, Malcolm Jenice-Goodine, and seven elected reves.

locations.name: Salem, Tir Tairngire
locations.description: Salem is a city of the Tir's rebuilt Portland-Salem-Eugene axis and was the temporary national capital immediately after independence. Salem Hospital, which once catered to rich elves willing to pay full price to jump the waiting list, has only recently been forced under the Tir's Medical Services Plan.
locations.notes: Many of the hospital's doctors earn far less under the Plan than they did privately, and some perform 'unsanctioned' procedures in its facilities to make up the shortfall; to some extent Salem Hospital has become one big body shop.

locations.name: Crater Lake
locations.description: Crater Lake, perhaps the most fascinating geographical feature in Tir Tairngire, fills the crater of an extinct volcano on the crest of the Cascades just north of Klamath Lake: nearly ten kilometers across and 610 meters deep at its deepest, its surface almost 1,900 meters above sea level, ringed by lava cliffs another 150 to 600 meters high. The island at its center, once Wizard Island, has been officially renamed Tesetelinestea, a name never translated. It is the closest thing the Tir has to a national park; access is not restricted, and many Tir elves revere the lake, giving it some kind of mystical significance. Crowds swarm over it on each solstice.
locations.notes:
Some believe the lake water has magical properties; others insist its shifting blues are beautiful but hold no magic. Street buzz says the Tir government has found orichalcum near the lake, which should be impossible.

[2054 – later developments] From May 2 the area is closed by the military, and nobody gets in and lives without half a dozen high-level authorizations: heavily armed troopers, combat mages, paranormal watchcritters and watcher spirits cover it, a dozen drones patrol the air, one or two Federated-Boeing Eagles orbit overhead, and every reconnaissance satellite that passes has its sensors dazzled by laser until the lake is out of its footprint.

locations.name: Royal Hill
locations.description: Royal Hill is the region beyond the Portland Wall, west of the city, taking in the old districts of Oak Hills and Meadowhurst. Rolling forests hide the palatial estates of the Princes of the Council and others of royal rank and influence. Low wire fences around it look more symbolic than functional, but the greenery hides a sophisticated perimeter of sensor arrays, pressure pads and cameras, and Knight Errant security responds quickly to any unauthorized incursion.
locations.notes: Even a single intruder over the fence brings a whole Knight Errant squad -- six troopers with enough firepower to toast a wizworm -- and larger incursions draw a larger response.

locations.name: Royal Palace
locations.description: The Royal Palace, the capital of Tir Tairngire and the home and working office of the High Prince, crowns a roughly circular hill about three kilometers across that rises 250 meters above the land around it. The complex sprawls over a square kilometer -- ten main buildings and twice as many outbuildings -- and its slender, graceful towers and spires, visible from the city, seem to burn with red fire in the last rays of sunset. The High Prince and his family live in the Residential Wing, the largest and most impressive building, and the Private Museum houses Lugh Surehand's personal collection.
locations.notes: The palace's architecture is bizarre: faint Celtic and Salish grace notes over forms of alien, Escher-like geometry that should not work without vast amounts of magic. The same unified style, with no predecessor school, appears in Ehran's and Laverty's estates, though three different people designed them.

locations.name: The Capitol
locations.description: The Capitol, at Center Street and State Street Northeast, is by far Salem's most luxurious hotel: eight floors of large, opulently furnished rooms around an atrium lobby that is a triumph of Tir Tairngire design. The cheapest room costs 400 nuyen a night. Its manager, Trish Aleta, is biased against non-elves. Incabulos, its restaurant, matches the hotel's opulence and serves what connoisseurs call the finest menu in Salem, with white-noise generators at every table and magical barriers against astral eavesdropping.
locations.notes: Some runners hole up here under their best fake ID to wait out the heat, on the theory that nobody expects them to live high. Incabulos is a good place to meet a high-toned Johnson. Its manager, Mark Yunker, hates reporting to Trish Aleta and is collecting dirt on her extracurricular activities.

locations.name: Clonmacnoise
locations.description: Near a gentle bend in the Shannon River in Offaly, the monastery of Clonmacnoise is a celebrated holy place. Founded in 548, it was a prominent center of worship and learning for centuries. Its extensive ruins, the churches built nearby in later periods and its grave slabs remain the focus of pilgrimages by die-hard Christians, especially on St. Ciaran's feast day, September 12. The Order of Sylvester, from its small community east of the monastery, administers the ruins as a pilgrimage site and tourist attraction.

locations.name: Glendalough
locations.description: High in the Wicklow hills, Glendalough -- the 'glen of two lakes' -- is an important early Christian site: a cluster of seven ancient churches and a monastery nestled in a hollow between two lakes that run into a spectacular waterfall. The buildings are all but abandoned, home to a few hardened hermits.
locations.notes: Rumors of fomorians in the area discourage most people from visiting the glen.

locations.name: Rock of Cashel
locations.description: The Rock of Cashel, the ancient seat of the Munster kings, is a steep, rocky outcrop rising from Tipperary's Golden Vale, crowned with jagged ruins. Brian Boru, tenth-century High King of Ireland, came here for his crowning in 977, as did many less legendary figures before and after him. The site is under the protection of a small band of elves, the Keepers of Cashel, who refuse non-elves access to the peak without special permission.
locations.notes: Some kind of construction has been seen on the summit, but neither physical sight nor magical assensing can make it out clearly. The sarcophagi and other treasures found on the Rock in earlier centuries are said to be returning to their rightful place. The Keepers of Cashel are not kin to the Danaan Families.

locations.name: Carnfree
locations.description: Carnfree, four kilometers due south of the Rathcroghan burial mound in Roscommon, is the inauguration mound of the O'Connors, the ancient kings of Connaught and a pre-eminent family among the Danaan-mor. It is the sacred burial site of Conn of the Hundred Battles and of the three famous Tuatha queens Eire, Fothla and Banba.
locations.notes: The mound holds an immense reservoir of stored power. Carnfree is a powerful mana locus in the cairn line network, and mages appointed by the O'Connor family keep it under constant guard.

locations.name: Brugh na Boinne / Newgrange complex
locations.description: Brugh na Boinne in Meath, enclosed on three sides by the River Boyne, holds at least fifteen ancient passage graves, among them the famous sites of Newgrange, Knowth and Dowth. In earlier centuries Ireland's humans let all and sundry wander through the graves and disturb the spirits at rest; since the formation of the Tir the burial sites have been under the jurisdiction of the O'Connor family, which has removed every later construction, such as the Christian souterrain, to remedy the desecration. As at Tara, visitors need a special permit from the office of Lord Diamuid O'Connor.

locations.name: Hill of Tara
locations.description: The Hill of Tara in Meath draws thousands of pilgrims every year, and tight government control protects it from them. Anyone who wishes to stand on the hill, especially on a sacred day, must apply for a permit from the office of its administrator, Lord Diamuid O'Connor, and anyone who wishes to view or touch the Lia Fail, the coronation stone of the ancient kings, needs his personal permission, which he rarely grants.
locations.notes: Constant contact with human and elven hands has eroded the Lia Fail, threatening to wear it away and dissipate its power. The 'true' Stone of Kings is not a single, unchanging object: a physical stone becomes the true stone through mana flow, symbolism and emotional reality. Likewise 'Tara' in the spiritual sense -- the mystical seat of the High Kings -- is created wherever in Meath ritual regalia and the presence of Great Spirits make it so.

locations.name: Giant's Causeway
locations.description: The Giant's Causeway in Antrim is the most spectacular site in all of the Tir: a massive platform of hexagonal basalt columns and eroded chalk arches that has existed for millions of years and still draws tourists to its striking formations. Among the more serious visitors, druids and mages come to find solitude in the sea-facing caves or to perform communal rituals among the columns at dawn and dusk. Many tales claim Finn MacCuill built it. Above one end stands Dunseverick, once the capital of the kingdom of Dalriada and the end of one of the five great roads from Tara, which the O'Neill family is rebuilding as the new capital of the northern Tir.
locations.notes: A band of the magical storms called daoineann draoidheil runs along ten kilometers of coastline east and west of the Causeway; its strength and position fluctuate. Since the Awakening, the ancient roadway to Dunseverick has re-emerged from the land.

locations.name: Lough Key Forest Park
locations.description: Lough Key Forest Park in County Sligo is administered by druids but owned by the SES corporation, which uses it as a research base. Lush and beautiful, it abounds with rhododendrons, azaleas and countless peat-loving plants and shrubs.
locations.notes: Given the commercial value of the organic resources SES develops here, security is extremely high. It is also good for poaching deer.

locations.name: Dublin
locations.description: Dublin, Baile Atha Cliath in Gaelic, is Tir na nOg's ancient capital: a place where the ancient world meets the modern, with more history in its buildings, monuments, memorials and museums than any other city its size in Europe, and modern developments competing with architecture from every period. Elves walk beside humans, nobles beside peasants, artists beside businessmen. It is crammed with culture, from the best traditional music in its concert halls to the backstreet bars and dancehalls, and its literary heritage runs from Beckett, Joyce and Yeats to the high-elven sagas and epic poems that have captured the world's imagination. The River Liffey divides the center: the south side keeps what is left of genteel old Dublin, with Trinity College and Fitzwilliam Square, while further west Dublin Castle and St. Patrick's Cathedral stand close to the bohemian bustle of The Liberties and Dolphin's Barn.

locations.name: Dublin Castle
locations.description: Dublin Castle, a thirteenth- to eighteenth-century jumble close to the heart of the city, has been reinstated as one of the president's official residences. It is used most often for entertaining visiting high-and-mighties, particularly the chiefs of the Danaan.

locations.name: Belfast
locations.description: Belfast lies at the mouth of the River Lagan on the deep Belfast Lough, a position that once made it a great shipbuilding city; it had more people than Dublin at the end of the nineteenth century. The decline of heavy industry has left large depressed areas, especially around the abandoned docklands, and the center is a jumble of grand Victorian buildings among ugly late-twentieth-century developments, with a tumbledown, abandoned air; every plan to improve it has stalled between the government and rebellious Protestant workers. The liveliest part lies between Donegall Square, the Cornmarket and Great Victoria Street, the 'Golden Mile', with the university at its southern end. The old Catholic neighborhood west of Falls Road has become a siege town, its concrete walls guarded by troops to keep Protestant bombers out. Belfast is a Security Risk Zone: visitors need a costly special permit, and without one they forfeit all rights to emergency medical response.
locations.notes: Strangers with their wits about them stay out of the Entries, a warren of alleys, drinking clubs and ramshackle shops east of the Cornmarket. The IRA and the Protestant URF may have set aside their differences against the elven government; the Irish Volunteer Faction, an ultraradical splinter of fewer than a hundred members, sometimes joins the URF against government targets. The Spear of Trogain has claimed nearly a dozen killings of URF and NURM members in two years with no witnesses; gossip calls it an IRA or INLA splinter, while another rumor says it is a cover invented by TRC assassins or the Reach Fuileach.

locations.name: Garda fort
locations.description: Between Victoria Street and the river, the immense Garda fort glowers over the Belfast skyline beneath a cluster of surveillance equipment on its roof. Locals call it the Castle; Protestants sometimes call it the Dungeon. Only official vehicles may use the roads that approach it. The original Belfast Castle, north of the city, was abandoned by the Garda after one terrorist explosion too many demolished most of it in 2039.

locations.name: Stormont Castle complex
locations.description: Beyond the easternmost Protestant neighborhoods of Belfast stands the heavily fortified Stormont Castle complex, a solid reminder to everyone of the Tir government's iron grip on the city.

locations.name: Berlin
locations.description: Berlin is a free city run on anarchy -- to some a shining example of a functioning anarchist society, to others a warning, but either way public life works fairly smoothly and no one really understands why. The Russian air assault of November 2032 and the fighting that followed devastated large parts of the city, and afterward an anarchist committee walked out of city hall, proclaimed a grand anarchist experiment, and replaced all democratic law with the Final Law. Power now flows through the 'Flux', or F-State: an amorphous structure of interest groups, policlubs, gangs and megacorp lobbyists in which Neo-anarchists are just one group among many, information brokers -- informers, deckers and fixers -- hold the bulk of the power, and every city service is privately run. Who you know matters more in Berlin than anywhere else in Germany.
locations.notes: Berlin's anarchist groups work to keep the power structure in constant change. Whenever a shift threatens to establish a status quo, the rest of Berlin's powers spring into action, and anyone branded a Bedrohung des Status F -- a threat to the F-State -- is immediately attacked. The Neo-Anarchist Policlub Berlin, the 'Nappies', is the largest policlub, recruited largely from university graduates; every interest group that wants to cut a rival down to size courts its support.

locations.name: Berlin Council / Berliner Rat building
locations.description: The Berlin Council (Berliner Rat) is the city's only conventional political body, reduced by the Final Law to a platform for open dialogue among Berlin's interest groups. So that it never becomes a new government, all its functions are redistributed among its members every six months, and it cannot use the trappings of an established government: no security force guards its small administrative building or its giant congress center, and its members rate no special protection.
locations.notes: Council members may in theory draw funds for bodyguards from the council bank, the Berliner Kasse, but with no tax revenue the council lives on donations from residents, and it marks it as a red-letter day when money actually appears.

locations.name: Berlin U-Bahn network
locations.description: Berlin's U-Bahn is one of the biggest subway networks in the world, and no spot in the city lies more than two hundred meters from an entrance. The star-shaped network built more than a century ago still runs, supplemented by a second network dug in 2009 fifty meters below the first. Its modernization was never finished, but it still runs faster than any other German city's system, and countless escalators and walkways connect the two levels.

locations.name: Freiburg
locations.description: Freiburg is the capital of the Troll Kingdom of the Black Forest, the metahuman land ruled by King Berthold I. The kingdom favors orks and trolls: humans who work its orchards and vineyards have the legal status of royal wards, and harming one is a felony. Besides agriculture it lives on tourism, as hikers come to the forested hills and valleys in winter and summer, though reports of dangerous paranormal animals and hostile trolls and orks may soon put an end to that. The kingdom has few friends; most other Lander regard the Black Forest as a dumping ground for bothersome metahumans.
locations.notes: The humans' status as royal wards cannot hide that they have almost no rights. Some political circles in the kingdom would welcome an end to tourism despite the lost revenue, and the corps resent the King's refusal to rent out his subjects cheaply for hard labor.

locations.name: Greater Frankfurt
locations.description: Greater Frankfurt stretches from Wiesbaden and Mainz in the west to Hanau and Aschaffenburg in the east, and from Frankfurt in the north to Mannheim and Ludwigshafen in the south. Historically Germany's financial center, it now essentially belongs to the Frankfurt Bank Association: when city hall tried to curb the banks' expansion early in the century, the banks simply bought large parts of the city through their real-estate holdings. The sprawl began to form in 2023, when Frankfurt incorporated Offenbach. Its south side is ruled by AG Chemie, and nearly a third of the area, including the former city of Ludwigshafen, is chemical factories, laboratories, suppliers and employee housing.
locations.notes: Because the banks control many businesses usually run by organized crime, the underworld has far less influence here than in other sprawls; the long-established Mafia spends its time defending what it had before the banks took over.

locations.name: Hamburg
locations.description: Hamburg is one of northern Germany's great cities and ports. With Bremen, it is one of only two German harbors that can still take passenger ships, and its airport offers transorbital flights.
locations.notes: [2059 – later developments] Hamburg is the headquarters of the Klabauterbund, which claims over five thousand members in the city and keeps close ties to the Green Cells and North Sea pirates, sponsoring piracy as self-defense against megacorporate oppression. The Marauders, pirates captained by the elven woman Morgana, are suspected of using Hamburg as their primary port.

locations.name: Hannover
locations.description: Hannover is the seat of the confederate government of the Allied German States. It was there that the 2045 constitution fixed the borders of the Lander, wrote the megacorporations' extraterritoriality into law and gave troublesome regions associate status: the Troll Kingdom, the dwarf Duchy of Westrhine-Luxembourg, the elven Duchy of Pomorya, the Saar Special Legislative Zone and the Free City of Berlin. Foreign business partners of the Alliance keep corporate consulates here, and the Copenhagen-Zurich Transrapid line runs through it.
locations.notes: The government in Hannover keeps a wary eye on the Aztlan corporate state, and seems to feel no qualms about collecting the millions of ecus in tax paid every year by AG Chemie's subsidiary General Genetics.

locations.name: Karlsruhe Special Legislative Zone
locations.description: The Karlsruhe Special Legislative Zone is Germany's largest garrison. In 2043 a series of earthquakes along the Upper Rhine tore Karlsruhe apart, killing 10,000 people in a day; after the Troll Kingdom was declared the same year, the state government in Stuttgart practically wrote the region off, keeping only the constitutional court there 'for reasons of national solidarity'. Radicals found followers among the homeless and embittered, and Hedwig Gabler of the Greater Badensian Crusade -- Badensian nationalism, religious fanaticism and a virulent hatred of metahumans -- became Lord Mayoress and hired mercenaries to make war on the Troll Kingdom.
