In April 2049 the Bundeswehr took the city in seven hours. Today close to 30,000 soldiers are quartered in its barracks, alongside the federal courts, research establishments and a prison.

locations.name: Muenster
locations.description: Munster is the capital of the Free State of Westphalia, the conservative, deeply religious Land that grows much of Germany's food. It is famous as the seat of the schism: during the Bishops' Conference of April 2014 the diocese of Munster broke from Rome, rejecting magic entirely, and proclaimed itself the center of the True Church of the Lord God and His Saints. The conflicts that followed turned violent more than once and drove the final separation of church and state in Germany. The True Church is headquartered here, and its political branch is the Ritter Christi, the Christian Knights.

locations.name: Munich
locations.description: Munich, officially the Isar Metro Area, is Bavaria's one great city after the state lost territory to Franconia and Wurttemberg. Culturally distinct from the rest of Bavaria, and despite its past as right-wing Germany's 'secret capital', it has become far more open and liberal than the state around it. The city counts about five million people; the state president's office counts only the 2.2 million with Bavarian papers. Just over half are human, with large elf, troll, dwarf and ork communities, and it is one of Europe's most popular refugee destinations: one resident in two was born elsewhere, usually in the Balkans, and many districts speak a polyglot of German and Balkan tongues.
locations.notes: Bavarian authorities will use any excuse to string up troublemakers.

locations.name: Papenburg habitat
locations.description: Papenburg is a giant habitat that Westphalia's economic power built at the mouth of the Ems River, named after a nearby town that sank beneath the waves in 2011. Just under a quarter of a million people live there, 98 percent of them human, making it Westphalia's most important city after Munster. Its port at Ludgershaven ships Westphalian produce overseas and takes in the high-tech goods paid for it; passenger traffic is sparse, given Westphalia's suspicion of outsiders. Wealthy meat barons and the city governor, who bears the archaic title of Drost, live in the restricted district of Kapernaum.
locations.notes: The heavily guarded Portus Christi at Ludgershaven is the war port of the Westphalian Coast Guard -- all of five torpedo boats, ten hovercraft and a few small vessels, though its order books with the Vulkan yards may say otherwise.

locations.name: Rhine-Ruhr Megaplex
locations.description: The Rhine-Ruhr Megaplex, the core of the Land of Northrhine-Ruhr, stretches from Bonn in the south and Neuss and Monchengladbach in the west through Leverkusen, Wuppertal and the cities of the Ruhr to Marl in the north and Unna in the east. Its defining feature, which school texts and tourist brochures fail to mention, is the hundreds of industrial waste areas -- the brachen, or fallows -- which have spawned bizarre ecologies of their own.
locations.notes: The fallows support every kind of misfit, from Green War camps to mutant squatters, toxic spirits and the occasional toxic shaman. They all know the latest buzz on the ecology, politics and crime of their areas, and they are all easily provoked.

locations.name: Saar-Lorraine-Luxembourg / SOX
locations.description: The SOX -- Saar-Lorraine-Luxembourg, officially the Saar Special Legislative Zone and often just 'the Zone' -- is the area irradiated by the 2009 nuclear disaster at Cattenom: Luxembourg, much of Lorraine, all of the Saarland and the country around Trier and Kusel. Trier, Kusel and Zweibrucken are the only points of entry. In the 2020s researchers found that the disaster had caused astral turbulence so powerful that even the mightiest magical entities can stay only briefly, and megacorps moved in to build sealed research installations behind the barrier; the German side holds about 200 research or production facilities with some 300,000 personnel. Most Europeans treat the SOX as a distinct country, though Germany and France do not.
locations.notes: The largest labs belong to Saeder-Krupp at St. Wendel, Ruhrmetall at Merzig and Ares Europa below the remains of Volklingen, mostly weapons research; AG Chemie's Leo-Bernhardt laboratory at Wadern does what is closer to illegal genetic research. Rumor says some corps keep researchers in sealed habitats and release them only when they produce results. The Zone also hosts semiannual corporate army maneuvers, which are slowly leveling what buildings remain, and the 'atomic punks' on the French side are very weird.

locations.name: Sassnitz
locations.description: Sassnitz, on Rugen Island, is the capital of the Duchy of Pomorya, the semi-autonomous Baltic state of elves and humans loosely associated with the German Alliance. Pomorya values nature magic over the hermetic tradition and has resurrected ancient polytheistic cults, rebuilding temples and sacred groves; most of its people follow the local nature religion, whose high priests double as talented shamans. In the far north of Rugen, the Jaromarsburg -- a temple of Svantevit grown by Pomoryan elves from living wood -- rises from a sacred grove atop the white cliffs of Kap Arkona.
locations.notes: Pomorya serves Svantevit as an incarnation of the Dragonslayer whose enemies are now the toxic spirits of the poisoned Baltic. Shamans and nature mages gather every month at a site sacred to the Great Mother near the Jaromarsburg. Pomoryan elves in torpedo boats just hate hovercraft.

locations.name: Shadowmarket
locations.description: Berlin's shadowmarket usually occupies Friedrichstrasse, where a flea and art market once stood, though it sometimes turns up elsewhere. Five square kilometers of stalls, tents, lean-tos and caravans make it the place to sell anything fast: information, cyberware, opera tickets, chips, exotic liquors, talismans, sleaze simsense, and especially whatever is illegal or confiscated elsewhere in Germany. Anyone who stays in Berlin without visiting it cannot claim to have seen the city.
locations.notes: A systematic search for any one item is virtually impossible; once inside the warren-like aisles, only luck or exact directions will find it. TelTech's security layout and the Humanis membership roll are the kind of goods on offer.

locations.name: Stuttgart / Mid-Neckar Metro Area
locations.description: Stuttgart, formally the Mid-Neckar Metro Area, is Wurttemberg's capital, lying in the Neckar River valley. Its people call it the 'plex of woods and streams', but it is a major industrial center with numerous IFMU factories, and absorbing Ludwigsburg, Esslingen, Sindelfingen, Heilbronn, Tubingen, Reutlingen and their neighbors has made it Germany's fourth-largest city at 5.6 million. The city fathers care far more about the smooth flow of business than about culture: apart from Tubingen University it has few cultural institutions, and no major newspaper or trideo station.
locations.notes: Tubingen mostly researches commercial applications of cybertech and magic.

locations.name: Wuppertal / Zombietown
locations.description: Wuppertal is one of Germany's most unusual cities. When construction around it was banned in 2017, the city built upward instead: from Elberfeld to Schwelm the whole Wupper valley is built over with concrete in four distinct levels, made livable by sophisticated ventilation and lighting, and linked by speedways and tube trains, while on the lowest level the old Schwebebahn suspension railway still runs beside the river. Artificial light is the only light for much of the city, which has drawn many people allergic to sunlight. Metahumans make up nearly 60 percent of the population, and because so many live underground and rarely see daylight, outsiders call the city 'Zombietown'.

locations.name: Front Range Free Zone
locations.description: The Front Range Free Zone -- the FRFZ, or just the Free Zone -- is the international region created by the Treaty of Denver, joining Denver, Boulder and Colorado Springs under six sovereign sectors: Aztlan, the CAS, Pueblo, the Sioux, the UCAS and the Ute. Each sector keeps its own law, borders and police; a maglev line, shared services and a great deal of cross-border trade tie them together. About 3.6 million people live here -- 62 percent human, 18 percent ork, 14 percent elf -- and more than half a million have no SIN. Nearly a third live below the poverty line. Denver changes faster than most cities, so any information about it goes stale quickly.

locations.name: Aztlan Sector
locations.description: The Aztlan Sector -- Azzietown to its neighbors -- is Aztechnology's corner of Denver, and it shows: 90 percent of its people are affiliated with the megacorporation, and its per capita income and proportion of active traders are far higher, and its poverty far lower, than anywhere else in the Free Zone. Anyone who is not an Aztech employee is driven out or kept down. Aztechnology security forces patrol both sides of the fence in high-risk areas, accompanied by lethal paracritters, and watcher spirits monitor most of the demarcation line.
locations.notes:
The official population of about 400,000 is well short of the real figure, closer to 600,000; the Azzies are tolerating, or creating, a large SINless underclass they keep out of the figures. Where no patrol covers a high-risk stretch, anti-personnel radar sweeps the fence line, and anything bigger than a small dog brings up a microturret -- one every thirty meters or so in no man's land -- that hoses down the area. The radar and gun systems are not linked to the Matrix.

[2061 – later developments] Ghostwalker's first act on returning in the last days of 2061 is to assault the Aztlan Sector, destroy its teocalli and make clear that Aztlan will be removed from the city entirely.

locations.name: CAS Sector
locations.description: The CAS Sector -- CAS-ville -- was carved out in 2034, when the Treaty of Richmond created the Confederated American States and gave it a seat on the Council; it takes in parts of both Denver and Colorado Springs. Its borders are lined with ten-meter fences broken by a few stretches of wall, dropping to five meters or less along the rural line between Denver and Colorado Springs through Elbert and Peyton. The demarcation line was drawn by committee: it runs strictly north-south and east-west regardless of the street grid, and makes an unholy jog around downtown.
locations.notes: Smugglers flying t-birds over the sector risk slow but nasty underground-to-air missiles that come up from beneath, where the armor is thin.

locations.name: Pueblo Sector
locations.description: The Pueblo Sector, belonging to the Pueblo Corporate Council, takes in Lakewood and Fort Carson and about 700,000 people, and is run like the rest of Pueblo, through shareholder government and private security. Its border relies on technology rather than manpower: linked sensor systems watched by software, and flocks of stealth drones that loiter a couple of hundred meters up the line, with no armed guards or sentry guns in sight.
locations.notes: A hit on one sensor raises only a tentative alert; it goes active when a second system confirms it. Then a stealth drone drops to look, pattern-recognition software decides whether to worry, and a Pueblo rigger, possibly kilometers away in a warm guardhouse, jacks in to scope out the intrusion, follow the intruders unseen, or mow them down, while a patrol is sent.

locations.name: Sioux Sector
locations.description: The Sioux Sector is governed by a five-member council and enforces strict immigration controls. Besides its main territory it holds a non-contiguous parcel downtown. The Council originally meant the downtown square to be a non-national, free-market Hub; when every sector realized it would be a highway for smugglers, illegal immigrants and terrorists, the idea was dropped, the Sioux and the UCAS both volunteered to 'take the area off the Council's hands', and the Council split it between them -- which is how the non-contiguous sectors came to be.
locations.notes: Henequen, the feathered serpent who runs Henequen Enterprises, lives in the Thornton district and seems to know everyone in the sector.

locations.name: UCAS Sector
locations.description: The UCAS Sector covers parts of Denver and Colorado Springs, including its half of the non-contiguous downtown parcel, and is policed by Lone Star through a wholly owned subsidiary. It is the poorest of the national sectors by some measures, with more than 220,000 SINless people and over a third of its population below the poverty line. Its border is a plascrete wall watched by day by as sophisticated a sensor suite as you would ever want to avoid; the UCAS neither mines no man's land nor patrols it by day.
locations.notes: After dark, guard-dog patrols take over: German shepherds gengineered for size, strength and unbelievable aggressiveness, with their larynxes surgically removed so they cannot bark. The guards call them the 'silent killers', and even their handlers are afraid of them; a sensor on each dog calls a patrol a couple of minutes after they engage. A good runner might slip the sensor line, but will spend at least two minutes in no man's land -- plenty of time for the dogs.

locations.name: Ute Sector
locations.description: The Ute Sector takes in western Denver and Boulder. It is run by an appointed administration, policed by the nominally private Sand Creek Security Services, and applies Ute immigration controls. Its border is watched above all by spirits, which usually respond to an intrusion by summoning Ute security fire teams in a Citymaster or LAV, and sometimes take matters into their own hands, messily.
locations.notes: No one knows how the Ute can afford to bind so many spirits; some of them, including the most powerful, may be free spirits watching the line for reasons of their own, and one observer sensed something like a great city spirit twisted out of true -- not toxic, but not normal. Ute law considers the dzoo-noo-qua sentient.

locations.name: Chinatown
locations.description: Denver's Chinatown is an enclave of businesses and homes in Englewood with a long Chinese-American history. Its residents are mostly second- or third-generation citizens, but they deal with outsiders little more than their parents and grandparents did, and years of political turmoil have made them more insular and clannish still. Chinese-ethnic humans and elves treat the dwarfs, orks and trolls on the fringe of the community as unfortunate souls for whom they must take responsibility -- though they will trust an ork of Chinese descent faster than a human of any other background.
locations.notes: The Triads and the local Humanis chapter both press on Chinatown. Unity accuses Humanis of betraying the cause by abandoning its confrontations with Chinatown's residents.

locations.name: Council Hall
locations.description: Council Hall, the former City and County Building, is where Denver's governing Council meets. It holds offices, press facilities and meeting rooms behind layered security.

locations.name: Denver Maglev
locations.description: The Denver maglev runs from Boulder to Colorado Springs. The nonstop express makes the run in under an hour; the commuter service stops at forty-three stations and takes four hours for the whole route. Fares depend on distance and time of day, from as little as 2 nuyen between neighboring stops to 85 nuyen or more for the Boulder-Colorado Springs express. The line crosses eight sector boundaries, which gives immigration officials fits. It is run by Front Range Transit International, a money-losing holding company jointly owned by the six nations.
locations.notes: UCASTrak, the outfit behind the Seattle-San Francisco maglev, has spent five years trying to buy out FRTII, promising profits, maintenance, unchanged service and fare rises under 5 percent a year; every council vote on the offer deadlocks because some faction fears the deal would favor the UCAS.

locations.name: Fort Carson
locations.description: Fort Carson, the old U.S. Army post outside Colorado Springs, was rebuilt by Pueblo in 2035 and 2036 and now serves as a Pueblo training and security complex. During the Indian Wars, construction brigades tore down the subdivisions that once crowded its fences to clear a broad security zone around the base.

locations.name: Boulder
locations.description: Boulder lies in the Ute Sector, and has kept its university and its New Age identity with unusual continuity through the Treaty. It is also home to the largest battalion of the Godz, the predominantly elven go-gang, about a hundred strong, who escort smugglers and Zoners across sectors -- mostly protecting them from other battalions of the Godz.

locations.name: Austin
locations.description: Austin, Texas, is where Lone Star began and where it keeps its head office. Its overall head, Theodore W. D. Winslow, works from the Austin headquarters for about fifteen weeks a year and runs emergencies the rest of the time by telelink from a private island in Indonesia. The city is home to Lone Star's corporate leadership, its central data core, laboratories and academies, and a long history of municipal policing.
locations.notes: [2056 – later developments] Austin is split by the Aztlan-CAS border: Aztlan reclaimed part of the city, and it lives with a contested airport, a buffer zone, restricted flights and visible militarization.

locations.name: Lone Star Austin Headquarters
locations.description: Lone Star's central Austin facility houses corporate command -- the executive chairs of each division, answering to a nine-member Executive Advisory Council -- together with major paranormal, Matrix-security, research, records and administrative operations.

locations.name: Rhonabwy's Llandovery territory and lair
locations.description: Rhonabwy's territory around Llandovery in Wales is 'Dragon Land'. A week after the Caerfyrddin incident the great dragon ordered everyone within five miles of the town to leave for good within 72 hours, and almost everyone did. He spent two months leveling the area and then began to burrow, and he lives there still. He paid double the value of everything he took, and the neighbors appreciate that his nature spirits patrol the land and keep hostile critters away from farms on its fringes.
locations.notes: Most people believe Rhonabwy dug down more than three miles until he struck a huge cache of gold; his wealth is inestimable. Access to the lair is difficult, and he deals with the world through couriers, spirits, paranimals and media systems.

locations.name: Aztechnology Tenochtitlan Headquarters Pyramid
locations.description: Aztechnology's worldwide headquarters pyramid rises on the Paseo de la Reforma near the Zocalo in Tenochtitlan, with executive offices, board facilities, the corporation's central systems and landing flats. It is not to be confused with the Seattle Pyramid.
locations.notes:
Its defenses, surveillance, the temple site beneath it, reported dragon sightings, the national election computer and the competing explanations for an explosion there in late 2054 are all closely held.

[2061 – later developments] The pyramid runs Aztechnology while technically sitting inside its North American division, and Jaguar Guards and satellite security protect it.

locations.name: Tenochtitlan
locations.description: Tenochtitlan, once Mexico City, is Aztlan's high-altitude capital, combining monumental temples and corporate towers with dense districts, public transit, civic institutions and a broad cultural and commercial life. Life on its streets is like Seattle's, only more so -- above all the pollution: the locals call the city Los Humo Grande, the Big Smoke, and its air is among the five worst in the world, so everyone wears a breather on the street. Going out without one marks you as 'too dumb to live, or too chromed to die'. Ollamaliztli, a fast, brutal ball game played with knees, elbows and hips, is played at every level.
locations.notes: The city's population, class divisions, uneven services, policing, surveillance, precinct security, transport, crime and environmental hazards are all a matter of record. 'Expect the unexpected.'

locations.name: El Infierno
locations.description: El Infierno -- 'Hell' -- is a walled district of Los Angeles taking in what were Hawthorne, Gardena and Compton. A decade or so ago, after the central government did its best to raze it, someone carved 'Abandon hope, all ye who enter here' over the main gate, and he got it right: there is no hope in El Infierno, and that sets it apart. It has a long history of poverty, violence and neglect, of checkpoints and curfews, and the few people struggling for decent lives amid drive-bys and ever bloodier gang wars grow fewer. The city authority ignores it and leaves the gangs to provide what law there is.

locations.name: Boston
locations.description: Boston is a historic coastal UCAS metroplex whose East Coast Stock Exchange, universities, high-technology corridor, neighborhoods and corporate economy support a dense shadow market. Boston Harbor has been an environmental disaster for as long as anyone remembers, and in 2053 the 'Toxic Tea Party' -- a United Oil tanker with damaged guidance ruptured and dumped millions of gallons of petrochemicals -- killed off much of its marine life and left the survivors mutated almost beyond recognition.
locations.notes: Strange sea creatures regularly wash up on the coast, and some suspect the UniOil accident was the work of a techno-savvy toxic shaman; the number of toxics around the harbor supports it.

locations.name: Catacombs
locations.description: The Catacombs are miles of old tunnels, maintenance shafts and stations under Boston, sealed off during the last two rebuildings of the city's 'T' subway -- the oldest in North America -- or simply abandoned and forgotten. No one knows their true extent, because people have been tunneling under the city for 150 years, and nearly all the early records were lost in a Hall of Records fire in 1929. They are used for hidden travel, residence, markets and shadow business.
locations.notes: Getting around the Catacombs means knowing the entrances and hiring a guide; they hold criminal markets, corporate surveillance, hazards, and Mama's base.

locations.name: Detroit
locations.description: Detroit, the Motor City, is an industrial UCAS metroplex organized around a central hub and its incorporated surrounding cities, and the world headquarters of Ares Macrotechnology -- 'Aresville'. Everyone seems to love Ares: its products, advertising, trideo and logo are everywhere. Detroiters love their cars, too, nearly all of them Fords and GMs, and anyone driving a foreign car hears about it.
locations.notes: Ares influence, refugees from Chicago, riots and corporate factions shape the city's shadows.

locations.name: Madagascar
locations.description: Madagascar is a large Indian Ocean island whose long coastline, between the African and Asian sea routes, shelters many pirate settlements. VITAS killed most of its people before the Crash, and much of it -- including a 'Haunted Forest' -- is lawless and poorly known.
locations.notes: Its factions, lawlessness, paranormal conditions and contradictory theories about the interior are a matter of rumor as much as record.

locations.name: New Orleans
locations.description: New Orleans is one of the premier smuggling stops in the Western Hemisphere, a major CAS port where ocean-going cargo ships unload onto Mississippi river barges. It is reachable by every method imaginable -- swamp skimming, international airports, several interstates -- and the swamps around it offer private entry from nearly every angle, if you don't get lost in them. Caribbean trade, tourism, music and magic shape the city.
locations.notes: Stories abound of travelers lost in the swamps, and of what they turned into. The city's syndicate balance, corruption and supernatural hazards are a smuggler's working knowledge.

locations.name: Vladivostok
locations.description: Vladivostok, on Golden Horn Bay, is Russia's principal Pacific port and a major smuggling hub. Called the 'San Francisco of the East' for its steep hills and cosmopolitan mix of Muscovite, Korean, Chinese and Siberian peoples, with a large influx of metahumans fleeing persecution in Japan, it is in many ways Russia's Seattle: a frontier town on the Pacific.

locations.name: Rat's Nest
locations.description: Rat's Nest, officially the North Seattle Refuse Center, is a huge open-air dump several kilometers wide just north of the Snoqualmie River near the Salish-Shidhe border. Nearly a thousand squatters live in ramshackle huts and tents on the mountains of garbage, some making a living salvaging whatever they can use or sell. Rats, devil rats and other scavengers infest it, and often come to the aid of local Rat shamans.
locations.notes: The trash-rats -- gomi-nezumi to the Yakuza -- find amazing things in what people throw away: tech, weapons, clothing, building materials and other treasures.

locations.name: Singapore
locations.description: Singapore is a dense corporate city-state and a major financial and Matrix hub.

characters.name: Maria Mercurial
characters.title: Novastar
characters.description: Maria Mercurial is Seattle's biggest rock star, a novastar in her mid-twenties who headlines Underworld 93. Her arms, legs and face are mirror-bright metal that throws the spotlights back in cascades of color, her golden hair a corona around a silver moon -- and her eyes are deep brown and human, the kind that make people want to cry or kill something. She speaks excellent English with an Aztlan accent, slipping into Aztec and Spanish when excited. On stage she prowls like a silver panther, radiating sexuality and danger, playing a synthlink driven by muscle and nerve; off stage she wears black armorcloth and opaque shades and unwinds by starting fights in razor-guy dives. Her albums include 'Night Tears' and 'Puta', and she has turned down lucrative simsense-rights offers, warning that parts of her performance would not be pleasant for fans to experience.
characters.background: She was once Maria Aguilar, indentured young to Aztechnology and made bodyguard, secretary and mistress to the executive Reynaldo Texamachach, who had Sorayama rebuild her in Chiba (Ultra #84, 2044) with a sealed memory space invisible to scanners -- holding proof of Perfekto Polymers' illegal waste dumping -- and a datajack routed through her pleasure and pain centers, then addicted her to custom chips. She killed him in the Seattle Pyramid in 2045, fled into the Barrens and fed her habit in a brothel until Armando Hernandez heard her sing a cantamuerte, killed her pimp and got her clean. She has no memory of her life before him. She switches without warning between three personas: the Amazon on stage, the quiet, businesslike Schoolmistress, and the rare, trusting Innocent. The Sorayama circuitry lets her sublimate the addiction into synthlinking and hold out against the sealed memory's recovery code, 'Silver Virgin', for days. She lives in a 1.5-million-nuyen penthouse at Star Gardens Endominium and rides in a mirror-chromed Mitsubishi Nightsky.
characters.notes:
In every persona she loves Hernandez more than she admits, relies on denial, and will not discuss dreamchips, her memory loss or her cyberwork. Jacking a dreamchip risks relapse and a coma that may burn out her nervous system. Her old client file sits in Sorayama's clinic host under 'Maria Aguilar'. The imprint '84 Sorayama' is high on one silver thigh. She played Warren Cartwright's 2049 acoustic jam at Club Penumbra and is preparing a world tour.

[2051 – later developments] She marries Armando Hernandez at City Hall and, after a long honeymoon, announces she will tour once her next simchip is done; a new release is out by summer, and a bootleg of her Underworld 93 set circulates. The young dragon Eliohann becomes infatuated with an earring she wore in an interview.

[2053 – later developments] Jetblack's biography names her among the first megastars who followed him.

characters.name: Perianwyr
characters.title: Morgan's Partner
characters.description: Perianwyr is a Western dragon with a taste for vintage rock and roll and beer, who speaks Ancient Celtic, Latin and Welsh in a rumbling basso profundo. He is the partner of Kyle Morgan, Aztechnology's court of last resort, and keeps a library of every Maria Mercurial recording.
characters.background: He woke in 2022 in a Welsh cavern, ate a flock of sheep, and was saved from the farmers by a local boy with a shotgun and sheer charisma -- Kyle Morgan, now empathically bonded to him. Morgan is his only friend, the only being for whom he feels affection; he may respect or fear the mightier of his own kind, but only that fierce and loving human has a fire of spirit to match his own. He lairs on the roof of the Taetzel Building, guarded by two griffins, a cockatrice and a basilisk he trained.
characters.notes:
He is ambivalent about the Mercurial job: he pulls Maria out of the Yakuza ambush under invisibility, then kills Sumiko Hotoda and her guard to tie off loose ends. He flies invisibly, attacks astral pursuers and lands only under his lair's missile cover, stays out of fights unless Morgan is threatened, and dives into the smoke after Morgan's body if he falls. His disapproval of the mission is a roleplaying lever.

[2054 – later developments] He wants to end the Aztechnology employment and start on his and Morgan's own plans, but answers any attack on Morgan mercilessly. During the Super Brawl job he shadows the runners astrally, quietly removes the three ISSV mages, and flies in to pull Morgan out when it goes wrong.

characters.name: Sally Tsung
characters.title: Street mage (the equalizer)
characters.description: Sally Tsung is one of the best-known faces in the Seattle shadows: a gorgeous street mage who carries a sword.
characters.background: One of the best-known faces in the Seattle shadows. Her real stats are certainly better than the fighter-orientation Street Mage archetype the scenario uses for her.
characters.notes: She stays clear of other people's fights but will not let a team she likes die: in the Stuffer Shack robbery she fades into the stockroom, keeps a spell defense up for the runners, blasts the Chiller Thrillers' shaman if they cannot handle him, and slips out the back, invisible, before the fight ends. Having seen a team work, she is a natural future contact or source of jobs.

characters.name: Blackwing
characters.title: Elven Assassin
characters.description: Blackwing is the essence of style and grace: the most expensive clothes in dark solid colors and simple tailoring, hair perfectly in place whatever happens, a permanent smile on a finely chiseled elven face, a cigarette flicked away in one smooth gesture. Icy calm and never afraid to die, he has loved every minute of his work for ten years.
characters.background: He is one half of the infamous Blackwing-Nightprince team of elven assassins -- his partner Cillian Nightprince is the spontaneous one -- with a perfect record of 37 confirmed kills, blamed for political killings in Los Angeles that Captain Grissim could never prove. Hired by a Tir Tairngire noble to recover an idol quietly, he killed three scholars, framed the runners for Topal's death, and ended up the dragon Geyswain's captive until the runners freed him. The noble then accused him of trying to pass off a forgery and had him sentenced to death for treason; Rhiannon, his lover in the Tir, broke him out, and they fled to San Francisco, where a shadow clinic reworked his chrome.
characters.notes:
He carries an associate ambassador's diplomatic pass. Toward runners who survived the idol affair he feels respect, gratitude for his life, and bitterness at being blamed for his failure: he warns them once to leave Seattle for good, and tries to kill them if they ignore it.

[2051 – later developments] Back in Seattle doing 'security' for Emerging Futures with Rhiannon, John Whitefeather and Render -- the Persuaders -- he leads the team sent to kill EF's escaped 'animal', warns that it is a dragon, goes 'right down its throat' with an iaido draw-cut, and loses his right cyberarm at the elbow. His team fights by bombs, sniping and ambushes on isolated targets, then fades. He is developing a phobia about runners and dragons.

[2060 – later developments] He is now Count Evan Parris of Tir Tairngire high society, married with a family, rebuilt as a black-operations coordinator for Prince Aithne Oakforest after Oakforest overturned his death sentence. He runs the Double Take frame-up of Saeder-Krupp through Telestrian's handler Banshee and hand-picks the Tir Ghosts sent after her; he loathes dracoforms.

characters.name: Arleesh
characters.title: Great Serpent
characters.description: In human form Arleesh is a beautiful woman in mirrorshades and an earth-toned headdress, leaning on a long white Mitsubishi Nightsky and scowling. She is a great feathered serpent, loyal only to herself: she keeps her word to humans but sees them as tools.
characters.background: Awake only ten months, she came to Seattle to slum and learn modern human culture, and sensed a dangerous idol. Young for a great dragon but ancient beside Geyswain, she has first-hand knowledge of the horrors behind the idol's power and will spend her own life to destroy it -- but she will not risk being weakened by Geyswain first, hence hiring runners. She is devoted to protecting the world against Awakened threats the young races do not know of.
characters.notes:
She heals the runners, buys everyone a Stuffer Shack meal, and invites them to assense her true form. She tears the idol from Geyswain and destroys it, and may return to lead runners into more adventures

[2062 – later developments] At the first Council of Dragons she sits among the feathered serpents and votes against the Rite, arguing there is too much else to be done.
contact_skills: Great Dragon patronage (magic beyond any human, knowledge of the old horrors)
A white Nightsky and a low profile in Seattle

characters.name: Karl Brackhaven
characters.title: Humanis Chapter President
characters.description: Karl Brackhaven, president of the Humanis Policlub's Central Seattle chapter, looks in his early forties as though he stepped off the cover of a megacorp annual report: conservative suit, bright turquoise tie and ear stud, perfect teeth, bonhomie, and a wristwatch worth a small yacht with the Aztechnology logo worked into its face. He is called a moderate, 'whatever that means for a Humanis type'.
characters.background: A low-level Aztechnology executive before he made the chapter his career, he still plays an Aztech Mr. Johnson to perfection. He truly believes in the Humanis cause and never lets the fanaticism show; educated in history and psychology, he knows Humanis must not go too far or it loses the limited sympathy it has built. The lunatic fringe thinks he has lost his nerve. 'Sincerity's the key; once you can fake that, you're in.' He and his late brother Charles were the only ones who knew that the real Kenneth Brackhaven, Charles's son, goblinized into an ork and was murdered by his own father in 2023 to protect the family image, then replaced with a conditioned SINless double; Karl calls it a mercy killing, and helped raise the substitute to share his hatred of metahumans.
characters.notes:
[2051 – later developments] When the toxic shaman Jesse John plans to blow the NAN apart, Karl hires runners under an Aztechnology cover to stop him -- 115,000 nuyen, 20,000 down, with a van and Salish-Shidhe visas and backup that never comes -- and pays on success; afterward he is always heavily guarded.

[2057 – later developments] He secretly runs Kenneth Brackhaven's Archconservative presidential campaign from its downtown Seattle headquarters and will kill to keep the family history buried: he tries to buy off investigating runners through 'Mr. Smith' at Matchstick's, then hires the hitman Fletcher Quinn. Asked why he hires metahumans, he smiles: 'My dear, because you're the most expendable, of course.' Runners who expose him make a lifelong enemy; blackmail him and he plots their deaths; hand back the evidence and he reneges anyway.

[2058 – later developments] He attacks Governor Schultz as 'soft on crime' over the Mob War and is widely expected to run for governor in 2060.

characters.name: Eliohann
characters.title: Western Dragon
characters.description: Eliohann is a young Western dragon, a mere seven meters long and two at the shoulder, scaled green-gold, with an earring on the base of his left horn. He speaks politely and distractedly, and is fascinated by technology.
characters.background: Awakened three years ago with intelligence and magic usually found only among the greater of his kind, he roamed the Sinsearach and Tir Tairngire mountains until a team trapping paranaturals for Emerging Futures' Project Cerberus baited him with a trideo player and tranquilizer darts. Too fascinated by their tech to take revenge, he let himself be taken, hid his abilities, and decided information was the hoard he would build at any cost. He learned the stock market from the keeper's trideo, arranged the 'accident' that cost Dr. Grier her arm and her diamond ring, turned a burnt-out ork mage into his agent, and bought a majority of Emerging Futures from inside his cage. When Ares ordered him killed he forced through datajack surgery and jacked into a prototype deck; the Matrix drove him berserk, and he came down on Seattle General with no memory of who he was.
characters.notes:
Under the trauma a dragon's crafty ruthlessness survives: it seeks to control whatever it cannot kill. Even other dragons do not know he is in Seattle.

[2051 – later developments] He hires runners to recover his memory, paying only with the earring. In the end he accepts Ares' offer of all the technology and Matrix simulation he wants as a 'researcher' in exchange for his interest in Emerging Futures, and Ares sequesters him in a remote facility far from Seattle; he may remember the runners who helped him and become a dragon contact.
contact_skills: A Dragon's favor (if Ares ever lets him call)

characters.name: Coyote
characters.title: Bassist, The Elementals
characters.description: Coyote plays bass and key-guitar for The Elementals: on stage a dark, solemn Amerindian brave in traditional clothing, his long black hair held back by a hand-tooled leather headband, named for his personal totem. Off stage he is a fun-loving young man with a biting, sarcastic wit who plays jokes on everyone -- and a generous one who will risk his life for friends or innocents. He rides a Yamaha Rapier.
characters.background: He served for years in the Ute Nation's military, grew bored, and came to Seattle for his true vocation, music. He lived at first in the Amerindian squatter camp on the grounds of the ruined Redmond Grand Hotel; now that the band's money has come in he has his own apartment across town, but he still brings the camp food and supplies once a week and stays the night.
characters.notes: He knows the camp's dirt road by heart and always beats a pursuer to it, but surrenders the moment a squatter is killed. Only the band would avenge him.
contact_skills: Amerindian squatter community of the outer Redmond Barrens

characters.name: Jetblack
characters.title: Nightstalker Boss
characters.description: Jetblack, the 'dead' founder of angst-rock, looks like a sensitive youth in his early twenties: tall, slim and slight, glossy black hair to his shoulders framing a pale, high-cheekboned, almost elven face, in tailored black leather, with the voice of a professional performer and an edge beneath the calm. He was a major Seattle star at eighteen and one of the first megastars -- Maria Mercurial, Concrete Dreams and The Shadows followed him -- and his music was the sound of a man terrified of his own mortality. Lone Star found his badly trashed body years ago, and 'Jetblack Lives!' is spray-painted all over town.
characters.background: He is a vampire. A fan who was one offered him the 'dark gift', and he took it to cheat death before he understood what eternity would cost -- vampire hunters, and fans following him into the same mistake. He chose the honorable course: faked his death in 'random street violence' and went underground, where he leads the Nightstalkers and studies magic in the vague hope of reversing his condition. He let The Shadows know he was alive but never told them what he had become; they knew almost from the start. Emotionally insecure to the point of paranoia about his secret, his slight build hides massive strength.
characters.notes:
He feeds only on willing Nightstalkers, never more than they can spare, never kills and never makes new vampires, and preys on the unwilling only if they have tried to kill him. He checks every statement with Analyze Truth and stuns rather than kills. The Shadows' toast to absent friends unlocks his help.

[2053 – later developments] Allenby's murder draws him out; if he lives, he is an excellent contact, and joins The Shadows for one private jam, all five on one stage for the first time.
contact_skills: The Nightstalkers' muscle and eyes on the street
Seattle music-business history and The Shadows

characters.name: Sting
characters.title: Leader of the Ancients
characters.description: Sting, leader of the Ancients, is slightly above average height with the light build of her kind, long loose copper hair she braids when trouble looks close, yellow Opticon cybereyes, long canine implants, and a ragged scar from her left eye to her pointed ear from a fight with the Tigers. Dominant and aggressive, she uses her image as a weapon -- a whipcord samurai who picks her shots, and once cut a barghest in half with her hand razors.
characters.background: A child of Seattle's streets, rejected by her parents, she found education and a home there and believes in the street's freedoms and codes; she knows the Elven District better than anyone. She was Wasp's lieutenant and open critic, possibly his lover, and took over when he died on Dexter. She has continued his move into mercenary work while trying, and failing, to rebuild ties with a Tir she has little use for.
characters.notes:
[2053 – later developments] She believes Elven Fire is a splinter led by a few ex-Ancients, has tried and failed to parley with it, and grows angrier as the Tir's hand shows. She does not know that a Tir cabal has been feeding the High Prince lies about her. She will deal with runners whose help seems genuine.

[2058 – later developments] She publicly argues for the Ancients' independence from Tir Tairngire while privately keeping the Prince's channel open through Green Lucifer.

characters.name: Hanzo Shotozumi
characters.title: Oyabun, Dungeness Crab Clan
characters.description: Hanzo Shotozumi is the regional oyabun of Seattle's Yakuza. The word 'inscrutable' might have been coined for him: his face might as well be carved from stone, he is polite and proper whatever happens, and he shows his deepest rage only by raising his voice slightly -- which terrifies anyone who knows him.
characters.background: He was sent to Seattle after the Schism, the 2043 purge of Korean members from the Watada-rengo's Seattle gumi, and has served as regional oyabun since 2044, restoring Yakuza dominance through traditionalist restructuring. He handles even the most unpleasant business as routine, and can order a kobun's death as casually as lunch. He is married with two sons -- the elder training as his second, the younger a kobun -- and a runaway daughter, Keiko.
characters.notes:
[2053 – later developments] Street rumor calls him the big oyabun giving the Whispering Nights grief 'about honor'; he wants resolution, not slaughter.

[2058 – later developments] He has spent fifteen years building his Shotozumi-gumi into the most powerful Yakuza clan in Seattle, and with the Mafia's capo dead he pushes to unite the Nishidon-gumi and Shigeda-gumi under him and break from the Watada-rengo into his own West Coast rengo. He cultivates the First Nations gang as deniable muscle and a bridge to the Native American Nations. His daughter Keiko works the shadows as the decker Kiku and secretly undermines him. Rumor says the great dragon Ryumyo is the true power behind the Watada-rengo.

[2059 – later developments] He breaks away to found the independent Shotozumi-rengo, ending Vory boss Dimitri Makaroff's blackmail hold on him but drawing new enemies from his old syndicate.

characters.name: Harlequin
characters.title: Great Game Challenger
characters.description: Harlequin is chaos personified: an elf half a head shorter than Ehran and lighter built, face painted in the harlequin markings of old, gray-streaked black hair in a ponytail, a long many-pocketed coat with pins on the left lapel, always slightly behind the times. His attitude, manner, dress and accent change at a moment's notice; he is quick-witted, with references only three people alive would get, quick to anger and usually quick to forgive. He plays a steel guitar at least a century old, displays his magic openly, and masks his aura as mundane. 'Gentlemen! Welcome to Mount Olympus. I've been expecting you.'
characters.background: He is an immortal elf and a hermetic initiate of incredible rank, Ehran's 'old friend' and 'once-brother', pupil of the same teacher, who lost his left ear to Ehran's rapier in a dawn duel on a stone bridge centuries ago. The two speak a tongue no one else, not even the Tir elves, has ever heard. When his anger lasts, as it has for Ehran, it becomes a consuming passion. The Amahuacas of the Jutai tell stories of his earlier visits.
characters.notes:
[2051 – later developments] He takes the top floor of the ruined Southwind towers in Tarislar, where the gangs flee 'the Laughing Man'. Bound by the chal'han of the Great Game against Ehran, he hires runners only through cut-outs and seals his envelopes with a laughing jester's head. At Ehran's sanctum Althain he duels Ehran and takes his left ear, pays the runners with a sixteenth-century heirloom rapier, and vanishes; a month later a holocard arrives from Phoenix: 'My God, it's hot. Wish you were here. -H.'

[2055 – later developments] Adrift and drinking heavily once his score with Ehran is settled, he is warned by a vision that the Enemy, ancient world-devouring beings, will breach the Sixth World some 2,500 years early because of the background-magic spike left by the Great Ghost Dance. With Jane Foster he leads a team on an astral quest across the metaplanes, preparing the Chasm and the Bridge for Thayla's return; he is captured and tortured by Darke before the climax at the Bridge.

characters.name: Ehran the Scribe
characters.title: Author and Social Theorist
characters.description: Ehran the Scribe is an author and social theorist who rose to national prominence in fifteen years, from newsfax opinion columns to The New Magic, Life After 2001, the Pulitzer-winning Mankind Ascendant, and Metagenes: Future Spiral. He appears to be in his thirties, just over two meters tall, with a strong square face and piercing green eyes, always impeccably dressed in suits from the finest tailors of Spain and Tokyo. Studied and solemn, eloquent enough to hold any crowd, he is a true parliamentarian for whom rules are everything. He keeps residences in Seattle, Portland and New York, chairs the Young Elven Technologists, and is tied into Tir Tairngire politics.
characters.background: He claims a youth in the Chicago Shattergraves and no formal education. The truth: he is an immortal elf and a hermetic initiate of incredible rank, who dueled Harlequin on a Paris bridge as 'Monsieur E.' and sat for portraits as a seventeenth-century French courtier and a sixteenth-century Spanish noble. He keeps the orchid plantation Fonte do Sul in Amazonia as 'Senor Aquilar', worshipped by the Jivaros as a warrior god's avatar; holds the free air elemental Ariel by her true name; and keeps his sanctum, Althain, under Mount Saint Helens. He grew a tracking spell lock into the thigh bone of his daughter, Jane Foster of Columbia, Missouri, whom he 'allowed to lose him' after her mother's death. In the early 2030s he was a close advisor and friend of Lugh Surehand, and he is alleged to sit privately on the Council of Princes.
characters.notes:
His aura reads mundane, though people have seen him work magic. Ten layers of thought sit behind his eyes, and angry he is frightening.

[2051 – later developments] Bound by chal'han to act only through intermediaries, he fakes his death with an expendable YET body, then meets Harlequin at Althain in centuries-old dueling clothes and loses his left ear, declaring them merely even. His next book is delayed six months by 'illness', and he returns fit and sporting two ears.

[2054 – later developments] He rejects the Danaan families' claims of reincarnation and warns that the Tuatha deceive. Some identify him with Walter Bright Water, which others dispute; an unverified challenge at Royal Hill around 2053 is reported.

characters.name: Mike
characters.title: Fixer
characters.description: 'Mike' -- he never gives a name, so the street guesses it -- is a low-profile Seattle fixer who works only at odd intervals, almost exclusively for law-enforcement and government clients. He dresses casually but carries himself like a cop: dark hair cut unfashionably short, sunglasses, shined shoes, and a hand that keeps drifting to a sidearm that isn't there. Blunt to the point of rudeness -- 'There's the offer. Take it or leave it' -- he is honest about the odds and will not send runners on a suicide job without telling them.
characters.background: His bearing suggests military service. Rumor links him to the Veil, ConsOps, the CIA, Lone Star and Ares; no employer is confirmed.
characters.notes: [2059 – later developments] Meeting runners in the Woodland Park Zoo insect house for 'the family of a victim' of the paranormal-animal attacks, he offers 20,000 to 30,000 nuyen, cleared records and new SINs -- almost certainly on Lone Star's behalf, to solve the crisis before Knight Errant can exploit it.

characters.name: Arthur Vogel
characters.title: Presidential Candidate
characters.description: Arthur Vogel, one of the first dwarfs born in Canada after UGE, is a dynamic courtroom champion of ecological causes, arguing the nation cannot heal until the Earth does, who built his career winning difficult settlements against major corporations. He founded the One World Association in 2052 as a Democratic Party affiliate and is running for president, with the troll Eagle shaman Gary Grey as his running mate; his slogan is 'Save the Earth'.
characters.background: Privately, for years, he ran what amounted to a protection racket, using the threat of eco-terrorism to extract lucrative settlements. He once secretly sent a TerraFirst! cell to sabotage a Hawkshorne Chemical plant; the sole survivor, Alan Riv, was horribly burned.
characters.notes:
Riv plots mass murder at a Vogel campaign rally. If he is stopped, Vogel calls the runners heroes of the environment and owes them a favor; if the poison is released, Vogel survives because he was absent, turns the tragedy against polluting corporations, and calls for the runners' deaths. Rumors that he or Gary Grey commands TerraFirst! or Save Our Seas remain unconfirmed.

[2058 – later developments] After the campaign he runs Sierra, Inc. and sits on the Ares board through Dunkelzahn's bequest, pursuing environmental reform from inside the corporation.

[2059 – later developments] In October he privately buys Leonard Aurelius's whole Ares stake, putting his holdings, with his inherited Gavilan Ventures shares, slightly ahead of Damien Knight's own. He has made no bold move against Knight; supporters call it caution, detractors say he sold out.

[2061 – later developments] He is a leading Ares shareholder; reports of unexplained financing and unusual travel in 2057 remain unconfirmed.

characters.name: Dunkelzahn
characters.title: Presidential Candidate
characters.description: Dunkelzahn is an ancient silver-and-azure western dragon, first sighted near Denver in 2012 and now one of the most recognizable beings on the planet through decades of media presence and philanthropy. He speaks through a series of human interpreters who voice his thought-speech. He bought the cutting-edge VR firm VisionQuest from Ares in 2037 and owns the Lake Louise resort in the Athabaskan Council. 'I am an ancient being. I've seen first-hand more history than many shorter-lived people have forgotten ... I do not concern myself with matters of species or race.'
characters.background: To his own kind he is Far-Scholar, and he was Loremaster of the dragons long before he appeared to the modern world: keeper of the greatest store of draconic knowledge, the authority on draconic tradition, respected and feared by his peers. Some feared his fascination with the young races would lead him to reveal things best kept secret, and made the consequences plain to him. His 2012 appearance inspired Jaelle Lester to found the Church of the Whole Earth.
characters.notes:
[2057 – later developments] On 15 March, live on his talk show 'Wyrm Talk', he announces an independent run for the UCAS presidency on 'A New Golden Age', pledging SIN amnesty for the SINless and casting the megacorps as obstacles to real innovation, with Boston investor Kyle Haeffner as running mate on Damien Knight's advice. He polls around 22 percent. His head of security Carla Brooks runs VisionQuest VR test scenarios; a Human Nation cell seizes one facility and threatens it unless he withdraws. His campaign keeps a team of deckers watching his Matrix presence at all times, and his agents remember any runner who takes his money and abandons a job. He wins, and is assassinated on inauguration night; his will -- human legal machinery used to disperse a hoard, which no dragon had ever done -- leaves the Loremaster's seat vacant for the first time in an Age.

[2061 – later developments] His bequest of the Seal of the Green Gloves to Inazo Aneki gets Aneki into Tibet. The New Orleans fixer Toshi Akimura, one of his watchers, built a continental shadow-brokering business on his inheritance.

[2062 – later developments] His bequests drive the Rite of Succession among the great dragons: the Jewel of Memory to Lofwyr, the Elemental Scrolls of Ak'le'ar to Hualpa, the Silver Songbird to Rhonabwy, the Shroud of Shadows to Aden, the Second Coin of Luck to Lung, the Ring Ouroboros to Ryumyo, the Jade Dragon of Wind and Fire to Wu Lung-Wei, and to Hestaby the key to his private datastore on Zurich-Orbital. The Children of the Dragon cult grew out of his assassination.

[2064 – later developments] Art Dankwalther's windfall from the will funded the decade of economic war that forced Novatech's IPO, and JackBNimble, the file he left Captain Chaos, saves the dying sysop as a copy when Jormungand tears Shadowland apart.

characters.name: Damien Knight
characters.title: Dunkelzahn's Advisor
characters.description: Damien Knight is president and CEO of Ares Macrotechnology and takes a direct hand in its Knight Errant Security division. He is a master manipulator whose rise is shadowed by rumors of financial killings during the Crash of 2029; the first reliable records show him taking control of Ares in the 2033 'Nanosecond Buyout'. Leonard Aurelius wrested the chairmanship from him in a 2049 proxy fight. He brokered Ares' sale of VisionQuest to Dunkelzahn in 2037, for reasons never made public.
characters.background: Shadowland holds that Ares did not sell VisionQuest out of fear, and that Knight got something more than nuyen from the deal. Rumor says Knight is really Major David Gavilan; Lucien Cross, who programmed the Nanosecond Buyout for 'David Gavilan', has kept the original planning records proving Knight's identity for decades as insurance. Dunkelzahn's secretly held Ares stock, through Gavilan Ventures, has swung votes his way for years.
characters.notes:
[2053 – later developments] He hires an assassin against Lucien Cross after Cross steals the bioware firm Bioleve out from under an Ares shell; the Seraphim take the bullet.

[2054 – later developments] He and Aurelius are deadlocked on the Ares board.

[2057 – later developments] He advises Dunkelzahn on metahumanity and picks his old friend Kyle Haeffner as the dragon's running mate; Knight Errant's efficient riot suppression after the assassination rebuilds Ares' public image. He privately calls fellow board member Arthur Vogel 'this greenhead dwarf lawyer I've been saddled with.'

[2058 – later developments] He orders Operation Extermination, the Strain III-Beta assault that clears Chicago's insect-spirit Containment Zone in under twelve hours -- a public relations win after, by some accounts, his own earlier Knight Errant raid unleashed the hive in the first place. Detroit is his power base.

[2059 – later developments] Aurelius sells his Ares stock and joins Cross Applied Technologies, turning their cold war hot.

[2062 – later developments] He wants the Gagarin data, and the module even as wreckage, as much as he wants Yamatetsu to lose.

[2064 – later developments] Within days of Lucien Cross's death in the Crash he puts on his war paint and declares open season on Cross Applied Technologies -- 'this time, it's for all the marbles' -- taking Fleche Armaments and Bioleve within 24 hours and freezing Cross Matrix Technologies' assets. Aurelius does nothing, perhaps because Knight is blackmailing him.

characters.name: Nadja Daviar
characters.title: Dunkelzahn's Interpreter
characters.description: Nadja Daviar is a raven-haired elven beauty with a mesmerizing voice, Dunkelzahn's interpreter and voice since 2039, who reigns over the dragon's Lake Louise resort like a queen. Someone has taken great pains to erase every trace of her background, and done a fine job of it.
characters.background: Persistent, unconfirmed rumor links her to Polish intelligence circles. She is a rival of Holly Brighton for influence in the dragon's circle.
characters.notes:
[2057 – later developments] She inherits Gavilan Ventures and the roughly 12 percent of Ares stock it controls from Dunkelzahn's will, becomes vice president of the UCAS and director of the Draco Foundation, and signs two years' voting proxy over to Damien Knight rather than Leonard Aurelius -- rumor says under blackmail or threat.

[2058 – later developments] A Yakuza bunraku prostitute, Shelly Greenbriar, overdosed on a personafix BTL until she believes she is Daviar, plans to assassinate the real one at a Seattle speaking engagement.

[2059 – later developments] She regains direct control of the Gavilan shares in August; gossip places a mystery man dining with her in Washington.

[2064 – later developments] Campaigning in Seattle when the New Revolution launches its coup on 3 November, she survives an assassination attempt; General Angela Colloton follows her orders in denouncing the coup and declaring martial law. President Haeffner is murdered in a 'failed' rescue, and her whereabouts become uncertain.

characters.name: Masaru
characters.title: Great Eastern Dragon
characters.description: Masaru is a young eastern great dragon who, in human form, passes as a salaryman. He is fiercely dedicated to his ideals, above all protecting 'his' islands, the Philippines, from outsiders, the Empire of Japan included.
characters.background:
Masaru attends the first Council of Dragons, quite possibly his first -- Hestaby cannot recall having had cause to encounter him before -- taking the third eastern quarter of the circle almost exactly between the feuding Lung and Ryumyo. He shows more composure than his elders, though his eyes glow with an eagerness Hestaby finds oddly disturbing. He glances at the other two easterns and then rears up with them for the Rite of Succession: 'Let this be settled honorably,' he says gravely, and Hestaby restrains a chuckle at the idealism of the young.

In January 2059, Masaru supports Philippine political and economic change and is associated with Huk activity, regional planning, and the coming election.
characters.notes:
[2057 – later developments] His egg -- new life, spiritual solace, proof of his adulthood -- is stolen from his caved-in Vancouver Island lair while he lies stunned by a specially engineered spell, part of a plot to have him rampage in public and drag Dunkelzahn's polls down by association. Confronting the thieves downtown, agitated and barely holding his fury in check, he gives one chance to surrender the egg before taking his true form.

[2059 – later developments] He backs political and economic change in the Philippines and is associated with the Huks and the coming election; the extent of his control is unconfirmed.

[2062 – later developments] At what may be his first Council of Dragons he sits between the feuding Lung and Ryumyo, shows more composure than his elders, and rises for the Rite of Succession: 'Let this be settled honorably.'

characters.name: Dodger
characters.title: Independent decker/otaku
characters.description: Dodger is an elf decker, perhaps one of the best in the world, and a Shadowland regular. A 'spike baby' born before the Awakening, he carries himself with gallant poise, a bit of a showoff and a clown with a sharp wit, and almost always affects a Dickensian English accent that slips under stress -- 'Avaunt, rascal!' His Matrix icon is an ebony-skinned, faceless boy in a white suit and a cloak of swirling silvery stars.
characters.background: He trained as a decker in the service of Sean Laverty, a Prince of Tir Tairngire, and broke from Laverty's inner circle for personal reasons. With the decker Twist, his intrusion into an early Renraku knowbot gave it the 'x-factor' that let it awaken as the AI Morgan; when Renraku moved to recapture her he helped erase her source code, and in 2058, with Devon Eurich, broke into the arcology to rescue her. What they brought out was damaged, and called itself Megaera. She travels with him everywhere, and he calls her his songbird.
characters.notes:
[2060 – later developments] He extracts the black-ops rigger Cassie Barnett from a Renraku clinic with 'Sir Wraith', and is the last Shadowland regular cut off defending the February Veso Lounge transmission against the Disciples of Deus; his fate is unknown for a time, with Megaera calling for him.

[2061 – later developments] He fights with Overwatch only to make Megaera whole again, and opens the node that lets her into Deus's home host.

[2064 – later developments] Hunting for Megaera's Nodes, he hacks Sherman Huang's private host and finds Huang's scheme to run a Nanosecond Buyout on company funds during the Novatech IPO; Huang recognizes his icon and sends a hit team, and Dodger goes to ground with an otaku tribe in the Barrens, writing to friends on paper. Mentioning 'his songbird' gets his attention. Inside the Exchange host on 2 November, he reaches into Deus's code and wakes Megaera.
contact_skills: The AI Morgan's history and vulnerabilities
AIs, Renraku's AI research, and who has been chasing them

characters.name: FastJack
characters.title: Independent Decker
characters.description: FastJack is a weary, wry veteran of the Matrix's earliest days and a Shadowland regular, who treats even a live firefight against fanatics in the Matrix with the calm of someone who has seen every trick invented at least twice. He is a mentor, programmer, information source and data-haven ally who exercises restraint.
characters.background:
Denver records connect FastJack to early Shadowland recovery, Internet and Egg history, Nexus routing knowledge, and his protection of Perri in 2055.

FastJack says he knows unnamed back doors into Aztlan systems and recovered the deleted constitutional section in 2055 before failing to establish a warm link to the Nexus.

In 2061, FastJack remains an indirect mentor, programmer, information source, and data-haven ally who exercises restraint.
characters.notes:
[2055 – later developments] He helped recover Shadowland after the Crash of 2029, knows the Internet's and the Egg's history and the Nexus's routing, and protects Perri. He claims unnamed back doors into Aztlan's systems and recovered a deleted section of its constitution.

He cleans corrupted files for Captain Chaos and fights the Disciples of Deus during the February raid until he is disconnected; even his skills are dwarfed by Deus.

characters.name: Captain Chaos
characters.title: Sysop, Shadowland Seattle
characters.description: Captain Chaos is the senior sysop of Shadowland Seattle and the editorial voice who introduces its files: wry, occasionally sardonic, and stubbornly committed to getting the story out whatever the risk.
characters.background: He is a former journalist named Jim, who works from a small Everett apartment threaded with the cables of his own mainframe, drinking real Amazonian coffee from a mug whose patina took years of not washing.
characters.notes:
[2055 – later developments] He edits and distributes the Denver files and moderates Shadowland's discussion of the Nexus.

[2056 – later developments] On 21 January he verifies and distributes the recovered Bug City files.

[2057 – later developments] Dunkelzahn's will leaves him a file, JackBNimble, which he never manages to crack.

[2060 – later developments] He gathers the Renraku Arcology files -- the UCC transcript, Neon Wraith's account, the Resistance testimony, Devon Eurich's headware dump -- and posts them in February, while the Disciples of Deus attack the Veso Lounge; he coordinates the defense and relays the 374-MP collection to Singapore before he is cut off. 'Jeez, it's fraggin' Bug City all over again.'

[2061 – later developments] He is Shadowland Seattle's elected senior sysop, spokesman and editorial coordinator.

[2064 – later developments] He dies in the Crash. With the Denver Nexus gone, he calls every Shadowland sysop into a war council and chooses to spread the news rather than chase the code eggs; he sends Smiley away, oversees the last backups alone, and cannot log off -- 'the captain goes down with his ship.' JackBNimble, shredded open by the worm, saves him as a flawed copy in a backup cluster, marked for deletion. His death ends the era of local Shadowland nodes.
contact_skills: Global sysop and data haven network

characters.name: Pax
characters.title: Leader of the Whites
characters.description: Pax, about twenty-four, led a cult-like tribe of otaku children in Atlanta -- herself the only adult -- into criminal enterprises including terrorist attacks on anti-technology groups, ruling with calculated cruelty and genuine ideology and loathing hypocrisy above all. She killed at least three people in the Matrix, among them P.A.S.S. Coalition leader Nelson Blythe, exposed as a secret simsense addict and rigged to die on his own feed, and left calling cards reading 'pax vobiscum'. She speaks in a slow, seductive CAS drawl.
characters.background: She answered Deus's call to the Renraku Arcology among the first wave of otaku 'summoned to witness the Coming' and was the first of them Transfigured. She leads the Whites, runs the arcology's otaku-conversion program with fanatical devotion and cold calculation, and keeps floor 280 as her domain. Unlike her followers she knows exactly what she serves, and does not care.
characters.notes:
[2061 – later developments] In Deus's home host she appears as a bone-white woman with elongated fingers, ratty black hair, bat wings and a black robe, her otaku as armored angels with flaming swords. It bothers her that she has been kept in the dark about parts of the plan, and she quietly makes contingency plans.

[2064 – later developments] Driven out of North America by Overwatch, she moved her tribe, Ex Pacis, to the Far East. The Fading has left her gaunt and twitching on the drugs she takes to delay it: 'The Matrix is nothin' but a cold grave to us.' She designed the Jormungand worm and brokered the Winternight alliance in person at Valhalla, thinking the cult perfect patsies while being double-crossed throughout. After the Crash she and her lieutenants vanish.
contact_skills: Otaku tribes of the Far East

characters.name: Sherman Huang
characters.title: Renraku America President
characters.description: Sherman Huang is president of Renraku America, the authority over Renraku's Seattle arcology, and a member of the United Corporate Council's Inner Circle. Formal and controlled, he answers for Renraku's UCAS performance through a Byzantine bureaucracy.
characters.background: He personally recruited Dr. Vanessa Cliber to Renraku's Artificial Intelligence Project in the 2040s and helped design early versions of the Arcology Expert Program himself.
characters.notes:
[2054 – later developments] Inazo Aneki bypasses him to deal with arcology project manager Donald Acres, while Huang tries to install Hiroshi Ushida.

[2060 – later developments] After the shutdown he calls an emergency UCC meeting and admits outright that Renraku has lost control of its Seattle arcology -- some 100,000 people trapped, some Red Samurai and residents went over to the enemy -- floats the decker Leonardo as a suspect, and deflects hard questions about Renraku's own AI research until Samantha Villiers forces the truth out. Options discussed include a military strike, Strain III bacteria, or magical barriers. Accounts disagree on whether he was in San Francisco or escaped from inside with his guard; an outlandish rumor says the Huang running Renraku America is a lookalike controlled by Deus.

[2061 – later developments] He manages Renraku America after the SCIRE disaster; his responsibility for Deus is unconfirmed. The Banded hold 'Sherman Huang' on floor 260 of the arcology.

characters.name: Samantha Villiers
characters.title: Fuchi Representative
characters.description: Samantha Villiers leads Fuchi Systems Design and sits on the United Corporate Council's Inner Circle. She is sharp, unflappable, and never shy of turning an accusation back on whoever made it. She is Richard Villiers' former wife.
characters.background:
Fuchi's representative at the emergency UCC meeting called after the shutdown; ex-wife of Richard Villiers, founder of the rival corp Novatech, whom Renraku publicly suspects of using the crisis to weaken Renraku further. She flatly denies Fuchi's or Novatech's involvement ('we're preoccupied with Fuchi's internal affairs at the moment') while trading barbed history with Federated-Boeing's Jessica Sirianni over an unrelated semiballistic crash.

In 2050, Villiers is a UCC Inner Circle member and leads Fuchi Systems Design.

She holds a voting stake, earlier worked at Fuchi Systems Design, and in 2054 leads Fuchi Northwest under Richard Villiers's faction.

In 2061, Samantha owns seven percent of Novatech, leads Novatech Seattle, and quietly pays runners to watch over Cara.
characters.notes:
[2054 – later developments] She holds a voting stake and leads Fuchi Northwest in Richard Villiers' faction.

[2060 – later developments] At the emergency UCC meeting after the arcology shutdown she denies any Fuchi or Novatech involvement and needles Sherman Huang about Renraku's AI project until he nearly admits Deus may be sentient. A useful contact for any Fuchi- or Novatech-adjacent run tied to the crisis.

[2061 – later developments] She owns 7 percent of Novatech from the divorce, runs Novatech Seattle, and quietly pays runners to watch over Cara Villiers.

[2064 – later developments] She stands beside Richard on the IPO podium making a show of unity, while noting Renraku's falling stock and hinting that Damien Knight will soon need a new chess partner. Tempted by Renraku at a depressed price, she may offer her Novatech stock to the mysterious owner of Trans-Latvian Enterprises for a loan large enough to bid; if TLE agrees, Villiers's mystery shareholder could hold 34 percent of Novatech.

characters.name: Leonardo
characters.title: Independent Decker
characters.description: Leonardo is a decker and a genius of extraordinary magnitude, with certain derangements. On 20 April 2057 he simultaneously infiltrated and shut down the main hosts of all eight AAA megacorporations without tripping a single alarm, then issued extortion demands. He has never appeared in person.
characters.background: Technology stolen or reverse-engineered from Leonardo went into the Arcology Expert Program alongside Morgan's dissected code; together they produced Deus. He secretly built a hidden ultraviolet host inside the SCIRE to watch for emergent AIs, and may have tracked Deus's birth in real time; Dunkelzahn apparently knew and wrote it into his will.
characters.notes: [2060 – later developments] Renraku names him its prime suspect in the arcology shutdown, with no evidence. Samantha Villiers suggests a megacorp may have quietly dealt with him after 2057. Whether he is alive, dead or complicit is unknown; alive, he could be an unpredictable ally.

characters.name: Richard Villiers
characters.title: Novatech President/CEO
characters.description: Richard Villiers, president and CEO of Fuchi Industrial Electronics, is one of the most respected and feared men in the UCAS and head of the Villiers family's third of Fuchi. Solidly built, black-haired, with no obvious cyberware and a photographic memory, he is a showman as much as a businessman, the center of attention wherever he goes, and forever touted as one of the most eligible bachelors in the country.
characters.background: He made his name as a Boston corporate raider, then saw the potential of Matrix Systems' prototype cyberdeck, the Portal; its founders, Ken Roper and Michael Eld, died within an hour of each other under murky circumstances, and Villiers bought the ruined company cheaply and parlayed its technology into a third of Fuchi. He has spent decades maneuvering against his co-owners, the Yamana and Nakatomi families, and is widely, never provably, believed to have arranged Kiyoshi Nakatomi's death in 2035. He wears a 2013 World Series ring from the last time the Yankees won.
characters.notes:
[2054 – later developments] He runs Fuchi Americas from New York.

[2057 – later developments] Dunkelzahn's will gives Miles Lanier a Renraku board seat and starts Fuchi's collapse. Through the shell Cambridge Holdings he strips some 22 subsidiaries out of Fuchi Americas.

[2058 – later developments] He uses Boston as a power base against the Nakatomi and Yamana factions.

[2059 – later developments] He sends Renraku's stock into a nosedive, drives Fuchi to self-destruction and builds his share into Novatech, one of the smallest corporations ever to earn AAA status. He is suspected, without proof, of sabotaging Flight 1118 to kill Corporate Court justice David Hague, and survives repeated assassination attempts.

[2061 – later developments] When his cleanup man Nigel Terwilliger is caught also selling to Renraku, Villiers receives the runners at his Seattle penthouse at 3844 Belmont Avenue, pays them with a bonus, has Miles Lanier execute Terwilliger on the spot, and asks them to cover his escape from a Red Samurai ambush -- a favor he repays on his own terms.

[2064 – later developments] Drunk in a Boston club in October 2063, he tells Lanier Novatech has a year at most against Art Dankwalther, and resolves on the IPO. He rings the opening bell on 2 November; at 10:39 the IPO cash lands and Novatech bids for every company Dankwalther holds, and then the Crash hits. Afterward he has everything he wanted -- Novatech the world's third-largest corporation, merged with Transys-Erika and holding the Seattle AR contract -- and hates running a public company: 'Dankwalther forced us into the IPO... I'm in hell.'

characters.name: Miles Lanier
characters.title: Novatech Security Director
characters.description: Miles Lanier heads Fuchi's internal security: an ex-UCAS Army sniper who would have made general had he stayed, and one of the great tactical minds of his generation. He looks years younger than he is -- a bit taller than average, slight, chestnut hair a week overdue for a cut, near-black eyes that never seem to blink and that he never admits are cyber. Arrogant, demanding and undeniably brilliant, he rarely smiles and notices what others miss. He is Richard Villiers' close friend.
characters.background:
Fuchi's head of internal security and Richard Villiers' close friend until Dunkelzahn's will handed him a Renraku board seat and four million shares of Renraku stock in 1957 -- he left Fuchi within the day. His inside knowledge helped Renraku leap ahead of Fuchi technologically for two years, until a June 2059 Corporate Court ruling forced him back to Fuchi custody. He resurfaced as Novatech's security director when Villiers formed the corp that October.

In 2054, former sniper Lanier heads Fuchi Internal Security, and his approach to magical security is changing.

Lanier's move from Fuchi security leadership to a Renraku board seat reshapes Boston corporate conflict in 2058.

In 2061, Lanier owns three percent of Novatech, directs security, and hires experienced runners as resource adjusters.
characters.notes:
He is changing Fuchi's approach to magical security.

[2057 – later developments] Dunkelzahn's will hands him a Renraku board seat and four million Renraku shares, and he leaves Fuchi within the day. Whether he truly defected or is part of an elaborate Villiers scheme is unknown; Renraku chairman Yukiako Watanabe's three deniable loyalty tests settle nothing. His knowledge puts Renraku ahead of Fuchi for two years.

[2059 – later developments] A June Corporate Court ruling forces him back to Fuchi custody, and in October he resurfaces as security director of Villiers's new Novatech, purging Yamana and Nakatomi loyalists and redesigning security.

[2061 – later developments] He owns 3 percent of Novatech and hires experienced runners as 'resource adjusters'. He shoots Nigel Terwilliger dead in Villiers's penthouse the moment his double-dealing is confirmed.

[2064 – later developments] He does the footwork to hold the IPO together, hunting Art Dankwalther's assets and hiring runners to shadow bought bank executives and find Dankwalther himself. He is a trained boxer who once dropped Villiers across a room with one punch.

characters.name: Tadashi Shiawase
characters.title: Shiawase President/CEO
characters.description: Tadashi Shiawase is president and CEO of the Shiawase Corporation and son of its chairman, Sadato Shiawase. Capable, and inclined to reject his father's pure bottom-line thinking when he gets the chance, he is too cowed to push hard for fear of being replaced.
characters.background: He is unlikely to come into his own until his father retires or dies, and neither seems likely soon. His weakness is his reckless teenage daughter Hitomi, who has nearly died at least once slipping her bodyguards.
characters.notes:
[2061 – later developments] He is privately involved in Etsu Powicke's HMHVV research.

[2064 – later developments] Korin Yamana replaces him as CEO in the post-Crash takeover, and his stake falls from 11 to 9 percent; he holds temporary control of his comatose father's 3 percent. He is quietly forging ties with politicians who dislike Yamana's growing friendship with the Emperor.

characters.name: Lucien Cross
characters.title: Cross Applied Tech CEO
