characters.description: Lucien Cross, president and CEO of Cross Applied Technologies, is nearing seventy and shows no sign of slowing down: he still oversees Cross Matrix Technologies personally, holds weekly division-head teleconferences and visits every major CATCo facility quarterly. Polite to a fault, he drives a hard bargain without raising his voice and never forgets a favor or a grudge; his employees call him 'Old Stone-Face'. He is Quebec's central power broker.
characters.background: He programmed Damien Knight's 2033 Nanosecond Buyout as 'David Gavilan's' collaborator, took a commission instead of stock, and kept the original planning records proving Knight's identity as insurance. Over two decades he built Cross Matrix Technologies into Cross Applied Technologies, quietly funded by Dunkelzahn for years before that patronage became public. In 2053 he survived Knight's hired assassin -- the Seraphim took the bullet -- after stealing Bioleve from an Ares shell company, and he has survived three more suspicious 'accidents' since Dunkelzahn's death removed his protection.
characters.notes:
[2059 – later developments] Leonard Aurelius sells his Ares stock to buy into CATCo, giving Cross cash and insider knowledge of Knight.

[2061 – later developments] He takes a personal interest in Dr. Olivia Marchand's Project Legion distributed-decking research -- 'If it doesn't pan out, heads will roll.'

[2064 – later developments] He dies on 2 November when the EMP kills every system on his corporate jet on its descent into San Francisco; his son Jean-Marie inherits CATCo, and Damien Knight declares open season on it. The shadows have conspiracy theories about the crash.

characters.name: Leonard Aurelius
characters.title: Cross Applied Board Member
characters.description: Leonard Aurelius has chaired Ares Macrotechnology's board since winning a 2049 proxy campaign against Damien Knight, who had taken the top spot from him in the 2033 Nanosecond Buyout. He has spent his life in the shadow of his famous, domineering father, Nicholas Aurelius, afraid of losing what Nicholas built -- a conservative, if intelligent, leader as a result.
characters.background:
Ousted from Ares' top spot by Damien Knight's Nanosecond Buyout in 2033; spent decades trying to reclaim it. An explosive argument with his youngest daughter finally pushed him to stop living for his dead father's legacy. Sold all his Ares stock in 2059 to buy into Cross Applied Technologies, giving Cross both cash and detailed insider knowledge of Knight.

Aurelius is Nicholas Aurelius's heir and won the 2049 proxy campaign that removed Damien Knight from the Ares chair.

Aurelius remains a major Ares shareholder and Knight rival in 2058, cultivating board influence and seeking information useful against Knight.

In 2061, Aurelius owns a major CATCo stake, leads Cross Global Development, and sponsors long-term runner contracts.
characters.notes:
[2054 – later developments] He and Knight are deadlocked.

[2058 – later developments] He cultivates board influence and gathers anything he can use against Knight.

[2059 – later developments] An explosive argument with his youngest daughter finally frees him from his father's legacy. He sells all his Ares stock -- privately to Arthur Vogel, to arm the man most likely to trouble Knight -- and buys into Cross Applied Technologies, giving Lucien Cross cash and insider knowledge of Knight. He still hopes to reclaim Ares on his own terms, but will sacrifice that to destroy Knight.

[2061 – later developments] He owns a major CATCo stake, leads Cross Global Development, and sponsors long-term runner contracts.

[2064 – later developments] While Ares dismembers CATCo he does nothing -- a rift with the board, preparation to retire to Zurich-Orbital with his son Nicholas carrying on, or blackmail, since his daughter Evelynn has not played with her band in months. Meanwhile he is making a fortune from the sales. One of his trusted Johnsons hires runners to steal the Seraphim's database from Cross's Quebec City headquarters and later plant an altered copy.

characters.name: Buttercup
characters.title: Yamatetsu Shareholder
characters.description: Buttercup is a free spirit who sits on Yamatetsu's board. In human form she is a petite, pretty Japanese girl of about eighteen with long black hair, an expressive face that glows when she is excited or agitated, and an unnatural grace; she sometimes floats slightly above whoever she is talking to.
characters.background: She was summoned centuries before the Awakening and has been free since before the twentieth century, long treating mortals as beneath her notice, rewarding and punishing them on a whim. After she clashed with Dunkelzahn, he bound her into an underprivileged ork's body for a year and a day to teach her humility; since then she has championed equality among all sentient life, and used Dunkelzahn's own investment strategy to build a major stake in Yamatetsu. Anyone who learns her true name can attempt a telepathic link with her. She bitterly resents, and mercilessly eliminates, anyone who tries to bind her.
characters.notes:
[2057 – later developments] After Dunkelzahn's death she pushes Yamatetsu toward its meta-friendly policies.

[2059 – later developments] She has chairman Tadamako Shibanokuji killed by a possessed nurse rather than let his anti-metahuman faction keep his votes -- only she knows for certain -- then produces proxies for nearly a quarter of the stock to move the headquarters to Vladivostok and buys more, reaching about 37 percent alongside Yuri Shibanokuji.

[2061 – later developments] She is Yamatetsu's largest shareholder and architect of its Pacific Prosperity Group alignment and public rehabilitation.

[2062 – later developments] As 'Ms. Johnson' -- 'Yes, I get that a lot' -- she hires runners for Hestaby's Balance plan to rein in Wuxing and put the two corporations on even footing, and never wants Wu Lung-Wei to learn of it. Hideo Yoshida's helicopter strike on the Eye of the Needle is meant to drive her out of the physical world for a month and kill whoever she is meeting.

[2064 – later developments] She and Yuri Shibanokuji use the Crash to remove CEO Saru Iwano and install Anatoly Kirilenko.
contact_skills: Yamatetsu board politics and the Pacific Prosperity Group
Geomancy, dragon lines and the power sites of the Pacific Rim

characters.name: Wu Lung-Wai
characters.title: President/CEO, Wuxing, Inc.
characters.description: Wu Lung-Wai heads Wuxing, Inc., the Hong Kong corporation his father built. Brilliant, charismatic and extraordinarily shrewd, he insists on meeting face to face rather than by telecom or Matrix conference -- which, with unconfirmed reports of magical activity around him, has some calling him a social adept.
characters.background: He inherited Wuxing from his father, Wu Kuan-Lai, who founded it and helped force Hong Kong's independence in 2015, but died in 2039 without seeing his dream of a united Pacific Rim front realized. Records also spell his name Wu Lung-Wei.
characters.notes:
[2057 – later developments] A 200-million-nuyen bequest from Dunkelzahn lets him finally build Wuxing into a real power, along with the Jade Dragon of Wind and Fire.

[2059 – later developments] He founds the Pacific Prosperity Group.

[2060 – later developments] He wants Dunkelzahn's bequest to Hualpa, the Elemental Scrolls of Ak'le'ar, badly enough to hire a Seattle runner team through the fixer Denise Pierce while the Scrolls are on loan to MIT&T.

[2062 – later developments] He used the Jade Dragon to intensify the power site under the Wuxing Skytower, which has drawn ever more chi since; the side effects -- warped magic across Hong Kong, disrupted dragon lines, perhaps Japan's disasters -- bring Hestaby and Buttercup against him, and Buttercup wants him never to learn of her part.

characters.name: Jessica Sirianni
characters.title: Federated Boeing CEO
characters.description: Jessica Sirianni is Federated-Boeing's director of aircraft weaponry, a self-made workaholic who rose from squatter origins and has a reputation for ruthlessness in business and personal dealings alike -- a hands-on manager unafraid to break the rules when it helps her or her company.
characters.background: Born in the poorest part of Auburn, she taught herself from stolen books and with the help of compassionate teachers, reached Seattle Central Community College, and paid her own way through an aerospace engineering degree at the University of Washington before rising from draftswoman. She keeps a wide range of shady connections, some from before her Federated-Boeing career, and is in a succession rivalry for the top job.
characters.notes:
[2057 – later developments] Late in the year, after a power struggle with William Yourel, she becomes president and CEO of Federated-Boeing.

[2060 – later developments] She trades barbs with Samantha Villiers over a semiballistic crash at the emergency UCC meeting.

characters.name: Lofwyr
characters.title: Saeder-Krupp CEO
characters.description: Lofwyr is the great dragon who owns and runs Saeder-Krupp Heavy Industries: he took over the corporation in 2037 and secured his control with a management buyout. He conducts his business behind a human face and a telecom line rather than in person, his voice 'like liquid amber'. His emotions always seem mild, only mild interest in nearly everything -- except his rage, which 'could shake down Everest'.
characters.background: To his kind he is Gold-Master. In dracoform he is larger even than Ghostwalker, his scales gold, copper and burnished brass with undertones of terra cotta, every movement studied and precise, his aura placid with tremendous control. He plans on a long horizon and works through agents, and takes obvious pleasure in a clever plan well executed. He sits on Tir Tairngire's Council of Princes.
characters.notes:
[2054 – later developments] He gives particular attention to Saeder-Krupp's position in Berlin, and is said to dislike the city's anarchist state.

[2059 – later developments] On 15 August he has his own Corporate Court electors appear to betray him by voting to seat Wuxing's Li Feng, winning Japan's trust, baiting Aztechnology and Ares into a vote he wanted, and sowing suspicion among his rivals. He hires Abu Khalid's Blackscarf Revolutionaries to raze an abandoned Renraku observatory near Altyar in Iran, erasing evidence that the decker Leonardo had been there.

[2061 – later developments] He remains Saeder-Krupp's sole owner while delegating more daily control, pursuing information and political influence.

[2062 – later developments] Dunkelzahn willed him the Jewel of Memory, making him Loremaster in fact without risk; the upstarts who contested it, Nachtmeister among them, paid the ultimate price. When Ghostwalker challenges the claim he declines to say whether he arranged Dunkelzahn's death rather than lie before witnesses, concedes a Rite of Succession fought through proxies, and lets his brother Alamais steal the physical Jewel, knowing its essence is what matters. To runners holding the gem in the metaplanar Citadel he offers anything within reason -- delta-grade cyberware, lore, wealth, longevity, an island -- sworn as an oath, or else all of Saeder-Krupp turned to ruining their lives. He may also sponsor a quiet recovery of the Gagarin data, wiping the module and leaving it for Yamatetsu to find empty. Beaten by Hestaby, he tells her he underestimated her and it will not happen again, and is thrown when she offers friendship: 'What is friendship to us?'

characters.name: Rowena O'Malley
characters.title: Finnigan Family Heir
characters.description: Rowena O'Malley, dark-haired, freckled and impish-looking, has a driving, ambitious personality behind her youthful face. Raised a Mafia princess but educated at Harvard and licensed to practice law in the UCAS, she is claiming her 'rightful place' as head of the Finnigan family and capo of Seattle after her father's death, convinced she can modernize the Mafia while honoring its traditions.
characters.background: Her father, Don James O'Malley, sent her East to school to keep her out of the family business; she stayed close to him and enjoyed 'family protection' through his friend Don Conor O'Rilley of Boston during ten years at Harvard. She survived an assassination attempt ordered by Bigio within a week of the funeral.
characters.notes: [2058 – later developments] Elite Mafia bodyguards protect her at all times, and runners may be hired to guard her. She wants her father's killer found and Bigio and Ciarniello involvement proved, which would discredit both rivals and win Don McCaskill's backing. James Michael Finnigan plots to force her into a marriage that would surrender her claim; rescued, she leaves him at the altar. Grateful runners can expect future work.

characters.name: Lickety-Splits
characters.title: Mr. Johnson
characters.description: Lickety-Splits, a Mr. Johnson, is extremely short but not a dwarf, with gnarled, twisted limbs that all still work, a scarred body, a thin, tightly groomed mustache and a shrill, nasal squeal of a voice. What disfigured him is not clear, and woe to anyone who asks; he is not self-conscious about it at all, and it has made him more confident. Sharp, calm and friendly, fond of colloquialisms, he dresses well but casually so as not to look like a corp shark, and two ork bodyguards in matching leather coats would die to get him out. 'Would any of you like some ice cream? It's quite good here.'
characters.background: He has worked for his employer for several years with a good track record. Whether that is Ares, Aztechnology, Saeder-Krupp, Shiawase, Novatech, Proteus, Shibata or a government is not known.
characters.notes:
He is weird and eccentric but reliable: he never screws anyone over, rehires productive teams, and tends to hire for jobs with more to them than meets the eye.

[2062 – later developments] He runs the shadow side of the Gagarin operation, paying 500 nuyen a head just to fly out on a week's notice and 20,000 each for the job; his employer decides whether the device is recovered, wiped, corrupted or destroyed.

characters.name: Hestaby
characters.title: Great Western Dragon
characters.description: Hestaby is the great western dragon of Mount Shasta, who has claimed the mountain as lair and domain for many years and defended the land around it against anyone who came for it, turning back an attempted Tir Tairngire invasion of northern California in 2053 -- which is why the Northern Crescent took her for its shield. In dracoform her scales are the color of amber and her wingspan would dwarf a fighter jet. In human form she is a tall, striking woman with long auburn hair framing an almost elven face and deep honey-amber eyes.
characters.background: She is a progressive as dragons go: she genuinely likes and admires the young races, has watched them develop, and was inspired by Dunkelzahn's willingness to defy custom. She plays her cards as close as he did, deflecting what she will not answer with 'You're better off not knowing that.' She also goes about as 'Abby Nightbird', a shaman of modest apparent ability whose aura masking no runner can penetrate; taken hostage, she allows it and leaves when she likes. To her kind she is the Orange Queen.
characters.notes:
Reports of her backing for the Talismongers Association, her personal meetings and her taking the form of a deer are unconfirmed.

[2062 – later developments] Her new seat on the Tir's Council of Princes reads to many in the Crescent as treason, costing her supporters and splitting her own lodge. Dunkelzahn left her the key to his private datastore on Zurich-Orbital, and she has taken up his cause. She enters the Rite of Succession unwillingly, to keep the dragons' conflict from wrecking what she is building and because someone must win it who will hand the prize back -- and she does, returning the Jewel to Lofwyr, refusing the Loremaster's title, ruling that Dunkelzahn's dispersal stands, and offering Lofwyr friendship instead of rivalry. She heals injured runners with a touch and loses esteem for those who kill unnecessarily.
contact_skills: Draconic politics and the rites of the Council of Dragons
Northern California, the Shasta Enclave and Tir Tairngire's Council of Princes
Half a million nuyen a head and personal gratitude

characters.name: Ghostwalker
characters.title: Great Western Dragon
characters.description: Ghostwalker is a great western dragon with scales the color of old ivory, a peer of Dunkelzahn, now master of the Denver Front Range Free Zone. In human form he is tall and thin, dressed all in white, his almost pure white hair slicked back from a high forehead.
characters.background: His body lay in a deep, dreamless sleep near Denver during a long sojourn in the higher astral planes. His spirit returned through the astral rift Dunkelzahn's death left in Washington in the last days of 2061; he immediately reclaimed his old domain, assaulted the Aztlan sector of Denver, destroyed its teocalli, and made clear that Aztlan would be removed and everyone else would acknowledge him. He was clearly close to Dunkelzahn and considers himself rightful heir to his position. His alliance with the Nexus data haven and his open-door petitioning policy show he is learning the new Age fast. To his kind he is Doll-Maker.
characters.notes:
Attacking him is suicide: he recently leveled much of a city sector and fought off armed attack craft, and he will kill anyone who tries, perhaps leaving one alive to warn others. He has a short temper, fits of pique, and no love for this new Age. He accepts the Children of the Dragon's worship as his due but dislikes the cult's name and has kept its prophet Morningstar waiting without an audience.

[2062 – later developments] Outraged at the violation of draconic tradition in Dunkelzahn's will, he calls the Council of Dragons -- 'HOLD!' -- and challenges Lofwyr's claim. At the Denver warehouse he questions runners, knows when they lie, pronounces Morningstar sincere, has Goldwing pay them, and then eats Goldwing for wasting his time.

characters.name: Hualpa
characters.title: Great Feathered Serpent
characters.description: Hualpa is perhaps the most prominent feathered serpent in the world: he led a coalition of Awakened forces, other dragons among them, that overthrew the government of Brazil and founded Amazonia, now recognized by most of the world as a legitimate nation and a bastion of Awakened rights and progressive ecology. He is something of an enigma even by dragon standards.
characters.background: Peace-loving at heart but willing to do whatever the future of the world requires, he is wary of technology for the damage it does and holds magic superior and more natural -- a philosophy that costs Amazonia the full use of modern tools. His great concern is Aztlan, the embodiment of everything he fears; he wants Aztlan and Aztechnology out of power so the damage, above all from the Yucatan War, can be healed.
characters.notes: [2062 – later developments] Dunkelzahn left him the Elemental Scrolls of Ak'le'ar. He backs the Rite of Succession partly because the fate of his bequest is already in doubt, and hopes greater standing will pull other dragons away from the power games of Lofwyr, Lung and Ryumyo. When runners return the Scrolls, a feathered serpent thanks them for Amazonia; if they impressed him he may hire them to root out Reynaldo Ocelopan's confederates in Macapa.

characters.name: Rhonabwy
characters.title: Great Western Dragon
characters.description: Rhonabwy is a great western dragon, scarlet and small-scaled with green eyes, who claimed a territory around Llandovery in Wales shortly after his awakening in 2012. He is a territorial investor and patron of the arts with lasting influence in the region. No human form of his is known.
characters.background: He plays the corporate game differently from Lofwyr: a shadow investor with shares in a great many corporations -- never enough to control a top-tier corp, more than enough for insight into most of them -- and tremendous wealth from shrewd investment. He and Lofwyr dance politely around each other, always testing. A collector with a vast hoard, some of it older than any known human civilization, he loves music above all, supporting education and performance, though his taste runs to folk, classical and opera rather than nova-rock. Legend gives him a rival sea dragon in Cardigan Bay and ties to the Arthurian legends; he neither confirms nor denies either. He has kept up a long, friendly rivalry with Celedyr.
characters.notes:
He is very difficult to lie to. Attacks bounce off him or are turned by automatic magical defenses, and persistent attackers become stone or toads until he has made his point.

[2062 – later developments] Dunkelzahn left him the Silver Songbird. Forbidden by the Rite from harming another dragon's agents, he offers thieves a hunt instead -- five minutes' head start, no spirits -- and keeps his word if they escape, having hidden a kilo of C-12 in the cage in case they do. He may be impressed enough to hire them later.

characters.name: Celedyr
characters.title: Great Western Dragon
characters.description: Celedyr is a great western dragon first sighted at Caerleon in southeastern Wales on 26 December 2011, where he lairs beneath an ancient Roman amphitheatre. Communication, and language in particular, fascinates him. The Knights of Rage, founded in 2043, serve him as patron.
characters.background: He is kinder toward the young races than Rhonabwy, and perfectly ruthless about his own interests. To his kind he is Stone-Diver. In human form he calls himself Mr. Johnson: a tall, fair-skinned man with brassy hair, in a long belted robe and sandals, a canny negotiator unused to being questioned.
characters.notes:
[2052 – later developments] Reports tie him to Transys Neuronet funding at Caerleon.

[2062 – later developments] Transys Neuronet has built a high-tech complex over his lair and given him millions in equipment and researchers for his support and occasional insights. At the Council of Dragons he speaks for Lofwyr's claim. Hestaby wedges his rivalry with Rhonabwy open by feeding him runners and intelligence on Rhonabwy's lair; he pays 150,000 nuyen each or up to twice that in Transys goods, with no advance and no scouting, and holds runners who decline as guests of the Knights of Rage until another team has done the job.

[2064 – later developments] He is a candidate for the chairmanship of the merged Novatech and Transys-Erika, though the Crash hits his portfolio and Malmstein outmaneuvers him. Online for the IPO through Transys' Project Cerebus, he is caught in the Singularity Event; his body goes on full life support with orders never to disconnect him, and what changed places that morning is unknown.

characters.name: Mujaji
characters.title: Great Feathered Serpent
characters.description: Mujaji, the Rain Queen of Africa, is a great feathered serpent who lairs near the Cape of Good Hope and tends to keep to her own affairs, markedly less involved in mortal politics than Arleesh.
characters.background: The Rain Queen of Africa lairs near the Cape of Good Hope and tends to keep to her own affairs -- markedly less active in mortal politics than Arleesh. Hestaby reads her support for the Rite as her own business, but suspects a desire to shore up her position in the face of events in Africa and perhaps to curry a little favour with Hualpa and his domain in Amazonia.
characters.notes: [2062 – later developments] At the Council of Dragons she keeps close to Hualpa and Arleesh and raises the practical objection, asking what becomes of the rest of his scattered hoard, then rises after Hualpa to back the Rite, perhaps to shore up her position against events in Africa and win a little favor with Amazonia. She is neither ally nor enemy, and may become a client.

characters.name: Ronin (Michael Bishop)
characters.title: Founder of Overwatch
characters.description: Ronin, founder of Overwatch, is a Eurasian man in his mid-twenties, thin and slightly shorter than average, with a stronger presence and a better speaking voice than most people expect of a Matrix jockey. His Matrix persona looks just like him, in a dark cloak, pulling program icons out of a pouch.
characters.background: Born Michael Bishop and raised in a Renraku corporate community, where his talent for computers was noticed early, he went from a company school to MIT&T on a company scholarship and was selected as a covert operations agent. As the otaku Babel, he learned first-hand what Deus is -- an insane god that must be stopped at any cost -- and knows it better than anyone in Overwatch.
characters.notes: [2064 – later developments] He leads a third faction among Deus's scattered Nodes, apart from both Deus and Megaera.
contact_skills: Matrix intelligence on Deus, the Banded and the arcology
Otaku tribes and the Deep Resonance

characters.name: Anatoly Kirilenko
characters.title: Yamatetsu CEO
characters.description: Anatoly Kirilenko is Yamatetsu's new CEO, a maverick with a hard-earned reputation as innovative and somewhat crazy, who wanted no settling-in period: within days he announced a radical five-year plan to transform the corporation. He was the mastermind of Yamatetsu's Mars mission, and is a descendant of the rocketry pioneer Konstantin Tsiolkovsky.
characters.background: His predecessor Saru Iwano was blamed for Yamatetsu's Crash losses -- he had nothing to do with it, but it gave Buttercup and Yuri Shibanokuji their chance -- and word in Vladivostok is that Iwano is leaving for Yakashima. Kirilenko has family in the Vory.
characters.notes: Turkestan is on fire, with Yamatetsu, Global Sandstorm and Saeder-Krupp fighting over its government. Yamatetsu preys on smaller Pacific Prosperity Group members alongside Federated-Boeing, has tried and failed to take Cross Biomedical, and has set up joint ventures with the Genesis Consortium.
contact_skills: Yamatetsu strategy and the Mars program

characters.name: Saint James
characters.title: Independent Fixer
characters.description: Saint James is an independent Seattle fixer: a tall man in a gray business suit with a clipped British accent and impeccable manners, who greets even a room of armed strangers graciously, offers real coffee, and waits for everyone to be comfortable before talking business. Two burly bodyguards stand in the corner. He is amused rather than offended by attempts to out-negotiate him, and prone to trailing off into old war stories.
characters.background: Until recently he was a shadowrunner himself and bodyguard to one of Seattle's most successful fixers; when that fixer was forcibly retired, he went into business on his own, surprisingly successfully. He remembers where he came from and looks after his people, and deals honorably with those who treat him honestly -- but if attacked he blacklists a team so thoroughly that their shadow careers end. He works with a man named Smithers.
characters.notes: [2064 – later developments] He is a trusted fixer for high-profile, high-paying runs, and a favorite ally of Rose Croix's Walter Broward -- until he sees Broward's contracts dry up before the IPO, sells him out to DocWagon, and runs the sting himself, meeting runners at the base of the Space Needle and paying 15,000 each plus the erasure of their DocWagon dossiers. 'The run was a set-up, a trap. This was my idea. Great isn't it?'
contact_skills: DocWagon executive access at franchise-CEO level

characters.name: Domingo Ramos
characters.title: Aztechnology Employee
characters.description: Domingo 'Ding' Ramos is the elf son of Julio Ramos, a founder of ORO, the cartel alliance that became Aztechnology. He is a major Aztechnology shareholder and board director with a protected residence near Concepcion.
characters.background:
Primary subject 99-804 is identified as Donald Ramos, a trideo actor and cousin of Domingo Ramos of Aztechnology. Another account identifies Domingo himself as the trideo action hero who attended the Rose Croix launch, became an Ebony customer, and served as official spokesperson. Records do not resolve the conflict.

The 2056 corporate profile identifies Domingo `Ding` Ramos as ORO founder Julio Ramos's elf son, a major Aztechnology shareholder, and a board director with a protected residence near Concepcion.

In 2061, Ramos remains a passive Aztechnology shareholder and international social figure; darker claims are reported but unconfirmed.
characters.notes:
[2061 – later developments] He is a passive shareholder and international social figure; darker claims about him are unconfirmed.

[2064 – later developments] Rose Croix courts him: accounts differ on whether its trid-star spokesman at the ribbon-cutting is Domingo himself or his cousin, the actor Donald Ramos, whose clone is on file.

characters.name: Chuck
characters.description: Chuck is a youngish, slender bartender with long hair, mechanical eyes and an unusually kind manner, who puts friends onto work and trades broad but low-grade information on a give-and-take basis.
characters.background: He links friends to work and trades broad but low-grade information on a reciprocal basis.

characters.name: The Chromed Accountant
characters.title: Financial Info Broker
characters.description: The Chromed Accountant is a Seattle-based information broker specializing in corporate finance and tax fraud, and a regular source on Shadowland for anything involving money: laundering, jurisdictional barriers, transaction sieves, and how the megacorps really stand.
characters.background: He is a former undercover financial-crimes operative for the IRS. No legal name or appearance is known.
characters.notes: [2064 – later developments] He writes up the Crash's corporate fallout, from Ares carving up Cross Applied Technologies to why Aztechnology could never go public.

characters.name: Toshiro Mitsuhama
characters.title: MCT President/CEO
characters.description: Toshiro Mitsuhama, son of the founder Taiga Mitsuhama, is president and CEO of Mitsuhama Computer Technologies, though he holds no major voting block of his own.
characters.background:
In 2054, founder Taiga Mitsuhama's son leads MCT despite holding no major voting block.

In 2061, Toshiro leads MCT's aggressive expansion and presents with extensive rejuvenation and visible cyberware.
characters.notes: [2061 – later developments] He leads MCT's aggressive expansion, and shows extensive rejuvenation and visible cyberware.

characters.name: Samba Oi
characters.title: MCT Chairman
characters.description: Samba Oi is chairman of the board of Mitsuhama Computer Technologies and sits on the boards of six other megacorporations, though MCT is the only AAA among them.
characters.background: Street talk holds that Oi and three fellow directors -- Shin, Saigusa and Uehara -- are the oyabun of four major Japanese Yakuza families, which funded Taiga 'Tiger' Mitsuhama's empire as a respectable front for laundering money and now draw a legitimate income from it besides. The claim is unconfirmed.

characters.name: Inazo Aneki
characters.title: Renraku President/CEO
characters.description: Inazo Aneki is president and CEO of Renraku Computer Systems, the aging founder who built it from the wreckage of Keruba International. Renraku's early years were plagued by scandal and corruption, but as he has aged it has become a strong, steadily growing firm. His elite Red Samurai grew out of the ceremonial guards he created, and his pet project is the Seattle Arcology, which he champions over the objections of board chairman Yukiako Watanabe.
characters.background: He survived an internal coup attempt, purged corruption through the 2030s, and returned Renraku to the first tier by 2045. Watanabe owns less stock than her forceful personality suggests and lets him run Renraku much as he likes; when she balks at money diverted to the arcology's sagging finances, he has so far always won her over.
characters.notes:
[2054 – later developments] He bypasses Sherman Huang to deal directly with arcology project manager Donald Acres.

[2060 – later developments] After the arcology shutdown he takes indefinite leave for Tibet; acting CEO Haruhiko Nakada invokes Dunkelzahn's bequest of the Seal of the Green Gloves to get him there, and the Tibetans pledge to try to heal his mind.

[2061 – later developments] Released in Hong Kong in May, still 'not ready' by the Tibetans' account, he remains chief executive in absentia. His killswitch shatters Deus's code on 11 May.

characters.name: Sadato Shiawase
characters.title: Shiawase Chairman
characters.description: Sadato Shiawase chairs the Shiawase Corporation and leads its dominant family faction; his son Tadashi is president and CEO.
characters.background: Sadato and his sister Soko hate each other and celebrate each other's birthdays by sending assassins. Their brother Ryoi is dead -- killed five years ago when one of Soko's birthday presents to Sadato missed -- but remains the registered owner of his shares. Tadashi sympathizes with his aunt, but his domineering father has him firmly in hand.
characters.notes:
[2061 – later developments] He uses family proxies and the MIFD in his struggle with Soko.

[2064 – later developments] He lies in a coma; Tadashi holds temporary control of his remaining 3 percent.

characters.name: Adolphe III
characters.title: Grand Duke
characters.description: Adolphe III, heir to the Grand Duchy of Luxemburg, has been head of state of the Grand Duchy of Westrhine-Luxemburg since 2043, when the governments concerned granted the Cattenom disaster area independence, glad to be rid of its people.
characters.background: When he was born in 2012, people thought him deformed by the radiation Cattenom spilled over Luxemburg. For the loss of his health and country the French paid him the highest compensation of all time -- rumor says five to ten million ecus a year, which would make him his Land's main source of revenue. Some say he made a great deal more selling his land rights inside the SOX to the corps.

characters.name: Berthold I
characters.title: King of the Black Forest
characters.description: Berthold I, King of the Black Forest, is a former citizen of Freiburg who helped found the Troll Kingdom and now rules it from that city. At 44 he has reached a remarkable age for a troll, and the experience of that long life may be what has let him steer his realm in profitable directions.
characters.background: He was supposedly a fairly good shadowrunner in his day -- 'Fairly good? There won't be a better street samurai in this century!' He refuses to rent out his subjects cheaply for hard labor, which the corps hate.
characters.organization_name: Troll Kingdom of the Black Forest

characters.name: Jaromar Greif
characters.title: Duke of Pomorya
characters.description: Jaromar Greif is Duke of Pomorya, the elven Baltic duchy loosely associated with the German Alliance. He presides over its governing council and advances a Baltic political and cultural mission. The Jaromarsburg, the living-wood temple of Svantevit on Kap Arkona, is named for him.
characters.background: Every month shamans and nature mages from Pomorya and beyond gather at the site sacred to the Great Mother near the Jaromarsburg for a rite he conducts himself. Claims about his priestly and magical powers are unconfirmed.

characters.name: Shiva
characters.title: Nexus Master Sysop
characters.description: Shiva is the master sysop of the Nexus, the Denver Data Haven. His icon is a tall, slender, black-clad man with perfect features and short, fine hair, rendered so perfectly it looks hyper-real. No one knows who he is, or will say; he has been a major part of the Nexus for more than a decade, and his expertise shows years of experience in high-capacity network operations before that. Of the four key figures of the Nexus, most people name him the most knowledgeable, and the most dangerous if provoked: generally calm, aloof, almost withdrawn, his anger is a force of nature once aroused.
characters.background: He mentors otaku. Some identify him with Gennedy Polemov; the identification is disputed.
characters.notes: [2061 – later developments] He remains a calm Nexus administrator, in a long rivalry with Bash.
contact_skills: Nexus master sysop and otaku mentor access

characters.name: Bash
characters.title: Influential Nexus sysop
characters.description: Bash is the mysterious rival of Shiva and one of the Nexus's two most influential sysops. No one has ever seen him in the flesh -- or if they have, they did not know it or are not talking. He can be brutally pragmatic.
characters.background: He may be Andrew Loewes, a hot icebreaker left a high quadriplegic by a motorcycle accident, blind and unable to interact with the real world, who lives in a long-term care facility in Quebec, is addicted to the Matrix and hides behind many handles and icons. Or 'Bash' may not exist at all, and be the second personality of Shiva.
characters.notes: [2061 – later developments] He is a volatile guardian and enforcer of the Nexus with long-standing rivalries.

characters.name: Cap'n Kluge
characters.title: Nexus Decker
characters.description: Cap'n Kluge is a Nexus decker whose icon is a cartoon rubber ball that gets around by rolling, bouncing frenetically off everything in its path, or waddling on stumpy legs; all his utilities are just as cartoonish. Since the decker Lachesis disappeared, he has the hottest reputation for using the Nexus's resources to dig up paydata anyone sane would call inaccessible. He comes across as young and brash, full of the ego of top deckers.
characters.background: He is Tom Kwan, a child prodigy who graduated from MIT&M in computer science at fourteen and was snapped up by Fuchi, making a major name at Fuchi-New York. The brashness is partly a front: he is a very private man with few friends and many acquaintances. He left Fuchi seven years ago for making the unforgivable error of continuing to investigate a hostile penetration of the Fuchi datacore after his supervisors told him to drop it.
characters.notes: [2061 – later developments] A report that he died in a Fuchi extraction conflicts with a later sighting at Novatech and cyberdeck evidence; whether he survived is unresolved.
contact_skills: Nexus decker and paydata specialist access

characters.name: Nahid Mostafavi
characters.title: Nexus Sysop
characters.description: Nahid Mostafavi -- Spirit in the Matrix -- is one of the four key figures of the Nexus. Her icon is a sheer, color-shifting scarf that moves almost hypnotically, making no pretense to human form, and her utilities are all colors and shifting fields of light. Iranian by descent, born and raised in France, she began at Siemens AG's Paris division before going freelance as a network consultant and sysop, came to Denver in 2047 on a short contract, and stayed. In her mid-forties, she has the clear-eyed wonder of someone half her age.
characters.background: Of the Nexus's four powers she is the most driven by the philosophical aesthetics of the Matrix rather than practicalities, and considers the Nexus worth existing in its own right -- but when necessary she can be as brutally pragmatic as Bash.
characters.notes: [2061 – later developments] She reportedly leaves the Nexus early in the year for a behind-the-scenes role with Mosaic and Vox; her motive is rumor.
contact_skills: Nexus sysop and network consultant access

characters.name: Bianca Cuthbertson
characters.title: CAS Sector manager
characters.description: Bianca Cuthbertson is the manager of Denver's CAS Sector, an experienced politician who used to serve as controller of the Dallas/Fort Worth metroplex. Less than a year into the job, she has done more good than anyone expected: she took on the sector's security force, a special division of Knight Errant notorious for brutality and corruption, kicked several of its worst managers out of the sector, and turned it into a disciplined and professional, possibly incorruptible, force.
characters.background: Reports indicate cas sector manager with reusable access through information, services, influence, negotiation, or a recurring rival path.

characters.name: Juanita Iglala
characters.title: Pueblo Sector Board Chair
characters.description: Juanita Iglala, black-haired and composed, chairs the governing board of Denver's Pueblo Sector, which appoints and fires the sector's officers; the sector president is Julio Caron.
characters.background: Reports indicate pueblo sector governing-board chair with reusable access through information, services, influence, negotiation, or a recurring rival path.
characters.notes: The street joke that she was a hired killer before going into politics is irony, not a rumor.

characters.name: Samuel Clemens Waybridge
characters.title: UCAS Sector commissioner
characters.description: Samuel Clemens Waybridge is the commissioner of Denver's UCAS Sector. He used to be General Samuel C. 'Bomber' Waybridge, commanding officer of the Fourth Mechanized Infantry Division out of Fort Carson -- a logistics wizard, originator of the 'security zone', or free-fire zone, and a major player in the Genocide Campaign, or would have been if it had ever got off the ground. His appointment says everything about how the UCAS government sees Denver.
characters.background: Reports indicate ucas sector commissioner with reusable access through information, services, influence, negotiation, or a recurring rival path.

characters.name: Henequen
characters.title: Trader
characters.description: Henequen is a feathered serpent, small for his kind at about ten meters, who runs Henequen Enterprises, a luxury import-export house in Denver's Sioux Sector. He presents himself as a Rain Forest shaman and a lighthearted bon vivant with a strong, unpredictable sense of humor, and often goes about as a staggeringly handsome Hispanic youth, his aura masked.
characters.background: He lives in the Thornton district. Those who have done business with him suspect the humor hides his true motives. He may have founded La Venta, the movement to overthrow the Aztlan government, before he had to flee Aztlan; Aztechnology hit squads have tried to kill him a dozen times.
characters.notes: [2056 – later developments] Aztlan reports say he founded La Venta in 2044; rumor places him in Denver hiding from Aztechnology retaliation, which another source disputes.

characters.name: Clayton Wilson
characters.title: Founder, Former CEO
characters.description: Clayton 'Clay' Wilson founded Lone Star Security Services, incorporating it in Austin, Texas, on 22 July 2017, and patterned it on the Texas Rangers of the Old West. Popular accounts paint him as a rough-and-tumble, hard-nosed man born in the wrong century, who would have been at home among the wildcatters of the Texas oil boom -- or on the deck of a pirate ship.
characters.background: He built Lone Star's early expansion, acquiring Bartholomew Security and Absolute Software, and was removed as chief executive and board chairman in 2036, when his brother James took over.
characters.notes: His wealth, his rivalry with the company he founded, and his alleged plans for revenge make him a patron or a recurring rival; claims about his patrons and blackmail are unconfirmed.

characters.name: James Wilson
characters.title: Chief Executive
characters.description: James Wilson is the chief executive of Lone Star Security Services, brother of its founder Clay Wilson, whom he replaced in 2036. He modernized Lone Star's recruiting and training, though standards have changed little since Clay's day apart from the acceptance of women 'peace officers'.
characters.background: He hands out titles like cigars, leaving Lone Star with a plethora of chiefs, captains and executive chiefs doing much the same job.
characters.notes: [2051 – later developments] In June he succeeds Wendy Manderscheid as board chairman, gives up the CEO post to Theodore W. D. Winslow, and steers most of a new stock offering into Winslow's portfolio.

characters.name: Theodore W. D. Winslow
characters.title: Chief Executive
characters.description: Theodore W. D. 'Teddy' Winslow of Austin, Texas, is Lone Star's chief executive, appointed by James Wilson in June 2051. He spends about fifteen weeks a year in the Austin headquarters and the rest on a private island in Indonesia, handling emergencies by telelink and delegating to the nine-member Executive Advisory Council.
characters.background: Teddy Winslow becomes Lone Star's chief executive in June 2051, delegates through the Executive Advisory Council, and handles emergencies by telelink while away from Austin.
characters.notes: [2054 – later developments] He is trying to standardize the job titles James Wilson scattered through the company.

characters.name: McBean
characters.title: Political Journalist
characters.description: McBean is a tall, weathered elder of mixed race with long off-white hair, blue-yellow eyes and arthritic, trembling hands, who looks and lives like a mountain hermit. He is a journalist, author and former political aide and a witness to the history of the Awakening.
characters.background: He was close to the events of the 2011 Great Ghost Dance, Howling Coyote, the Sovereign Tribal Council's politics, and Edna Wallace.
characters.notes: He is evasive, fearful, volatile and hard to find, and gives up what he knows only after runners advance his own obscure agenda.

characters.name: Madeleine Muller
characters.title: Corporate Investigator
characters.description: Madeleine Muller is a corporate investigator and media patron: a slim, exceptionally beautiful French-German woman with honey-blonde hair and gold-flecked hazel cybereyes, elegantly dressed, with controlled gestures.
characters.background: She made her name exposing a scandal in Naples in 2050 and went on to corporate and environmental reporting, building transatlantic influence.
characters.notes: She hires researchers and bodyguards and trades corporate intelligence for service. Claims of assassination attempts, a stalker and blackmail are unconfirmed.

characters.name: Roz Nuaru
characters.title: Magical Historian
characters.description: Roz Nuaru is a magical historian who teaches shamanic and metaplanar history: a short, broad-shouldered woman of mixed Maori and European appearance, with very long curly black hair, dark eyes and long hands, restlessly sociable and never without her cat.
characters.background: She is a free spirit who took the identity of the human Roz after Roz disappeared in 2047, and masks her nature. She is linked to Carruthers and has turned down government approaches.
characters.notes: She acts as a patron and adviser on free spirits and the metaplanes.

characters.name: Kung Soo
characters.title: London criminal patron
characters.description: Kung Soo -- Grandfather Soo -- is a major London crime boss: a small, tanned, unusually youthful Chinese-British man with long gray hair in a single braid, silver-gray eyes, Western dress and a clay pipe, with a quiet, dangerous refinement.
characters.background: His family emigrated from Hong Kong in 1997. He rose through the Zhing Wo, switched to the Xiao Ziang side in 2017, and now runs a network of his own that rivals the Xiao Ziang and the Si Peng.
characters.notes: He hires specialists, pays well, and demands loyalty, discretion and obedience; his police connections and operations are well hidden.

characters.name: Thomas Roxborough
characters.title: Aztechnology Director
characters.description: Thomas 'Roxy' Roxborough is a corporate raider, a major Aztechnology shareholder and one of its most influential directors. He has no public physical presence: he deals with the world only through the Matrix.
characters.background: He was diagnosed with a medical condition in 2049 and has been treated since at Universal Omnitech's Anderson facility. His physical state and who really controls him are the subject of competing theories.
characters.notes:
[2061 – later developments] He remains an influential director and raider, active through the Matrix.

[2064 – later developments] A falling-out with the board sends him to Universal Omnitech, souring that relationship badly.

characters.name: Ivar J. Lindstrom
characters.title: Governor of Seattle
characters.description: Ivar J. Lindstrom is the mayor of Downtown Seattle and the son of Charles C. Lindstrom, the charismatic mayor who in 2018 and 2019 annexed the towns around Seattle into the metroplex and is remembered as its father.
characters.background: He has wanted the governor's chair for as long as anyone remembers and considers Marilyn Schultz an upstart who robbed him of his rightful place. He has deep corporate connections and the support of Humanis sympathizers.
characters.notes:
[2060 – later developments] With Governor Schultz lost inside the Renraku arcology, Seattle elects him governor in an emergency election. He promises to do everything in his power for those trapped inside, but the street says he will let Schultz rot, and is arranging for her never to come back.

[2061 – later developments] During the blackout he calls out the Metroplex Guard, souring relations with Lone Star over jurisdiction.

characters.name: Marilyn Schultz
characters.title: Governor of Seattle
characters.description: Marilyn Schultz is governor of the Seattle metroplex, elected on a promise of clean government. From day one she has prosecuted anyone in her administration caught breaking the law and shown no mercy to officials even suspected of underworld ties; Seattle's administration is reckoned one of the cleanest anywhere, and she is seen as a pillar of honesty and courage.
characters.background: She abhors the syndicates' violence, chips and prostitution, but knows the metroplex has neither the money nor the resources for an all-out war, and keeps a kind of unofficial truce with them.
characters.notes:
[2053 – later developments] She mobilizes the Metroplex Guard at Lone Star's request during the gang war.

[2058 – later developments] Kenneth Brackhaven attacks her as 'soft on crime' over the Mob War.

[2060 – later developments] She disappears inside the Renraku arcology when Deus seizes it; her fate is unknown.

characters.name: William Loudon
characters.title: Head of Lone Star Seattle
characters.description: William Loudon has led Lone Star's Seattle division since 2049 as Marshal and Seattle's Chief of Police, working from the Lone Star Security Building at Second Avenue and Union Street. He is a better administrator than military commander, steady and competent, and careful to cover himself in case a crisis blows up in his face.
characters.background: Loudon has led Lone Star's Seattle operation since 2049 and survived multiple corporate administrations.
characters.notes:
[2053 – later developments] He treats the gang war as warfare, puts every officer on active duty and asks the governor to mobilize the Metroplex Guard.

[2058 – later developments] As the Mob War escalates, he fears Lone Star Central will replace him if the cops cannot keep a lid on organized crime, and quietly looks into hiring 'freelance operatives' for missions his officers cannot legally do.

[2059 – later developments] He publicly promises more patrols during the paranormal-animal crisis while Lone Star secretly hires runners to end it quietly.

[2060 – later developments] He has survived two changes of corporate administration.

characters.name: Kenneth Brackhaven
characters.title: Executive and Politician
characters.description: Kenneth Brackhaven runs Brackhaven Investments, the umbrella for his family's wide-ranging Seattle interests, from Wordsworth department stores to Golden Lion Inns, MiniMarts and malls, out of humble offices at Third and Union. He is well known for his charity -- research centers, youth havens, crisis hotlines, hospital and museum wings -- and is running for president of the UCAS on the Archconservative ticket. His uncle is Karl Brackhaven, president of the Seattle Humanis chapter, which leads many to assume Kenneth is involved with Humanis too, though no evidence has been found.
characters.background: The real Kenneth Brackhaven goblinized into an ork and was murdered by his father Charles in 2023; this Kenneth is a conditioned SINless double, raised by Karl to share his hatred of metahumans. Karl runs his campaign and will kill to keep the secret.
characters.notes:
[2058 – later developments] He is widely expected to run for governor of Seattle in 2060.

[2060 – later developments] Brackhaven Investments ambushes a runner team at the Salish-Shidhe border with Humanis muscle hired through his defected Yakashima fixer Anthony Munson. A former presidential candidate, he campaigns repeatedly for governor; his Humanis ties, funding and influence over Governor Lindstrom are rumored but unconfirmed.

characters.name: Crystal / Maria Dancer
characters.title: Nexus Data Organizer
characters.description: Crystal has organized the Nexus Heap in Denver for almost ten years and supports the local otaku. Her Matrix persona looks like quartz; her physical appearance is not known.
characters.background: Her real name is Maria Dancer, and she may once have programmed for the Pueblo Corporate Council.

characters.name: Oni
characters.title: Mosaic Security Chief
characters.description: Oni is a physically imposing Japanese ork who goes by his street name. He oversees programming, architecture and security for Mosaic, and backs up Tenchi at meetings.
characters.background: In 2061, Oni oversees Mosaic programming, architecture, and security and supports Tenchi at meetings.

characters.name: The Smiling Bandit
characters.title: Scientific data broker
characters.description: The Smiling Bandit is a private Matrix explorer and prankster whose persona is a grinning, bandana-wearing bandit. He studies research systems, sells selected findings, and publishes dangerous discoveries through the data havens. He takes only scientifically interesting work. He is said to be a Latino man; nothing else is known of his appearance.
characters.background: He also works as B. Traven and Professor Frink; whether he is El Bandito is unproven.

matrix_hosts.name: Ares Macrotechnology -- Ares Arms public catalog host
Federated Funds Net
matrix_hosts.notes: A small, relatively lightly protected host containing Hernandez's account, worth about 180,000 nuyen. An active alert starts a shutdown countdown. The host's LTG is not publicly listed.

matrix_hosts.name: Max Foley's System
matrix_hosts.notes: A seven-node system containing Max Foley's blackmail files, Hotoda's recorded threat, and a bank interface, plus a public decoy datastore. On an active alert, Gum E. Bear can respond personally from his cyberdeck.

matrix_hosts.name: New Horizons Development (Matrix)
matrix_hosts.notes: A phone-accessible dead-end host containing legitimate zoning and public-relations files. New Horizons keeps its illicit business off the Matrix, and the host's LTG is unlisted.

matrix_hosts.name: Sorayama's Clinic (Chiba)
matrix_hosts.notes: A nine-node, samurai-and-castle-themed host in Chiba containing Maria's original modification records under the name Maria Aguilar. Its defenses appear as temple guards, oni, and a fu dog; an alert can also bring yakuza decker support.

matrix_hosts.name: Dragon Knights Mainframe -- System B
matrix_hosts.notes: The Dragon Knights' private mainframe contains mission briefings, Aztechnology resource lists, personnel dossiers, security clearances, and armory inventory. It is reachable only through System A's Security-Interface SPU. On an active alert, Lin Hwang can respond personally from his quarters.

matrix_hosts.name: Taetzel Building -- System A (Building Control)
matrix_hosts.notes: The Taetzel Building's public control system operates its servoguns, security cameras, and elevators. A hidden trap door behind the Security-Interface SPU leads to the Dragon Knights' private mainframe.
